clusters.architecture_notes: ReconciliationHarness (harness.py, one class with 71 methods) owns the per-project loop and drives Stage 1 (MemoryConsolidator), Stage 2 (TaskKnowledgeSync) and Stage 3 (IntegrityCheck). It does this through two hand-mirrored S1→S2→S3 drivers, run_full_cycle and _run_remediation_pass, plus crash-recovery, judge spawning, escalation filing and cycle-summary backstops. Each stage is a one-shot Claude CLI agent. It gets a prompt that tells it to pass agent_id 'recon-stage-<id>', and per-stage deny-lists (cli_stage_runner.STAGE*_DISALLOWED). Its writes go back through the fused-memory MCP tools, where server/tools.py and middleware guards route on the agent_id prefix. Findings flow through ReconReportState (server/recon_report.py), an in-process, persisted, per-run report with about 9 write-time and read-time dedup/fold rules. Stage 1 flags are then post-processed by about 12 incident-driven false-positive filters in flag_dedup.py, hand-chained in MemoryConsolidator.run (about 1,140 lines), before ledger dedup and suppression. Stage 2 merges flags from three channels: Stage 1 items_flagged, a Mem0 flag_for_stage2 semantic search (limit=100), and recon_report systemic findings. Control-plane state is now split. The SQLite ReconLedgerStore (recon_ledger.py) owns flag markers, suppressions, cycle summaries, standing decisions and suppression streaks. Mem0 still holds flag_for_stage2 markers, stage2_persistence_marker and escalation markers, task_count snapshots, and a write-only suppression mirror (answer to ask 2: partly migrated). Deterministic Graphiti sweeps run inside Stage 1: stale_status_snapshot_edge_sweep, stale_priority_override_edge_sweep and degenerate_task_node_sweep. Each one reverse-parses free-text LLM-extracted edge facts to retire mirrors of task-store and scheduler state. Their stats reach report.stats one key at a time. Prose dominates the core files: comments and docstrings are 76% of stale_status_snapshot_edge_sweep, 60% of flag_dedup, 61% of task_filter, 54% of recon_report and 49% of harness. That leaves 342 code lines in the 2,293-line sweep.
clusters.churn_exoneration: Partly misleading, not exonerating. Some of the counted churn is TDD step commits of real features: the 3037 blocked-family series and the 4386 enumeration-completeness feature. Roughly 10 of the 61 window commits on stale_status_snapshot_edge_sweep.py only maintain prose: d28a4231b8, 459acfb83b, e6023c29b8, eef5fdfc75, dc0097121f, 1f0057f348, 5f25db773e, fca657951c, 9178d652ef and 7264c546f4. The remainder are genuine bug-class fixes, and structure explains them. The same over- and under-matching class recurs because the sweep parses English, and every cancellation fix lands twice because there are two run drivers. The 13.5% fix ratio is a real signal for this cluster.
clusters.cross_system_notes: Graphiti ingestion (memory_service.add_episode and the graphiti-core LLM extraction) gives live task and scheduler state no typed edge. That is why the prose-parsing sweeps exist (stale_status_snapshot_edge_sweep, stale_priority_override_edge_sweep, degenerate_task_node_sweep) and why server/tools.py runs write-time prose lints for recon-stage writers only. middleware/task_interceptor.py returns gate refusals as untyped dicts, which drove the window's six targeted.py 'classify the response' fixes. Recon stage identity crosses into server/tools.py, five middleware guards and config/schema.py as a 'recon-stage-' string prefix. The repeated update_memory, reassign_edge and ensure_entity_node exposures to Stage 3 come from the CLI deny-lists and those allowlists disagreeing. fm-recon.1 stays weakened at high severity. The ledger now owns markers, suppressions, cycle summaries and standing decisions. Mem0 still holds the flag_for_stage2 channel (semantic search with a limit=100 top-N risk, no suppression), stage2_persistence_marker and escalation markers, and a write-only stage1_flag_suppression mirror that no reader consults.
clusters.root_cause: Identity and live state travel as strings and prose: stage identity is a prompt-instructed agent_id [[fm-recon.10]], live task state is mirrored into Graphiti as LLM prose and retired by an English regex grammar [[fm-recon.7]], flag identity has no home [[fm-recon.9]], and the S1→S2→S3 run driver exists twice [[fm-recon.8]].

clusters.architecture_notes: A task write goes through three strata. server/tools.py::create_mcp_server is a single 9,386-line function holding 62 MCP tools as closures. Its tool bodies run per-tool guard functions, then hand off to middleware/task_interceptor.py::TaskInterceptor, which applies further gates under a per-project asyncio write lock and emits reconciliation events. That ends in backends/sqlite_task_backend.py::SqliteTaskBackend, which owns the write-authority floors, metadata merge, schema validation and candidate_key dedup. On one update_task call I counted about 22 distinct checks across the three layers. The metadata blob is parsed about 13 times along the way: in tools.py by strip_markup_override, extract_files and model_overrides_error; in the interceptor by _reject_directory_locks_in_update_metadata, extract_snapshot_token and is_terminal_annotation_exempt; in the backend by the floor json.loads, strip_machine_authored_metadata, _strip_reserved_control_keys, _merge_metadata, a second incoming json.loads and parse_metadata twice (warn, then enforce). The typed shared/task_metadata.py::TaskMetadata is used only for validation. The backend discards the parsed model and stores merged raw JSON. Only two orchestrator consumers read the typed model (scheduler, flake_ledger), against about 138 raw metadata dict accesses in orchestrator/src. The status FSM vocabulary is single-sourced in shared/task_statuses.py. The legality table shared/task_transitions.py::TRANSITIONS is consulted in one fused-memory place, gate 2e of TaskInterceptor._apply_status_transition (595 lines, about 12 sequential gates). The store's set_task_status checks vocabulary only. Caller identity is the self-reported agent_id string. Who counts as a recon stage, an orchestrator or an authorised provenance writer is decided by string prefixes, separately at each consumer. Rejections reach callers through two channels: dicts with ad-hoc keys returned by the guards, and typed exceptions raised by the backend. The interceptor converts only two of those exception types, and mcp_tool_errors turns everything else into {'error': str(e), 'error_type': class name} on the wire. The orchestrator scheduler then re-classifies those by string. The backend's cached write connection uses Python sqlite3's legacy implicit-transaction mode, with no explicit BEGIN. A separate cached autocommit read connection and a per-call fresh connection serve reads.
clusters.churn_exoneration: The window's fix density (139 commits matched '^fix') overstates bug-driven churn. 48 are TDD step commits named 'fix(...) GREEN ... step-N', for example task 4853's six steps. About 20 are lint, pyright, import-order or rebase-surfaced decorator fixes, for example 'collapse nested if (SIM102)', 'resolve pyright errors', 'decorate set_task_claimant surfaced by inter-iteration rebase'. 5 are the INV-8 loop-blocking ratchet being burned down: ea3f38bb11, 35e9d7480f, 92f145fc12, baade1b2d3, 2002a64e5f. That ratchet is a healthy gate working, not a defect class. Together that is about 73 of 139 (53%). Of the get_statuses staleness 'four recurrences', the first three (2455, 2651, 2694) were genuine connection-pin fixes. The fourth (3007) was diagnosed in reconciliation/flag_dedup.py::filter_stale_bulk_get_statuses_flags as a harness capture-versus-live read skew, not a store defect, so that recurrence chain is closed. The real bug classes are concentrated in metadata write semantics (2180, 3581, 4039, 4216, 2735, 3777, 3446, 3579, 5810), done-provenance authority (d553bc9571, 3777), the curator degraded streak (4448 x4) and provenance-stamp stripping (4532/4569 x5). Growth is also part of the picture: tools.py was touched by 262 commits from 72 distinct tasks in the window, the interceptor by 141 commits from 51 tasks.

clusters.architecture_notes: The dashboard is a FastAPI app (app.py plus api/ routers) over data/ aggregators. It reads three substrates. (1) The orchestrator's runs.db and each project's SQLite files, by raw SQL with string event_type and outcome literals. (2) Fused-memory over a hand-written MCP client that lives in data/memory.py (McpSession, _post, mcp_tool_call, invalidate_session). (3) The escalation queue files, through the escalation package. MCP calls fan out via mcp_fanout.first_success (per-URL failover with a default 75s whole-operation deadline and transition-only logging) and are memoized through module-level TTLCache instances (8 of them, enrolled in a weak registry so the lifespan teardown can reap detached bypass tasks). http_pool.OrphanReaper reaches into httpcore internals to reclaim connections that native cancels strand. Numbers cross to the SPA as Datum envelopes (data/datum.py, server-side frozen dataclasses with to_wire, mirrored by static/redux/datum.js), and the task vocabulary is generated once from shared/task_statuses.py into task_vocab.js. The recent PRD leaves (5586-5596) moved handlers into api/ and counters into single readers (task_snapshot.js, merge_queue.js), which is real SPOT progress. The SPA is about 45 classic scripts loaded by hand-ordered tags in index.html, communicating through window.DF_* globals, with in-browser Babel for .jsx and a single hand-bumped ?v=NN literal on every tag. Tests cover the frontend by regex over served source, by node:vm reconstruction of the shared script scope, and by git-history-based checks of the cache-buster integer. Orchestrator vocabularies (WorkflowOutcome, OutcomeKind, EventType) are not importable from the dashboard, which depends only on shared and escalation, so they are re-spelled as strings.
clusters.churn_exoneration: Partial. Much of the app.py (13/86) and tabs.jsx (12/50) fix-prefixed churn is the dashboard-one-datum-one-path PRD (tasks 5586-5596) landing as small `fix(NNNN): GREEN ...` TDD steps: healthy feature work with a fix prefix, and it deleted duplicate counters (task_status_counts.js, task_done_count.js, orch_summary.js). The tabs.jsx size was explicitly measured against the 1,500-line ceiling in commit d99ed11c60 and stayed under it. Neither file is the structural problem. The 35% fix ratio of mcp_fanout.py, the cache-buster commit stream (57 subject matches since 2026-07-06) and the three shared-scope blank-screen incidents (5849, 5949, 6017) are genuinely bug-driven and map to findings 1 and 2.
clusters.cross_system_notes: Finding 3: the dashboard's paged census walk (data/tasks.py::_walk_pages, _walk_statuses) compensates for fused-memory's get_tasks/get_statuses lacking a snapshot token, an aggregate/count tool and field projection, and for get_statuses' docstring that contradicts its implementation (advance by page_size versus returned); the fix belongs in fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/tools.py. Finding 6: the dashboard cannot import the orchestrator vocabularies (WorkflowOutcome, OutcomeKind, EventType), so the fix is to relocate them into shared/ as shared/task_statuses.py already is. Finding 4: the dashboard's OrphanReaper and shielded _post compensate for httpcore 1.0.9's PoolByteStream.aclose stranding connections on a native cancel (task 5319/6063); this is a third-party defect, so the reaper stays a version-pinned shim. Finding 5: the repo has three MCP clients (dashboard memory.py, orchestrator mcp_lifecycle.py, shared mcp_post.py/mcp_envelope.py), and the dashboard is the one that did not adopt the shared primitives created after task 4023.
clusters.root_cause: A private MCP protocol copy with a five-dict single-flight cache [[dashboard.6]] [[dashboard.10]], orchestrator vocabularies re-spelled as strings [[dashboard.11]], and SPA load-order invariants held by comments and source-text tests [[dashboard.7]] [[dashboard.5]].

clusters.architecture_notes: memory_service.py::MemoryService is the single service object behind every memory MCP tool. It is wired by post-construction setters and attribute assignment from server/main.py (set_write_journal, set_known_projects, set_recon_journal, set_recon_ledger, set_event_buffer, `memory_service.taskmaster = ...`). It holds at least ten responsibilities: lifecycle, durable-queue dispatch (_execute_durable_write routes on operation strings and sends every unknown operation to Graphiti), the nine-pass post-ingest identity reconcile (lines ~2878-5836, about 26% of the file), the add_memory/add_episode/add_system_record/replay write paths, the module-level metadata-vocabulary and canonical-uniqueness seam, unified RRF search, cycle-summary presence, child cascade delete, update_memory/update_edge/reassign_edge, entity administration (mint/rename/merge/delete/summaries) and status. GraphitiBackend (graphiti_client.py) is a thin per-method wrapper over graphiti_core and about 52 raw FalkorDB `graph.query`/`ro_query` sites. It has no single egress, so timeout, row cap, group scoping and edge liveness are decided at each site. Mem0Backend, by contrast, has one `_timed` helper. Write-content policy lives in two places. Most of it sits inline in the add_memory/add_episode closures inside server/tools.py::create_mcp_server (about 17 tool-level gates for add_memory), above the layer that resolves category=None. The rest is in the service (flag-record contract, metadata validation, referent resolution). Answers to the four asks: (1) memory_service.py has about ten responsibilities and is 53% prose (2,196 comment and 3,833 docstring lines of 11,323). (2) Entity identity is a write-time guarantee only on the ingest path (_execute_graphiti_write holds GraphitiBackend._identity_lock_for across add_episode plus _reconcile_episode_identity) and in ensure_entity_node. merge/rename/delete/reassign do not take the lock, the lock is in-process only, and there is still no store-level uniqueness constraint. (3) One add_memory call crosses about 17 tool-level gates and then about 6 service-level gates. Each sibling entry point applies a different subset. (4) Timeout and cancellation are per-call-site in Graphiti: 15 wait_for sites, 4 of which swallow TimeoutError into []/None, and most raw Cypher has no bound. Mem0 has one convention. The durable-queue payload is an untyped dict with three producers (add_episode, add_memory, replay_from_store) whose key sets differ. The consumer pops keys and has legacy branches (the 3561 'uuid' key, the 5262 ambiguous key that can be None or ()). That is a secondary instance of the same missing-schema pattern and is not reported separately here.
clusters.churn_exoneration: Partial only. Of the 86 fix-prefixed commits on the core files in the window, 37 are TDD GREEN/step commits inside one task. Another 7 are mechanical (invariant renumbering after rebase, ruff/pyright, annotations, citing a rule by symbol). The 86 collapse to about 32 distinct task ids: 2451 = 6 commits, 4986 = 5, 3671 = 5, 5265 = 4, 3561 = 4. So the commit ratio overstates the incident rate by roughly 2.5x. The distinct-task themes are still genuine recurring bug classes: guard bypasses and false positives, timeout false-absence, row-cap truncation, edge-property loss on copy, regex fragments fixed one pattern at a time, and write-success misclaims. The churn should not be dismissed as feature churn.
clusters.cross_system_notes: graphiti_core (upstream) is missing three guarantees that drive most of the patching here. Its add_episode uuid= means LOAD, which needed four 3561 commits and a legacy-payload pop. Its entity resolution has no exact-name lookup and no Entity.name uniqueness constraint, which is why nine post-ingest reconcile passes exist. Its edge invalidation semantics around invalid_at/expired_at feed the 4714 saga. orchestrator/fused-memory durable_queue.py classifies graphiti NodeNotFoundError by regex over the message (_parse_not_found_uuid) because it refuses to import graphiti_core, which is a stringly-typed cross-module contract (3568/3586). reconciliation/stage_stats.py and middleware/dead_letter_escalator.py compensate for MemoryService.add_memory's conflated per-op success and its at-enqueue store claim. Recon Stage 1 (reconciliation/) and link-heal (maintenance/link_heal_*) are the main callers of merge_entities, rename, reassign_edge and update_edge, the mutators that bypass the identity lock. Qdrant has no unique constraint, so canonical uniqueness (memory_service.py::_check_canonical_uniqueness) is a documented TOCTOU check-then-write. It also ships warn-mode, so a second canonical lands, and that is owned by the 3626 enforce-flip gate. The 'recon-stage-' prefix routing spans middleware/task_interceptor.py and the execution_class, premise_lint and recurring_gate guards, so a CallerRole type would also simplify the task-routing hotspot.
clusters.root_cause: No Cypher egress chokepoint [[fm-memory.9]] and no home for write-content policy [[fm-memory.6]]; edge lifecycle is two nullable timestamps [[fm-memory.8]]; the identity lock is a docstring contract [[fm-memory.7]].

clusters.architecture_notes: TaskWorkflow (workflow.py) is one class covering about 16.7k of the file's 18,039 lines, with 180 methods and 69 distinct self attributes. Besides the PLAN→EXECUTE→VERIFY→REVIEW→MERGE driver, it hosts the recovery guards, merge-train coordination, steward supervision, main-health auto-heal and routing of review suggestions to the curator. W9 moved the core types into workflow_types.py: WorkflowStateMachine, a thin validator over shared.task_transitions that in practice only enforces terminal absorption, because every working phase projects to IN_PROGRESS; the frozen TerminalReport; the StewardOutcome union; the classify_failure→BlockDisposition table with 27 exception rows; and CancellationScope with an ordered on_terminal cleanup list. run() supervises _drive. It returns the stashed self._terminal_report when its outcome matches and otherwise builds an empty report; exit_contract.judge_exit then cross-checks report phase, machine state and the persisted status row, in log mode by default. Block exits funnel through _mark_blocked (555 lines, 12 parameters, 68 call sites). It enters BLOCKED, writes the row, files an L0 or an L1, starts the per-task TaskSteward, and maps the steward's typed outcome to DONE, REQUEUED, ESCALATED or BLOCKED. The steward's outcome arrives on an in-process asyncio.Queue but is then overridden by a fresh status read and an escalation-queue has_open_l1 probe. The ESCALATED branch's waiter (_wait_for_resolution) never reads that queue: it wakes only when an L0 is dismissed, via harness._on_escalation_resolved. Inner phases return a WorkflowOutcome with no payload, and the facts about a block travel on instance stash dicts. Retry and anti-thrash state lives in four places: RetryLedger in task metadata, the steward's PersistentMaps in guard JSON files, the scheduler's in-process requeue dicts, and the workflow's in-memory signature history. Prompts are assembled by agents/briefing.py::BriefingAssembler, which workflow.py mirrors with a hand-copied _BriefingLike protocol, from hand-written role constants in agents/roles.py. W9 answers: there is still no single authority for terminal state. The exit-contract judge and its write-failure ledger are a fourth mechanism that audits agreement after the fact.
clusters.churn_exoneration: The churn is partly misleading. In the window workflow.py grew from 8,835 to 18,039 lines over 345 non-merge commits: 189 feat and 43 fix-prefixed. Most fix subjects on the core files are TDD GREEN steps (for example 3170 step-2 through step-22, and 4023 GREEN) or corrections to prompt prose. So the 11.9% fix density mostly reflects feature growth under TDD, not instability. The recurring defect classes that are real are the orphan-L0 reaper, the steward's waits and fall-throughs, and misattributed block reports; the findings trace each to structure. The cost signal that remains is the growth itself: each feature lands as more methods and more instance state on one class.
clusters.cross_system_notes: Escalation subsystem: an L0 has no owner lease tied to the filing incarnation, and Escalation.category/severity are bare strings. That gap drives the dismissal loops in workflow.py and steward.py and the orphan-L0 reaper's liveness proxies in harness.py (_has_fresh_dispatch, _has_fresh_merge_phase, the merge_phase_liveness stamp). Merge lane: MergeOutcome encodes the blocked sub-kind in prose reasons, which drives workflow's six startswith arms plus a 'ff' substring fallback, unblock_types.classify_block_reason and b3_gate.check_proposal's prefix test. Fused-memory task store: metadata is written by whole-dict read-modify-write with no field-level compare-and-set, which drives workflow's _merge_fresh_metadata last-writer-wins merge for RetryLedger (prior workflow.5). Prompt prose in agents/roles.py restates escalation/dedupe.py and escalation/server.py policy and currently contradicts the server's severity-downgrade gate.
clusters.root_cause: Block facts ride instance stash dicts and five parallel vocabularies [[workflow.9]] [[workflow.11]]; terminal state is checkable but not single-sourced after W9 [[workflow.3]]; the L0 escalation lifecycle has no owner [[workflow.12]].

clusters.architecture_notes: verify.py (11,086 lines, 54% prose: 2,371 comment-only and 3,568 docstring lines) is still the hub. It holds the pytest-output regex layer, the subprocess/cgroup/admission executor (_run_cmd, _run_segmented, _target_subprocess_env), the log/junit archive, run_verification, run_scoped_verification with _aggregate_results, and the whole main-baseline / main-tip-sweep / isolated-rerun flake-confirm family. The W7 satellites are verify_cmd (structured VerifyCmd), verify_plan (derive_verify_plan), verify_classify (classify_failure dispatched on ToolKind), verify_categories (FailureCategory + CATEGORY_POLICY) and verify_cancel. They are clean leaves: none imports verify.py, so they pass heuristic 13. verify_runner (3,759 lines) is the exception: it reaches back into verify privates and up into merge_lane, and it also holds the wire codec, Local/RemoteRunner, the runner pool, HostAllocator, drift detection and unwired env-parity code. The key state crossing every seam is VerifyResult, a flat mutable dataclass with 18 fields: three output text blobs, a ', '-joined summary string, category as a plain str, and parallel attribution lists (failing_test_ids, failing_test_ids_by_module, failing_leg_categories) added one per incident. Per-leg facts exist only briefly as CheckRun inside run_verification and are flattened at the boundary. Every downstream consumer then re-derives leg and session facts by regex over the concatenated text: aggregation, failure_report, the merge cross-check veto, flake confirm, the sweep and offline_lane. Local merge verify runs LocalRunner on live config objects and ignores MergeVerifySpec. Remote verify ships the spec over ssh, rebuilds ModuleConfigs on the laptop and overlays four spec fields onto the laptop's own OrchestratorConfig. Its wire codec is dataclasses.asdict with a strict VerifyResult(**d), and no schema version. Answers to the four questions: (1) about 13 of the 22 recent verify.py fixes trace to the flattened, text-reparsed leg outcome. (2) Local and remote are parallel paths with two sources of truth, not one environment contract. (3) Classification is tool-dispatched, but its inputs and most downstream predicates are still regex over merged text. (4) Satellites pass heuristic 13 except verify_runner.
clusters.churn_exoneration: Partly misleading. Of the 22 'fix' commits on verify.py in the last three weeks, 10 are TDD step commits of just three tasks, labelled 'fix(verify): GREEN — ... step-N': 5627 ×6, 5337 ×2 and 5199 ×2. A further 4 are follow-through on the junit-retention feature (5670 series). So the raw count roughly doubles the number of distinct defects. The remaining genuine defect classes (3173 / 5082 / 5337 / 5492 / 6247 / 5580, plus the 5627 attribution loss) are real and share one root, finding 1. The churn is not healthy feature churn, but it is about 8 distinct bugs, not 22.
clusters.cross_system_notes: (1) The wire-skew outage was triggered from ANOTHER project's dispatcher. reify's RemoteRunner.sync_if_stale moved the laptop DF checkout that DF shares, so a VerifyResult schema change in DF broke both lanes. The missing guarantee (code identity and schema version on the verify wire) belongs in verify_runner, but the blast radius is the whole multi-host fleet. (2) merge_lane/worker.py's cross-check veto reads VerifyResult.failing_leg_categories and INDETERMINATE_VERDICT_CATEGORIES. It is a second consumer of the per-leg verdict facts that verify.py flattens, and it got its own 3173 patch. (3) offline_lane.py, workflow.py / workflow_types.py, evals/snapshots.py and merge_lane/worker.py import verify.py privates (_extract_failing_test_ids, _serial_pytest_str, _is_infra_oserror, _target_subprocess_env, _derive_task_files_from_git). Changes to those helpers propagate silently. (4) The laptop host substrate (tzdata, git config, CPython version) drove remote false-reds that the verify environment contract (ambient env minus a denylist) cannot express. The in-flight task 4843 (branch task/4843) is the current owner of the rc=143 / lint-type-as-unknown_test_failure class, and it is adding further regex arms.
clusters.root_cause: Leg outcomes are flattened to text and re-parsed by every consumer [[verify.8]]; local and remote verify have two sources of truth [[verify.10]] and an unversioned wire synced to checkout HEAD rather than running code [[verify.9]].

clusters.architecture_notes: The lane lives in orchestrator/merge_lane/. worker.py (22,081 lines, 57% prose) holds SpeculativeMergeWorker: 13,015 lines, 139 methods and about 105 instance fields. Above the class, worker.py also holds about 8,800 lines of module-level pipeline code: post-merge verify, main-health probe, admission/coalesce, train merge and landed-outbox reconcile. A request's state is spread across the request's own asyncio Future, five containers (_queue, _lane_buffers, _verifier_queue, _redispatch, _inflight), the ItemLifecycle registry with its _LEGAL_TRANSITIONS table, the _live_items object index, InflightEntry.status/vacated, InFlightMergeRegistry (one slot per branch, released by the future's done-callback), RequestLedger (passive sweep of futures) and the queue_store journal (pruned by a done-callback). Only ItemLifecycle has to be moved by hand at every exit arm. Train state is split across five places: GroupMergeRequest (in memory only; the scheduler callbacks come from a factory keyed on train_id), task-store status 'merge-deferred', stack-base git refs (branch_stack.py, driven from git_ops), a PersistentSet of derailed task ids, and runs.db train events. Landing has two authorities. LandedOutbox records write-ahead intent before advance_main. landing_evidence.py re-derives "did it land" from git for seven sites in harness, workflow and the escalation server. completion.py is an unblock-eligibility predicate and disposition.py does skew attribution; neither is a view of landed-to-done. gates.py runs post-advance gates through Gate/GateVerdict, but the verdict's OutcomeKind is dropped when the result becomes a MergeOutcome, which carries the failure class only as a reason-string prefix. Invariants are uniformly fail-soft: _note_transition never raises, _assert_single_writer runs only under ORCH_DEBUG_ASSERTS, and the *_violations/two_layer_invariants checks return list[str] after the fact. Fourteen old merge_*.py paths are sys.modules alias shims (removal owned by task 5037). 46 production import statements and 162 test files still use them. drift.py and shadow.py still read and write worker privates and import SpeculativeMergeWorker under TYPE_CHECKING (prior merge-queue.4, still weakened). A ratchet (scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py + orchestrator/tests/merge_lane_ratchet_baseline.json) gates every measure, including raw lines and prose_lines.
clusters.churn_exoneration: Partial exoneration only. About 10 of the 75 window fix commits are mechanical: ratchet bookkeeping, lint, typing and alias fixes (64d8021a19, 435869ea61, 6db3956661, b4fb450010, e9d3b12464, 721e655452, 73a4447bb7, bb5de0e8c7, 203cdc69b1, dc18791b80). The 221 commits on merge_lane_ratchet_baseline.json, including the 34 'fix' commits, are instrument bookkeeping; see the ratchet finding. The Aug-Sept merge_gates rename cluster (4d0f399461, b090822b66, 26e126340f, fa3f932b7d, 9d845f4c0d, feb139f697, d1ff3c9738, f72a570a4b, a478bee1b5) is partly the TDD build-out of a new rename-awareness feature rather than regressions. Across the last 3 weeks (21/60) the remainder is genuine, recurring defect structure: missed exit-arm transitions (the 4582 series, 10-04), coalesce trains stranding members across restarts (5371 R6/R7, 4737), and train CAS/derail handling (5070). These point at two seams: a request's terminal edge, and the fact that no durable record owns a train.
clusters.cross_system_notes: Several fixes in the lane compensate for guarantees missing elsewhere, and in some cases the lane leans on other systems. (1) The task store (fused-memory) holds a train member's state as the status string 'merge-deferred'. The harness stranded sweep excludes that status by design (Harness._reconcile_one_stranded), so the lane's in-memory GroupMergeRequest is the members' only owner; that is why crash and drain strandings land on the merge lane (4737, 5371 R7). (2) Fused-memory's set_task_status re-checks kind='merged' SHAs with merge-base --is-ancestor (middleware/task_interceptor.py). That is the real backstop for LandedOutbox write-ahead rows that the workflow guards and task_ground_truth treat as authoritative. (3) The scheduler dispatch gate (Harness → reconcile_landed_task) prunes non-landed outbox rows before re-dispatch. That ordering keeps the workflow's journal-first guards correct, and it is encoded nowhere in the lane. (4) workflow.py, unblock_types.py, b3_gate.py and scripts/review_model_admission.py parse MergeOutcome.reason prefixes, and the dashboard's merge-outcome vocabulary drift (prior dashboard.1) sits downstream of the same missing kind field. (5) The escalation server (escalation/server.py, git_authority.py) imports orchestrator.landing_evidence through function-local imports, so landing-authority fixes (3103) cross packages. (6) The verdict-integrity theme (laptop wire-skew 10-06, fast-PASS where a verify ran nothing, the laptop warm-verify flock orphan) surfaces in the lane, but its causes sit in verify_runner, the remote verify hosts and the verify gate code, not in merge_lane. The lane's _QUEUE_VERIFIED_MAIN_TIPS process-global (gates.py, fa95988c8e) is itself a compensation for main drift that no verify has seen green.
clusters.root_cause: Trains are the one unjournaled request kind [[merge-queue.7]]; terminal edges are taken by hand on each exit arm [[merge-queue.8]]; the outcome class survives only as a reason-string prefix [[merge-queue.10]]; outbox intent is read as a confirmed landing [[merge-queue.11]].

clusters.architecture_notes: harness.py has grown from 9,259 lines at 7f618211bb to 18,264 at 6551b75aba. Over 363 commits it became one Harness class with 197 methods, and 48.7% of its lines are prose (4,612 comment lines plus 4,278 docstring lines, with 461 'task NNNN' citations). By what the methods touch, it splits into five clusters: run()/dispatch core (101 methods), recovery and stranded sweeps (32 methods, 4,319 lines), escalation filing (29 methods, 2,270 lines), merge/offline-lane wiring (15), and the watcher supervisor (8). Background loops now go through background_service.LifecycleRegistry. Restart execution has a single seam, proc_supervision.RestartPlan, but deciding whether a fleet redeploy may start is still done separately by three deciders: the in-process StaleServiceRestartCoordinator (service_restart.py), the watchdog staleness backstop and the watchdog liveness probe (scripts/orchestrator-watchdog.py, a 3,243-line stdlib-only oneshot). All of them coordinate through JSON files that restart-all-orchestrators.sh writes with bash printf: the deploy clock, the lease, drain requests and heartbeats. Answer to ask (2): RestartPlan only executes a restart. The decision layer is still the script plus the watchdog plus the coordinator, and each re-implements the gating. Answer to ask (1): TaskGroundTruth.recovery_for has exactly one consumer, Harness._reconcile_one_stranded and its appliers. _recover_crashed_tasks, _already_landed_dispatch_gate, merge_lane/worker.py::reconcile_landed_task, _run_deterministic_recon_sweep and Scheduler._phase_redispatch_stranded_blocked still derive landing or stranding on their own, so at least five independent derivations remain. Even the one consumer rewrites the table's answer four times. Answer to ask (3): session_registry.py has no single purpose. It is a stdlib-only file holding session records and pid pointers, fleet-global cockpit DecisionRecords that mirror escalations, role leases, X11 window liveness and a 1,500-line argparse CLI. One file is forced only because skills/spawn/spawn-claude.sh runs it by absolute path. Its consumers are cockpit, scripts/sitting and session_hooks; the harness runtime uses only build_session_slug and the private _pid_alive (via service_restart). task_ground_truth.py is pure: frozen TruthReport plus a 10-row _RECOVERY dict. Policy that the table cannot express lives in comment-justified if-blocks in the harness applier.
clusters.churn_exoneration: Partial. session_registry.py (5,772 lines) did not exist at 7f618211bb. Its 157 window commits are mostly the Attention Rail and Fleet Cockpit features landing under TDD, and many are 'amend: document ...' commits. Its line growth and commit count therefore overstate defect density. Its real fix chain (3528, 3807, 3559, 3640, 3872, 4237, 4755) clusters on the decision-mirror join and the pid/lease contract, and finding 4 covers that. The churn in harness.py, the restart/watchdog files and task_ground_truth.py is genuinely bug-driven: crash-window recovery shapes, deploy-clock and lease collisions, and landing-attribution phantom-dones recur, as the fix subjects below show.
clusters.cross_system_notes: Escalation package: it issues no stable queue identity and emits no terminal-transition notification. session_registry compensates with a polled DecisionRecord mirror, a hand re-implementation of EscalationQueue's archive layout (read_escalation_status) and about 450 lines of string normalisation for the (project, escalations_dir) join (finding 4). Merge lane: its durable landed-outbox covers only landings it performed. The harness therefore keeps a live-git _already_landed_dispatch_gate for out-of-band landings, and TaskGroundTruth carries an INV-5 mirror of merge_lane/landing_evidence.validate_landing_evidence (finding 1). Deploy tooling: restart-all-orchestrators.sh has no lock of its own, so the in-process coordinator and the watchdog each pre-check an advisory lease. systemd-run's transient-unit-name collision acts as an accidental second overlap guard (finding 2). restart-fused-memory.sh has no lease at all. Workspace/uv layout: no component exports the per-unit import closure, so the watchdog and the coordinators hand-copy watched paths, and the fm tier fixed its copy only on 10-09 (finding 3). GitOps keeps lane-lifecycle and registration checks private, and harness recovery reaches into git_ops._lane_lifecycle seven times.
clusters.root_cause: Landed/recoverable disposition is decided in five places beside TaskGroundTruth [[harness.7]]; fleet-redeploy exclusion is an advisory check-then-act lease [[harness.8]]; each deploy unit's code closure is hand-listed five times [[harness.9]].

clusters.material_change: new cluster (not in the 2026-07-06 list; package created 2026-07-14)
clusters.architecture_notes: The package is a two-stage pipeline around one shared codebook. The nightly trickle (nightly.py::run_nightly) samples one UTC day (sampling, digest), has the coder (coder.py) code the digests, merges the codings into docs/legibility/confusion-codebook.yaml with codebook.apply_coding_record, commits the codebook, and then asks census_trigger.decide_for_project whether to launch census.py as a subprocess. census.py::run_census mines a ledger-keyed window to saturation, verifies novel clusters, synthesises, applies promote/reject/retire transforms (defined in census.py, not codebook.py), files tickets through submit_fn, writes the record and report, dumps the codebook, advances census-state.json, commits, and then ledgers the coded sessions. Durable state is spread over five stores. census-state.json is written only by census.advance_census_state and read by census_trigger.load_census_state, census_trigger.compute_tasks_landed and census_identity.prior_census. trickle-state.json is written only by trickle_state.record_run and read by nightly._escalate_barren_streak, check_trickle_progress and check_trickle_health. The codebook yaml is written by codebook.dump from both nightly and census. coded-sessions.sqlite is written by session_ledger, with the census as reader and both stages as writers. Each census run also leaves a plans/*.json record and .md report. Fail-loud is not one mechanism. nightly.post_escalation, census._build_default_escalate_fn, check_trickle_health.post_health_finding and check_transcript_persistence.post_findings each build an escalate_info envelope, and census.py adds ad-hoc best-effort try/except wrappers at _defer, _unlanded and the mass-rejection site. Every seam is injected (invoke, verify_fn, submit_fn, escalate_fn, commit, roll_back), which keeps the suite hermetic but makes run_census take 25 parameters. Question 4: census_trigger does NOT use the contract section 11 completion share. compute_tasks_landed is a raw fleet-wide done-count delta (threshold 120). scripts/check_run_completion.py does not exist in this tree. plans/completion-driven-triggers-prd.md and census-incremental-prd L8b own the convergence, so this is tracked, not an unowned defect.
clusters.churn_exoneration: Partial exoneration. Of 475 commits touching scripts/legibility since 7f618211bb, 63 carry a fix prefix, but 32 of those are RED/GREEN step commits of TDD task sequences. Examples are 3268 (5 steps), 3644 (4), 4751 (4), 4511 (3), 5782 (3), 5956 (3) and 4514 (3). Those sequences are mostly feature work, such as a new cost basis, richer retry-line rendering and the non-human-origin rule, and carry a fix prefix only because the task was filed as a fix. The 63 fix commits cover about 21 distinct task ids, and the package is only about 3 months old. The churn is NOT misleading for the escalation, transport and state-file classes: 2951/2952, 4511, 2953, 3644, 3291/4085 and 4514 each recur through the same missing owner. The silent-failure repairs were applied one site at a time (for example 4511 hardened one of five posters; 3644 fixed four transport consumers one by one) rather than at a shared seam.
clusters.cross_system_notes: Defects in other subsystems that drive patching here: (1) The escalation server is stateful streamable-HTTP while fused-memory is stateless, so legibility carries an adaptive-400 handshake client. A fifth-plus MCP session client also exists in dashboard/data and fused-memory/scripts, and shared.mcp_post/mcp_envelope cover part of the same ground. (2) The escalation channel cannot distinguish a test-minted escalation from a real one, so census.py grew a PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST guard (esc-legibility-census-dark_factory-2 dedupe_count=21). The right guarantee is hermetic test configuration or an origin field on the escalation, not a guard in one of five posters. (3) The Claude Code project-dir encoding rule is re-implemented in scripts/legibility/inventory.py::encode_cwd and scripts/legibility/digest.py::_encode_cwd, mirroring orchestrator/src/orchestrator/session_registry.py::encode_cwd, and kept in agreement by a lockstep test (3272) instead of one importable home in shared/. (4) The quality-findings contract section 11 says the census trigger fires on the weighted completion share via scripts/check_run_completion.py, which is absent from this tree. census_trigger still uses a raw fleet-wide done-count delta, and plans/completion-driven-triggers-prd.md plus census-incremental-prd L8b track the convergence. (5) The nightly trickle is date-keyed (yesterday UTC) and never retries a failed night (5678), while the census is ledger-keyed and resumable. The two coverage mechanisms answer 'which sessions still need coding' differently, and the session ledger could serve the trickle too.
clusters.root_cause: Fail-loud has no owner: five hand-copied escalation posters [[legibility.1]]; codebook merge precedence and lifecycle are duplicated [[legibility.3]]; durable state documents are untyped dicts [[legibility.6]].

clusters.architecture_notes: Persistence is a file-per-record queue (queue.py::EscalationQueue): a pending record is queue_dir/{id}.json, a per-id flock sidecar ({id}.json.lock) serialises read-modify-write, and resolving moves the file into archive/YYYY-MM-DD/ (state is encoded as location). server.py is a single create_server() closure of about 4,300 lines that registers every MCP tool. Roughly lines 1000-3520 are the escalation tools (filing chokepoint, resolve_issue, promote_to_l2, stamp_triage, declare_pin, amend), all closing over `queue`. Lines 3524-5232 are orchestrator operations (merge_request, merge_status, merge_cancel, release_workflow, halt/resume scheduler, reload_config, warm worktrees); they close over harness, event_store and merge_queue and never touch `queue`. The orchestrator process hosts the server on its own event loop, and escalation reaches back into orchestrator through 14 function-local imports. Q1 (legality): action legality is one table (action_effects.py::ACTION_EFFECTS, consulted by resolve_issue and by the harness), but every row wildcards level and category, and the per-action record outcome (resolve, dismiss or keep open) lives in a second constant (server.py::_DISMISS_ACTIONS). The record's own status and level have no transition table, and Escalation has no construction-time validation. Q2 (capability): server-enforced only for identified callers (ROLE_LEVEL_ALLOWLIST ceiling in resolve_issue, PROMOTE_ALLOWED in promote_to_l2); a header-less caller is unrestricted, and the operator-only ops tools have no server-side gate at all (their docstrings say "appears in no agent role's allow-list"). Q3: shadow_ruling.py is a measurement-only codec and weekly-count CLI for hypothetical L2 auto-rulings, carried as an `x_shadow_ruling:` JSON line inside triage_note and designed for deletion. Its 8 fixes are the review tail of one young feature (task 5374). Q4: heuristic 6 fails in server.py. The file mixes the escalation API, an MCP-markup alarm sink, and the orchestrator's merge-lane and scheduler operations behind one function, and the part that can be separated cleanly is separated by closure inputs.
clusters.churn_exoneration: Partly misleading. (1) shadow_ruling.py: the 11 commits (5374) are one feature built under TDD (feat, then reviewer-driven fix(5374) and amend commits). It is measurement-only, grants no authority, and its docstring plans its own deletion. Its churn is healthy and not a defect cluster. The one structural note is that its HUMAN_FOREVER/DETECTABLE gate vocabulary deliberately differs from authority.py's deny list in one cell (design_concern), a divergence it documents and guards with a doc-contract test. (2) Many of the window's "fix" commits on server.py and queue.py are `fix(escalation): GREEN -` steps of feature tasks (2846, 2810, 4887, 4829, 3103), meaning the TDD green phase of planned work, not escaped bugs. Examples are the git_authority extraction (4887), the lane parameter (4888) and the severity ordering (3976). (3) The real bug-driven churn is concentrated in two seams: the root/archive relocation races (#5111 series, 5118, 4552, 2810, 4566) and merge-lane admission/status logic hosted in the escalation server (3103 x6, 2945, 2927, 2928).
clusters.cross_system_notes: Escalation hosts orchestrator work: the merge-lane admission, status, cancel, release_workflow and warm-worktree tools run in the escalation package behind runtime reverse-imports. That is why merge-lane defects (3103, 2945, 2927, 2928) are patched under escalation/, and why layer-direction constants (the watcher identity, sentinel roles, deny categories) are duplicated and pinned by tests. In the other direction, the task store treats an OPEN escalation record as a preservation mechanism for its task (the declared-pin gate cites orchestrator/task_ground_truth.py::_RECOVERY: closing a marked record flips has_open_escalation and the same shape recovers to REVERT_TO_PENDING). Escalation record state therefore carries task-store semantics, and orchestrator sweeps (stranded-blocked, revalidation, reaper) and escalation closes are patched against each other (INFO parks being re-pended, pin refusals, auto-close allowlists diverging from harness allowlists). The long-lived task-status/escalation interplay would be better owned by one lifecycle table on the task-store side. Escalation should only report facts to it. The event-loop hosting problem (finding 7) is likewise an orchestrator property that escalation compensates for.
clusters.root_cause: Record identity changes with lifecycle state, so every reader re-implements locate/retry/vanish [[escalation.8]]; lane, scheduler and worktree ops live inside the escalation server and reach back into orchestrator [[escalation.7]].

clusters.architecture_notes: git_ops.py is 15,857 lines. One class, GitOps, takes up 12,987 of them, and 9,280 lines of the file are prose (58.5%, from the merge-lane ratchet baseline). GitOps holds eight separable jobs: lane-lock leases, worktree create and seed, warm-lane acquire and release, task-branch lifecycle (rebase, stack, unstack, solo, delete, rename), main-evidence probes, diff queries, merge-to-main with persistent merge worktrees, and advance_main/recover_red_main/WIP park. Every git call goes through the module-global git_ops._run. Seven other production modules import that private name, and tests patch 'orchestrator.git_ops._run' 235 times across 25 files. The newer satellites, branch_stack.py and rebase_recovery.py, take an injected runner and import downward cleanly, which is the right shape. They were split out partly because the ratchet refused further growth of git_ops (commit ef6717321b). Lane state is two layers. WarmLanePool holds an in-memory FREE/ASSIGNED cache and is the authority in practice, because a failed durable write never fails acquire or release. LaneLifecycle holds the durable 6-state LaneRecord with a legal-transition table. Two enums are both named LaneState. Answer to Q4: lane state is not single-writer. GitOps writes through the pool, and Harness writes the durable record through the private self.git_ops._lane_lifecycle.transition at 3 sites, and the cache through pool.restore_assignment at 5 sites in _recover_crashed_tasks (630 lines) and _reconcile_lane_checkouts. The carried finding git-worktrees.3 stays weakened. Answer to Q2: refs/heads/task/* has no owner. It has 5 create sites (worktree add -b x3, checkout -B x2), 12 rebase sites across git_ops, workflow, merge_lane/worker, suffix_graph and branch_stack, 4 delete paths with different safety predicates, and a rename. The stack-base ledger is a side record that only 2 consumers read. The lane lock (<lane_dir>.lock) is a raw flock shared with shell scripts: DF's own scripts/warm-lane/*.sh and reify's seed/gc timer. DF works out who holds it from /proc/locks plus an fd registry kept per process. offline_lane.py is a singleton worker owned by Harness. It parses reify script stdout and dedups auto-filed fix tasks through three JSON sidecars keyed by a fingerprint of the failing-test set.
clusters.churn_exoneration: This answers Q1. rebase_recovery.py's 57% fix ratio is misleading. All 12 of its fix commits (09-13 to 09-21) are pre-landing TDD and review rounds of one task, 4797. Many are labelled 'GREEN —' and come from an under-review branch that landed once around 09-21/22. No commit has touched the file since. The property behind the rounds is that the module promises never to raise against a worktree that is damaged by construction. Each review round found one more path that could raise: an unspawnable cwd, a quarantine failure, an unbounded probe, SHA-256 ids, a backup-name race. That is a module converging under review, not one that keeps breaking in production. Its real cost is upstream (see the rerere finding). Part of git_ops.py's 'fix' count is also not bug-driven: 504b996013, a82d7010dd, 8f4182d742 and ef6717321b exist only to keep git_ops.py under the merge-lane line and prose ratchet. The remaining recent churn is genuinely bug-driven and is not exonerated: lane-lock and leak races, branch contamination, offline-lane guard divergence.
clusters.cross_system_notes:
1. Repo config owned by the operator: the shared repository's .git/config sets rerere.enabled=true and rerere.autoupdate=true. That setting is the only reason rebase_recovery.py exists, and task 5697 shows it is a correctness hazard as well.
2. Reify and DF warm-lane shell scripts: the seed script and the warm-lane-gc timer, whose passes overlap, share <lane_dir>.lock with no versioned interface. Many of DF's lane-lock fixes are disagreements with those scripts.
3. Fused-memory task store: offline_lane.py keeps its own copy of whether a fix task is open in three JSON sidecars instead of reading task status. That is where the promoted-fingerprint latent bug comes from.
4. merge_lane/gates.py reads git_ops' private _last_* attributes. merge_lane/worker.py and suffix_graph.py call the unguarded rebase_onto_main. Branch-contamination fixes are therefore spread across git_ops, workflow, merge_lane and suffix_graph, and pending tasks 4752, 5144 and 5697 each patch a different one of those sites.
5. harness.py writes lane records through the private self.git_ops._lane_lifecycle (Harness._recover_crashed_tasks). Before writing RELEASED it reads the record first, because LaneLifecycle.transition is not idempotent; the step-16 review-fix comment there explains why. This keeps the carried finding git-worktrees.3 open.
6. Seven production modules import the private git_ops._run.
clusters.root_cause: A task branch ref has a dozen writers and no owner [[git-worktrees.7]]; the lane-lock protocol is defined in prose across repos [[git-worktrees.8]]; seven 'holds work?' predicates fail in opposite directions [[git-worktrees.9]].

clusters.architecture_notes: Scheduler.acquire_next is now a loop over Scheduler._TICK_PHASE_ORDER, a tuple of 21 strings. Each label is dispatched by getattr(self, f'_phase_{label}') and threads one mutable TickContext with about 20 fields. Each phase's read and write sets are declared only in its docstring. (Q2) W10 split the tick into phases, but the ordering constraints between them are still recorded only as tuple position plus a test that pins the literal tuple. Nothing in code says which field a phase may read. (Q1) Parks, pin reservations and fairness parks live in one in-memory owner, ModuleLockTable, with one expiry site, Scheduler._expire_parks. That part is sound. The policy that decides who may hold a park is spread out. It sits in the kwarg-selected Scheduler._deps_satisfied, a hand-recoded inverse in Scheduler._owner_is_live_dispatchable, the reserve_now phase (no status filter), and _complete_earned_fairness_parks. The policy's inputs live in three more stores: Scheduler._skip_count, scheduler_overrides.db (written by both the orchestrator and fused-memory) and park_eviction_requests.db (written by fused-memory, drained by the scheduler). Task 6518 (in progress) adds dependency_verdict.py for park GC only. (Q3) Most of delivered_check_polarity's 8 of 13 fix commits are one task's review iteration (all fix(3500), 2026-09-28) on a module that was a month old. The recurring delivered-check bugs instead come from the runtime gate. That gate is evaluated by three independent callers (the scheduler cache, verify_delivered_checks_on_main, landing_evidence) with different caching, timeout and collapse code. It is fed by an active-only task fetch that hides terminal dep records, so phases backfill_dep_status and backfill_terminal_dep_records exist to patch that gap. (Q4) A typed DeployState with a legal-transition table (deploy_state._LEGAL, shared.deploy_state) exists. The legacy stamps (gate_escalated_at, before_done_ran_at, before_done_verified_at, before_done_scheduled_at) are still written next to it as 'evidence' and still steer the resume branches of the 1,212-line DeterministicRunner.run. A pre-ζ fallback shim and cross-process readers in fused-memory and escalation still depend on the stamps. Stranded-blocked recovery has two deciders: task_ground_truth._RECOVERY (harness) and Scheduler._phase_redispatch_stranded_blocked. Only the pin predicate (recovery_pins) is shared between them.
clusters.churn_exoneration: This is a partial exoneration. 39 of the window's 310 commits on these files are fix commits, and a large share of those are not defects in behaviour. About 10 are pyright, lint or mock-typing repairs (4f64da0055, 7c5ef373b5, 9c964f2277, b578427026, 102bfebe08, 9673c5b22d, 182e8121b9, ca50326a48, 2bcd5bd2bd, 6260326e75). Another 8 are the fix(3500) series on shared/delivered_check_polarity.py: all from 2026-09-28, one requeue's reviewer iteration on a module created 2026-08-25. That makes polarity's 61% fix ratio a young-feature artefact, not evidence of a recurring defect. deterministic_runner.py's 91 commits are mostly GREEN steps of feature tasks (2238/2239/2240 DeployState, 2336 predicate mode, 2632 unit-less deploys, 4252 teardown measurement). Genuinely recurring bug classes remain, and the findings below are tied to them: crash-window resume inference (2954, 2983, 4048, 4157), delivered-check gate coherence (2692, 2783, 2975, 2977, 5910), and park/pin eligibility (5308, 6040, esc-6040-7/6518).
clusters.cross_system_notes: fused-memory: the scheduler's per-tick get_tasks is limited to ACTIVE_TASK_STATUSES (minus infra-hold; about an 11.6MB payload per its own comment), and there is no 'records for these dep ids at any status' read. That missing guarantee forces two compensating phases in the scheduler (_phase_backfill_dep_status and _phase_backfill_terminal_dep_records, with a never-evicted record cache). It also makes absence from tasks_by_id ambiguous (terminal, infra-hold, deleted, or transiently dropped), which drove the 2743/2746 streak-GC narrowing and its accepted leak. fused-memory also hosts the second implementation of the override and park-eviction stores (fused_memory/server/tools.py). The scheduler.py exception family (TerminalExitRejection, DoneGateRejection, ProvenanceValidationRejection, StaleEvidenceRejection) mirrors fused-memory's server-side status gates on the client, decoded from error strings by extract_rejection. escalation: deterministic_runner and the scheduler's stranded-blocked sweep infer resolution or pinning by scanning the escalation queue and its archive by task_id, because no typed 'this gate was resolved' fact is written back to the task. harness: the harness reconcile sweep (task_ground_truth._RECOVERY) and the scheduler's _phase_redispatch_stranded_blocked both recover blocked rows under contradictory rules.
clusters.root_cause: Dependency readiness [[scheduler.8]] and stranded-blocked recovery [[scheduler.9]] each have several deciders; DeployState landed beside the legacy stamps [[scheduler.12]]; one dispatch lifecycle spans 18 dicts [[scheduler.13]].

clusters.architecture_notes: Three layers share one cycle. shared/cli_invoke.py (4,459 lines, 57% prose) holds AgentResult, transcript evidence readers, failure predicates and taxonomies, the cap-retry loop invoke_with_cap_retry (1,016 lines, 595 of them prose), argv construction and the subprocess runner. shared/invocation_outcome.py holds the InvocationOutcome sum type, classify_invocation and the cap-prose tables. shared/usage_gate.py (3,052 lines, 50% prose) holds AccountPhase, a _LEGAL_TRANSITIONS table, UsageGate._transition, AccountLease, InvokeSlot, a per-(account, model) ScopeCap overlay, probe loops and the SIGHUP reload. Answers to the four asks. (1) Production phase writes do go through UsageGate._transition, but AccountState keeps public boolean setters that write phase directly (about 280 test sites use them), acct.resets_at is written outside the transition at three sites, and scoped caps are a second, table-less state machine. (2) Classification is not in one place: classify_invocation is the taxonomy, but cli_invoke re-decides the verdict through UsageGate.detect_cap_hit, which re-classifies a synthetic result, through an inline heuristic cap net and through two side predicates. (3) Cap and reset detection still scrapes prose (CAP_HIT_PREFIXES, CAP_CONFIRM_KEYWORDS, _parse_resets_at, plus the looser cap_markers tables). Only 401/403/5xx use structured api_error_status. (4) orchestrator/usage_gate.py is a 10-line star re-export shim; the real duplication is orchestrator/agents/invoke.py re-implementing the claude spawn recipe. Seams: invoke_slot to InvokeSlot.report to private gate handlers; the probe path (_run_probe) mutating AccountState directly; the invoke_kwargs dict bag mutated across retry attempts.
clusters.churn_exoneration: Partial. Only 2 of the last 29 commits in the window are fixes, and the recent churn on these files is task-driven feature work under TDD (6042 park-free pool and legibility runner, 5944 probe re-admission, 3995 transcript evidence, 6022 refusal classification, 4448 argv resolution). The older fix density (15/116 on cli_invoke) came from the since-closed classification and phase-machine bugs. The structure is not exonerated: the same files grew by about 5,400 lines in the window, and each feature added a parameter, a branch or a measurement narrative to invoke_with_cap_retry. The remaining risk is the shape that makes each new feature a patch to an ordered if-chain, not a stream of new bugs.
clusters.cross_system_notes: Cross-system. (1) The Claude CLI exposes no structured cap signal, so the gate scrapes prose banners (CAP_HIT_PREFIXES, CAP_CONFIRM_KEYWORDS, _parse_resets_at) and returns exit-0 banners as successes. That is why successful replies must be scanned (the second finding) and why cap_markers keeps a second, looser table with a drift guard. If a structured rate_limit field exists in the stream-json, it is unused here (grep finds no rate_limit or resetsAt handling in cli_invoke.py); I did not verify upstream. (2) orchestrator/agents/invoke.py patches around shared by copying the spawn recipe and importing four private names, so a fix in shared must be mirrored there. (3) orchestrator/harness.py writes usage_gate._cost_store, _project_id and _run_id after construction: three private reach-ins where public project_id/run_id setters already exist for two of them and none exists for the cost store. Cap and failover events fired before that wiring are silently dropped (_fire_cost_event returns when the store is None), which is another temporal coupling to remove with a constructor argument.
clusters.root_cause: The cap-retry loop re-decides the invocation verdict beside classify_invocation [[shared-infra.7]]; AccountPhase is the single writer only by convention [[shared-infra.1]].

findings.statement: A permit is just an anonymous decrement of asyncio.Semaphore _speculation_slot; nothing records WHICH item holds one. So the conservation check _inflight_speculative_count (merge_queue.py) must enumerate every place a permit-holding item can physically be: _inflight entries, _verifier_queue._queue internals, _redispatch (added by task 2063), _finalizing_head (added by task 2096 after the detector false-alarmed for entire 20-60min head verifies), and _dispatching_item (task 2096 again, for the dispatch-gap await). Every new await point in the pipeline silently creates a new uncounted window and a new false-positive class. Releases are scattered across ~10 raw self._speculation_slot.release() sites (:6321, :6425, :7824, :8279, :8932) plus SpeculationController's merger-side half plus _resolve_and_release's slot_held branch; callers must pass release_resources=False on POST-finalize paths (:7686, :7722, :7939) and even release_resources=not _entry_released (:7872) to avoid double-release — ownership phase is tracked in the caller's head. SpeculationController (task 1993) reified only the merger-side lifecycle; its docstring explicitly says verifier-side releases keep hitting the raw semaphore, and the semaphore must stay unbounded specifically to tolerate a known double-release race.
findings.proposal: Introduce a SpecPermit token object and a PermitLedger as the single owner of the semaphore. acquire() returns a SpecPermit registered in a live set; the token is stored ON the item (SpeculativeItem.permit / InflightEntry.permit) and travels with it through every queue, park, dispatch and finalize; release(token) is idempotent (token.released flag) and asserts the token is live, killing both the double-release race and the release_resources caller flags. Conservation becomes structural: slot_available + len(ledger.live) == depth by construction, regardless of where items sit — the five-location census, _dispatching_item, and the _finalizing_head census term all die. Ban raw _speculation_slot access with a grep-guard test (the repo already uses this idiom for SpeculativeItem construction sites). Same treatment for _merge_ahead_cap (counts_against_cap field becomes a CapPermit).
findings.title: Speculation-permit conservation is audited by a five-location census instead of owned permit tokens
findings.bug_history_link: 10x mined theme: tasks 1741/1756/1789/1698/1993/2063/2068/2096; commits 519afbfe71 '_finalize_inflight sets/clears _finalizing_head', f5e0d73879 'count _redispatch-parked speculative permits', 3097d78eb2 'held_spec_permit fixes merger deadlock', 9048aed1c9 slot-leak guard; live incidents esc-__merge_resource_leak__-9/-10/-23/-24 were detector false positives from exactly this census gap.
findings.verdict_notes: Permits are now SpecPermit tokens in a PermitLedger. merge_lane/worker.py::SpeculativeMergeWorker._inflight_speculative_count is len(_speculation_ledger.live) minus held_by_merger, with no five-location scan. _finalizing_head and _dispatching_item are deleted (task 2435).

findings.statement: Where an item IS in its lifecycle is derivable only by knowing which of five containers holds it (_queue, _lane_buffers, _verifier_queue, _redispatch, _inflight) plus whether one of four worker transient fields points at it (_inflight_req :3898, _remerging_item :3908, _finalizing_head :3913-3919, _dispatching_item :3921-3931 — each added by a separate bug fix for an 'invisible window'). On top of that, InflightEntry carries a free-form phase: str ('verifying'/'gate_reverify'/'finalizing', merge_types.py, written at merge_queue.py/8801/8864), a separate InflightStatus sentinel enum (DROPPED/REQUEUED/... merge_types.py), AND vestigial _verify_phase/_verify_item fields dual-written 'to avoid a large diff' (:3900-3906, :8701, :8800, :8863) that previously caused a stale phantom snapshot entry (comment at :5552). Every consumer that needs global state — snapshot() (:5468, sections 0/1/1b/2/3 mirror the census), speculation_accounting_violations, the request-liveness ledger — re-derives it by scanning all locations, and the consumers have already diverged once (task 2068: _redispatch-parked items were counted by the audit but missing from snapshot; _dispatching_item is deliberately in the audit but NOT in snapshot).
findings.proposal: Add an ItemLifecycle registry keyed by request_id with an explicit state enum (QUEUED, LANE_BUFFERED, MERGING, AWAITING_VERIFY, REDISPATCH_PARKED, DISPATCHING, VERIFYING, GATE_REVERIFY, FINALIZING, TERMINAL) and a legal-transition table enforced by a single transition(rid, from, to) method that raises/escalates on illegal moves. Queues keep holding the objects, but every put/pop site calls transition() — the four transient side-fields become the states DISPATCHING/MERGING/FINALIZING instead of nullable fields to remember to clear in finally blocks. snapshot(), the permit audit and the liveness ledger become single reads of the registry, guaranteeing they can never disagree. Delete _verify_phase/_verify_item and the free-form phase string (phase = registry state).
findings.title: Item lifecycle is encoded by container membership plus four side-fields and three parallel status mechanisms — no state machine
findings.bug_history_link: Tasks 2063/2068/2096 (each added one more invisible-window field), d5bf12c73e 'surface _redispatch-parked items in snapshot()', stale-phantom-entry fix noted at merge_queue.py, I4 false-positive incident class in operator memory (finalize-head census FP 2026-07-05).
findings.verdict_notes: merge_lane/worker.py::ItemLifecycle registry, guarded by a legal-transition table, is the single lifecycle state per request_id. The four transient side-fields and InflightEntry.phase str are deleted (the phase string is derived via _entry_phase). _verify_phase and _verify_item survive only as a code comment, and the containers remain. | Reviewer (merge-queue): The legal-transition table (ItemLifecycle/_LEGAL_TRANSITIONS) and the deletion of the four side-fields are real. But container membership is still the operative state: dispatch-control reads use the raw _inflight deque, and _finalizing_head_entry derives the finalize head from the _live_items object type plus deque absence. ItemLifecycle is a parallel record moved by hand on each exit arm through a _note_transition that never raises. The prior's defect class, consumers re-deriving state from containers and disagreeing, recurred on 10-04: 4582 found one request rendered twice by snapshot(). The response added InflightEntry.vacated, _occupying_inflight_entries and a render-time dedup (_first_copy_per_request) in 84ef5a7e31, 175114ca51, ccc9d1f561 and 2e1616027b. So the finding is reduced, not closed. The new terminal-edge finding gives the specific remaining mechanism.

findings.statement: The merge queue advances main (git, in-process) and the task's done status is written afterwards to fused-memory via a callback chain that can be lost on crash/restart. The missing guarantee — a durable, consultable record that branch X landed as SHA Y for task Z — is compensated by independent detectors: workflow.py pre-PLAN ghost-loop recovery plus a second post-PLAN guard with deliberately different semantics and a comment ordering maintainers to keep both in sync; merge_queue.py already-merged is_ancestor detection inside classify_and_merge (with its own uncommitted-work sub-guard); scheduler.py's exception family mirroring fused-memory's server-side phantom-done/terminal-exit/provenance gates; plus 'terminally mark unknown-branch merge requests' (4a98702a48). Each detector was added by a separate incident and each has had its own false-positive/race fixes (e6d958a133 fixed the pre-PLAN guard DONEing phantom reify tasks). MergeQueueStore (task 1772) already journals accepted requests durably but records nothing on the landing side.
findings.proposal: Extend MergeQueueStore with a landed-outbox table written in the same code path as the CAS advance (task_id, branch_tip_sha, advanced_sha, wall time) — git's reflog proves the advance, the row makes it queryable. Make it the single source of truth: (1) scheduler consults it before dispatch (replacing workflow's two is_ancestor guards with one lookup + one is_ancestor confirmation), (2) a startup reconciler drives status=done with merged-provenance from unconsumed rows (replacing the lost-callback window), (3) ghost-loop detection collapses to 'row exists but task not done'. The fused-memory server-side gates stay (defense in depth at the boundary) but the orchestrator-side guard count drops from ~6 to 1.
findings.title: Merge-landed→task-done is non-atomic across subsystems; six ghost-loop/phantom-done detectors compensate in three places
findings.bug_history_link: 6x mined ghost-loop theme: 99d13ad6cc, 7dfe0e69bc, e6d958a133, 492bb8f126, 833806f7dc, dc33b760c8; operator memory 'reify merge queue from a DF session' documents the live hazard (manual merge lands but task stays pending → re-dispatch).
findings.verdict_notes: The durable landing record now exists: merge_lane/landed_outbox.py::LandedOutbox plus MergeProvenance, and the ghost-loop guards do a journal-first MergeProvenance.lookup. Git-derived detectors remain as fallbacks (merge_lane/landing_evidence.py lists seven sites), so the multi-detector compensation is reduced but not gone.

findings.statement: The df 1985-2002 split moved text, not state or dependency edges. merge_drift.py and merge_shadow.py take the live worker and read/write its privates (_drift_land_count, _runner_quarantine, _drift_check_tasks, _shadow_compare_tasks, _shadow_state_path) — the state stayed in the god-class, so the seam is fake. Worse, merge_gates.py functions import their own co-located siblings BACK through merge_queue at function level (:361 'reaches back through orchestrator.merge_queue._check_post_merge_equivalence ... so the existing suite's string-path monkeypatches stay effective', also :400, :439, :533, :1353, :1430), creating a deliberate circular dependency whose only purpose is preserving 7 test monkeypatch string paths; merge_queue.py carries 9 noqa:F401 re-export blocks (~70 names) and 64 test files still import from merge_queue. Consequence: merge_queue.py stays the #1 churn file because every satellite change still routes through it, patching one namespace while calls resolve through the other is a live silent-divergence hazard, and the god-class __init__ keeps absorbing each satellite's state fields with paragraph-long ownership comments (e.g. the SuffixConflictTracker lambda-injection block :4096-4130).
findings.proposal: Finish the extraction along state lines: give each satellite an owning object holding ITS state — DriftDetectorSchedule(_drift_land_count, _runner_quarantine, _drift_check_tasks), ShadowCompareScheduler(_shadow_state_path, _shadow_compare_tasks) — instantiated as one worker field each, mirroring what SuffixConflictTracker already did for suffix state. Kill the reach-back convention with a one-time mechanical test migration (repoint the 7 string-path monkeypatches to the defining module), then delete the function-level back-imports and shrink the re-export shim to the public surface (MergeRequest, MergeOutcome, enqueue_merge_request, SpeculativeMergeWorker). Enforce the direction with an import-linter contract: merge_gates/merge_drift/merge_shadow/merge_liveness must not import merge_queue.
findings.title: The 17-task refactor extracted the wrong seam: satellites are function-bags over worker privates, wired through circular reach-back imports frozen by test monkeypatch paths
findings.bug_history_link: Refactor batch df 1985-2002 (commits b8162ffad7, f49a36cd67, fa12fd894a, 541eb10868, 146a7f013f); post-refactor churn evidence: 21 more merge_queue.py commits in the following 3 weeks; 11b2c470d3 'SuffixConflictTracker re-reads git_ops/frozen_prefix live' is a bug fix caused directly by the snapshot-vs-live-reference ambiguity this half-seam creates.
findings.verdict_notes: The gates.py reach-back imports through merge_queue are gone, and merge_queue.py is now a 12-line alias shim. drift.py::_maybe_run_drift_check and shadow.py::_maybe_schedule_shadow_compare still take SpeculativeMergeWorker and read or write its privates (_drift_land_count, _runner_quarantine, _shadow_state_path). worker.py has grown to about 22k lines.

findings.statement: MergeRequest.branch is a bare str that historically arrives either bare ('4778') or prefixed ('task/4778'), so correctness depends on consumption-site normalizers added one incident at a time: canonical_queued_branch_name (git_ops.py, 'prepend unless already present'), GitOps.resolve_queued_branch_ref with try-both-forms plus an explicit tie-break rule (git_ops.py), MergeQueueStore.record() stripping the prefix at journal-write (merge_queue_store.py) while the recovery path re-canonicalizes shape-tolerantly (merge_queue_store.py), and ~8 inline f'{branch_prefix}{...}' constructions scattered through git_ops (:1246, :1307, :1770, :2649, :3378). Every new feature that touches branch names (recovery, journaling, warm lanes, suffix graph) has re-introduced the ambiguity and required another central-resolver retrofit; the resolver at 3 call sites was itself a 3-commit propagation task (1911).
findings.proposal: Parse, don't validate: a frozen QueuedBranch value type in merge_types.py with fields bare_id and full_name and a single classmethod parse(raw, branch_prefix) that is the ONLY place prefix logic lives. MergeRequest.branch becomes QueuedBranch (constructed at the two entry boundaries: enqueue_merge_request and journal recovery); git refs are always built from .full_name. canonical_queued_branch_name, the try-both logic in resolve_queued_branch_ref, and the journal strip/re-add pair all die; a mixed-shape value becomes unrepresentable past the boundary. pyright then enforces the invariant at every one of today's drift sites for free.
findings.title: Branch identity is stringly-typed; shape-tolerance is patched in at every consumer instead of parsed once at the boundary
findings.bug_history_link: 8x mined theme: 420e20aa2c 'recover_pending_merges shape-tolerant branch resolution', ac6dd342d6 'MergeQueueStore.record() strips branch_prefix', d396ff9bbb 'canonical_queued_branch_name shape-normalizer', 1d0d1f1cc1/f4eb1722fa/534a35ef10 resolver propagation (task 1911), 4a98702a48 'terminally mark unknown-branch merge requests'.
findings.verdict_notes: merge_lane/types.py::QueuedBranch is a frozen type parsed at the boundary, and MergeRequest.branch uses it (the journal now stores bare_id). GitOps.resolve_queued_branch_ref still tries both forms, and git_ops.py still has 27 inline branch_prefix f-string constructions.

findings.statement: The retired serial MergeWorker survives verbatim as a 384-line frozen fixture (orchestrator/tests/_serial_merge_worker.py) because ~89 test constructions were never migrated; production merge_queue.py cites 'the test-local MergeWorker reference' 10 times as the behavioral spec its counters and outcomes must mirror 'byte-identically' (e.g. classify_and_merge's docstring :2400-2410, the _cas_retries/_post_merge_verify_timeouts/auto_heal_registry comments :3833-3910). Similarly _verify_and_advance (:9229) is a 'thin compat shim ... retained so the ~18 tests calling it directly stay green', and _verify_item/_verify_phase are write-only vestigial fields 'retained to avoid a large diff'. The effect is bidirectional coupling with the test suite's accidental structure: refactors must preserve retired-implementation quirks and dead namespaces, which is exactly why the 17-task refactor ended as re-export shims and reach-back imports (finding above) rather than a real decomposition — and why merge_queue.py remains the churn hotspot.
findings.proposal: Declare the speculative worker the sole spec and pay down the anchors: (1) migrate the ~18 _verify_and_advance direct-call tests to drive the public run()/merge() surface or a small test harness around _dispatch_item+_finalize_inflight, then delete the shim; (2) delete the write-only _verify_item/_verify_phase fields and their 4 dual-write sites; (3) freeze _serial_merge_worker.py usage with a ratchet test (no NEW imports of it) and strip the 10 'mirrors the test-local reference' claims from production docstrings so future agents stop treating the retired worker as normative; (4) adopt a convention (enforceable via grep-guard) that tests monkeypatch the defining module, unlocking shim deletion.
findings.title: A retired serial worker and compat shims are load-bearing test anchors that freeze production structure
findings.bug_history_link: c06819470b 'consolidate retired-MergeWorker doc prose onto _TrainMergeHost' (task 1998/R7b created the fixture); the reach-back convention (esc-1990-4 / commit 2499caacf6 shows test-anchor meta-churn); partly speculative as a direct bug source, but it is the documented mechanism that blocked the 1985-2002 refactor from extracting real seams.
findings.verdict_notes: orchestrator/tests/_serial_merge_worker.py is deleted, and tests were re-homed onto the lane. worker.py has no references to the test-local MergeWorker and no _verify_and_advance shim. The _verify_phase and _verify_item fields are gone and survive only as a comment.

findings.statement: Because advance_main and the status=done write are not atomic (a run can die between them), the next run must re-derive 'did my work land?' forensically. Three guards do this with deliberately different semantics: pre-PLAN _recover_if_already_merged (workflow.py, SHA-primary), the pre-EXECUTE already_on_main check (1776-1816, iteration-log-only — 'SINGLE SIGNAL' comment), and the merge-phase ancestor check. Comments at 1649-1654 and 1771-1775 explicitly warn 'do not collapse them' and 'if you change the is_ancestor/has_work logic, check both guards'. The shared heuristic _has_prior_implementation (7202-7289) is 90 lines of trade-off analysis defending against .task/ contamination, rebased-HEAD==base_commit, architect scratch, and fused-memory auto-commit races — each clause a past false-done incident.
findings.proposal: Make merge provenance a durable, write-ahead record instead of a heuristic: the merge queue writes a per-task journal entry (task_id → merge_sha, branch_tip_sha, ts) in the same critical section that moves refs/heads/main (it already stamps metadata.done_provenance on some paths — make it mandatory and ordered BEFORE the ref update, fsynced, e.g. a MergeJournal in the event_store or a git note on the merge commit). All three guards collapse to one MergeProvenance.lookup(task_id) call; _has_prior_implementation survives only as a legacy fallback behind the journal miss path. Enforce with a test that no code path can return WorkflowOutcome.DONE without either journal provenance or an explicit human done_provenance.
findings.title: 'Already merged?' is answered by three divergent heuristic guards instead of one durable merge-provenance record
findings.bug_history_link: 6x false-done class: tasks 846 (_has_prior_implementation guard), 851 (harden _mark_blocked false-done), 882/883 (DONE early-return — 28 test regressions), 954 (.task/ contamination), 1141 (ESCALATED-branch rebase-before-verify); task-2911 incident cited at workflow.py and 1793-1801
findings.verdict_notes: All three guards (_recover_if_already_merged, _recover_before_execute, _recover_before_merge) now start with MergeProvenance.lookup (landed_outbox journal) and finalise via _finalise_recovery_done. The git/iteration-log heuristic _has_prior_implementation (~90-line docstring, SHA+iter-log both required) remains as the fallback.
