findings.statement: The workflow↔steward contract is mediated entirely through shared mutable state: after _await_steward_completion, _mark_blocked runs five probes to guess what the steward did — status in TERMINAL (workflow.py), status=='deferred' (7961), L0-queue-empty (7938), L1-open (7946), and dismissed-L0s whose resolved_at ISO string falls inside a steward_window_start window (7913, 7980-7998, 'Fix A broadened'). run()'s ESCALATED branch duplicates the status-honoring subset with a comment 'Mirrors the inline returns inside _mark_blocked (~L3125–3168) but bypasses it' (1849-1873). Crucially there is no INTERRUPTED signal: steward_max_attempts=1 (steward.py) plus a wall-clock kill looks identical to 'steward failed', which is exactly the healthy-WIP-misdiagnosed-as-failure class in operator memory.
findings.proposal: Give TaskSteward.handle_escalation a typed StewardOutcome sum type returned (or queued on an asyncio channel) to the owning workflow: RESOLVED(resolution_text) | REESCALATED_L1(esc_id) | TERMINAL_DECISION(new_status) | INTERRUPTED(timeout|attempt_cap, wip_commits_present) | BUDGET_EXHAUSTED. The workflow branches on it in exactly one function; the escalation queue remains persistence/notification but stops being the RPC channel; the timestamp-window dismissal heuristic dies. INTERRUPTED with wip_commits_present routes to a resume-plan path instead of L1, encoding the 'triage WIP health before restarting' lesson structurally.
findings.title: Steward outcome is inferred from escalation-queue side effects and timestamp windows instead of a typed result
findings.bug_history_link: 8x steward timeout/retry chain (tasks 638, 690, 721, 722, 737, 738, 746, 753, 769); task 1141 'honor steward deferred/cancelled status'; feedback memory 'Steward re-escalated = incomplete-impl triage' (task 2060, 4775a5e30d)
findings.verdict_notes: _mark_blocked now does a single isinstance dispatch on typed StewardOutcome (workflow_types.py: StewardResolved/ReescalatedL1/TerminalDecision/Interrupted/BudgetExhausted) from _await_steward_completion. The status/L0/L1/timestamp-window probes are gone and there is an explicit StewardInterrupted signal. | Reviewer (workflow): Only the _mark_blocked path consumes the typed StewardOutcome. _await_steward_completion still overrides the queued outcome with a fresh status read (synthesizing StewardTerminalDecision) and an escalation-queue has_open_l1 probe (substituting StewardReescalatedL1 and dismissing L0s itself). _honour_steward_terminal_decision re-derives the steward's decision from the status row a second time. The ESCALATED-branch waiter _wait_for_resolution never reads the queue and is woken only by an L0 dismissal through harness._on_escalation_resolved, so the steward's outcome is still partly inferred from escalation-queue side effects.

findings.statement: WorkflowStateMachine.transition rejects only out-transitions from DONE/CANCELLED, because STATE_TO_STATUS maps all five working phases to IN_PROGRESS. It has no state for a REQUEUED exit (TerminalReport's docstring: 'a REQUEUED exit that never transitions'), and force_set exists only so tests can assign `wf.state`. The persisted row is written separately: workflow.py has 22 scheduler.set_task_status calls taking string literals ('merge-deferred', 'pending', 'blocked'). Callers pair each write with _enter_phase by hand, as in _enter_merge_deferred and _handle_superseded, and in the '_persist_blocked_row + _enter_phase(BLOCKED) pairing' named in _mark_blocked. TerminalReport is still an instance stash, self._terminal_report, set at four sites (_mark_blocked._record, the WarmLaneRequeue clause, two lock-conflict requeue paths). run() uses it only when its outcome equals the returned one and otherwise builds a report with reason=''. 37 direct `return WorkflowOutcome.BLOCKED/ESCALATED/REQUEUED` sites exist, and paths such as the architect-desync BLOCKED in _handle_ready_to_merge_report and _honour_steward_terminal_decision build no report. Such an exit reaches the harness with an empty block_reason, or with a stale one from an earlier stash that happens to share the outcome. Harness._run_slot builds its own CANCELLED or BLOCKED TaskReports via a defensive getattr(workflow.state). W9 then added exit_contract.judge_exit and the _note_exit_status_write ledger, which re-derive agreement after the fact (shipped in log mode). That is the 're-derives state from several containers in order to check it' smell named under heuristic 10, and each new exit writer must remember to report to the ledger (task 6051).
findings.proposal: Make WorkflowStateMachine the single writer of phase and row. An async enter(to, *, report: TerminalReport | None) validates the move, writes the TaskStatus projection through an injected StatusWriter, records any write failure on the machine, and refuses an exiting state without a report (an invariant checked at construction and again at run()). Add a REQUEUED/PENDING state so a requeue projects to 'pending'. run() returns machine.terminal_report and raises a named invariant error if it is missing. This makes the following deletable: the self._terminal_report stash and run()'s outcome-equality fallback, _note_exit_status_write/_exit_status_write_failure, the hand-paired _persist_blocked_row+_enter_phase and the literal set_task_status calls, force_set and the state setter (tests pass initial=), the phase half of exit_contract.judge_exit (true by construction), and the harness's getattr(workflow.state) fallback. It would have prevented the false-done/mismatch class (851, 882/883, esc-2073-15), 6051's lost re-pend, and empty or stale block_reason reports.
findings.title: W9 made the terminal state checkable, not single-sourced: machine, status row, stashed TerminalReport and a post-hoc exit judge still have to agree
findings.bug_history_link: 11d87a36b5 'a blast-radius requeue's dead re-pend reaches the run()-exit write-failure ledger (task 6051)'; task 3542 series (973781e23d, d64e0036fa: SM-2 assertion turned into a recorded verdict because the harness converted it to an empty-reason BLOCKED); task 3172 (harness synthetic report cause/phase); prior workflow.3 history 851, 882/883
findings.verdict_notes: Re-observed this run as workflow.10 (equal key, contract §9); statement and proposal restated from this run's reviewer, skeptic verdict confirmed: force_set exists as test back-door. self._terminal_report is assigned at 4 sites (workflow.py ~3146, 4567, 4650, 16250). The multi-container agreement and exit_contract.judge_exit shape is plausible; I did not enumerate the 37 return sites or the 22 set_task_status calls exactly, so the counts are approximate, but the structure is real. || Re-verification: WorkflowStateMachine (workflow_types.py) raises IllegalTransition from _enter_phase, so transitions are enforced. The _last_block_* side channel is deleted in favour of the frozen TerminalReport returned by run(), with an exit-consistency check (c8bca5e2f8 added the machine). | Reviewer (workflow): WorkflowStateMachine enforces only terminal absorption (all working phases project to IN_PROGRESS; there is no state for REQUEUED; force_set lets tests bypass it). The status row is still written separately via 22 literal set_task_status calls paired by hand with _enter_phase. TerminalReport is still an instance stash (self._terminal_report, 4 writers) that run() uses only on outcome equality; many direct BLOCKED/ESCALATED exits build no report and reach the harness with reason ''. W9 added the exit_contract judge as a post-hoc cross-check rather than a single writer (see the new state-machine-gap finding).

findings.statement: run() ends with catches for AllAccountsCappedException (workflow.py), _SessionBudgetExhausted (1929), SetTaskStatusRejected (1957), WarmLaneRequeue with a 3-subclass isinstance triage (2014-2068), VerifyInfraError (2070), bare OSError re-classified via verify.py's underscore-private _is_infra_oserror (2090, imported at :87), and broad Exception (2114) — each added after an exception 'escaped' a deeper handler. The comment at 2094-2097 even documents duplicating the generic path because Python can't re-raise into a sibling clause. The same cap exception is separately caught in steward.py, review_checkpoint.py, and dry_run_unblock.py with independently-written dispositions; the warm-lane clause admits in-comment (2026-2044) that its requeue-cap accounting is wrong for two of three subclasses and defers to a scheduler change.
findings.proposal: Create one classify_failure(exc) -> BlockDisposition(category, escalate_to_human, requeue_kind, counts_against_requeue_cap, reason_prefix) table in a shared module (natural home: next to task_status.py, or shared/ since steward/review/dry-run also need it). _mark_blocked accepts a BlockDisposition; run() keeps one except clause per outcome kind (requeue / block / cancel) that consults the table. New failure types become table rows with a completeness test (every exported exception type in git_ops/verify/cli_invoke/usage_gate has a row), ending the per-call-site whack-a-mole and fixing the requeue-cap misaccounting in one place.
findings.title: run()'s seven-clause exception ladder re-implements failure classification owned by other subsystems
findings.bug_history_link: 4x AllAccountsCapped whack-a-mole (f66a04d61f, 6e905017c3, a946399937); VerifyInfraError escape hardening (fe5e23479c task 1883, da09ca5569); WarmLanePoolHardDown requeue-cap NOTE (99307a84be)
findings.verdict_notes: Classification now comes from a classify_failure -> BlockDisposition table. TaskWorkflow._drive still has a SetTaskStatusRejected clause, a WarmLaneRequeue clause, and a broad Exception clause that isinstance-ladders the cap/budget/infra/OSError cases, and it still imports the private _is_infra_oserror. steward.py, review_checkpoint.py and dry_run_unblock.py still catch AllAccountsCappedException separately.

findings.statement: Loop/thrash protection is implemented as ad-hoc metadata keys — consecutive_no_plan_failures, total_no_plan_failures, last_no_plan_main_sha, consecutive_infra_resume_failures, last_infra_resume_iteration_count, consecutive_merge_thrash, last_merge_outcome_signature, plus merge_first_enqueued_at — each parsed defensively (int(metadata.get(...) or 0) inside try/except at workflow.py), persisted best-effort ('failed to persist infra-resume thrash counter: log and proceed', 3456-3464, so the counter silently loses increments and the guard under-fires), and merged via the hand-rolled last-writer-wins _merge_fresh_metadata (3233-3280) whose own docstring admits 'memory_hints may be clobbered'. The concurrency story is a comment: 'same per-task concurrency assumption as the existing writer; no new hazard' (3381-3383). Each new thrash mode historically added a new counter cluster and a new fix task.
findings.proposal: Define one schema-versioned RetryLedger dataclass under a single metadata key (retry_ledger) with typed fields per guard, one load(validate-or-reset-loudly) and one persist path; guards become pure functions RetryLedger -> GuardVerdict. Make persist failure escalate (the guard exists to stop money-burning loops — silently losing an increment defeats it), or move the ledger into the .task/ artifacts dir where the workflow is the single writer and persistence is a local fsync, keeping only the final blocked verdict in metadata. Signature normalization (_normalize_cause_hint / _compute_merge_outcome_signature, 367-424) moves in as ledger methods so signature-keying can't be recomputed differently at different call sites.
findings.title: Anti-thrash guards are eight untyped counters in task metadata with best-effort read-modify-write over the MCP boundary
findings.bug_history_link: 6x escalation-dedup/anti-thrash chain: 6a631d537f 'anti-thrash guard on repeated infra-issue resumes', eded4bb2a6 'merge-phase thrash guard via signature-keyed counter', 0f2b207530 'lock no-requeue contract'; task 1739 zero-output classification
findings.verdict_notes: Counters now live in a typed shared.task_metadata.RetryLedger under metadata.retry_ledger. They are built by _build_retry_ledger and updated by the pure evaluators _evaluate_no_plan, _evaluate_infra_resume and _evaluate_merge_thrash. The infra-resume persist failure now escalates instead of being swallowed. Still metadata read-modify-write through the _merge_fresh_metadata last-writer-wins merge, justified by a 'per-task concurrency' comment.

findings.statement: AgentRole.allowed_tools (roles.py, ...) declares which MCP tools a role may call, but whether the backing servers are actually wired is decided elsewhere by name-string membership: _MCP_CONFIG_ROLES/_PLAN_TOOLS_ROLES tuples (workflow.py, consulted at 6925/6938), a hardcoded sandbox check role.name in ('implementer','debugger') (6913), a reviewer-prefix special case (6903-6909), and the role_key = role.name.split('_')[0] config-lookup convention (6892). The invariant is stated only in a comment (96-98: a role listing a tool 'MUST also appear here... or the session is told to call tools that do not exist'). SIMPLE_TASK shipped violating it: its success contract was unsatisfiable without the plan-tools server, so the fast path silently always fell through to the architect and its cost saving never materialized (comment at 109-114).
findings.proposal: Make wiring a property of the role: add mcp_families: frozenset[Literal['orchestrator','plan_tools']] and sandboxed: bool to AgentRole; _invoke derives every gate from the role object and the tuples die. Add a module-import-time assertion in roles.py that any role whose allowed_tools reference fused-memory/escalation/plan-tools names declares the corresponding family — a new role that forgets fails at import, not weeks later in a watched project with no static .mcp.json.
findings.title: Agent capability wiring split across roles.py declarations and workflow.py name-string gate tuples
findings.bug_history_link: 2bc564ee12 'fix(workflow): wire simple_task into _invoke's MCP role gates' (reify esc-4943-54); 103bfd35e5 '_BriefingLike protocol sync' shows the same drift pattern on the briefing seam
findings.verdict_notes: AgentRole now declares mcp_families and sandboxed (agents/roles.py::AgentRole), replacing the _MCP_CONFIG_ROLES/_PLAN_TOOLS_ROLES tuples and the implementer/debugger sandbox check. The split('_')[0] key convention is gone (routing submodels). Only a minor role.name env-override check remains at workflow.py::TaskWorkflow.

findings.statement: Hard cancel (asyncio task.cancel from the harness) is detected in run()'s finally by sniffing sys.exc_info() for CancelledError (workflow.py), and correctness depends on a two-file comment contract with harness.py's B2 synthetic_cancel guard ('both must fire', 2148-2153; harness.py). Soft cancel (_cancel_event) is honored only where a call site opted in: _await_cancellable wraps exactly two awaits (1069, 5503), plus scattered is_set() checks (2312, 8776) — any other long await (steward waits, agent invocations, verify subprocesses) ignores soft-cancel until it finishes. _handle_soft_cancel (8691) then re-derives intent from a racy status read with a documented watcher-race caveat (8709-8720). The mined history shows this defect class being fixed one await at a time.
findings.proposal: One cancellation seam: run the workflow body under a CancelScope-style supervisor that converts both harness hard-cancel and _cancel_event into a single typed WorkflowCancelled(kind=hard|soft) control signal caught at exactly one place in run(); register terminal cleanups (lane release, config-dir cleanup, steward stop) in an ordered on_terminal list executed by the supervisor with the cancel kind as input, replacing the exc_info sniffing and the B1/B2 dual-guard coordination. Every future long await is covered by construction because it runs inside the scope, eliminating the opt-in gap.
findings.title: Cancellation is three parallel mechanisms with per-call-site opt-in, coordinated by comment contracts across files
findings.bug_history_link: 8x CancelledError/shutdown-race chain: 981ab6c68f (merge_to_main cleanup), 32a04a0999 (_run_slot hard-cancel), 473b3f07ea/e75a60b941/cfbb5efbb9 (abort-mid-flight 3-part), d00f4c9fc5 (watcher subprocess termination), task 1913 α/β branch-survival guards (6239451223, c3c3ea2fe2)
findings.verdict_notes: workflow_types.py::CancellationScope supervises the whole body, racing _cancel_event against it, and raises one typed WorkflowCancelled('hard'|'soft'). The sys.exc_info sniff is deleted, so soft cancel is no longer per-await opt-in. _await_cancellable and _handle_soft_cancel remain, with the watcher-race note.

findings.statement: workflow.py defines a hand-copied structural protocol of Scheduler that has grown one method per incident (13 methods and counting); each growth required a fix commit to the protocol AND to the mirrored conformance-assertion blocks and fakes in at least three test files (_workflow_helpers.py, test_workflow_dry_run_hook.py, test_workflow_e2e.py). The underlying defect is that TaskWorkflow's seam to the scheduler is 'the whole Scheduler': status CRUD, task CRUD, train queries, requeue accounting, blast-radius handling, and MCP tool dispatch all flow through one ever-widening protocol, so every new workflow feature widens it again.
findings.proposal: Split the seam along its three real usage clusters and define each protocol next to its implementer in scheduler.py (so pyright checks Scheduler's conformance at the definition site, not at N test files): TaskStore (get_task/update_task/get_status/set_task_status/mark_done/dispatch_tool), TrainView (tasks_by_train/get_tasks/get_statuses), and RequeueAccounting (clear_requeue_count, handle_blast_radius_expansion). TaskWorkflow takes the three narrow deps; one canonical fake per facade lives in tests/_workflow_helpers.py. Drift then surfaces as a compile error in the commit that adds the dependency, not as a follow-up fix task.
findings.title: _SchedulerLike shadow protocol plus N hand-maintained fakes drift with every new scheduler dependency
findings.bug_history_link: 5x protocol-drift chain: 62e2941359 (tasks_by_train), 93ba999122 (clear_requeue_count), f4b17c9716 (get_tasks/get_statuses), f89b62d78c + 3f5ef18837 (statuses param, protocol then fake), a5c7c6fb6a (persist_files on mock), 743d197257/ca4feadca0/1052a11656 ('add 4 missing methods' remediation batch)
findings.verdict_notes: _SchedulerLike moved out of workflow.py to a public, runtime_checkable scheduler.py::SchedulerFacade (f79938d925), owned by the Scheduler and conformance-tested in test_scheduler_callbacks. Still a hand-copied 13-method protocol with a FakeScheduler and pyright conformance blocks in tests, and it is still wide.

findings.statement: The 'restart a service safely' job is implemented four times: (1) StaleServiceRestartCoordinator._default_restart_executor (service_restart.py, fire-and-forget start_new_session spawn, no verify), (2) schedule_detached_systemd_restart (service_restart.py, systemd-run transient unit — its own docstring at :89-102 admits it mirrors the runner's argv pattern 'but WITHOUT its /bin/sh on-failure escalation wrapper — an accepted gap', and it passes no --working-directory), (3) DeterministicRunner._default_schedule_detached_restart (deterministic_runner.py, has --working-directory + cwd absolutization + on-failure escalation — added only after task 2105's exit-127 bug), and (4) DeterministicRunner's blocking cross-unit run + fresh-PID verify (deterministic_runner.py+, 1196+). Each path re-discovered a different subset of the invariants (absolute script path, explicit cwd, own-unit detection, escalate-on-fire-time-failure, verify-by-fresh-PID, timeout+group-kill). Own-unit detection (deterministic_runner.py) fails OPEN to the cross-unit blocking path when ORCH_UNIT is unset — which is the self-kill path (task 2064 fleet incident).
findings.proposal: Create orchestrator/proc_supervision.py with a single RestartPlan dataclass {script: absolute Path, args, cwd: required, target_unit, own_unit, on_failure_escalation: EscalationSpec|None, verify: FreshPidVerify|None} and one execute() that (a) derives detached-vs-blocking from own-unit comparison, (b) FAILS CLOSED when target==unknown-own-unit (refuse + escalate instead of blocking self-kill), (c) always sets --working-directory and absolutizes the script, (d) always wraps detached payloads with the on-failure escalation shell, (e) always runs fresh-PID verify against a persisted baseline for blocking restarts. service_restart.schedule_detached_systemd_restart and DeterministicRunner._default_schedule_detached_restart both become thin callers; the 'accepted gap' dies. Any future restart caller inherits all five invariants for free.
findings.title: Four parallel restart/self-restart mechanisms, each independently re-hardened — no single process-supervision contract
findings.bug_history_link: task 2064 (ORCH_UNIT unset → in-cgroup restart self-kill, fleet-wide), task 2105 (detached systemd-run ignores before_done.cwd → exit 127; fix landed only in deterministic_runner 72b1c24332/8021eecc5a while service_restart.py had the absolutize half all along), task 1902 f86f33004e (defer self-restart escalation behind fire-time failure), task 1973/2017 (executor failure split permanent/transient, counter reset fix fca1d415ee)
findings.verdict_notes: All restart paths are now thin callers of orchestrator/src/orchestrator/proc_supervision.py::RestartPlan (RP-1..5: fail-closed own_unit guard, explicit cwd, escalation wrapper, persisted verify baseline). service_restart.py::schedule_detached_systemd_restart and ::StaleServiceRestartCoordinator._default_restart_executor, and deterministic_runner.py::DeterministicRunner._default_schedule_detached_restart, delegate to it. aaf49a43ff converted the detached path.

findings.statement: Deploy progress is persisted as independent write-once dict keys in task metadata (before_done_ran_at, before_done_verified_at, gate_escalated_at, done_provenance) with the legal states only implicit in code. Every crash window between two stamps invented a new undefined state: 1900's phantom-done (ran_at set, nothing else → resume drove straight to done), 2059's silent strand, 2066's lost terminal writeback. The harness recon sweep must reverse-engineer runner state from the raw dict shape via _is_stranded_deterministic_shape (harness.py) — runner-internal knowledge duplicated across module boundary. Worse, the fresh-PID verify baseline (ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic) is a local variable never persisted, so retroactive verification is provably impossible — harness.py documents this at length and settles for a 'near-constant healthy' liveness check that cannot distinguish 'deploy took effect' from 'unit was already up'.
findings.proposal: Define a DeployState schema module (e.g. orchestrator/deploy_state.py): a typed dataclass with from_metadata()/to_metadata(), a single metadata.deploy_state phase enum (scheduled → ran → verified|failed|escalated → done) plus a persisted verify baseline field, and a transition table enforced at every write (illegal transition → loud escalation, never silent). DeterministicRunner writes phase+stamp atomically in one update_task call; harness sweeps and the resume path branch on the explicit phase instead of stamp-combination archaeology. This makes every crash window land in a NAMED state with a defined recovery action, and makes post-hoc freshness verification possible (persisted baseline vs live ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic).
findings.title: DeterministicRunner deploy lifecycle is an implicit state machine of four scattered metadata stamps with no legal-transition enforcement
findings.bug_history_link: task 1900 3c3cbd13cd (crash-window phantom-done, fixed by requiring positive-proof stamps), task 2059 strand + task 2074 recon sweep (Source A/B recovery, _deterministic_deploy_health_verdict CAVEAT about unpersisted baseline), task 2066 (writeback retries + durable escalation on budget exhaustion), ad436389c6 (resume guard hardening) — the mined '5x DeterministicRunner resume/crash-window correctness' theme
findings.verdict_notes: Deploy progress is now a typed shared/src/shared/deploy_state.py::DeployState with DeployPhase and a persisted VerifyBaseline. orchestrator/src/orchestrator/deploy_state.py::enforce_transition checks the _LEGAL table. The recon sweep no longer uses the raw-dict _is_stranded_deterministic_shape (harness.py now mentions it only as deleted).

findings.statement: _recon_inspect_unit (harness.py) is an admitted 'standalone duplicate of DeterministicRunner._default_inspect_unit' (its own docstring, :354-357), copied because the runner's inspector is a private bound method. The twins have already diverged: after task 2091, the runner's version wraps proc.communicate() in asyncio.wait_for(timeout=self._inspect_timeout_secs) with kill+bounded-reap (deterministic_runner.py); the harness copy still does a bare `stdout, _ = await proc.communicate()` at harness.py. A wedged `systemctl --user show` (the exact 2087/2091 signature: systemd busy, or a grandchild inheriting the stdout pipe) will hang _run_deterministic_recon_sweep — and since the sweep loop awaits the pass, the deterministic-strand recovery subsystem silently stops forever.
findings.proposal: Hoist the inspector to one module-level function inspect_systemd_unit(unit: str, *, timeout_secs: float) -> dict in the new proc_supervision.py (or a shared systemd helper), containing the wait_for + kill + sentinel-return hardening exactly once. DeterministicRunner._default_inspect_unit and harness._recon_inspect_unit both delegate to it (the runner keeps its injectable seam). Also fold _deterministic_deploy_health_verdict next to it so verdict semantics live beside the data they classify.
findings.title: Duplicated systemctl inspector diverged: harness copy lacks the task-2091 timeout guard — latent sweep-loop hang
findings.bug_history_link: task 2091 6ed42af750 (wedged systemctl show strands runner, timeout added — but only to the runner's copy); task 2074 c6f72ec25e created the harness duplicate; task 2087/2090 hang class
findings.verdict_notes: The hardened systemctl show call is hoisted into orchestrator/src/orchestrator/systemd_inspect.py::inspect_systemd_unit, with timeout, kill and a sentinel. harness.py::_recon_inspect_unit and DeterministicRunner._default_inspect_unit are thin delegates, so there is no unbounded duplicate.

findings.statement: Harness has 11 _start_X/_stop_X/_X_loop triplets (harness.py/4461, 4535/4560, 6069/6166, 6262/6306, 6488/6677, 6686/6712, 6886/6910, 6935/6973, 7370/7395, 7418/7442, 7820/7845), each hand-rolling the same idempotent-start check, cancel+suppress stop, and CancelledError-re-raise/log/backoff loop body — with subtle per-copy variations (the watcher supervisor loop alone, harness.py, carries four nested try/except layers, two counters and two deques added across tasks 1388/1430/1443/1449). run()'s startup is a ~20-step sequence whose ordering constraints exist only in prose comments (step labels 0..1c1g, with 1c1c1 ordered before 1c1c), and shutdown is a finally-ladder of per-subsystem try/except (harness.py+) whose ordering (cancel workflows BEFORE usage_gate.shutdown, checkpoint stores while loop healthy) is again comment-enforced. This structure is exactly why shutdown correctness took 5+ passes and why cli.py needs a daemon-thread os._exit(137) watchdog as a backstop.
findings.proposal: Introduce a BackgroundService/LifecycleRegistry abstraction: a small class per loop (name, interval/backoff policy, single async pass_fn, failure-log bounding) plus a registry the Harness populates in declared order — registry.start_all() starts in order, registry.stop_all() cancels in reverse with a per-service timeout and one uniform CancelledError contract. The 11 triplets collapse to registrations; run()'s finally collapses to one stop_all() call; the os._exit watchdog remains as last resort but the hang class (one loop swallowing CancelledError or one stop call wedging the ladder) becomes structurally impossible. Task 1907's 'bound background-loop failure logging' fix becomes a property of the class, not of each copy.
findings.title: Eleven hand-rolled background-loop triplets + a comment-ordered startup/shutdown ritual — the source of the recurring shutdown-hang class
findings.bug_history_link: mined '5x graceful shutdown/SIGTERM hang' theme (tasks 108, 161/162/169, 875 'hangs in asyncio cleanup after SIGTERM — never exits', 1080 '45s os._exit timer leaks into pytest'), ad69a8d093 (1907: bound background-loop failure logging), watcher-loop fix chain 1388/1430/1443/1449
findings.verdict_notes: Most loops moved to background_service.py::BackgroundService/LifecycleRegistry (harness registers them around line 2348). Hand-rolled start/stop pairs remain for the merge worker, offline lane, escalation server and the watcher supervisor. The supervisor loop is still large (_watcher_supervisor_loop with nested try layers). The cli.py os._exit watchdog is still there. Harness has grown to 18k lines.

findings.statement: A task's true state is spread over five substrates (fused-memory status string, git branch existence/ancestry/merge-marker, worktree directory, in-memory scheduler._dispatched + workflow dict, escalation queue), and no single component owns the mapping. Consequently harness accreted at least seven reconciliation sweeps that each re-implement parts of the derivation: _recover_crashed_tasks (:1932), _reconcile_stranded_in_progress (:2779, with R3 cancel-grace and R4 blocked-status guards bolted on), _reconcile_one_stranded (:2964, is_ancestor fast-path + branch-deleted merge-marker archaeology + degenerate-branch check), _revert_in_progress_if_no_live_claimant (:3399), _scan_for_terminal_active_tasks (:7288), _run_main_tip_sweep (:7483), and _run_deterministic_recon_sweep (:7738, which needed explicit Source-A/Source-B within-pass mutual exclusion, c6f72ec25e). Each sweep has its own dedup counters (_reconcile_failure_counts), race guards, and status whitelists (_RECONCILE_SWEEP_STATUSES) that can disagree; the 7x fix theme shows the same state machine kept producing new stuck-task shapes (stuck-done, degenerate-branch, stranded-in-progress, stranded-blocked, out-of-band-merged-blocked).
findings.proposal: Extract a TaskGroundTruth resolver module: one async derive_truth(tid) -> TruthReport{db_status, live_claimant(plan.lock/owner_pid), branch_state ∈ {on_main(sha), exists_off_main, gone_with_merge_marker(sha), gone_no_marker}, worktree_present, open_escalations} plus ONE classification table mapping TruthReport → recovery action (mark_done_with_provenance / revert_to_pending / re_file_escalation / leave). All sweeps become thin schedulers over this shared derivation; the is_ancestor→rev-parse→find_merge_marker archaeology and the done_provenance convention exist exactly once. New crash shapes then require adding a table row, not a new 400-line sweep with fresh race guards.
findings.title: Task ground truth re-derived independently by seven sweeps across five state substrates — every new crash shape spawns a new sweep
findings.bug_history_link: mined '7x stuck/stranded task reconciliation' theme: 920a56a4e9 (stuck-done recovery via diff-based reconcile), 8df3540aec (degenerate-branch revert), ca3a9d5754 (stranded-in-progress Fixes 1,3,4), a58cc2717c (stranded-blocked orphan-escalation recovery), 4c09b4728 (is_ancestor guard), d8d76c6e67 (1883 reconcile double-fetch)
findings.verdict_notes: A single resolver now exists: TaskGroundTruth.derive_truth composes the substrates, with one classify_recovery/_RECOVERY table. The seven sweeps in harness.py (_recover_crashed_tasks, _reconcile_stranded_in_progress, _reconcile_one_stranded, _revert_in_progress_if_no_live_claimant, _scan_for_terminal_active_tasks, _run_main_tip_sweep, _run_deterministic_recon_sweep) still exist and route policy through it. Substrate spread is the same; re-derivation is reduced.

findings.statement: Harness.__init__ wires the scheduler by assigning private attributes: scheduler._on_park_stop_trip, _on_external_dep_block, _on_starvation_warn/_resolve, _warm_base_health_probe, _on_warm_base_warn/_promote_l2/_resolve, _suppress_blocked_write (harness.py), and later writes scheduler._module_cache[task_id] directly (:1923). The mid-run stranded sweep reads scheduler._dispatched and scheduler.lock_table._held (harness.py) to decide whether a task is 'actively held' — a liveness judgment duplicated outside the single writer of that state. There is no declared interface, so (a) the dispatch-vs-sweep race had to be patched with the R3 cancel-grace window and dispatched/held filters after stranded tasks were reverted out from under live workflows, and (b) tests must mock privates, producing the fixture-drift failures that forced the supervisor loop to deliberately re-raise AttributeError (harness.py, task 1449).
findings.proposal: Define a SchedulerCallbacks protocol (dataclass of the nine hooks) accepted by Scheduler's constructor, and add public accessors scheduler.is_actively_held(tid) and scheduler.cache_modules(tid, modules) so _dispatched/lock_table stay single-writer with the holding judgment computed where the state lives (including the cancel-grace semantics, which currently live in harness's _workflow_cancel_recent). This turns the sweep-vs-dispatch race from a comment-guarded convention into an API guarantee and lets tests fake one protocol instead of nine private attributes.
findings.title: Harness↔Scheduler seam is private monkey-patching: nine _on_* callback assignments plus direct reads of scheduler internals
findings.bug_history_link: ca3a9d5754 (stranded-in-progress accumulation — mid-run sweep racing the scheduler required the dispatched/_held filter and R3 grace guard), task 1449 (AttributeError re-raise added because private-attr mocking drifted), task 1880 5dfca8d2f6 (starvation hooks wired as privates)
findings.verdict_notes: The nine _on_* private assignments are replaced by a declared SchedulerCallbacks bundle passed to the Scheduler constructor. Sweeps use the public Scheduler.is_actively_held instead of _dispatched/_held. Residual reach-ins remain: harness.py assigns scheduler._landed_outbox_gate and _already_landed_gate, and reads scheduler._module_cache and _workflow_cancel_at.

findings.statement: The Jul-3/4 incident (orphan-reaper ran `git worktree prune` over an unmounted lane mount and wiped ALL lane registrations, then reuse fast-path + restore_assignment re-poisoned lanes on every requeue) was fixed by task 2099 with a pool_storage_present() refuse-gate — but that gate lives ONLY inside prune_worktrees() (git_ops.py). Five other raw `_run(['git','worktree','prune'])` sites bypass it entirely: create_worktree leftover-branch cleanup (git_ops.py), materialize_member_solo (4341), delete_solo_branch (4426), prune_stale_merge_worktrees (5365), reap_interactive_worktrees (5725), plus the harness substrate-gate cleanup (harness.py). The merge-lane sites (4341/4426/5365) run on merge-queue activity independent of lane-pool health, so during the exact mount-down window 2099 guards against, a train-stacking or solo-branch cleanup can still wipe every mount-resident lane's admin entry — recreating the CRITICAL incident through a side door.
findings.proposal: Create one chokepoint: GitOps._prune_registrations(context: str) that (a) refuses when pool_in_use() and not pool_storage_present() (firing _note_pool_storage_absent), (b) is the ONLY place the literal ['git','worktree','prune'] argv may appear. Convert all 6 raw sites to call it. Enforce with a repo test that greps orchestrator/src for the argv literal and asserts exactly one occurrence (same pattern as the existing .task defense tests) — the invariant 'nobody prunes registrations except the guarded chokepoint' becomes machine-checked instead of convention.
findings.title: git worktree prune has 6 unguarded call sites bypassing the 2099 registration-wipe guard
findings.bug_history_link: task 2099 (dd02f3b772, 6d587d2d5a, 64b3a58111) and the 2026-07-04 warm-lane orphaned-registration incident (fix tasks 2097-2100; 2099 flagged CRITICAL)
findings.verdict_notes: Every raw git worktree prune now routes through git_ops.py::GitOps._prune_registrations, a single chokepoint documented as covering every call site, and it calls _reconcile_pool_storage_before_sweep (the 2099 guard). grep finds only one raw prune argv left. Raw prune sites in harness.py are gone too.

findings.statement: acquire_warm_lane has four divergent teardown idioms: release_warm_lane (detach HEAD + branch-retention + pool release; lines 2751, 2803, and via _reset_and_seed_recycled_lane at 3320/3348 — the task-2062 fix sites), `git worktree remove --force` + bare pool.release (2870-2874, 2912-2916), degenerate-ref delete on exactly one of those paths (2936), and the top-level `except Exception` handler at 3060-3065 which does a bare `self.warm_lane_pool.release(lane)` with NO HEAD detach. Any exception raised AFTER a branch checkout succeeded flows to that handler — e.g. _reuse_warm_lane -> commit() raising RuntimeError('Commit failed') (3887), or a shared-tail failure after _reset_warm_lane's `checkout -f -B` (3043-3053). Result: lane marked FREE while task/<id> stays checked out in it; the task's requeue then hits `git worktree add`/`checkout -f` failing with 'already used by worktree at _lane-K' — the exact second root cause of the repeatedly mis-triaged acquire-fault class. Task 2062 fixed three named paths but not the catch-all that backstops all of them.
findings.proposal: Introduce one teardown primitive `_abort_lane_acquisition(lane, bare_id, *, remove_worktree: bool)` that always: commit-or-discard per policy, `checkout --detach`, apply the branch-retention rule (_delete_branch_if_on_main + degenerate-ref check), then pool release. Route every fault exit in acquire_warm_lane/_reset_and_seed_recycled_lane — including the top-level except — through it. Add a test that injects an exception after the reuse-path checkout and asserts the lane HEAD is detached post-fault.
findings.title: Catch-all fault path in acquire_warm_lane still uses bare pool.release, re-creating the task-2062 stale-checkout collision
findings.bug_history_link: task 2062 (35dafc12d4 'close mid-run recycle-lane checkout leak via release_warm_lane', 8c17646619, bd763d6bbe); operator memory: acquire-fault has TWO root causes, stale-checkout collision 'already used by worktree at _lane-K'
findings.verdict_notes: The catch-all in acquire_warm_lane's impl now calls git_ops.py::GitOps._abort_lane_acquisition, which commits WIP, runs checkout --detach, cleans a degenerate ref, and only then calls pool.release as its last action. No bare pool.release remains on the fault path. Task 2199.

findings.statement: The lane lifecycle (seed -> registered -> assigned -> in-use -> released) is NOT an enforced state machine with a single owner. WarmLanePool models only FREE/ASSIGNED in memory (warm_lane_pool.py) and is mutated by TWO modules: GitOps acquire/release paths and Harness recovery (restore_assignment at harness.py/2397/2418/2434, note_assignment at git_ops.py). Everything else — registration, branch attachment, occupant identity — is re-derived per call from git admin dirs, .task/plan.json, branch refs, and the mount sentinel. acquire_warm_lane (2502-3065) and _recover_crashed_tasks (harness.py) are both giant decision trees over the cross-product of these sources, and each historical bug is one unhandled cell: orphaned registration with surviving assignment (task 2097), stale plan.json re-pinning a broken lane (task 2098/reify 4655/4947), detached-HEAD stale branch ref (task 1923 residual at git_ops.py), recycled-id identity adoption (reify 3770 -> worktree_identity.py), previous occupant's .task/ inherited on reattach (reify esc-4920-163 -> the rmtree at git_ops.py). Derived state silently diverges by design because nothing records what state a lane is SUPPOSED to be in.
findings.proposal: Add a durable per-lane record written transactionally at every transition: <worktree_base>/.lane-state/<lane-name>.json holding {state, task_id, title, branch, seeded_from_sha, updated_at} (lives ON the pool mount, so it vanishes with the mount — coherent with the 2099 sentinel logic). Wrap it in a LaneLifecycle class that is the SINGLE writer for both the in-memory pool and the record, with an explicit legal-transition table (assert on illegal transitions, escalate instead of heal). Startup recovery then becomes: read record, verify git reality matches, quarantine on divergence — replacing the heuristic adopt/clean/re-pin tree in _recover_crashed_tasks. The disk-backstop plan.json probe, note_assignment/restore_assignment split, and the identity title guard all collapse into record-vs-DB comparison in one place.
findings.title: Warm-lane lifecycle has no authoritative durable state — five derivable sources reconciled ad hoc at every decision point
findings.bug_history_link: tasks 1923, 2062, 2097, 2098 (cc8084fa2a 'gate lane re-pinning on git-worktree registration'), 2099, 2100; reify 3770 and esc-4920-163; 9x mined 'warm-lane pool bootstrap/reseed/orphan-reuse races' theme
findings.verdict_notes: A durable single-writer LaneRecord now exists in lane_lifecycle.py::LaneLifecycle, with an AcquireRoute-to-edge table and a quarantine step. The crash-recovery decision tree in harness.py still reconciles git, plan and pool state. WarmLanePool.restore_assignment is still called from both harness.py and git_ops.py.

findings.statement: Task metadata (.task/plan.json, iterations.jsonl, reviews/, agent_session.json) is stored INSIDE the worktree that hostile-by-accident LLM agents run arbitrary git commands in. The module docstring (git_ops.py) openly catalogs SIX belt-and-braces guards: scrub_task_dir_from_tree (244+, called at warm-lane acquire 3044, merges, worktree create), _assert_no_task_dir before advance_main, create_worktree inherited-contamination scrub, commit()'s :!.task pathspec PLUS post-staging unstage net (3859-3878, 'agents bypass them routinely'), merge_to_main post-merge scrub, plus .gitignore layers (artifacts.py) — and STILL new cells appear: the occupant-switch rmtree at git_ops.py (reify esc-4920-163 cross-task contamination) and four :!.task/ pathspec exclusions in merge_gates.py (1087, 1117, 1261, 1282). The mined fix history shows 5+ separate hardening rounds for this ONE class. The structural cause is the location: any in-tree path can be staged by an agent, and any checkout/clean/reset interacts with it, so every new git operation needs a new guard forever.
findings.proposal: Move task artifacts out of the git tree: <worktree_base>/.task-meta/<worktree-name>/ (sibling pattern already proven by quarantine_base, git_ops.py), with artifacts.py TaskArtifacts as the single path-derivation owner and the path handed to agents/mcp_lifecycle via config. Then the entire defense layer — scrub functions, pathspec exclusions, post-staging nets, per-incident rmtrees, .task/.gitignore writers — becomes dead code, and contamination of main becomes structurally impossible rather than 6x-guarded. Bonus: lane identity metadata survives `git clean -xfd`/`checkout -f`, simplifying the reuse/identity guards too. Keep _assert_no_task_dir as a cheap tripwire during migration.
findings.title: .task/ sidecar lives inside the git worktree — one leak class defended by six redundant guards instead of removed
findings.bug_history_link: de7398eb91 'block .task/ from reaching main with 6 redundant safeguards', 0157796b74 'prevent .task/ contamination on worktree branches', 13e8eca1e5 'clear previous occupant's .task/ on reset-in-place reattach', task 14 'git add -A in worktrees commits .task/ artifacts', reify esc-4920-163
findings.verdict_notes: Task metadata now lives outside the worktree, under .task-meta. scrub_task_dir_from_tree, _assert_no_task_dir and the commit unstage net are deleted (tasks 2261 and 2262). The git_ops.py docstring says no .task-specific guards remain. Three :!.task/ diff pathspecs remain; they are residual, not the guard layer.

findings.statement: The .pool-root mount-health protocol is smeared across the codebase: the ONLY writer is _seed_warm_lane on rc==0 (documented at git_ops.py), while readers each hand-roll the guard + bootstrap escape: acquire_warm_lane create-once (2778-2804) and acquire_spec_lane create-once (2302-2326) duplicate the same ~25-line 'exists && !present -> bootstrap_ok? mark : refuse' block verbatim; prune_worktrees (6780-6805), _run_warm_lane_gc_reclaim, and harness crash recovery (1959-1967) each carry their own variant plus the pool_in_use() pre-gate added in step-16 because pool-less hosts were misread as mount-down. The 64b3a58111 chicken-and-egg deadlock (first lane acquisition refused forever on a fresh host) existed precisely because writer and readers live in different control flows with no encapsulated protocol; and the documented spec-only-host caveat (994-1041: spec pool health proxied through the WARM base) is another asymmetry born of the same scattering.
findings.proposal: Extract a PoolStorage class owning: sentinel path constant, present(), mark_present(), bootstrap_ok(), require_present(context) -> Enum{PRESENT, BOOTSTRAP_OK, ABSENT} that internally handles pool_in_use gating, marks the sentinel on BOOTSTRAP_OK, and fires the absence callback on ABSENT. All 6 guard sites become one call + a match on the enum. The writer/reader coupling, the bootstrap escape, and the pool-less-host exemption get one unit-tested implementation instead of N copies that must be co-evolved (2099 needed a same-day review-fix + two amendments because they weren't).
findings.title: Pool-storage presence is a scattered sentinel protocol with one hidden writer and duplicated bootstrap escapes
findings.bug_history_link: task 2099 chain (dd02f3b772, 6d587d2d5a, 5f20073166, 943bed9ad3) and its review-fix 64b3a58111 '.pool-root bootstrap deadlock' + amendments c149f02085/85c00d2fae
findings.verdict_notes: The sentinel read and write moved into lane_lifecycle.py::LaneLifecycle, with GitOps as thin delegates. The two sweep sites share _reconcile_pool_storage_before_sweep. But the create-once bootstrap block (worktree_base.exists() and not pool_storage_present(), then _pool_storage_bootstrap_ok) is still inlined at two places in git_ops.py (acquire_spec_lane and acquire_warm_lane). The spec-only-host caveat remains.

findings.statement: acquire_warm_lane (2502-3065) inlines route classification AND per-route pipelines: in-memory reuse, identity-mismatch reset (2724-2752), create-once fresh (2878-2940), create-once reattach (2826-2876), disk-backstop reuse (2950-2979), reset-in-place reattach (2992-3031), fresh recycle (3036-3040). Sibling routes that should behave identically have drifted: the identity-mismatch path re-implements reset+rmtree+reseed inline WITHOUT the R4 one-shot transient retry that the fresh-recycle route gets via _reset_and_seed_recycled_lane (3252-3353, task 1932); the task-2112 degenerate-ref cleanup runs only on the create-once -b seed-fault (2936) — correct today but enforced solely by comment; seed-fail rc handling (127/75 discrimination + operator hint) is copy-pasted four times (2732-2746, 2858-2868, 2898-2911, 3329-3343). Every fix task in the 9x mined theme (1932, 1934, 2097, 2099, 2112) had to find and patch the right subset of routes by hand — the structure guarantees the next fix misses one.
findings.proposal: Split into (a) a pure route classifier `_classify_lane_acquisition(lane, reused, ...) -> AcquisitionRoute` (enum of the 7 routes — unit-testable against the source-of-truth matrix without git), and (b) a table of route pipelines each composed from shared named steps (reset_step with R4 retry, seed_step with rc-discrimination, reattach_step, identity_step) plus the single fault-teardown primitive from the release-idiom finding. Divergence between sibling routes then becomes a visible table diff instead of a 565-line archaeology exercise; the identity-mismatch route inherits the R4 retry for free.
findings.title: acquire_warm_lane is a 7-route god-function whose sibling routes silently diverge
findings.bug_history_link: tasks 1932 (R4 retry), 1934 (reseed-trash hardening, 7f90e86c32), 2097 (9fcd8988b8), 2112 (20db8596d8); identity-mismatch route lacking R4 retry is speculative (no incident yet) but is exactly the shape of prior route-divergence bugs
findings.verdict_notes: Routes are now an explicit AcquireRoute enum with a durable edge per route, and fault exits share _abort_lane_acquisition. However _acquire_warm_lane_impl is still about 890 lines with every route inline. The seed rc==127 handling is still repeated at several sites in git_ops.py.

findings.statement: DeterministicRunner.run reconstructs its persisted state from stamp-presence combinatorics (gate_escalated_at, before_done_ran_at, before_done_verified_at, before_done_scheduled_at) plus escalation-queue scans keyed ONLY by task_id. deterministic_runner.py sets ever_escalated = bool(self.escalation_queue.get_by_task(task_id)) with no agent_role/category filter and archive included (queue.py scans archive when status=None); branch (b) at :1013-1029 then drives the task to done with note 'resumed after human resolution'. But the starvation watchdog files escalations with the same task_id into the same queue (harness.py, agent_role='orchestrator-starvation-watchdog'), and gate escalations from the task's own earlier life also persist in the archive. Similarly the section-1 quiescence check at :861 blocks on ANY pending escalation for the task, not just the runner's own gate.
findings.proposal: Replace stamp-combinatorics with one explicit persisted state field: metadata.deterministic_state = {state: enum(created|action_stamped|action_verified|scheduled|gate_filed|failed_escalated|done), evidence: {...}} written atomically via update_task(metadata_mode='merge') as a single key, with a legal-transition table in DeterministicRunner (module-level dict, assert on every write). Scope all escalation queries with the runner's sentinel agent_role ('orchestrator-deterministic') — add an agent_role filter parameter to EscalationQueue.get_by_task and use it at deterministic_runner.py, :922 and :952. The 'ever_escalated' inference dies entirely: resolution proof becomes state==failed_escalated + that specific escalation's resolved record.
findings.title: DeterministicRunner proves 'human resolved the deploy' by task-scoped escalation existence — any unrelated escalation aliases as resolution proof
findings.bug_history_link: Dense fix arc on exactly this inference logic: 3c3cbd13cd 'guard before_done resume against crash-window phantom-done' (task 1900), f86f33004e 'defer self-restart escalation behind fire-time failure branch' (1902), 00a0947540 'surface epsilon self-restart terminal-write failures loudly', tasks 2004/2105 (self-restart drops terminal transition; detached cwd bug), 72ae9d6c83/efdf2d4dc5 (task 2066 writeback guards). The ever_escalated aliasing itself is a confirmed-by-reading residual phantom-done vector of the same class 3c1900 tried to close.
findings.verdict_notes: deterministic_runner.py::DeterministicRunner now scopes every get_by_task (quiescence, ever-escalated resolution proof) with agent_role=DETERMINISTIC_AGENT_ROLE; starvation-watchdog filings no longer alias (task 2120).

findings.statement: task_status.py is three frozensets — there is no (from_status, to_status, actor) legality table anywhere. The scheduler dispatches only 'pending' (scheduler.py); the escalation server's resume action leaves tasks 'in-progress' by contract (escalation/server.py 'stays in-progress'), a status nothing re-dispatches; the external-dep policy blocks tasks and documents 'blocked tasks are not re-evaluated automatically — manually set back to pending' (scheduler.py). Recovery of these dead ends is delegated to the harness's periodic stranded-sweep (harness.py _RECONCILE_SWEEP_STATUSES, :2780-3400), which infers claimant liveness from plan.lock/owner_pid and infers merged-ness by grepping main's commit subjects (find_merge_marker). Server-side enforcement exists only as spot gates (terminal-exit, done-gate, provenance — scheduler.py handles their rejections).
findings.proposal: Add a TaskLifecycle transition table enforced at the single write chokepoint that already exists (fused-memory TaskInterceptor, which already gates terminal-exit): a dict of (from, to, actor_class) → allowed, where actor_class comes from the existing agent_id tagging. Make 'claimant' a first-class task field (run_id + heartbeat timestamp, stamped at dispatch, cleared at release) so 'stranded' becomes a queryable predicate instead of plan.lock/pid forensics. Change resume semantics to blocked→pending when no live claimant (the exact esc-2073-15 fix, but enforced structurally). The harness sweep shrinks to 'claimant heartbeat expired → pending', and find_merge_marker dies once the merge queue durably records task→merged-sha before branch cleanup.
findings.title: Task-status lifecycle has no transition authority; dead-end states are recovered by heuristic compensation sweeps in another subsystem
findings.bug_history_link: esc-2073-15 / feedback memory 'stranded_blocked resume leaves task in-progress' (2026-07-04); task 52 'Scheduler dispatches tasks with in-progress dependencies'; harness 'Fix 4: stuck-blocked recovery' and 'R4: sweep blocked for out-of-band merges' comments (harness.py); external-dep arc tasks 1854/1855/1799 all include 'manually re-pend' remediation text; C3.2/task 1620 _suppress_blocked_write patch for racing teardown writes.
findings.verdict_notes: A (from,to,actor) table now exists: shared/task_transitions.py::TRANSITIONS, wired into task_interceptor and scheduler. Stranded in-progress/blocked states are still recovered by the harness sweep (find_merge_marker, claimant liveness), so the compensation remains.

findings.statement: The pipeline strip_directory_locks → files_to_modules(depth) is independently coded in Scheduler._get_modules (scheduler.py), Harness._tag_task_modules (harness.py, which also writes scheduler._module_cache directly), Scheduler._persist_files_metadata (scheduler.py), and handle_blast_radius_expansion (writes _module_cache at :4456). The 54ec90fefc commit message documents the exact failure: the strip was added to the read path but a write site (module-tagger writeback) missed it, so the fused-memory lock-charter guard rejected the ENTIRE payload and silently dropped valid file entries. _module_cache has two writers (harness startup + blast-radius) while _get_modules itself never populates it after deriving (:4742 returns without caching) — cached and derived values can diverge after a metadata update.
findings.proposal: Create module_charter.py owning: derive_modules(files, depth) -> list[str] (strip + files_to_modules + diagnostics), and sanitize_files_for_persist(files) -> list[str] used by every metadata.files write path. Make _module_cache single-writer: only _get_modules populates it (write-through on derive), harness seeds via a public Scheduler.seed_modules(task_id, files) that routes through the same function. The lock-charter file-shape rule (Contract 1: file-level always, coarsen at read) then has exactly one implementation on each side of the wire.
findings.title: Module-lock derivation from metadata.files duplicated at 4+ sites with the lock-charter strip re-implemented per site, plus a dual-writer module cache
findings.bug_history_link: 54ec80/54ec90fefc 'strip directory entries in module-tagger writeback' (esc-1905-31), b0acbd7684 'fix update_task structured-rejection nesting bug' (1905 step-10), 8e94d0fdc5 'persist file-level paths in _persist_files_metadata', lock-charter Contract-1 decision (task 1905); reify-3468 subtree-lock incident cited at scheduler.py.
findings.verdict_notes: Derivation centralised in module_charter.py::derive_modules; the cache has one writer, scheduler.py::Scheduler._write_module_cache. _get_modules now caches. Harness no longer touches _module_cache except a log read (task 2122).

findings.statement: The 'N consecutive ticks then fire, reset on clean tick, GC on terminal' pattern is implemented five separate times with subtly different semantics: _external_unresolved_counts (scheduler.py), _external_resolver_degraded_counts (:2001-2060), _external_hold_streak/_external_hold_cause (:1898-1937, cause-change reset), _local_backfill_unresolved_counts (three near-identical inline nested loops in acquire_next :3396-3488, one per degradation mode), and _starvation_first_seen/_starvation_escalated (:2179+). The acquire_next stale-id GC sweep (:3552-3633) must manually enumerate every dict, with dedicated comment-documented carve-outs ('sweep separately to avoid mutating while iterating', 'uses a SEPARATE guard... so it runs even when those dicts are empty'). Every new watchdog re-litigates reset-on-recovery and leak-on-terminal by hand.
findings.proposal: Introduce a StreakCounter/BookkeepingRegistry class: register(name, key_fn, threshold, on_fire) with touch(key)/clear(key)/gc(stale_ids) methods; the tick GC becomes registry.gc(stale_ids) over all registered counters, and 'reset streak on clean tick' / 'cause-change resets streak' become constructor options instead of re-derived logic. The three duplicated backfill-degradation loops in acquire_next collapse into one helper taking the missing-dep set. This structurally prevents the leak-and-drift class (counter must equal derived reality but can drift after recover→degrade gaps or terminal-before-threshold exits).
findings.title: Five+ hand-rolled consecutive-tick streak counters, each with bespoke reset/GC, manually enumerated in the per-tick stale-id sweep
findings.bug_history_link: eae2b3931b 'fix consecutive-tick semantics, partial-backfill guard' (1807); 817b7acd5c 'reset resolver-degraded streak on clean tick' (1855 step-4); 31778d43f3 (1855 coverage); 827437a44d 'starvation watchdog GC backstop in stale-id sweep' (1880 step-10); comment at scheduler.py documenting the permanent-leak case the sweep was patched to close.
findings.verdict_notes: The counters now use streaks.py::StreakCounter/StreakRegistry, and the GC sweep goes through the registry (dc684ecf97). Legacy dict aliases in Scheduler only point at the counters' internal dicts.

findings.statement: Two same-named predicates disagree: substrate_gate.carries_substrate_probe (substrate_gate.py) is True whenever the substrate_probe KEY exists — written specifically so run_substrate_recheck fails CLOSED (verdict=FLIP) on a declared-but-malformed descriptor (:265-280). Scheduler.carries_substrate_probe (scheduler.py) instead returns extract_probe_set(task) is not None, which is False for a malformed/empty descriptor. The production gate at harness.py uses the Scheduler version to decide whether to run the recheck at all — so a task whose substrate_probe descriptor is malformed (non-dict, or missing/empty probe_set, e.g. after a metadata-shape drift like the c20c69b28c/a083114d00 class) silently SKIPS the substrate gate entirely; the fail-closed branch in run_substrate_recheck is unreachable.
findings.proposal: Delete Scheduler.carries_substrate_probe. Harness:5108 should call substrate_gate.carries_substrate_probe (key-presence) and let run_substrate_recheck's own SKIP/FLIP logic decide policy — the module already encodes the fail-closed invariant correctly, the wrapper defeated it. Add a test asserting a task with substrate_probe='garbage' produces FLIP (blocked dispatch), not a skipped gate. This also matches the stated intent in the Scheduler docstring ('single source of truth') by making the substrate_gate version the actual single source.
findings.title: Substrate-probe predicate duplicated with divergent semantics — malformed probe fails OPEN at the real dispatch gate
findings.bug_history_link: Speculative as an incident, but it is a textbook instance of the mined 6x theme 'caller sends a shape the write path doesn't expect' (c20c69b28c update_task dict-or-string, a083114d00 reopen_reason coercion, b0acbd7684 structured-rejection nesting) — metadata-shape drift is the documented normal failure mode, and this gate fails open under exactly that drift.
findings.verdict_notes: The production dispatch gate in harness.py now calls substrate_gate.carries_substrate_probe (key-presence). The Scheduler variant is gone, so a malformed probe fails closed (task 2121).

findings.statement: Harness installs eight callbacks onto private Scheduler attributes post-construction (harness.py: _on_park_stop_trip, _on_external_dep_block, _on_starvation_warn/_resolve, _warm_base_health_probe, _on_warm_base_warn/_promote_l2/_resolve, _suppress_blocked_write), writes scheduler._module_cache (:1923), reads scheduler._dispatched at 6+ sites (:2544, :2701, :2754, :2866) and lock_table._held (:2867) as liveness oracles, and reads _requeue_history (:5820). Correctness depends on startup ordering documented only in comments ('runs while scheduler._dispatched is still empty' at :1408/:1418/:1422/:2453/:2789) — nothing enforces that the orphan reaper and stranded sweep actually run before the first acquire_next. Scheduler.release itself reaches into lock_table._held (scheduler.py). Every new watchdog adds another private-attr pair, growing the god-module in both files.
findings.proposal: Make the seam explicit: (1) a SchedulerCallbacks frozen dataclass passed to Scheduler.__init__ (all _on_* hooks become constructor state — no post-hoc mutation, no half-wired window); (2) public read API is_dispatched(task_id) / holds_lock(task_id) / requeue_history(task_id) replacing the _dispatched/_held/_requeue_history reach-ins; (3) a Scheduler.seed_modules() for the cache write (see module-charter finding); (4) an explicit started flag asserting acquire_next is not called before Harness.finish_startup(), turning the comment-only ordering invariant into a runtime check.
findings.title: Harness drives Scheduler through private state: 8 callback installs, cache writes, and _dispatched/_held reads form an unnamed contract whose ordering invariants live in comments
findings.bug_history_link: The mid_run filter at harness.py exists because the sweep once raced live workflows via exactly this shared-private access; task 1620 C3.2 _suppress_blocked_write and its 'MUST sit BEFORE dispatch_tool' placement note (scheduler.py) show the callback seam already produced a placement bug class; bc7ae6f303 'expose Scheduler.override_store' is a prior instance of retrofitting a public alias onto this private surface.
findings.verdict_notes: Callbacks are installed through scheduler.py::SchedulerCallbacks, passed at construction. Public accessors (is_dispatched, note_workflow_cancelled, requeue history) replaced the harness reach-ins. Only a log-only _module_cache read remains at harness.py; acquire_next asserts that startup ran first.

findings.statement: acquire_next (scheduler.py) inlines: warm-base watchdog, active fetch, dep-status backfill (with three duplicated degradation loops), park-eviction drain (which must run BEFORE park-GC 'so the operator audit event wins' :3490-3493), park-GC, a five-dict stale-id sweep, cooldown GC (must run 'before both candidate loops' :3635-3640), external-dep policy pass (exactly-once-per-tick invariant :3642-3677), override GC + reserve-now short-circuit with pre/post-snapshot diff bookkeeping (:3707-3808), starvation pass, pin loop, and scored loop. Each ordering constraint is enforced by nothing but position and comment; several historical fixes were pure reordering/scoping of these phases. The method also mixes pure selection with persistence (snapshot writes at three exits).
findings.proposal: Decompose the tick into an explicit pipeline: a TickContext dataclass (tasks, status_map, tasks_by_id, external_cache, overrides, candidates) built once, and an ordered list of phase objects (Hygiene: evictions→park_gc→stale_sweep→cooldown_gc; Policy: external_dep→starvation; Selection: pins→scored) where each phase declares what it reads/writes on the context. Ordering becomes data (a list literal) that a unit test can assert against, phase-level tests stop needing a full acquire_next harness, and the three duplicated backfill loops merge inside one Backfill phase. Split along the real seams only — the lock table and selection scoring already have clean boundaries; do not split the file for line count alone.
findings.title: acquire_next is a 720-line tick with 10+ ordered side-effecting phases whose sequencing constraints exist only as prose
findings.bug_history_link: 52c2c3981a 'clear blocked transitions deque on scheduler resume' and 1d20fa0f25 'de-dup park-stop blocked transitions' (phase-interaction bugs); 1c9a1ea64b/b51fb01d9d (1871: drain wired 'into acquire_next before park-GC' as its own fix step); 827437a44d (1880: GC backstop added because a phase was missed by the sweep); eae2b3931b (1807 backfill-loop semantics); γ2 correctness-crux comment :3363-3374 documents a whole bug class caused by one phase (active-only fetch) invalidating another's assumption (dep statuses present).
findings.verdict_notes: scheduler.py::Scheduler.acquire_next is now about 145 lines. It loops over _TICK_PHASE_ORDER (ordering as data) and calls separate _phase_* methods, with TickContext/TickOutcome (task 2236). | Reviewer (scheduler): The 720-line inline tick is gone: acquire_next is about 145 lines over _TICK_PHASE_ORDER (task 2236). The finding's central claim still holds: 'each ordering constraint is enforced by nothing but position and comment'. Phases are still dispatched by label string, their read and write sets are declared only in docstrings, the guard is a test pinning the tuple literal, and TickContext's empty-dict defaults turn an ordering mistake into a silent wrong answer (see the new TickContext finding; task 6518 D3 hits this live).

findings.statement: A verify command is a raw shell string from config, and every scoping/adaptation step is a find/replace hack on that string: _scope_command truncates at the first tool keyword and re-extracts dash-tokens (verify.py, explicitly 'naive dash-token extraction' per _build_fallback_config's docstring at 1559-1566), _strip_directory_flag does 4 replace() variants (204-219), _strip_leading_cd regex-strips one 'cd X &&' (222-243), _reproject_bare_uv_run rewrites 'uv run <tool>' into 'uv run --project shared <tool>' (254+), _scope_cargo_workspace substitutes --workspace and loops a regex until stable to strip --exclude pairs (1246-1279), _force_serial_pytest rewrites the pytest span (666), and _maybe_govern_merge_cmd wraps everything in bash -c (2399-2452). Each helper exists because a previous helper's output was un-runnable in some layout: _scope_command's truncation strands a leading 'cd fused-memory &&' (fixed by _strip_leading_cd, 4bb128496f), stripping --directory then broke uv venv resolution for structural files (dcfbd5ff11 preserves it in one branch), rewriting --workspace left an invalid --exclude (fd4758fcff). The tool identity, working directory, venv project, targets, and flags are all implicit in one string, so no transformation can be verified for well-formedness.
findings.proposal: Introduce a structured command model in a new module verify_cmd.py: @dataclass VerifyCmd(tool: ToolKind[PYTEST|RUFF|PYRIGHT|CARGO_TEST|CARGO_CLIPPY|NPX|OPAQUE], uv_project: str|None, cwd_rel: str|None, base_flags: tuple[str,...], targets: tuple[str,...], env: Mapping, wrappers: tuple[Wrapper,...]). Parse each config command string ONCE at config load (shlex-based; anything unparseable becomes ToolKind.OPAQUE and is never scoped — today it is scoped anyway and breaks). Scoping becomes 'replace targets', reprojection becomes 'set uv_project', cd-stripping becomes 'clear cwd_rel', cargo scoping becomes 'targets=[-p crate...]' with --exclude dropped structurally, cpu-governance becomes a wrapper entry. Render to a shell string only inside _run_cmd. All six string-rewrite helpers die. A single render() function can assert invariants (e.g. cwd_rel=None when targets are worktree-root-relative) that today are only comment lore.
findings.title: Verify commands are opaque shell strings mutated by textual surgery — replace with a structured VerifyCmd rendered at spawn time
findings.bug_history_link: 9x fix theme 'wrong shell command assembled for edge-case layouts': cb7277926d (task 1077), 4bb128496f (task 1643, esc-1643-4 rc=127 and pyright rc=4), ef68777a17/58d9de6987/8e6dc01b59 (task 2036 bare uv-run reprojection), fd4758fcff (--exclude vs -p), 05c2d87a72 (already-scoped guard mis-scope)
findings.verdict_notes: Raw-string surgery helpers (_scope_command, _strip_directory_flag, _strip_leading_cd, _force_serial_pytest) are gone. verify_cmd.py::VerifyCmd, parse_config_command, render and pure mutators replace them. verify.py::_reproject_str and _serial_pytest_str are thin parse-mutate-render wrappers. A raw/OPAQUE fallback remains for unparseable chains, but the stated defect is resolved.

findings.statement: The which-tests-for-this-diff decision is duplicated: scope_module_config (verify.py) and _build_fallback_config (1548-1691) each independently compute has_conftest, collectable_tests, and has_test_data and then take DIFFERENT fallback actions (module path: fall back to mc.test_command; fallback path: parent-dir targeting for conftest at 1638-1662, silent skip-with-warning for lone data modules at 1667-1684). Every file-classification bug had to be fixed in both places (task 1077 commits d7504d432d + cb7277926d; task 1852 commits 4fbed6c4fb + 7c9b316260). On top of that, run_scoped_verification duplicates the trivial-pass/pipeline-guard-override decision in its two branches (3140-3159 vs 3192-3211), and the overall scope decision is interleaved with execution so it is never inspectable except as log lines ('Verification mode: ...'). The structural-file (Protocol/TypedDict → unscoped pyright) check exists only in scope_module_config — the fallback path never widens pyright for structural files (a latent gap the 1852 pattern predicts will become a bug).
findings.proposal: New module verify_plan.py with a pure function derive_verify_plan(existing_files, module_configs, config, worktree_reader) -> VerifyPlan, where VerifyPlan is a list of PlannedRun(module_prefix, VerifyCmd, scope_kind: FULL_SUITE|FILE_SCOPED|SKIPPED|TRIVIAL, reason: str) plus plan-level flags (needs_pipeline_guard_check). File classification happens exactly once via a FileKind enum (CONFTEST, COLLECTABLE_TEST, TEST_DATA, STRUCTURAL, SOURCE, INERT) so predicates like _is_test_file/_is_collectable_test_file can't be recombined inconsistently. run_scoped_verification shrinks to derive-plan → execute-plan → aggregate. The plan is serializable, so it can be logged, unit-tested against the exact historical layouts (root conftest, data module, structural file), and attached to VerifyResult for post-hoc triage — closing the 'why did verify run/skip X' class permanently. The has_conftest-forces-full-suite convention (now CLAUDE.md operator lore) becomes an assertable property of the plan.
findings.title: Scope policy is computed twice with deliberately divergent semantics — extract a single derive_verify_plan() producing a declarative plan
findings.bug_history_link: 5x fix theme: tasks 1077 (d7504d432d + cb7277926d — same conftest bug fixed in both functions), 1078 (74888da488 _is_test_file invariant), 1852 (4fbed6c4fb + 7c9b316260 — same data-module bug fixed in both functions, plus a55ecdb3d8 warning amend); durable conftest convention had to be written into CLAUDE.md because the code can't express it
findings.verdict_notes: scope_module_config was deleted (de4acb2d00). The module path is derived once by verify_plan.py::derive_verify_plan and executed from the plan, with a single FileKind classification. The fallback path still has two implementations: verify.py::_build_fallback_config executes, and verify_plan.py::_derive_fallback_runs only mirrors it (its docstring admits it omits the subproject rescoping). Executed output is folded back into the plan, so the duplication is reduced but not removed.

findings.statement: _classify_failure (verify.py) and _extract_cause_hint (359-416) run the SAME pattern ladder over any check's output. _summarize_checks (703-749) calls them per-check but discards the one thing it knows — which command (and therefore which tool) produced the text. So every pattern must be safe against every tool's output universe: cargo prefixes must not swallow rustc diagnostics (the 3x re-grounding tasks 1103/1109/1116 — the allowlist comment block at 470-504 is a museum of dropped tokens), pytest progress lines pollute the fallback hint (405-413), infra tests that PRINT pytest-like markers polluted clock-stop matching (89256fc8e2), and the env_transient pip pattern needed a lookahead so 'pipeline'/'pipx' don't false-positive (32329ac44b, 442-457). This is the defining property behind BOTH mined classifier themes: patterns are written against assumed output shapes because no single tool's grammar bounds them.
findings.proposal: Make classification tool-dispatched: classify_failure(tool: ToolKind, rc: int, output: str, timed_out: bool) with per-tool classifier tables — cargo patterns only ever see cargo/clippy output, pytest patterns (incl. rc=5 semantics, INTERNALERROR, env_transient xdist-absence) only see pytest output, and the generic ladder survives only for ToolKind.OPAQUE. Where a tool offers structured output, prefer it over regex: pyright --outputjson, ruff --output-format json, cargo --message-format json (parse in the classifier, not the command — keep human logs). This removes the need to 'ground' each token against the union of all tools: a cargo allowlist token can no longer swallow a pytest or rustc line by construction. The env_transient patterns stop needing inverse-misattribution lookaheads because they run only under ToolKind.PYTEST. Depends naturally on the VerifyCmd model (finding 1) which carries tool identity to the call site — but can be shipped independently by keyword-sniffing the cmd string once, centrally.
findings.title: Failure classifier is tool-blind: one regex ladder over all tools' merged output — dispatch on tool identity instead
findings.bug_history_link: 3x cargo_cli_error re-grounding (tasks 1103/1109/1116; commits 1703f86f95, 18f57fe922, 1aed67cd56, 264d5b5e8a, b40a3e0a7f) + 6x flake-classifier tightening (2928f97da5 task 1025, 89256fc8e2 clock-marker anchor, 32329ac44b pip word-boundary, 339127ca11)
findings.verdict_notes: classify_failure(tool, rc, output, timed_out) dispatches per tool. verify.py::_summarize_checks passes the tool via _tool_for_cmd. Residuals: _classify_environmental is a tool-blind guard, and verify.py::_extract_cause_hint is still a single tool-blind regex ladder.

findings.statement: VerifyResult.category is a free string whose per-category policy is scattered: _ARCHIVE_DENY_LIST (verify.py), _CATEGORY_PRIORITY ordering (584), PREEXISTING_BREAK_SKIP_CATEGORIES (606), the endswith('_error') archival convention in _should_archive_category (640-657), inline infra-sentinel sets {'pytest_internalerror','env_transient'} duplicated at run_main_tip_sweep:3552 and 3580, the env-recovery gate `category == 'env_transient'` at 2720, sentinel categories minted in a different module (verify_runner.py UNSCOPED_TYPECHECK_*), and raw string comparisons in merge_queue.py/924 and workflow.py/4939. Adding one category (env_transient, task 2048) required a dedicated commit literally titled 'wire env_transient into non-misattribution collections' (40012ffba3) touching every registry — and nothing detects a registry that was missed; a forgotten entry silently gets default behavior (unknown → lowest priority, not archived, probed on main).
findings.proposal: Define class FailureCategory(StrEnum) in a small verify_categories.py with a single declarative policy table: CATEGORY_POLICY: dict[FailureCategory, CategoryPolicy(severity_rank:int, archive:bool, preexisting_probe:bool, is_infra_transient:bool, retry_kind: NONE|TIMEOUT|ENV_SERIAL)]. Derive _CATEGORY_PRIORITY, _ARCHIVE_DENY_LIST, PREEXISTING_BREAK_SKIP_CATEGORIES, and the sweep's infra-sentinel set from the table; delete the endswith('_error') heuristic. A module-import-time assert enforces every enum member has a policy row (exhaustiveness). VerifyResult.category stays str on the wire (StrEnum keeps JSON codec byte-identical for verify_runner's Invariant 1) but all in-process branching goes through the enum. New categories then require exactly one row, and the retry behavior (currently three different ad-hoc retry mechanisms keyed on category/timeout flags) becomes visible in one place.
findings.title: Category taxonomy is bare strings synced across 5+ registries and 3 consumer modules — replace with a FailureCategory enum + one policy table
findings.bug_history_link: task 2048 (40012ffba3 'wire env_transient into non-misattribution collections', ad50006219, 96e524e85f — one new category = 4 registry edits + 2 inline-set edits); 5cff9af691 (pytest_internalerror → deny-list + skip-preexisting, same multi-registry dance)
findings.verdict_notes: verify_categories.py defines the FailureCategory StrEnum and a CATEGORY_POLICY table. The registries (archive deny list, priority, preexisting-skip, infra sentinels) are derived from it, and _validate_exhaustive fails at import if a member lacks a row. verify.py::_should_archive_category delegates to should_archive. VerifyResult.category is still typed str, and a few raw string compares remain, e.g. 'pytest_internalerror' at about line 9172. The unsynced-registry failure is gone. | Reviewer (verify): The table exists, but the category domain is not closed where it matters. VerifyResult.category is still `str`. Sentinel categories live outside FailureCategory: verify.py::_MERGE_NO_EVIDENCE_CATEGORY (added this window, 92af0716e8), verify_runner's UNSCOPED_TYPECHECK_* and FLOCK_CONTENTION_CATEGORY, and merge_lane's landing_detector_git_error. verify.py keeps its own category sets beside CATEGORY_POLICY: _VERDICT_BEARING_LEG_CATEGORIES and _RERUN_NON_VERDICT_CATEGORIES. CategoryPolicy.retry_kind is populated for every row but dispatched nowhere, because run_verification still hard-codes `category == FailureCategory.ENV_TRANSIENT`.

findings.statement: Two coupled defects. (a) Contract: b3_gate reads metadata.dry_run_proposals[-1] straight out of tasks.db JSON (b3_gate.py) — a dict with no schema, where 'is this a failure entry' is inferred from the PRESENCE of a 'status' key (359-360) and the highest-blast-radius class is detected by block_reason.startswith(POST_MERGE_RED_MAIN_REASON_PREFIX) (341-352), a human-readable string re-declared from merge_queue and kept in sync only by a coherence test (b3_gate.py). Any producer rewording the block reason silently disables the hard-abort. (b) Coverage gap: proposals are written ONLY by workflow._spawn_dry_run_unblock at agent-block time (workflow.py/7803/8228); merge_queue's block path writes block_reason but never a proposal, so check_proposal returns ABORT 'no proposal to gate' (b3_gate.py) for the ENTIRE merge-verify failure class — including the trivial scoped-lint/type reds that are B3's cheapest wins. Result: every merge-verify failure escalates to a human even when the fix is one import line (operator memory confirms this is a standing AFK pain point).
