findings.proposal: Define a typed BlockRecord (dataclass in a new unblock_types.py: block_class: BlockClass enum {AGENT_FAILURE, REVIEW_ISSUES, MERGE_VERIFY_RED, POST_MERGE_RED_MAIN, ...}, risk_label, head_sha, main_sha, files_referenced, investigated_at) with to_dict/from_dict validation; workflow AND merge_queue construct it (merge_queue sets block_class explicitly instead of encoding it in prose), b3_gate branches on block_class — the re-declared prefix constant and the 'status'-key sniff die. Then close the coverage gap: merge_queue's block path spawns the same dry-run investigation (it already has worktree, failing VerifyResult, and scoped diff; the investigator's input is strictly richer than the agent-block case), with POST_MERGE_RED_MAIN remaining hard-abort by enum. This converts the biggest always-human escalation class into B3-gateable work while making the gate's precedence ladder type-checked rather than string-sniffed.
findings.title: B3 gate consumes a schemaless dict via string-prefix matching, and its required input artifact is never produced on the merge-verify path
findings.bug_history_link: task 1680 (post-merge red-main hard-abort added as defense-in-depth against a mislabeled-low proposal — the 1643 failure mode); operator memory feedback_b3_gate_aborts_on_merge_verify_no_proposal ('trivial merge-verify type/lint fixes ALWAYS fall to human /unblock'); coherence-test-only sync noted in b3_gate.py
findings.verdict_notes: (a) check_proposal now reads a typed block_class (unblock_types.BlockClass) and uses the startswith(POST_MERGE_RED_MAIN_REASON_PREFIX) and 'status'-key sniffs only for legacy entries with no block_class. (b) merge_lane/worker.py::_spawn_merge_verify_dry_run now writes proposals on the merge-verify RED and unscoped-typecheck paths (f72565b492, 28f4466403). A string-prefix legacy fallback remains.

findings.statement: verify_failure_is_preexisting_on_main (verify.py) and run_main_tip_sweep (3496-3634) are structural clones: build path under git_ops.worktree_base with a magic prefix ('_mainprobe-'/'_mainsweep-'), 3-retry `git worktree add --detach` with linear backoff for git lock contention, and a finally block doing scoped `git worktree remove --force` + rmtree — with the safety invariant 'INTENTIONALLY NO git worktree prune (DD5)' stated three times as comments (3288, 3410, 3623) and enforced nowhere. Worse, the prefixes' protection from the disk-pressure reaper depends on prune_stale_merge_worktrees matching only '_merge-*' — a coincidence-of-globs contract spread across modules, exactly the shape that produced the warm-lane orphaned-registration incident where a broad `git worktree prune` from another subsystem wiped live registrations (July 2026 incident; fix task 2099 is a prune-guard). A third sibling (the _merge-* creation path in git_ops/merge_queue) implements the same lifecycle a third way.
findings.proposal: Add an async context manager to git_ops: ephemeral_worktree(kind: WorktreeKind, sha) -> Path, owning naming (prefix registry per kind), the retry-on-lock-contention loop, and guaranteed scoped cleanup. Maintain a module-level PROTECTED_PREFIXES registry derived from WorktreeKind so prune/reap routines (prune_stale_merge_worktrees, orphan reaper) consult it instead of hardcoded globs — turning the comment invariant into code. Enforce DD5 mechanically: a repo test (or the existing silent-fallthrough-gate style check) asserting no source file outside git_ops invokes `git worktree prune`. Both verify probes shrink to ~15 lines each; the retry policy stops drifting between copies (today one caller could get a fix the other misses, as happened with the archive-prune throttle history).
findings.title: Ephemeral probe-worktree lifecycle copy-pasted with a comment-only 'no broad prune' invariant — extract git_ops.ephemeral_worktree()
findings.bug_history_link: 87ba2e7509 (probe worktree moved under worktree_base — fixed in one copy first), f0289c4e2c (single SHA resolve hardening for sweep only); cross-system: warm-lane `git worktree prune` registration-wipe incident 2026-07-04 (df tasks 2097-2100, 2099=prune-guard) shows the comment-only prune invariant fails in practice
findings.verdict_notes: Both probe and sweep in verify.py (verify_failure_is_preexisting_on_main, run_main_tip_sweep) now use git_ops.ephemeral_worktree(WorktreeKind.MAIN_PROBE / MAIN_SWEEP). That method owns the retry, scoped remove and no-prune lifecycle. The prefixes are a WorktreeKind enum registered in PROTECTED_PREFIXES (edbd493e43). fixed_by is the commit that moved verify.py onto ephemeral_worktree; it was found by pickaxe, so confidence is moderate. | Reviewer (verify): The probe and the sweep use git_ops.ephemeral_worktree, but a third site does not. verify.py::confirm_main_tip_failure_is_real still hand-rolls the 3-retry `git worktree add --detach` and the finally remove+rmtree, under a literal `_mainsweepconfirm-` prefix that is neither a WorktreeKind nor a PROTECTED_PREFIXES band. It survives the reaper only through classify_worktree_entry's generic '_'-prefix rule, and no owner reaps it after a crash.

findings.statement: Each of the three checks is tracked as five parallel locals (test_rc/test_out/test_timed_out/test_started_at/test_duration ×3, verify.py), and the derived invariant 'timed_out flag must be consistent with per-check rc/timeout state' is a 6-clause boolean formula written out twice — in the retry loop (2672-2678) and again in the env-recovery branch (2747-2753). The inline comment at 2735-2744 documents the exact bug this duplication already produced: a recovery run hitting the wall-clock left a stale timed_out=False while category flipped to infra_timeout, wrongly marking the worktree warm and hiding the timeout from merge_queue/workflow callers. The same data is then re-materialized as ad-hoc dicts in `runs` (2769-2797) whose keys are a second implicit schema consumed by _persist_attempt_logs/_build_summary_payload/_verify_duration_secs.
findings.proposal: dataclass CheckRun(label, cmd, rc, output, timed_out, started_at, duration_secs) with classmethod skipped(), plus a small VerifyAttempt(checks: list[CheckRun]) exposing derived properties passed, any_timed_out, pure_timeout_failure — computed in exactly one place so first-pass and env-recovery cannot disagree. run_verification's loop carries one VerifyAttempt instead of 15 locals; `runs` becomes [c.to_dict() for c in attempt.checks], deleting the parallel dict schema. The 'pre-loop initialisation satisfies static analysis' scaffolding (2626-2636) and both formula copies die. This is a small, mechanical refactor that removes a documented drift-prone invariant.
findings.title: run_verification's check state is nine parallel scalars with a hand-recomputed timeout-consistency formula — introduce a CheckRun dataclass
findings.bug_history_link: The stale-timed_out inconsistency fixed inside task 2048 (documented at verify.py); 10771d9bb0 richer-timeout-message amend; the _summarize_checks extraction itself was a 2048 'code_duplication fix' — evidence the seam is already under pressure
findings.verdict_notes: verify.py::CheckRun is a per-check dataclass whose to_dict() is the single runs-dict schema. verify.py::VerifyAttempt holds the checks and exposes pure_timeout_failure and any_timed_out as the one timeout-consistency formula. The parallel scalars in run_verification and the duplicated 6-clause formula are gone. The dict is still a plain JSON-native shape. The rationale is the underlying heuristic h11 (SPOT).

findings.statement: metadata carries ~15 load-bearing keys consumed by the orchestrator (a different process) with no shared schema, no version, and no single parser. The subsystem contains at least 8 independent parse helpers with divergent failure semantics: task_interceptor.py (_parse_metadata, unparseable→{}), 1428-1440 (_extract_metadata_dict, unparseable→None), 3860-3869 (inline parse in _merged_audit_metadata), deterministic_task_guard.py (→{}), lock_charter_guard.py, tools.py (→None, skip guard), sqlite_task_backend.py (_row_to_task, warn-once + coerce {}), 1354-1431 (_merge_metadata, corrupt-existing→raise, corrupt-incoming→last-write-wins). Field vocabularies drift silently: producer and consumer each declare the schema in their own constants. sqlite_task_backend.py (_normalize_legacy_memory_hints_value) exists solely to repair a shape drift that already shipped. The scheduler reads (task.get('metadata') or {}).get('external_deps') (scheduler.py) trusting a shape nothing enforces.
findings.proposal: Create shared/src/shared/task_metadata.py: a versioned pydantic model (TaskMetadata v1) with typed sub-models (BeforeDone, DoneProvenance, MemoryHints, ExternalDep) and a single parse_metadata() with one documented failure policy. shared/ is already imported by both sides (shared.usage_gate, shared.async_sqlite_base), so no new coupling. Enforce at the single write boundary — SqliteTaskBackend.add_task/update_task validate incoming blobs against the model (unknown keys pass through a reserved 'x_' namespace or warn) — and delete the 8 ad-hoc parsers in favor of the shared one. The orchestrator imports the same model for reads. Would have prevented: the deterministic-deploy-scheduled drift, the memory_hints legacy-shape class, and the external_deps shape assumptions.
findings.title: Task metadata is an unversioned cross-process contract parsed by 8+ divergent best-effort parsers
findings.bug_history_link: Commit 9493fa073d: orchestrator task 1902 added done_provenance.kind='deterministic-deploy-scheduled' but fused-memory's _VALID_PROVENANCE_KINDS was never updated — every own-unit self-restart deploy's done write was rejected and the task landed silently permanently blocked (tasks 1976, 1982). Also _normalize_legacy_memory_hints_value repairing shipped shape drift; external-dep gate bugs 1854/1855/1799 (CLAUDE.md); before_done.cwd ignored by the runner (task 2105) — cwd/args/env are never validated because no schema names them.
findings.verdict_notes: Versioned shared schema now exists (shared/task_metadata.py::TaskMetadata, schema_version=2, apply_migrations, legacy memory_hints migration). Scheduler reads via _task_external_deps. But divergent best-effort parsers remain: _parse_metadata copies in execution_class_guard, routing_intent_guard, model_overrides_guard, deterministic_task_guard etc., plus TaskInterceptor._extract_metadata_dict and sqlite _merge_metadata. Write path is enforce=False (census only). | Reviewer (fm-task-layer): Re-measured at 6551b75aba. There are 11 private metadata parsers in middleware/: _parse_metadata in execution_class_guard, routing_intent_guard, model_overrides_guard, operational_suggestion_guard, operational_routing_guard, recurring_gate_guard and deterministic_task_guard (twice); _coerce_metadata_dict in recon_write_policy; three in task_interceptor. shared has two identically named _as_metadata_dict helpers (toolcall_markup, uuid_prefix). The resolve-once helper middleware/metadata_dict.py::raw_metadata_dict is adopted by 1 guard (gitignored_deliverable_guard). One update_task call parses its metadata about 13 times across tools.py, the interceptor and the backend. The backend validates with parse_metadata and then discards the typed model. Only 2 orchestrator consumers (scheduler, flake_ledger) read typed TaskMetadata, against about 138 raw metadata dict accesses. The versioned schema exists, but metadata is still not parsed once at the boundary into typed values.

findings.statement: Every defensive branch in _process_add_tickets_batch_prepared degrades to 'create': idempotency-check failure → create (task_interceptor.py), curator exception → decisions=[None]*N → create (2926-2936), batch_target_index out of range → create (2867-2882), sibling failed → create (3001-3013), dependency cycle → create (3082-3097), worker cancelled mid-add_task → caller retry may duplicate (documented at 1553-1563). Since 'create' is the failure default, every new failure mode manifests as duplicate tasks — hence six stacked in-memory dedup layers, each with a DIFFERENT key: _intra_batch_key hashes title+description (task_curator.py) while _normalize_key hashes title+files (663-680), plus the R4 escalation-idempotency lookup, the LLM decision, the TTL'd _recent_creates cache (lost on restart), and the blocklist. The dispatch loop also maintains correlated parallel arrays across two index spaces ('non_none-space' vs 'ticket_data-space' remapping, 2843-2884) — the structure that produced the pass-1/pass-2 blank-title mismatch. No layer is durable: nothing at the store level makes duplicate creation impossible.
findings.proposal: Make uniqueness durable at the store: add a nullable candidate_key column to the tasks table (single normalization function, one key definition owned by task_curator.normalize_title + files) with a partial UNIQUE index over non-cancelled rows; add_task computes it, and a constraint violation resolves the ticket 'combined' with the existing id. This one root fix subsumes _recent_creates, _pre_llm_exact_match, and the intra-batch pre-pass (they become optimizations, not correctness layers) and survives restarts, which the in-memory caches do not. Separately, replace the parallel arrays (decisions[i], curator_degrade_reasons[i], resolved_task_ids[i], non_none_to_ticket_data) with a single per-ticket record dataclass so index-space remapping dies.
findings.title: Curator dedup pipeline fails open to CREATE on every failure branch, forcing endless dedup layering
findings.bug_history_link: 9x mined theme: tasks 833/893/894/917/981/1014/1015/1020/1136; commits 2640fa2d2d 'restore curator + add 4-layer dedupe defense', d41ff3b6bd 'layered deduplication', 43877f3e24 'intra-batch dedup pre-pass', 01698fa26b 'align pass-2 blank-title guard with pass-1'; the tracker itself holds duplicate-ID pairs (999/1000, 1001/1002, 1026/1028) and task 1042 exists to scan for residuals.
findings.verdict_notes: Failure branches still degrade to create (batch_target_index out of range, curator exception sets decision None) and TaskCurator._intra_batch_key, _normalize_key and _recent_creates persist. Mitigated: a durable partial UNIQUE index on candidate_key in sqlite_task_backend.py (v4), compute_candidate_key as single owner, and the parallel-array remap replaced by _TicketLifecycle records.

findings.statement: tools.py duplicates the overrides DDL from orchestrator/overrides.py, and set_task_priority_override/clear/reorder_pin_queue/get_pin_queue (tools.py, ~450 lines) re-implement the orchestrator's pin_order allocation, PinOrderCollision detection, and BEGIN IMMEDIATE read-then-write serialization against the SAME SQLite file, in a second language dialect (aiosqlite vs sqlite3). The two implementations are kept aligned by 17 'Mirrors orchestrator/src/orchestrator/overrides.py:<line>' comments — line-number references that rot on any upstream edit. Same pattern for park_eviction_requests (tools.py). Two writers in two processes with two codebases enforcing one concurrency contract is exactly the structure that produced the get_statuses protocol-drift class (implemented on one side, assumed on the other).
findings.proposal: Extract one store module into shared/ (shared/src/shared/scheduler_overrides.py): schema constant, pin-order allocation, collision rule, and the BEGIN IMMEDIATE contract in one place, with thin sync (orchestrator) and async (fused-memory) execution adapters over the same statement builders. Both sides import it; delete tools.py's private copies and the 17 mirror comments. Any schema or invariant change then lands in both processes atomically.
findings.title: scheduler_overrides.db and park-eviction store are fully dual-implemented across two processes, synced by line-number comments
findings.bug_history_link: Same class as eb21502b68/95d0a08772 (get_statuses protocol added but not implemented — 'would AttributeError at runtime'); park-eviction test-leak fixes e1074c1233/2d4fecdb1a/6c853c53b9 show the duplicated store already generating churn. Direct override-mirror bug: speculative, but the mirror-comment density is the leading indicator.
findings.verdict_notes: tools.py still carries its own _OVERRIDE_SCHEMA and park_eviction_requests DDL, and re-implements set/clear/reorder/get_pin_queue with BEGIN IMMEDIATE. About 9 'Mirrors orchestrator/src/orchestrator/overrides.py:<line>' comments remain (lines ~10029-10288). The comment block states these are intentional duplicates because fused-memory cannot depend on orchestrator. Nothing moved to shared/.

findings.statement: The invariant 'set_task_status is the only writer of status and done_provenance' is enforced by re-implementation at every deck: tools.py (_reject_status_in_update_task, _reject_done_provenance_in_metadata), task_interceptor.py (same two, labelled 'defence-in-depth alongside server/tools.py'), and a backend floor (sqlite_task_backend.py, status only). The copies already disagree on error shape — tools.py's done_provenance guard returns {'error':…,'error_type':'ValidationError'} while the interceptor's returns {'success':False,'error':'done_provenance_via_update_task'} — which forced interceptor_write_succeeded (task_interceptor.py) to enumerate every known rejection-dict shape. Root cause: writing done_provenance isn't a privileged capability — the sanctioned writer (_apply_status_transition, lines 719-724, 782-787) persists it through the SAME public tm.update_task it must guard, so 'who may write' can only be enforced by re-checking at every entry point, and the backend floor can never cover done_provenance.
findings.proposal: Make the backend the single enforcement point with a privileged internal API: SqliteTaskBackend.update_task unconditionally rejects status and metadata.done_provenance (extending the existing floor); add a non-protocol method stamp_audit_metadata(task_id, fields) that only TaskInterceptor holds a reference to, used for done_provenance/reopen_* persistence. Delete the tools.py and interceptor guard copies (tools.py keeps only the ticket-id shape check), and define the rejection dict shape once in task_backend_errors.py so interceptor_write_succeeded stops enumerating shapes.
findings.title: update_task write-authority enforced by three drifting guard copies instead of one privileged seam
findings.bug_history_link: 8daed1734a 'close update_task(status=) bypass + 4 defence-in-depth fixes' (2026-05-08 forensics: 9 unauthorized done writes in 36h); 92d9c7d28e 'backend floor rejects non-None status' — the third layer added because the first two could be bypassed by in-process callers; 3daade6fd8 done_provenance kind discriminator + role gate.
findings.verdict_notes: tools.py guard copies deleted (f0a46af6bd, task 2203). Canonical rejection shapes and typed errors added in 24107cb526: backends/task_backend_errors.py StatusWriteAuthorityError and DoneProvenanceWriteAuthorityError. The enforcement is now the backend floor in sqlite_task_backend.py update_task, which raises them; the interceptor only catches and maps them (task_interceptor.py ~5604). One error shape, one seam.

findings.statement: tasks.status is 'TEXT NOT NULL' with no CHECK (sqlite_task_backend.py), and set_task_status writes any string verbatim (658-692). The legal vocabulary is declared four times: orchestrator/task_status.py (TERMINAL/ACTIVE/WORKFLOW_PRESERVE, with an explicit 'DRIFT RISK' comment warning that a stale set silently strands tasks from dispatch), fused_memory/reconciliation/task_filter.py (ACTIVE_TASK_STATUSES), task_interceptor.py (TERMINAL_STATUSES, comment: 'Duplicated from orchestrator.task_status… duplication is cheaper than cross-package coupling' — contradicted by the CI guard test that already imports across packages, and by shared/ being an existing cross-consumed package). A typo'd or novel status ('in_progress' vs 'in-progress') persists silently, falls outside ACTIVE_TASK_STATUSES, and the task is never fetched or dispatched again — silent stranding, the worst failure shape this system has.
findings.proposal: One shared/src/shared/task_statuses.py exporting a StrEnum plus the derived frozensets (TERMINAL, ACTIVE, WORKFLOW_PRESERVE, STATUS_TRIGGERS); SqliteTaskBackend.set_task_status/add_task reject status not in the enum (loud TaskmasterError), optionally backed by a CHECK constraint at the next schema bump. Both packages import it; delete the three local copies and the cross-package equality test (it becomes tautological). Adding a status ('merge-deferred' took synchronized edits in 3 files + 2 regression tests per the task-1519 comments) becomes a one-line change.
findings.title: Status vocabulary duplicated in four modules with zero store-level enforcement
findings.bug_history_link: task 1519 'merge-deferred' required coordinated edits in task_interceptor.py, orchestrator/task_status.py, and two lock-tests; 475b16dbce 'trust store over stale _status_cache for reinstated tasks'; mined theme 4x backend/protocol conformance drift (eb21502b68).
findings.verdict_notes: shared/src/shared/task_statuses.py::TaskStatus is the single vocabulary, with TERMINAL, ACTIVE and WORKFLOW_PRESERVE derived. orchestrator/task_status.py is a re-export shim (51adf3e709); task_interceptor imports TERMINAL from shared. sqlite_task_backend.set_task_status rejects any status outside _VALID_STATUSES, so a typo'd status no longer persists. The column has no SQL CHECK, but the guard is in code.

findings.statement: Project routing is decided by regex-scanning free prose (title/description/details) for path prefixes (path_scope_guard.py, hand-tuned boundary class excluding '/' and '.'), where mention ≠ ownership — so precision/recall is structurally unwinnable at the regex layer. The system compensated by stacking: lookbehind tuning (tasks 1095/1096/1100/1111/1118), a 454-line LLM adjudicator on guard HIT (path_scope_adjudicator.py, task 1822), a routing_override_reason escape hatch (task 1845), and a scope-violation escalator. Meanwhile dark_factory_path_guard.py declares itself a back-compat shim 'for one merge cycle' yet is still the import used by task_interceptor.py, keeping two guard mechanisms (registry-configured multi-project vs hard-coded dark-factory short-circuit, _path_guard_check task_interceptor.py+) alive in parallel.
findings.proposal: Split the decision by signal quality: REJECT only on structured evidence — metadata.files prefixes matched exactly against ProjectPrefixRegistry (no regex, no prose) — and demote prose scanning to an advisory: attach a 'possible_scope_mismatch' warning to the created task / fire the escalator instead of rejecting, letting the existing adjudicator+curator handle the ambiguous middle asynchronously. This ends the FP/FN tuning treadmill because exact file-prefix matching has no recall/precision dial. Delete the dark_factory_path_guard shim by switching the interceptor's imports to path_scope_guard and folding the hard-coded prefix list into the registry default.
findings.title: Path-guard routes tasks by regex over prose, compensated by a four-stage patch stack plus a permanent 'temporary' shim
findings.bug_history_link: 6x mined theme: task 1088 (introduce guard), 1094 'prompt-only bypass', 1095 'false positives: tighten lookbehind', 1096/1100/1111/1118 successive polish; then 1822 (adjudicator) and 1845 (override hatch) as compensation layers; meta-fix task 2085 for the mis-routing class.
findings.verdict_notes: The dark_factory_path_guard.py shim is gone (retired in task 2208; the module docstring says so), and the interceptor imports path_scope_guard directly, so the dual guard mechanism is gone. Regex-over-prose routing remains: _build_pattern and find_paths, with PathScopeAdjudicator (496 lines) as compensation. The guard is now two-sided and gated on declared files, and prose is advisory unless soft_scope_enforced.

findings.statement: The B10 invariants (task_kind enum, deterministic⇒before_done∨always_escalates, before_done only on deterministic, script exists+executable+timeout_secs) run once at tools.py submit_task (tools.py). update_task's guards reject only status/done_provenance/directory-locks (task_interceptor.py) — nothing stops update_task(metadata={'task_kind':'deterministic'}) on a normal task, injecting or mutating before_done (e.g. pointing script at a path that no longer exists), or flipping always_escalates, all of which the DeterministicRunner in the orchestrator will trust at dispatch. Separately, deterministic_task_guard._parse_metadata (48-60) maps an unparseable metadata string to {}, so validation passes vacuously AND inject_task_kind (236-238) then REPLACES the caller's entire metadata with {'task_kind':'normal'} — silent data loss with no warning (contrast _inject_routing_override, task_interceptor.py, which at least warns).
findings.proposal: Two enforcement moves: (1) extend the interceptor's update_task guard chain with _reject_kind_fields_in_update_metadata rejecting any metadata write that touches task_kind/before_done/always_escalates unless it passes deterministic_task_error() against the POST-merge blob (fetch-merge-validate under the existing write lock); (2) make submit_task fail loudly on unparseable metadata strings (ValidationError) instead of best-effort-{} — the interceptor already fails fast on non-serializable kwargs (task_interceptor.py), so this matches existing policy. Both collapse into the shared TaskMetadata schema (finding 1) if that lands first.
findings.title: Deterministic-task invariants enforced only at submit_task; update_task can violate them, and malformed metadata is silently discarded
findings.bug_history_link: Partially speculative for the update_task bypass (no incident yet); the silent-discard is the same class as the routing-override data-loss note, and the before_done validate-at-submit-only gap is adjacent to task 2105 (before_done.cwd never validated, detached self-restart 127 failures) and the 1962 deferred-filer pattern that exists precisely because before_done is only checked at submit time.
findings.verdict_notes: deterministic_task_error is still called only from tools.py submit_task (line ~8979). The update_task write path calls parse_metadata(direction='write', enforce=False), so it only logs a census and an update can still set task_kind or before_done. Fixed: inject_task_kind now warns when it discards unparseable metadata, and _parse_metadata_with_discard delegates to shared parse_metadata. TaskMetadata._deterministic_invariants exists but is not enforced on update.

findings.statement: At least six kinds of system records (stage1_flag_marker, stage1_flag_suppression, stage2_persistence_marker, flag_for_stage2, fixc markers, stage1/stage2 cycle_summary) are stored as Mem0 memories and used as a transactional dedup/lifecycle ledger. Mem0 offers no atomic replace, no read-after-write consistency, and silently drops similar writes, so flag_dedup.py's 241-line module docstring (flag_dedup.py) narrates seven stacked compensations: best-effort write-then-delete replacement (non-atomic, leaves transient duplicates), in-batch memoization for read-after-write lag (task-1978), post-write read-back confirmation with one retry (task-1400), a per-invocation confirmation circuit-breaker (task-1412), a limit=50 reclamation bound, and self-healing-on-next-cycle semantics. On the consumer side TaskKnowledgeSync.run() needs FOUR separate GC sweeps (_sweep_stale_fixc_markers task_knowledge_sync.py, _sweep_stale_flag_markers:1246, _sweep_terminal_task_flag_markers:1424, _sweep_stale_persistence_markers:1624), each added by a separate incident-driven task, because there is no TTL or status predicate on the store itself.
findings.proposal: Introduce ReconLedgerStore: a SQLite table (the codebase already runs transactional SQLite for the journal, write journal, and event buffer) with schema (project_id, record_kind, task_id, flag_type, run_id, payload_json, created_at, expires_at, state) and PRIMARY KEY on the identity tuple. Marker replacement becomes a single UPSERT transaction (kills the write/confirm/delete dance, the circuit breaker, and the in-batch memo); all four GC sweeps collapse to one 'DELETE WHERE expires_at < now OR referenced-task-terminal' pass; suppression lookup becomes an indexed query instead of a project-wide semantic search. Mem0 keeps only a best-effort human-searchable mirror of narrative content. flag_dedup.py shrinks to signature computation + ledger calls; the marker sections of task_knowledge_sync.py move into the ledger module (real seam: single-writer marker lifecycle).
findings.title: Recon control-plane state (markers, suppressions, counters, summaries) lives in Mem0, an eventually-consistent deduplicating vector store
findings.bug_history_link: Tasks 1097/1120/1121/1122/1128/1134/1146 (marker GC/None-metadata/atomicity re-fixes), 1144/1145 (Stage 1 snapshot/marker atomicity, still open at snapshot), 1944/f5e60b43cd and 2103 and 2095 (three separate new sweeps), 2047/16ce25d4c6 (fp: marker enrichment), 1786/5c77b2dbc6 (unique_groups IndexError), 2026-07-05 solar_challenge_platform 16-record manual bulk GC incident cited at task_knowledge_sync.py.
findings.verdict_notes: Stage1 flag markers moved to the SQLite recon_ledger (flag_dedup.py docstring, task 2227/2406). Mem0 still holds flag_for_stage2, suppression mirror and cycle summaries. Several GC sweeps remain (_sweep_stale_mem0_pool, _sweep_stale_persistence_markers, _sweep_stale_mem0_flag_markers, _sweep_stale_mem0_flag_for_stage2_markers), and flag_dedup.py is now 6021 lines.

findings.statement: Because MemoryService.add_memory silently dedups at ~0.92 cosine similarity, the stage prompts teach the LLM to prepend a Python-generated CSPRNG summary_nonce line and, on dedup-retry, to construct a deterministic retry_nonce (prompts/stage1.py, prompts/stage2.py; generate_summary_nonce cli_stage_runner.py). When the write is still swallowed, Python compensates post-hoc: _verify_stage2_summary_written (task_knowledge_sync.py) confirms via count_memories_by_metadata, _repair_stage2_summary_stage_metadata (:1890) re-adds identity metadata, and _reconstruct_stage2_summary (:2040) fabricates a placeholder record (run() wiring at :2629-2680). This is a genuine arms race: a prior nonce fix reused an already-embedded token and re-triggered the same 0.92 dedup it aimed to defeat (commit 2777f2b227). The upstream defect is that the memory service has no dedup-exempt write path for machine-generated, per-run records.
findings.proposal: Add a dedup-exempt system-write path in MemoryService — add_memory(..., dedup_exempt=True) or a dedicated add_system_record operation — permitted only for recon-stage agent_ids and enforced server-side (the interceptor already discriminates by agent_id in the write journal). Then delete: all summary_nonce/retry_nonce prompt directives, generate_summary_nonce/build_summary_nonce_section, and the entire verify->repair->reconstruct chain (three functions plus their run() wiring and four stats keys). Cycle summaries get written once, deterministically, by Python after the stage completes (content from the StageReport), removing the LLM from the reliability path entirely.
findings.title: Recon's own per-cycle writes are routed through the LLM-facing dedup pipeline, spawning the nonce arms race and a verify/repair/reconstruct chain
findings.bug_history_link: Nonce-hardening series tasks 1590/1796/1821 and commit 2777f2b227 (Stage 1 retry_nonce realignment); tasks 1963 (stage-metadata repair, 5e7b501c33/0e4b036974) and 1964 (fully-absent reconstruction, cbd4f1fc68/1254e1da3a) exist solely because dedup swallowed recon's own summary writes; confirmed incidents run 6467daca and 2026-07-01 cited in task_knowledge_sync.py.
findings.verdict_notes: The nonce and verify/repair/reconstruct chain was deleted by 3225a1094f (task 2229 step-10). Stage 2 now writes through reconciliation/summary_pool.py::write_cycle_summary. No summary_nonce, _verify_stage2_summary_written or _reconstruct_stage2_summary remains in source.

findings.statement: Both identifiers are plain str and travel side by side through dozens of signatures (e.g. targeted.py '_on_task_done(self, task_id: str, project_id: str, project_root: str, ...)', :622, :1143), so swapping them type-checks clean and fails only at runtime — the mined 10x bug class. Task 1143's registry hard-bind (_known_project_root_for, harness.py) fixed the harness entry point but not the mechanism: BaseStage defaults self.project_root to '' (stages/base.py) and relies on the harness remembering to inject it after construction (harness.py); downstream code then 'degrades to a no-op (0) when taskmaster or project_root is unset' (task_knowledge_sync.py) — a silent-skip failure mode for a forgotten injection. Every new call site re-creates the swap opportunity, which is why the fix chain (156, 186, 927, then 930/931/932/948/958/959/961/963) spanned weeks.
findings.proposal: Introduce a frozen dataclass ProjectScope(project_id: ProjectId, project_root: ProjectRoot) using typing.NewType for both fields, constructed in exactly one place — _known_project_root_for at cycle entry (which also asserts os.path.isabs) — and threaded as a single parameter through harness, stages, targeted.py, and the sweep/guard helpers. BaseStage takes scope as a required __init__ argument (delete the '' default and the post-construction attribute injection). Because pyright already gates every merge, any future project_id/project_root transposition at a new call site becomes a compile-time type error instead of a runtime cross-project contamination bug.
findings.title: project_id and project_root are interchangeable bare strs threaded through every signature, with mutable post-construction injection into stages
findings.bug_history_link: Tasks 156 ('targeted.py project_root fallback silently uses project_id as path'), 186 (task_knowledge_sync lines 46/99), 927 ('_fetch_filtered_task_tree receives project_id as fallback'), follow-ups 930/931/932/948/958/959/961/963, cancelled duplicate 880, and 1143 (registry hard-bind, the partial structural fix this completes).
findings.verdict_notes: models/scope.py defines ProjectId and ProjectRoot as NewTypes plus a frozen ProjectScope. targeted.py uses them. BaseStage.project_root is a read-only property over self.scope (stages/base.py), so the '' default and post-construction injection are gone.

findings.statement: The Stage 2 LLM holds unrestricted task-write tools (STAGE2_DISALLOWED blocks only built-ins, cli_stage_runner.py). Invariants like 'never update_task a terminal task', 'never write status to a task under a live workflow', and 'snapshot must be fresh at write time' are checked only AFTER the run by _apply_post_flight_guards (task_knowledge_sync.py), which re-fetches every touched task and reclassifies journal ops — _classify_terminal_state_violations (:283) admits 'the skip-the-write semantics cannot be enforced post-hoc (the LLM's write already landed), so this helper reclassifies the op instead'. Meanwhile the interceptor already enforces a server-side terminal FSM for set_task_status (terminal-exit gate task_interceptor.py, bulk-reset guard :685, done-provenance gate :744) but has no per-agent policy covering recon's update_task-on-terminal or live-workflow cases. The result: bad writes land, counters get corrected, and each newly discovered liveness signal (plan.lock, owner_pid, branch ancestry, deleted branch) became another incremental guard fix.
findings.proposal: Move enforcement to the single write boundary: a ReconWritePolicy consulted inside the interceptor's _apply_status_transition and update_task paths whenever agent_id starts with 'recon-stage-' — reject update_task when live status is in TERMINAL_STATUSES, reject status writes when services.live_workflow_detector.is_workflow_live_for_task is true, and require a payload-issued snapshot token whose staleness the server checks (replacing the post-hoc stall-guard freshness gate). Rejections return structured errors the LLM can read mid-run (like the existing DarkFactoryPathScopeViolation). _apply_post_flight_guards then shrinks from a ~650-line forensic suite to pure counter reconciliation, and the rejected-write class of stranded/terminal mutations becomes impossible rather than detected.
findings.title: Stage 2 write invariants are enforced post-hoc by journal forensics instead of at the interceptor write boundary
findings.bug_history_link: Task 1137 ('enforce terminal-state pre-check, stall-guard freshness gate' — the guard suite), task 1655/69dd6139d3 (Guard 5 live-workflow classifier), and the 9x stranded-in-progress hardening chain 886/911/912/913/916/1087/1092/1106/1114 where each new liveness edge case was patched into prompts+guards instead of the write path.
findings.verdict_notes: ReconWritePolicy (task 2224) is wired into middleware/task_interceptor.py update_task and set_task_status for recon-stage callers and rejects terminal-state and live-workflow writes pre-write. _apply_post_flight_guards no longer reclassifies them (its docstring says so). Landed via 6956850d68 and ca52625c43.

findings.statement: Stage agents self-report counts (memories_added, tasks_modified, flagged_count); reality is derived from the write journal. Three independent reconcilers exist: stats_verifier.py overwrites self-reported values via a hand-maintained _OP_TO_STAT map plus an alias map for names 'the LLM may emit' (stats_verifier.py — the alias map is itself a patch for prompt drift); _check_flag_counter_completeness and _check_mem0_flag_counter_completeness (task_knowledge_sync.py) audit flag counters separately; and the post-flight guards decrement tasks_modified when writes are reclassified (:2843-2847). Every counter not yet in the map is a latent drift bug, and the judge flags mismatches as run-quality problems, generating follow-up fix tasks.
findings.proposal: Invert the source of truth: report.stats is COMPUTED, not reported. Add one derivation function beside WriteJournal (derive_stage_stats(ops, stage_agent_id) -> dict) that produces every write-shaped counter from journal ops; StageReport.stats is populated exclusively from it, with the LLM's numbers preserved only under stats['_reported'] for the judge's divergence signal (the pattern stats_verifier already half-implements). Enforce with a stats-key allowlist in the report schema so a new counter cannot be introduced as an LLM-reported field. stats_verifier's alias map and both flag-counter completeness checkers die.
findings.title: LLM-authored counters are the primary stats channel, perpetually reconciled against journal-derived reality by three separate mechanisms
findings.bug_history_link: Tasks 1150 ('memories_written count' — the exact alias in _STAT_ALIASES), 1589/ee2dca83d1 (counter amendments), 5b820f3bcd (inc_stat prompt kwarg fix), and the open-at-snapshot Stage 1/2 correctness cluster item on counter completeness; root mechanism documented in stats_verifier.py (Mem0 silent dedup makes agents over-report).
findings.verdict_notes: The alias map and the _check_*flag_counter_completeness audits are gone, and the tasks_modified decrement is gone. One journal override remains (_apply_observed, with _reported kept for the judge). TaskKnowledgeSync._apply_post_flight_guards still repairs tasks_created upward from LLM-reported records.

findings.statement: Stage 2 can submit_task into any known project (prompts/stage2.py); the only gates are the curator ticket flow (dedup/combine — validates neither the finding's factual premise nor whether the work is executable by the TDD pipeline) and the path-scope guard (project routing only). The system's self-model — what markers mean, how fingerprint dedup anchors work, exact tool-call shapes — is hand-transcribed into prompt prose that provably drifts from code: stage2.py narrates _derive_affected_ids and compute_content_fingerprint internals to coax dedup-compatible behavior; commit a2327a65e1 fixed a system/user-prompt disagreement on count_memories_by_metadata arg shape; the false-premise cleanup batch 2083/2092/2093 was filed on a wrong model of stage1_flag_marker/run_id behavior that nothing could check. Filed tasks also carry no execution-class field, so operational live-data work is dispatched to the TDD architect pipeline that must refuse it.
findings.proposal: Two enforcement points. (a) Single-source the self-model: a recon_self_model.py module that exports the mechanism constants and invariants (marker kinds and their lifecycle, fingerprint identity fields, dedup thresholds, exact MCP call signatures) and RENDERS the prompt sections describing them — prompts import the rendered text instead of hand-duplicating it, so prompt/code drift becomes structurally impossible, and the same module exposes assertable predicates (e.g. 'run_id is fresh-per-run', 'markers are deleted only by sweeps X/Y') that a premise-lint can run against recon-authored task descriptions before filing. (b) Require metadata.execution_class in {code_tdd, operational, decision} on every recon-filed submit_task, validated at the curator (reject absent/unknown), with 'operational' routed to the recon escalation queue (port 8103 watcher) instead of the orchestrator's TDD dispatch — encoding the actionability contract the operator memory shows is missing.
findings.title: Recon files tasks with no machine-checkable premise or executability contract — the self-model lives only in drifting prompt prose
findings.bug_history_link: False-premise batch 2083/2092/2093 (filed on a wrong stage1_flag_marker model, unactionable-on-TDD, human abandon-closed); task 2085 (meta-fix for operational live-data tasks mis-routed to TDD, recurring class); commit a2327a65e1 (prompt/system drift on call shape); operator memory 'recon files tasks that are unactionable on the TDD pipeline'.
findings.verdict_notes: recon_self_model.py is now the single-source self-model with an execution_class contract and premise-lint. Stage 2 submissions can come back 'refused' from the premise registry. prompts/stage2.py renders sections from it, but still hand-narrates _derive_affected_ids and fingerprint internals. Partly mitigated.

findings.statement: UsageGate._transition is documented as the 'sole writer of AccountState.phase' and enforces _LEGAL_TRANSITIONS, but AccountState exposes four public setters (capped, probing, probe_in_flight, auth_failed) whose bodies assign self.phase directly, skipping the legality check, the generation bump, the _open recompute and the task start/cancel side effects. Production does not call them (only sc.capped on ScopeCap), but about 280 test lines across 12 files do, so the suite builds states the gate cannot legally reach and pins behaviour against them (Tests stance). acct.resets_at is a CAPPED/AUTH_FAILED-scoped field that _transition accepts as a parameter but does not store; it is written at three sites outside the transition (_handle_cap_detected, _run_probe's demotion arm, the SIGHUP reset inside _transition via force). The parameter name therefore lies (heuristic 1). Scoped caps (ScopeCap.capped/near_cap/resets_at/capped_at) are a second state machine with no transition table: _handle_cap_detected(scope=...) 'deliberately bypasses _transition', _refresh_scope_capped uncaps on a clock with no event, and the writes are 'not lock-protected'. Because the scoped branch takes no transition, the PROBE_IN_FLIGHT claim is not released by it, and release_probe_slot is therefore called separately in InvokeSlot.report (CapHit and NearCap arms and the else arm), InvokeSlot.detect_cap_hit, InvokeSlot.confirm via confirm_account_ok, and __aexit__. The set of releases was found one bug at a time (4096), and report() reaches the gate's private _handle_cap_detected, _handle_auth_failure, _handle_near_cap_warning and _fire_cost_event.
findings.proposal: Delete the four setters. AccountState exposes read-only properties, and tests seed a phase through one public test-support constructor (for example `UsageGate.seed_account_phase(name, phase)`, which goes through `_transition(force=True)`). Make _transition store `resets_at` (clear it on leaving CAPPED/AUTH_FAILED) and delete the three external writes. Give scoped caps one `_scope_transition(acct, scope, new_state, resets_at, reason)` writer with a small legal-edge table that owns the cap_hit/uncap event and the waiter wake. Add one public `UsageGate.apply_outcome(lease, scope, outcome)` that owns the handler dispatch and calls release_probe_slot once in a `finally`, so InvokeSlot.report is a one-line call and the six per-arm releases die. This would have prevented 4096, the esc-2128-2 raced-phase bug, the no-op auth-failure on a CAPPED account, and the fabricated-ETA class.
findings.title: AccountPhase is the sole phase writer only by convention: public boolean setters, resets_at writes and the scoped overlay all bypass _transition, and probe-slot release is scattered across six sites
findings.bug_history_link: 4096; esc-2128-2 (guard resume-probe success against raced-away phase); 'no-op _handle_auth_failure on an already-CAPPED account'; 'stop _handle_auth_failure fabricating a reset ETA'; 2857 (scope no-freeze wait robustness bound)
findings.verdict_notes: Re-observed this run as shared-infra.10 (equal key, contract §9); statement and proposal restated from this run's reviewer, skeptic verdict confirmed: AccountState has setters for capped, probing, probe_in_flight and auth_failed (lines 400-433) that assign self.phase directly, bypassing _transition. _transition (887) is documented as the 'Sole writer of AccountState.phase' and its resets_at parameter is not stored. acct.resets_at is written at 1863 and 2745 outside the transition (1010 is the reset case). Production sets only sc.capped (1730, 1849), on ScopeCap. The setters are used heavily in tests, with 291 assignments repo-wide that include the sc.capped ones. release_probe_slot has 16 references in the file. The scoped branch has no transition table. || Re-verification: AccountState now holds one AccountPhase enum (shared/usage_gate.py::AccountPhase) written only via UsageGate._transition, which owns the _open recompute. The capped/probing/etc booleans survive only as read-compat properties over phase. | Reviewer (shared-infra): UsageGate._transition is the sole phase writer in production, but AccountState keeps four public boolean setters that assign phase directly (about 280 test sites use them), resets_at is stored outside the transition at three sites, and scoped caps (ScopeCap) are a second table-less state machine that deliberately bypasses _transition. 'AccountPhase is the single authority' holds by convention, not by construction.

findings.statement: The decision 'what did this CLI invocation mean?' is duplicated with divergent rules: (1) UsageGate.detect_cap_hit — prefix + CAP_CONFIRM_KEYWORDS guard (usage_gate.py); (2) _run_probe — prefix-only, a deliberate asymmetry defended by a 20-line do-not-fix comment (usage_gate.py); (3) invoke_with_cap_retry — its own 401/403 auth routing (cli_invoke.py), zero-output wedge guard (842), zero-cost heuristic cap detector plus NON_CAP_CLI_ERROR_MARKERS exclusion table (905-964, 120-132); (4) _parse_claude_output — is_error/subtype/salvage semantics (1141-1248); (5) classify_agent_failure — a parallel AgentFailureKind taxonomy for the steward (453-538). Because the InvokeSlot abstraction only auto-settles on detect_cap_hit/confirm, the retry loop must call gate privates usage_gate._handle_auth_failure (cli_invoke.py) and usage_gate._handle_cap_detected (cli_invoke.py) and remember slot.settle() — exactly the seam where the 4x probe-slot-leak fixes landed. Each new CLI wording or error shape must be patched into 2-3 of these tables independently.
findings.proposal: Create shared/src/shared/invocation_outcome.py with a sum type `InvocationOutcome = OK | CapHit(resets_at, reason) | NearCap(reason) | AuthFailed(status) | CliLocalError(marker) | ZeroOutputWedge | Failure(kind)` and one classifier `classify_invocation(result: AgentResult, *, strict_confirm: bool, backend: str) -> InvocationOutcome` holding ALL string tables (CAP_HIT_PREFIXES, CAP_CONFIRM_KEYWORDS, NON_CAP_CLI_ERROR_MARKERS, CODEX/GEMINI patterns) adjacent, with the probe's prefix-only policy expressed as strict_confirm=False instead of a separate loop. Replace the private reach-ins with one public `InvokeSlot.report(outcome)` that performs the matching gate transition AND settles the slot atomically — making 'slot settled iff gate informed' an enforced invariant rather than caller discipline. classify_agent_failure becomes a projection of InvocationOutcome.
findings.title: Invocation-outcome classification is computed in five places with different rules; cli_invoke reaches into UsageGate privates to apply its verdicts
findings.bug_history_link: 10x cap-message whack-a-mole (ba38ce4ee1, b88b4625d5, e3df395c9f revert cycle, 77d1d18c49, b5f6b04ac1 — the probe path lacked a demotion the retry path had); 4x probe-slot leaks fixed per-call-site (065e95a4c9, feb22158da, 3a341db462, 75047c16bc); 734932b8bf 'gate heuristic cap-retry on _handle_cap_detected return'; 7d1fa90075 / reify-3604 'don't treat CLI errors as caps' infinite loop.
findings.verdict_notes: Classification is now consolidated in classify_invocation. cli_invoke calls it, and the slot applies verdicts via InvokeSlot.report. The steward copy is gone. No gate-private calls remain in cli_invoke. Residue: classify_agent_failure remains a separate taxonomy, the probe path has its own asymmetry, and the invocation_outcome/cap_markers string tables are still partly duplicated.

findings.statement: steward._invoke_steward (steward.py) reimplements the invoke_slot/detect_cap_hit/resume-on-next-account loop and has diverged from the canonical invoke_with_cap_retry on every policy axis: fixed 5s cooldown vs exponential backoff; bounded _MAX_CAP_RETRIES then RuntimeError vs 14-day patient wait + AllAccountsCappedException; no 401/403 auth-failure routing; no zero-output wedge guard (a wedged steward session gets re-resumed forever); no zero-cost heuristic cap detection; no NON_CAP_CLI_ERROR_MARKERS exclusion. The fix history shows the same defect class being patched independently in both copies — the definition of a defect-generating structure.
findings.proposal: Delete the steward loop and route it through invoke_with_cap_retry, extending the shared function with the two hooks the steward actually needs: (a) an optional `rebuild_prompt: Callable[[bool session_lost], Awaitable[str]]` invoked on cap-retry when the session cannot be resumed (steward rebuilds its initial prompt with fresh pending escalations), and (b) an optional `max_cap_retries: int | None` bound for callers that must not wait 14 days. Steward keeps only session-id bookkeeping. Same treatment for any future caller tempted to hand-roll (grep gate.invoke_slot outside cli_invoke: steward is the only remaining one).
findings.title: Steward hand-rolls a second cap-retry loop that has already drifted from invoke_with_cap_retry
findings.bug_history_link: Task 729 'Prevent probe_in_flight leak on exceptions in invoke_with_cap_retry AND steward' (same leak, two copies), tasks 805/806 'missing usage_gate cleanup in steward _pre_triage_suggestions', 3a341db462 'release probe slot when invoke_agent raises in _invoke_with_session'.
findings.verdict_notes: Steward now calls the shared invoke_with_cap_retry (orchestrator/steward.py, around line 880 and 1002). The hand-rolled loop and its divergent policy are removed.

findings.statement: before_invoke selects an account with the predicate `not (capped or probe_in_flight or auth_failed)` (usage_gate.py) but returns only the bare token. InvokeSlot.__init__ then re-derives the name via gate.active_account_name (usage_gate.py), whose predicate omits probe_in_flight (1137-1139). Concrete failure: account[0] is PROBE_IN_FLIGHT (claimed by another task), a second caller is handed account[1]'s token, yet its slot.account_name — used for cost_store.save_invocation and failover logs at cli_invoke.py/863/979-998 — reports account[0]. The same identity-by-token-string pattern (_find_account_by_token, _resolve_account fallback) already produced misattribution bugs. All attribution downstream (dashboard per-account cost, cap_hit events) inherits the error.
findings.proposal: Make before_invoke return the selected AccountState (or an immutable AccountLease dataclass with name+token+generation) instead of a raw token; InvokeSlot carries the lease, and every gate mutation path takes the lease rather than doing token-equality resolution (_resolve_account/_find_account_by_token become fallbacks for token-only external callers only). Delete the active_account_name re-derivation in the invoke path. This makes 'the account you report on is the account you invoked with' a type-level invariant.
findings.title: Account identity re-derived by a predicate that disagrees with the selection predicate — cost/log attribution can name the wrong account
findings.bug_history_link: 18c6a6c393 '_resolve_account: return None for explicit unknown tokens (no fallback)' fixed the same misattribution class; 4359d3f35c 'correct cap-status logic' and 0bd57513d9 'capture probe_count before reset in cost-event label' are attribution-drift siblings. The probe_in_flight name-skew itself is unfixed today (speculative as a shipped incident, confirmed in code).
findings.verdict_notes: InvokeSlot.account_name now comes from the lease (shared/usage_gate.py::InvokeSlot.account_name), the same lease the token comes from, so it cannot name a different account. The docstring cites this exact bug. active_account_name still omits probe_in_flight but no longer drives attribution.

findings.statement: The upstream Claude CLI provides no machine-readable rate-limit status in its JSON envelope, so this layer compensates by scraping wording: CAP_HIT_PREFIXES/CAP_CONFIRM_KEYWORDS (usage_gate.py) chase verbatim marketing copy ('You're now using extra…'); _parse_resets_at (usage_gate.py) regex-parses 'resets Mar 30, 6pm (Europe/London)' and SILENTLY falls back to now+1h on any parse failure — that fabricated time then drives probe scheduling, soonest_resets_at, and dashboard ETAs; the zero-cost heuristic (cli_invoke.py) exists because pattern matching is known-incomplete, and NON_CAP_CLI_ERROR_MARKERS exists because the heuristic over-fires. Every CLI wording change lands as another fix commit; misfires loop forever (reify-3604) or silently return junk success.
findings.proposal: Invert the precedence and make prose-matching a monitored fallback: (1) primary classification from structured fields already parsed into AgentResult — is_error, subtype, api_error_status==429, returncode — extending _parse_claude_output to surface any rate-limit metadata the CLI exposes; (2) when ONLY the prose matcher fires (no structured corroboration) or _parse_resets_at hits its 1h fallback, emit a distinct loud cost-store event ('cap_prose_only' / 'resets_parse_failed') and persist the raw unmatched text, so a wording change surfaces as one alert instead of a silent retry storm followed by a whack-a-mole commit; (3) pin a contract test that runs the real CLI's cap fixture set per CLI version bump (e3df395c9f already added credential integration tests — extend into a versioned fixture corpus). This doesn't eliminate the upstream gap (it can't) but converts an unbounded arms race into a bounded, observable fallback.
findings.title: Cap/reset signal scraped from human-facing CLI prose with silent fallbacks — the structural driver of the string-matching arms race
findings.bug_history_link: 10x whack-a-mole theme: ba38ce4ee1, b88b4625d5, e3df395c9f (reverting an earlier addition), 77d1d18c49, 1e8a9b2dd0 'respect is_error field', 66daedbc76 documenting verbatim messages; e71c833354 centralised reset-time parsing after dashboard drift; operator memory 'usage_gate account-pool weekly cap 2026-07-03'.
findings.verdict_notes: Prose scraping persists: CAP_HIT_PREFIXES, NEAR_CAP_PREFIXES and the CAP_CONFIRM_KEYWORDS table. The fabricating reset-time parser fork was removed (dc33622bda, 174f267a17), and a missing probe time is now explicit (usage_gate.py::UsageGate._account_resume_probe_loop still defaults to 1h, with a warning).

findings.statement: Roughly 6 orchestrator processes plus fused-memory's curator/reconciliation runners each construct an independent UsageGate over the SAME account pool, with no shared state: check_at_startup is an explicit no-op (usage_gate.py), so each process re-discovers each cap by burning a real, mid-task agent invocation, and each runs its own resume-probe loop (N processes × M capped accounts haiku probes). Worse, every gate builds TaskConfigDir('usage-gate-probe') (usage_gate.py) which resolves to the FIXED path /tmp/claude-config-usage-gate-probe (config_dir.py) — all processes' probes, and the SIGHUP parallel all-account probe gather (usage_gate.py), concurrently rewrite the same .credentials.json with different tokens (usage_gate.py). Probe correctness silently depends on CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN env precedence over the racing credentials file — an assumption asserted nowhere; if the CLI ever prefers or writes back to the config-dir credential, probes test/attribute the wrong account fleet-wide.
findings.proposal: Two steps. Cheap now: make the probe config dir unique per account+process (TaskConfigDir(f'usage-gate-probe-{acct.name}-{os.getpid()}')) and add a comment-level assertion/regression test that env token wins over config-dir credentials. Systemic: add an `account_status` table to the existing shared CostStore SQLite (capped_until, auth_failed_at, updated_by), written through the F1 transition function; before_invoke consults it so a cap discovered by one process is honored by all, and a single-prober election (shared.locking file lock keyed by account) makes exactly one process run the resume probe per capped account, publishing the uncap.
findings.title: Host-wide shared 6-account pool with per-process in-memory cap state and a shared mutable probe credentials file
findings.bug_history_link: Operator memory 'usage_gate account-pool weekly cap 2026-07-03' (fleet-wide 429 triage pain); 49b3858f6f 'per-task config dir, fresh probes, and admission control' fixed the sibling per-task credential race but left the probe dir shared. The concurrent-probe credential race itself is speculative (no confirmed incident), the N× rediscovery cost is confirmed by design.
findings.verdict_notes: Probe config dirs are now per-(account,pid) with atexit cleanup and a stale-dir sweep (UsageGate.__init__), so the shared-credentials race is gone. Cap state is still per-process in memory and check_at_startup is still a no-op, so N-process cap rediscovery remains.

findings.statement: _execute_graphiti_write (memory_service.py) chains four independent best-effort post-hoc passes after every add_episode: _dedup_episode_edges (line 484), _restore_superseded_dependency_edges (612), _dedup_episode_nodes (531), _normalize_task_node_names (687). Each is a near-identical copy of the same shape (extract touched names/edges from the just-returned result, look them up again via find_duplicate_entity_nodes, best-effort merge with except Exception: log and continue). The _dedup_episode_nodes docstring states the root cause: graphiti_core's ingestion-time entity resolution only resolves each extracted node against hybrid embedding+BM25 candidates -- there is no guaranteed exact-name Cypher lookup. No FalkorDB uniqueness constraint on Entity.name exists (build_indices_and_constraints at graphiti_client.py is stubbed to a no-op for the multi-tenant driver). Because each sweep only re-scans names/uuids touched by the episode that just completed, a duplicate created across two unrelated episodes, or by a concurrent sibling worker if workers_per_group is ever raised above 1, is invisible to all four sweeps and survives until a human manually merges it in FalkorDB.
findings.proposal: Enforce node identity at creation time, not after the fact: add a single _resolve_or_create_entity(name, group_id) chokepoint in GraphitiBackend that does an exact-name Cypher lookup (get_nodes_by_exact_name, already implemented at graphiti_client.py) BEFORE minting a new node, guarded by a FalkorDB uniqueness constraint on (group_id, Entity.name) or a per-group_id asyncio.Lock serializing the check-then-create window. Retire or fold the four reactive sweeps into one _reconcile_episode_identity(result, group_id) helper once the write-time gate exists, since they would then only catch pre-existing legacy duplicates rather than being the sole defense.
findings.title: No write-time identity guarantee for entity nodes -> 4-function reactive sweep chain
findings.bug_history_link: tasks 429,433,438,441,442,446,447,459,461,465,484,487,490,491,494,504,511,513,514,516,517,526,549,656,657,719,754,772,818,820 (rebuild/refresh churn) plus 2110/2084 (task-node-name canonicalization, edge dedup) and operator-memory-documented duplicate-Graphiti-node manual FalkorDB merges
findings.verdict_notes: The post-hoc sweeps remain and have grown to nine passes, folded into _reconcile_episode_identity. Each pass still runs best-effort and touches only the names the just-finished episode touched. _execute_graphiti_write now holds a per-group _identity_lock_for, which closes the concurrent-sibling race. The docstring claims a write-time guarantee, yet no uniqueness constraint was added, so a duplicate created across two unrelated episodes is still not caught.

findings.statement: redirect_node_edges (lines 897-903, 934-940) copies new.uuid = old.uuid when redirecting an edge onto the surviving node during a merge -- it deliberately mints a second graph relationship element carrying an already-used uuid. Edge.uuid can therefore no longer be treated as unique across the graph, so every edge-reading query must defend against it: get_valid_edges_for_node (720-730) and get_all_valid_edges (799-811) both carry multi-paragraph comments explaining why they must 'WITH DISTINCT e' / 'WITH DISTINCT n, e' (graph-element identity) instead of deduping by the (uuid, fact, name) property tuple, explicitly because redirect_node_edges copies uuids. Two prior commits (cfed95c706 removing a misplaced/wrong DISTINCT, and task-2084 pair be71e7850a/c3193549a7 adding correct DISTINCT) show this has already been gotten wrong twice in production.
findings.proposal: Stop copying old.uuid in redirect_node_edges; mint a fresh uuid for the redirected edge and carry superseded_edge_uuid=old.uuid as an audit property instead. That restores 'uuid is unique per edge' as a graph-wide invariant, lets every current and future edge query use a plain uuid-keyed dedup instead of the fragile hand-written WITH DISTINCT idiom, and removes the class of bug that produced cfed95c706 / be71e7850a / c3193549a7.
findings.title: merge_entities' redirect_node_edges deliberately breaks edge-uuid uniqueness, forcing every edge-read query to hand-roll graph-element dedup
findings.bug_history_link: cfed95c706 'remove misplaced DISTINCT in get_all_valid_edges', be71e7850a 'get_valid_edges_for_node dedupes by edge identity' (task 2084 step-2), c3193549a7 'get_all_valid_edges dedupes by (entity, edge) identity' (task 2084 step-4)
findings.verdict_notes: GraphitiBackend.redirect_node_edges in backends/graphiti_client.py now sets new.uuid = $new_uuid, a fresh uuid4 per redirected edge. It keeps the old uuid in superseded_edge_uuid. Commits 991ea73c39 (outgoing) and 5101698b6a (incoming) did this. The uuid-preserving cypher that remains (edge reassign, MENTIONS move) deletes the old relationship, so uuids stay unique.

findings.statement: The mined theme (8 fix commits: 484, 512, 516, 647, 191/192, 519, 1151) shows CancelledError-swallowing across gather sites was a recurring bug class. propagate_cancellations (utils/async_utils.py) now correctly centralizes Pass-1 (re-raise structured cancellation before any per-item logging), but Pass-2 ('log every Exception, then raise/accumulate the first one') is still copy-pasted by hand at every call site with slightly different wording and behaviour (get_entity's two branches raise the first exception outright; rebuild_entity_summaries instead accumulates a per-entity error status and keeps going). Each new gather call site is a fresh chance to forget to call propagate_cancellations at all, or to get the exception-vs-continue policy wrong for that call site.
findings.proposal: Extend fused_memory.utils.async_utils with two named helpers built on propagate_cancellations: gather_or_raise(coros) (Pass1 + raise-first, for get_entity-style call sites that must fail the whole read on any error) and gather_collect(coros) (Pass1 + per-item Exception/success tuple, for rebuild_entity_summaries-style call sites that tolerate partial failure). Migrate all current call sites onto these, so the cancellation-safety contract is enforced by one tested function rather than re-derived at each new gather() site.
findings.title: asyncio.gather cancellation-then-first-exception pattern duplicated at several call sites; only the cancellation check was extracted, not the whole idiom
findings.bug_history_link: tasks 484,512,516,647,191,192,519,1151 (asyncio.gather/CancelledError swallow fixes across memory backends, context_assembler, burndown, get_entity)
findings.verdict_notes: utils/async_utils.py now has gather_or_raise (commit d3ba80d41a) and gather_collect, which wrap both passes: cancellation propagation, then log every exception and raise or collect. The call sites in memory_service.py (get_entity, rebuild_entity_summaries) and graphiti_client.py (~4668) use these helpers. The hand-copied Pass-2 idiom is gone.

findings.statement: 42 of the ~47 exception-catching @mcp.tool() functions in this file follow the convention 'except (asyncio.CancelledError, KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit): raise' immediately before a broader 'except Exception as e:' handler that converts errors into error-dict responses -- the same pattern the mined CancelledError fix theme addressed elsewhere (tasks 484/512/516/647/191/192/519). But the convention exists only as a repeated hand-written idiom with no shared decorator or lint rule enforcing it: submit_task, resolve_ticket, list_tickets, and cancel_ticket (task/ticket-routing tools in the same file) catch bare except Exception with no cancellation guard, so a cancellation delivered while these coroutines await task_interceptor.* gets silently converted into a normal error-dict response instead of propagating.
findings.proposal: Introduce an mcp_tool_errors(operation=...) decorator in tools.py that wraps the handler body, re-raises (CancelledError, KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit), and converts any other Exception to the standard error dict with logging -- then apply it uniformly to all @mcp.tool() functions, removing the 42 hand-copies and closing the 4 gaps so the invariant is structural rather than a convention that can silently regress per-function.
findings.title: The CancelledError re-raise convention used by most MCP tool handlers in tools.py is unenforced and already regressed in 4 task-routing handlers
findings.bug_history_link: tasks 484,512,516,647,191,192,519 (same CancelledError-swallow class, different subsystem instances) -- the 4 gaps in tools.py are a fresh, previously-unfixed instance of the same class
findings.verdict_notes: server/tool_errors.py::mcp_tool_errors (b28fc6eeca) is a shared decorator holding the cancellation guard and the error dict. It is applied across server/tools.py, including submit_task, resolve_ticket, list_tickets and cancel_ticket. All four now re-raise cancellation. The convention is now enforced uniformly by that one mechanism.

findings.statement: _CYCLE_SUMMARY_STAGE_TO_RECON_POOL (memory_service.py) is documented as an intentional duplicate of _STAGE1_CYCLE_SUMMARY_RECON_POOL/_STAGE2_CYCLE_SUMMARY_RECON_POOL in reconciliation/stages/*.py, kept in sync only by a drift-guard test, because importing the canonical constants directly would create a circular import. This is real duplicated business logic (which recon_pool a cycle_summary write lands in) that two independently-evolving modules must keep manually synchronized; a missed update to either side silently breaks pool-cap trimming and the ops prune script rather than failing loudly.
findings.proposal: Extract the stage->pool map into a leaf module with no dependents in either direction (e.g. fused_memory.reconciliation.recon_pool_map) that both memory_service.py and reconciliation/stages/*.py import, eliminating the circular-import constraint that currently forces duplication; keep the existing drift-guard test as a regression check during the migration.
findings.title: Duplicated canonical stage->recon_pool constant map creates a drift-prone cross-module contract (mitigated but not removed)
findings.bug_history_link: speculative -- mitigated in task 2077 with a drift-guard test and explicit documentation, but the duplication itself remains a live cross-module coupling
findings.verdict_notes: Task 2140 (942a547ac0) extracted the stage-to-pool map into the leaf module reconciliation/recon_pool_map.py. memory_service.py imports CYCLE_SUMMARY_STAGE_TO_RECON_POOL from there, and stages/memory_consolidator.py imports STAGE1_CYCLE_SUMMARY_RECON_POOL from it. The duplicate is gone.

findings.statement: RESOLVE_ACTIONS (server.py, resolve_issue at 506-629) is validated as a bare string enum with no notion of which record states (level, category, whether a live workflow owns the task, whether the task is 'blocked' vs something else) each action is legal for. queue.resolve()/park() only check status=='pending' (queue.py) — level, category, and current task status are invisible to them. The actual per-action effect on the task/workflow is reconstructed independently in harness.py's _on_escalation_resolved (7958-8085) and _cascade_unblock_member (8428-8511): 'resume' only flips blocked→pending if escalation.level>=1 AND (is_l2_cascade OR task_id not already tracked by a live workflow) AND the task's CURRENT status is literally 'blocked' — any other current status causes a DEBUG-level silent no-op with no error surfaced to the caller of resolve_issue. This is the exact shape of the documented stranded_blocked resume bug (operator memory: 'resume on stranded_blocked leaves task in-progress, not pending' / feedback_stranded_blocked_resume_leaves_in_progress.md, esc-2073-15).
findings.proposal: Introduce one authoritative transition table — e.g. escalation/src/escalation/state_machine.py exporting LEGAL_TRANSITIONS: dict[(action, level, category), TaskEffect] — imported by BOTH resolve_issue (to reject illegal action/state combos with a loud {'error':...,'code':'illegal_transition'} instead of silently mutating the record) and by harness.py's callback (to compute the task effect, replacing the ad hoc if/elif chain). Any precondition failure (task not in the expected pre-state) should raise/return a typed rejection surfaced to the resolver, not a DEBUG log the human never sees. This directly targets the recurring class the escalation-repend-state-machine-prd.md (D1-D11) tried to solve but which regressed once task 1883 added a new branch outside that design.
findings.title: resolve_issue action semantics live in two files with no shared state-machine table, and preconditions fail silently
findings.bug_history_link: feedback_stranded_blocked_resume_leaves_in_progress.md (esc-2073-15, 2026-07-04); plans/escalation-repend-state-machine-prd.md (D1-D11, authored 2026-06-04) documents the same defect class this was meant to close
findings.verdict_notes: Table B (action_effects.py::ACTION_EFFECTS) is now the single legality authority and resolve_issue rejects unknown actions loudly (illegal_transition). Level/category still never narrow legality (all wildcards). Harness resume keyed on claimant liveness, not status=='blocked' (Harness._cascade_unblock_member). queue.resolve/park still check only pending. Original shape much mitigated.

findings.statement: resolve_issue's level_forbidden check (server.py) only fires when the caller's transport happens to set the X-Escalation-Levels header; the function's own docstring/comments admit get_http_headers() returns {} for in-process tool.fn() calls and stdio transport, so the gate is a no-op for those callers ('default-open is preserved byte-for-byte'). The only caller that ever sends the header is the orchestrator's own auto-watcher, via the hardcoded _WATCHER_ESCALATION_HEADERS = {'X-Escalation-Levels': '0,1'} dict in harness.py. Any other MCP client (a differently-configured watcher, a buggy script, an interactive session that reuses agent_role='escalation-watcher-auto') can call resolve_issue(action='close_only'|'abandon', ...) on an L2 record with zero restriction, because the restriction is self-declared by the caller rather than derived from caller identity server-side.
findings.proposal: Move the level-gate from 'does the caller declare a restriction' to 'does the caller prove a capability': mint a signed/opaque capability token per connection type at MCP-session-establishment time (or at minimum require the identity header — already present as X-Escalation-Identity — to resolve to a role→allowed-levels mapping maintained server-side, e.g. a small ROLE_LEVEL_ALLOWLIST in server.py) so omitting the levels header defaults to the caller's role-derived ceiling rather than 'no restriction'. This closes the same hole that produced the L1→L2 overstep incident, but for the general case rather than just the one watcher client that was patched.
findings.title: Level-based capability gate (level_forbidden) is an HTTP-header opt-in, not a server-enforced authorization boundary
findings.bug_history_link: project_escalation_watcher_L2_is_orchestrator_autowatcher_2026_07_03.md — PRD 18d2a490e9 (df 2041-2044) added level_forbidden specifically for the auto-watcher's own header; this finding shows the same gap remains open for any other caller
findings.verdict_notes: Identity-derived server-side ceiling added (authority.py::ROLE_LEVEL_ALLOWLIST); header may only narrow. But identified callers only: header-less/in-process callers remain default-open by design (server.py::create_server resolve_issue comment), so the gap persists for unidentified callers.

findings.statement: promote_to_l2 (server.py) explicitly bypasses the terminal-task chokepoint and the severity→level dedupe gate, minting a level=2 human-facing record directly via queue.submit()/add_members_to_l2(). Its docstring says 'this tool is for the auto-watcher' but agent_role is an unchecked free-form string parameter — nothing server-side restricts which callers may invoke it. Given the entire point of the L0→L1→L2 ladder is to gate access to the scarce human-attention channel, the RESOLVE side now has (a leaky, see finding 2) level check, but the CREATE side that mints new L2s has none at all.
findings.proposal: Reuse the same role→allowed-levels mapping proposed in finding 2 to gate promote_to_l2 symmetrically with resolve_issue: require the caller's declared/derived identity to be in an allowlist (e.g. {'escalation-watcher-auto', 'operator'}) before minting level=2, returning {'error':..., 'code':'level_forbidden'} otherwise. This is the missing half of the L1→L2 overstep fix — closing the write path, not just the resolve path.
findings.title: promote_to_l2 has no capability/role check on its create side
findings.bug_history_link: companion gap to project_escalation_watcher_L2_is_orchestrator_autowatcher_2026_07_03.md; no direct incident yet observed — speculative but structurally identical to the resolved incident
findings.verdict_notes: promote_to_l2 now checks X-Escalation-Identity against PROMOTE_ALLOWED and returns level_forbidden, plus sentinel-bound and eval-lane refusals. Header-less callers remain unrestricted, so partially mitigated only.

findings.statement: _cascade_unblock_member (harness.py, task 1883 step-16) writes status='in-progress' for a stranded_blocked task carrying metadata.infra_hold, meaning something categorically different from the normal 'a live coroutine currently owns this task' meaning of in-progress — there is no live claimant started by this write. The ONLY thing that keeps this row from being permanently invisible to recovery is that _revert_in_progress_if_no_live_claimant (harness.py, also task 1883 step-14) independently re-checks the same metadata.infra_hold flag and skips the row while it's set. The invariant 'in-progress rows without infra_hold are eventually reconciled by plan.lock liveness; rows with infra_hold are deliberately exempt' is enforced by two hand-written flag checks in two different functions with no shared type or single-source-of-truth — a future caller that sets metadata.infra_hold without knowing about _revert_in_progress_if_no_live_claimant's guard (or vice versa) silently produces a permanently-orphaned in-progress task.
findings.proposal: Replace the metadata.infra_hold boolean with an explicit sub-status on TaskStatus (e.g. a real 'in-progress-hold-infra' state, or a typed `InProgressReason` enum stored once and read by both call sites via a single accessor function `is_infra_held(task) -> bool` in one module) so the exemption is expressed once and any new consumer of 'in-progress' is forced to go through it rather than re-deriving the flag check.
findings.title: 'in-progress' status is overloaded with a second, ad hoc meaning (infra_hold) that must be tracked identically in two separate reconciliation call sites
findings.bug_history_link: git log -S infra_hold: fccdbfd0a8 / d775e4e916 (task 1883, itself a workaround for the '3465 starvation' dispatch-footprint-lock defect); speculative that this has caused a second incident beyond esc-2073-15, but the structural gap is confirmed in code
findings.verdict_notes: The metadata.infra_hold boolean was retired (task 2200). Infra hold is now a distinct status read via orchestrator/src/orchestrator/task_status.py::is_infra_held, so the two hand-written flag checks and the overloaded in-progress meaning are gone. Only legacy-migration comments remain in harness.py.

findings.statement: make_id() (queue.py) derives the next sequence number by globbing the queue root fresh every call, combined with a per-task_id _archive_max_seq_cache that is explicitly documented as 'correct only for the single-writer model... a concurrent process archiving an escalation for a task_id whose entry is already seeded in this instance's cache will not reflect that higher seq'. get_by_task (queue.py) similarly reconstructs correctness via a manual cross-tier pre-scan + seen-set dedup rather than a single lookup. This is the area with the densest fix history in the mined themes (4x get_by_task dedup-before-filter fixes across duplicate tasks 999/1000/1001/1002; 6x archive/ID-collision hardening commits including 28feb9cd1e, baa7f96f0a/task 1879, 9cf4dd3b42/task 1324, 4c407593ff) — each round patched a specific manifestation (TOCTOU race, filter ordering, cache staleness) without removing the underlying re-derive-from-directory-scan design.
findings.proposal: Replace directory-scan-derived sequencing with a single durable counter file per task_id (fsync'd increment under the existing escalation_id_lock sidecar mechanism) as the sole source of the next sequence number, eliminating both the archive-scan cache-staleness class and the get_by_task cross-tier dedup class in one move — the lock primitive to do this safely already exists and is well-tested (escalation_id_lock, queue.py).
