findings.title: Escalation ID uniqueness is reconstructed by re-scanning two directory tiers plus a per-instance cache, rather than a single authoritative counter
findings.bug_history_link: tasks 999/1000 (duplicate), 1001/1002 (duplicate follow-up), 1879 (baa7f96f0a), 1324 (9cf4dd3b42), 28feb9cd1e, 4c407593ff — 6+ discrete fix commits against the same design
findings.verdict_notes: EscalationQueue.make_id now uses a durable per-key esc-{key}.seq counter; the _archive_max_seq_cache is retired, disk scan only when counter absent. get_by_task still does two-tier scan with a cross-tier pre-scan, seen-set dedup and vanished-record recovery, so that half remains.

findings.statement: Six alternating commits (46d8aaec0b → ad76ac658f → 3545e5edfa → 50321469bd → 3e73e109ab) toggled server.py between datetime.UTC and timezone.utc, twice justified by 'Python <3.11 compat'. escalation/pyproject.toml pins requires-python = '>=3.11,<4' and selects ruff rule 'UP' (which includes UP017, the rule that mandates datetime.UTC once py311 is the floor) — so the compat rationale was factually false both times it was asserted, and nothing in the fix workflow checked the stated premise (requires-python) before committing a revert.
findings.proposal: No code fix needed beyond settling on datetime.UTC (already the current state); the systemic fix is procedural: fix-agents touching lint/typing churn should be required to grep the target package's requires-python / ruff target-version before asserting a version-compat rationale in a commit message, or CI should simply trust ruff's own UP017 finding as authoritative (it already knows the configured target-version) rather than allowing a manual override commit to fight the linter. Low-value to build tooling for a 6-commit churn, but worth a one-line convention note (e.g. in escalation's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md or the verify skill) telling fix-agents to trust `ruff check` over ad hoc compat claims.
findings.title: datetime.UTC vs timezone.utc flip-flopped 6x on a false 'Python <3.11 compat' premise never checked against pyproject
findings.bug_history_link: 46d8aaec0b, ad76ac658f, 3545e5edfa, 50321469bd, 3e73e109ab — mined theme '[6x] Timezone/UP017 datetime.UTC alias flip-flopping'
findings.verdict_notes: escalation/src/escalation/server.py now imports UTC from datetime and has no timezone.utc; the flip-flop is settled and consistent with requires-python >=3.11 in escalation/pyproject.toml. Specific removing commit not identified.

findings.statement: merge_queue.py hardcodes two overlapping outcome allowlists — _CANONICAL_OUTCOMES (4 values) and _TERMINAL_MERGE_OUTCOMES (8 values, frozen at merge_queue.py) — used by outcome_distribution and, critically, by active_queued_merges (line 783: `if et == 'merge_attempt' and outcome in _TERMINAL_MERGE_OUTCOMES: continue`) to decide whether a task is still 'in_flight'. But orchestrator's _emit_merge_attempt is called with at least 18 distinct free-form strings across orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py ('main_health_red', 'merge_failed', 'verify_failed', 'advance_failed', 'train_incomplete', 'train_rebase_conflict', 'train_partial_flip', 'cas_failed', 'cas_retry', 'gate_retry', plus the 8 already covered) — there is no shared enum; MergeOutcome.status in merge_types.py is a Literal with yet a THIRD, different set of values ('wip_halted', 'done_wip_recovery', 'unmerged_state', 'superseded', 'error' — none of which appear in either dashboard set or in the _emit_merge_attempt string set, since outcome and MergeOutcome.status are different fields entirely).
findings.proposal: Promote the merge-attempt outcome to a real closed type owned by orchestrator (e.g. an `OutcomeKind` StrEnum in merge_types.py with an explicit `is_terminal` classmethod/property), have _emit_merge_attempt accept only that enum, and have dashboard import the enum (or a small shared `orchestrator.merge_types` re-export) instead of hand-maintaining two divergent string lists. If a hard import dependency is undesirable, invert the default: classify outcomes as terminal-unless-listed (an explicit ACTIVE_ONLY allowlist for retry states like cas_retry/gate_retry) since new terminal outcomes are added far more often than new active ones, so drift fails safe instead of failing stale.
findings.title: Merge-outcome vocabulary silently drifted from orchestrator's actual (unenumerated) outcome strings
findings.bug_history_link: _TERMINAL_MERGE_OUTCOMES was defined once in 8553b388ad (~2 months ago) and never touched again per `git log -S`, while orchestrator kept adding outcome strings after that point (88473b9e73 6wk ago, 8fba07f70d 4wk ago, c1869a71a5 2d ago) — confirmed by git -S searches on both files.
findings.verdict_notes: _TERMINAL_MERGE_OUTCOMES/_CANONICAL_OUTCOMES gone from dashboard/data/merge_queue.py. MergeAttempts.outcomes now counts every recorded outcome string (Counter) and active_queued_merges was inverted to terminal-unless-listed (776d4d433c). No hardcoded allowlist to drift.

findings.statement: merge_queue.py's aggregate/timeseries functions all accept an explicit `now` parameter and resolve `effective_now` once, threaded through every per-DB call in asyncio.gather (fixed by commit 0020b1d0ac / task 692, which explicitly documents 'eliminating the race where skewed datetime.now(UTC) calls could produce divergent label sets and silent data loss'). burndown.py's get_burndown_series (line 509) and costs.py's get_cost_trend/_cutoff (lines 33, 440) still call datetime.now(UTC) directly inside functions that ARE invoked concurrently per-project via asyncio.gather in aggregate_burndown_series and aggregate_cost_trend — the identical shape of race, unfixed.
findings.proposal: Extract the merge_queue.py pattern into a shared helper (e.g. dashboard.data.utils.resolve_now / a tiny `WindowClock` passed into every aggregate_* function) and thread a single request-scoped `now` from each app.py route handler down through burndown.py's and costs.py's aggregate_* functions exactly as merge_queue.py already does; add a repo-local grep-based CI check forbidding bare `datetime.now(UTC)` inside any function reachable from an asyncio.gather fan-out in dashboard/data/, so the next new aggregator can't reintroduce task-692's race.
findings.title: Per-DB clock-skew race fixed once (task 692) but left latent in sibling aggregators
findings.bug_history_link: task 692 (dashboard fix 0020b1d0ac, 'add now param to aggregate_queue_depth_timeseries, fix race') proves this exact bug class occurred and was fixed in merge_queue.py; burndown.py/costs.py were never updated to match, confirmed by grep showing raw datetime.now(UTC) still present at burndown.py and costs.py/440 today.
findings.verdict_notes: costs.py::_cutoff takes now via resolve_now; burndown.py::aggregate_burndown_series resolves now once and threads it into get_burndown_series. Remaining datetime.now sites in burndown.py are single-capture writers marked clock-exempt. Threaded by task 2170 steps (fe8784e4e2, f274c69434, 6ae31043a0).

findings.statement: Two policies are copy-pasted rather than centralized: (1) the 'iterate config.fused_memory_urls, try mcp_tool_call, on failure invalidate_session and continue to next URL' failover loop appears independently at 9+ call sites with inconsistent exception tuples (memory.py/tasks.py catch httpx.ConnectError/TimeoutException/HTTPStatusError/ValueError; metrics.py catches only httpx.HTTPError/ValueError); (2) the '{TTL constant, dict[str, tuple[float, T]] cache, _clear() test hook, store-only-on-success}' TTL-cache pattern is hand-rolled 3 times (tasks.py, merge_queue.py, app.py) — tasks.py's own docstring names this explicitly as tech debt deferred out of scope. A prior fix (d66f6fef79, 'harden load_task_titles cache — path normalization') added os.path.realpath keying to ONE of the three caches; the current merge_queue.py load_task_titles code no longer contains that normalization (superseded by the MCP-based fetch_tasks path), and tasks.py's own _fetch_tasks_cache keys on raw `str(project_root)` with no realpath normalization at all.
findings.proposal: Add a single `dashboard.data.mcp_client.FusedMemoryClient` (extending memory.py) that owns URL fan-out (one canonical exception tuple + invalidate_session policy) and a generic TTL-cache-with-realpath-normalized-keys; delete the 3 ad hoc caches (tasks.py._fetch_tasks_cache, merge_queue.py._task_titles_cache, app.py._task_cards_cache) and the 9 duplicated fan-out loops in favor of calling through it — this finishes the refactor tasks.py's own docstring explicitly deferred.
findings.title: MCP fan-out-with-failover and TTL caching each reimplemented independently in 4-5 modules
findings.bug_history_link: d66f6fef79 ('harden load_task_titles cache — path normalization, mutation safety, and edge-case tests') is direct evidence this exact defect class occurred once and was patched locally rather than in a shared cache abstraction.
findings.verdict_notes: Failover loop is centralized in mcp_fanout.first_success, and TTLCache is shared (scheduler.py, task_lookup.py, escalation_corpus.py, app.py::_memory_evals_cache). Residue: memory.py loops over get_queue_stats/get_wal_status still hand-roll per-URL invalidate_session, and metrics.py catches its own exception tuple. performance.py::_HISTORY_CACHE is a separate hand-rolled cache.

findings.statement: orchestrator.py independently re-implements: (a) orchestrator config.py's `${VAR:default}` env-var expansion via its own regex (comment literally says 'matching orchestrator config.py behavior', confirming it is a manual duplicate, not a shared import); (b) orchestrator process discovery via `ps aux` + regex over the command line, keyed to specific `--prd`/`--config` CLI flag spellings; (c) `.task/` worktree artifact parsing (metadata.json, plan.json, iterations.jsonl, reviews/*.json) with its own notion of plan 'steps' progress that only reads plan.json's `steps` collection, never the `prerequisites` collection that orchestrator's own artifacts.py:Artifacts.read_plan/get_completed_steps treats as part of the same step-status state.
findings.proposal: Follow the precedent already set successfully elsewhere in this codebase (dashboard/data/scheduler.py imports `shared.locking.modules_conflict` directly rather than re-deriving lock logic): move `_expand_env_vars` and plan-progress computation (steps+prerequisites) into the shared package, or expose them as thin public functions on orchestrator.config/orchestrator.artifacts that dashboard imports; longer-term, replace ps-aux discovery and .task/ file scraping with a small orchestrator-side status MCP tool (mirroring the get_merge_queue precedent already used successfully for live queue state in task-1606) so dashboard stops parsing orchestrator's process list and on-disk layout altogether.
findings.title: Dashboard re-derives orchestrator's process-launch and file-artifact formats instead of importing or being served them
findings.bug_history_link: speculative for a specific dated incident (no single commit isolates this), but the duplication is structurally proven (two independently-maintained copies of the same env-var-expansion regex) and the `steps`-only vs `steps+prerequisites` gap is directly visible by comparing orchestrator.py to artifacts.py.
findings.verdict_notes: Part (c) is gone: the .task/ artifact reader (read_task_artifacts) was deleted (3f78c8a09c); runtime state now comes from the get_task_runtime_state MCP tool. Parts (a) and (b) remain. _expand_env_placeholders still re-implements orchestrator config.py env expansion by regex, and find_running_orchestrators still parses `ps aux`.

findings.statement: Several tests were written to assert on served .jsx/.js source via substring or regex match rather than exercising rendered/API behavior, and had to be deleted and replaced with behavioral tests on review — the same anti-pattern recurred at least 4 separate times.
findings.proposal: Add a project-level test-writing convention (review-briefing rule or CI lint) forbidding substring/regex assertions against served frontend source files in dashboard/tests/, requiring behavioral assertions (rendered DOM state, API JSON response, or a parsed-AST structural check) instead — enforced at code-review time so new agent-authored tests stop reintroducing this class.
findings.title: Recurring test-authoring anti-pattern: assertions coupled to served frontend source text
findings.bug_history_link: d53cd62b68 (remove source-text grep tests per review, explicit rationale given), 6eedce5c51 (remove source-text meta-test test_tab_load.py), 2c81cd24fa (replace non-discriminating evict label test with structural assertion), 7234194827 (scope o.current_task assertion to JSX expression regex)
findings.verdict_notes: Tests still assert on served frontend source text. test_tab_merge_queue.py reads tabs.jsx and app.jsx with strip_js_comments. test_tab_tasks_layout_memo.py and test_tab_memory_evals.py regex-match .jsx source, and test_jsx_source_helpers.py provides shared helpers for it. The pattern persists as an institutionalised helper layer.

findings.title: A coalesce train is the only owner of its members' merge progress, yet it is the one request kind never journaled; train state is spread over five substrates and routed on a train-id prefix
findings.statement: When _maybe_coalesce_waiting_singles forms a coalesce train, it does three things to the absorbed members: it resolves each member's own future 'superseded' (so the member's workflow exits and the task goes to 'merge-deferred'), retires the member's request_id, and lets the journal _on_terminal callback drop it from merge_queue.json. The new GroupMergeRequest is registered straight into a lane buffer. queue_store.py skips every GroupMergeRequest on purpose ('train merges carry live scheduler callbacks that cannot be serialized'). Yet the worker builds those callbacks from the train id alone (self._train_callback_factory(train_id)), so they could be rebuilt at recovery. Harness._reconcile_one_stranded returns early on merge-deferred by design: 'the stranded sweep provably cannot reach a merge-deferred task'. So a crash with a coalesce train buffered or in flight leaves every member merge-deferred, with no queue entry, no journal row and no sweep that will find it. This is the 09-16/17 census class (11 stranded tasks). Commit 46e0933101 (5371 R7) says so outright: 'an unstarted coalesce train left in the buffer until the drained restart is lost ... (task 4737 owns the general defect)'. Its fix dissolves trains only on an admission halt, so the crash case stays open. Train state has no single record. It lives in GroupMergeRequest (memory), task-store status strings ('merge-deferred' / 'pending' / 'done', checked by statuses.get(mid) == 'merge-deferred'), stack-base refs (branch_stack.py via GitOps.stack_train_branches / unstack_from_unlanded_base / forget_stack_bases), the coalesce_derailed_task_ids PersistentSet, and runs.db train events. Declared versus coalesce behaviour is chosen by req.train_id.startswith(_COALESCE_TRAIN_ID_PREFIX) at four sites. Derail recovery is inline in _merger_loop. That code carries a comment, 'Known gap (out of scope): ... mark_member_done suffers a transient get_statuses error, one or more members may be left un-flipped in merge-deferred', and GroupMergeRequest.redrive_member is Optional 'for back-compat with existing test constructions'. When it is None, _redrive_coalesce_members logs and returns with the members stranded. Un-stacking is attempted twice, best-effort: once at redrive (_unstack_redriven_member never raises) and again at solo admission (_unstack_before_merge).
findings.proposal: Add merge_lane/train.py with three parts: a frozen TrainRecord(train_id, kind: TrainKind{DECLARED, COALESCE}, member_task_ids, tip_task_id, tip_branch: QueuedBranch, state); a TrainState transition table FORMED -> VERIFYING -> LANDED | DERAILED | DISSOLVED, enforced in a TrainLedger.transition() that raises on an illegal edge; and a TrainLedger journaled by queue_store. The coalescer writes the TrainRecord durably before it resolves any absorbed future. That makes the invariant 'a merge-deferred member is always named by a non-terminal TrainRecord or is being flipped' checkable at write and at recovery. At startup, recover_pending_merges rebuilds callbacks from the factory for every non-terminal COALESCE record. It then either re-enqueues the train or runs one TrainLedger.derail(), which owns the redrive, the un-stack and the one-strike mark, all in one place. TrainKind replaces the four prefix checks. Derailed membership becomes TrainRecord state and the coalesce_derailed_task_ids PersistentSet goes. redrive_member becomes required. These become deletable: the _merger_loop derail block, _dissolve_coalesce_trains_if_halted and the coalesce half of _stand_down_train (dissolution becomes a state edge, valid at any time, not a drain special case), the second best-effort un-stack, and the 'Known gap' comment. This would have prevented the 09-16/17 stranding (4953), 4737, 5371 R7, 1867 and 5352.
findings.bug_history_link: 46e0933101 fix(5371) R6-R7 'the drain never strands a coalesce train' (names 4737 as owner of the general defect); 2d46e25dcf feat(5352) 'a derailed coalesce train stays derailed across a restart'; 5618 stack-base ledger (0b7b6a95a0, 7866e3464f, e9039bf958, 87bcfd79e3, 2bdd8e9e0b, 8313285526); e3f5b8e138 'make the train coalescer reachable in a healthy pipeline'; 1c752d15e1/5e7df9e003 (5070 train CAS/derail); census 09-16/17: 11 tasks stranded merge-deferred (task 4953); LIVE 4737.
findings.verdict_notes: Verified queue_store.py skips GroupMergeRequest (isinstance check, 'train merges are not journaled'); worker.py::SpeculativeMergeWorker builds callbacks via _train_callback_factory(train_id); _COALESCE_TRAIN_ID_PREFIX startswith routing at several sites; the 'Known gap (out of scope)' comment exists in _merger_loop; redrive_member Optional in types.py::GroupMergeRequest; harness.py has the merge-deferred early-return; the 4737 owner note is in worker.py. Crash-strand claim follows. Exact site counts (four) are not individually checked.

findings.title: A request's terminal edge is taken by hand on every exit arm; the lifecycle registry is the one terminal record not driven by the request's own future
findings.statement: Four structures record that a request ended. Three follow the request's own future automatically: InFlightMergeRegistry releases its slot from future.add_done_callback, the queue_store journal is pruned by _buffer_owned_request's _on_terminal done-callback, and RequestLedger sweeps resolved futures passively. ItemLifecycle, the registry the 07-06 remediation made 'the single lifecycle state', is the exception. It reaches TERMINAL, and _live_items is popped, only when an exit arm remembers to call _retire_item, _resolve_or_drop_abandoned or _note_requeue. worker.py has 21 raw .set_result( calls in code and about 30 hand-placed retire/requeue calls. _finalize_inflight alone (957 lines, 13 returns) holds 24 of them, and _run_inflight_verify (1,499 lines, 840 of them comment lines) has 16 returns. _note_transition 'NEVER raises' and turns an illegal edge into an L1. Container membership is still what dispatch control acts on, and the finalizing head is derived as 'the sole _live_items InflightEntry whose request_id is absent from _inflight'. Commit eae3102515 states that the 'MergeRequest-for-InflightEntry object swap in _live_items, not the state change, is what actually clears the phantom head'. Each missed arm has been its own incident: bdbd56ecf7 and d93e383fb3 (terminal-failure arms never retired), eae3102515 (sentinel exits), bc954d22a9 (dead-verify abort), 421119b978, 16e12f1f82, 7c279229ea, and the 10-04 series for 4582: 84ef5a7e31 (a requeue from inside verify leaves a corpse holding its host), 175114ca51 (readers must skip vacated entries), ccc9d1f561 (the corpse's finalize bounced its re-dispatched incarnation) and 2e1616027b. That last commit gave snapshot() a dedup that keeps the 'head-of-line copy' and logs a WARNING, which masks the divergence rather than preventing it.
findings.proposal: Add merge_lane/request_handle.py::RequestHandle, which wraps one MergeRequest and makes its future private. resolve(outcome), requeue(target_container) and drop(reason) become the only ways a request leaves a stage. Each of them performs the lifecycle transition, the container move and the _live_items update together. TERMINAL is fired from the same done-callback that releases InFlightMergeRegistry and prunes the journal, so all four records share one trigger. Containers hold handles. Each put/pop asserts lifecycle_state in EXPECTED_STATES[container], raising in tests and under the lane's own assertion mode, escalating in production, with the values named per INV-2. That replaces the debug-only _assert_single_writer and the never-raising _note_transition as the uniform check. A requeue gets a new incarnation id, so a late finalize of the old entry can no longer address the new one. These become deletable: _resolve_or_drop_abandoned, the hand-placed _retire_item/_note_requeue calls on exit arms, the REQUEUED repair in _finalize_inflight's sentinel branch, InflightEntry.vacated and _occupying_inflight_entries, _first_copy_per_request, and the type-scan in _finalizing_head_entry. This would have prevented the 18x 'registry/lifecycle state diverging on one exit arm' theme and the 16x slot-leak theme (2609, 3015, 3082, 3148, 4582, 5495).
findings.verdict_notes: worker.py has 24 .set_result( matches; InFlightMergeRegistry releases via future.add_done_callback (types.py) and the journal _on_terminal done-callback exists (worker.py ~11481), while ItemLifecycle retirement is manual (about 31 retire/requeue calls, 19 of them after _finalize_inflight starts); _first_copy_per_request and _finalizing_head_entry exist as described. The per-function line figures are roughly right.

findings.title: The merge-lane ratchet gates raw file lines and prose_lines, so every net-additive fix pays line-count bookkeeping or reflows comments
findings.statement: build_report writes 'lines' and 'prose_lines' per cluster file, and derive_totals (_SUMMED_FILE_MEASURES) adds them into totals. test_merge_lane_ratchet fails on any rise. The code-quality definition names raw line count first under 'Do not steer by', because driving it 'rewards deleting prose instead of rehoming it'. The fix history shows exactly that pressure. 221 commits touched the baseline. The append-only ledger holds 47 authorized raises: 38 include a 'lines' measure, 36 'prose_lines', and 8 (tasks 5352, 5460 twice, 5303, 5034, 4094, 5475, 4830) raise only lines or prose. Commits have reshaped prose to hold the count: 64d8021a19 'reflow the 2823 gate comment so merge_queue.py holds its ratchet line count', 435869ea61 'hold merge_queue.py prose_lines at its baseline', a82d7010dd 'trim duplicated SeedLaneLock prose so git_ops.py holds the merge-lane ratchet', 504b996013, 6db3956661 'home the elision outside the cluster', and b0d9cb1479, whose message says 'The comment keeps its line count, so merge_lane_ratchet_baseline.json, which is outside this task's locked scope, still matches'. Worker.py's 22,081 lines and its line-alarm are context only. The ratchet's genuinely structural measures (function_local_imports, reexport_names, private_reads, patch_targets, external_importers, per-function cognitive) are the ones the definition endorses.
findings.proposal: Keep the measures in --report but take 'lines' and 'prose_lines' (per file and in derive_totals) out of the ratcheted set in scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py. Keep the per-function cognitive ceiling, function_local_imports, reexport_names, private_reads, patch_targets and external_importers. Those are the heuristic-13 and Tests-stance symptoms, and lowering any of them is never achieved by moving prose. Prose quality returns to review under the Comments stance. These become deletable: the line-only authorized-raise ceremony (8 ledger entries so far) and a class of reflow/trim commits. It also removes the cross-scope scope_violation escalations a regenerated baseline triggers (c0e13f0b35 notes 'regenerating ... is outside the plan's scope, so a scope_violation escalation comes first').
findings.bug_history_link: 64d8021a19, 435869ea61, a82d7010dd, 504b996013 (esc-3778-18), 6db3956661 (4194), 711407128d, 4d3b797644, f4de28d6a6, b0d9cb1479, 82004b6a60; c0e13f0b35 (scope_violation for a baseline regeneration); 5406 (no authorized-raise mechanism blocked net-additive fixes); 34 fix commits on the baseline file.
findings.verdict_notes: build_report emits 'lines' and 'prose_lines' per file, and both are in the summed measures (lines 594-595, 766-767). The authorized-raises ledger has exactly 47 raises. The commit-message quotes were not individually re-read; the structural claim holds.

findings.title: MergeOutcome carries the failure class only as a reason-string prefix: the OutcomeKind known at the gate is dropped, and four consumers route by startswith
findings.statement: MergeOutcome has status: Literal[...12 values] and reason: str, with no failure-kind field. Producers do know the kind: GateVerdict.block carries emit_subtype: OutcomeKind (post_merge_equivalence_failed, post_merge_pyright_broken), and OutcomeKind already enumerates dropped_plan_targets, main_health_red, train_incomplete and the rest. That kind goes only to the merge_attempt event. The caller-facing MergeOutcome gets status='blocked' plus a reason string that starts with one of 17 *_REASON_PREFIX constants, and the merge_lane façade exports all 17 as public API. Consumers then recover the kind by parsing. workflow.py routes escalation level and auto-heal on result.reason.startswith(...) at 9 sites, among them TaskWorkflow's blocked handler checking WORKTREE_MISSING, DROPPED_PLAN_TARGETS, POST_MERGE_EQUIVALENCE_FAILED, POST_MERGE_PYRIGHT_BROKEN, TRANSIENT_INFRA and MAIN_HEALTH_RED in order, and TRAIN_INCOMPLETE/TRAIN_VERIFY_FAILED. It re-stringifies kinds as literals ('dropped_plan_targets', 'main_health_red') for _write_merge_failure_review and fetches the prefixes through function-local imports from the alias shim orchestrator.merge_queue. unblock_types.py classifies BlockClass with four startswith checks, b3_gate.py hard-aborts on POST_MERGE_RED_MAIN_REASON_PREFIX, and scripts/review_model_admission.py filters event payloads by prefix. Inside the lane, _derail_on_train_verify_failure decides tagging on not reason.startswith(MAIN_HEALTH_RED_REASON_PREFIX) plus failure_category != '' as a discriminator, then rewrites the reason as f'{TRAIN_VERIFY_FAILED_REASON_PREFIX}: {reason}'. The queue_store journal keeps an entry for restart recovery only when result.reason == MERGE_WORKER_SHUTDOWN_REASON. Adding a blocked class means a new prefix constant, a façade export and an order-sensitive startswith in each consumer.
findings.proposal: Add kind: OutcomeKind | None to MergeOutcome. Every producer sets it: _finalize_advanced_merge copies GateVerdict.emit_subtype, _map_advance_failure, the train paths and main-health set theirs, and a shutdown outcome gets OutcomeKind.worker_shutdown instead of a sentinel reason. reason becomes display-only. A construction check in MergeOutcome.__post_init__ requires kind whenever status == 'blocked'. workflow's blocked handler dispatches through a single mapping {OutcomeKind -> handler}. unblock_types.classify and b3_gate key on kind, and the journal keep/remove decision keys on kind is worker_shutdown. These become deletable: the 17 *_REASON_PREFIX exports from merge_lane/__init__.py, the startswith ladders in workflow.py/unblock_types.py/b3_gate.py, the reason-prefix re-tagging in _derail_on_train_verify_failure, and the failure_category-emptiness discriminator. Downstream, the dashboard's merge-outcome vocabulary drift (prior dashboard.1) loses its source.
findings.bug_history_link: abfe0d9e2b (2591, failure_category emptiness used as a routing discriminator); task 1680 (b3_gate prefix hard-abort class); 2383 β integration_skew routing ordered after MAIN_HEALTH_RED by prefix; prior dashboard.1 (merge-outcome vocabulary drift); speculative for a specific mis-route incident.
findings.verdict_notes: MergeOutcome has status Literal plus reason: str and no failure-kind field. startswith routing is real: workflow.py has 9 reason.startswith sites, unblock_types.py has 4 checks, and b3_gate.py checks block_reason.startswith(POST_MERGE_RED_MAIN_REASON_PREFIX). The merge_lane façade references REASON_PREFIX 17 times.

findings.title: A LandedOutbox row means write-ahead intent, but four of five readers treat MergeProvenance.lookup as a confirmed landing
findings.statement: _journal_landed_then_advance records a LandedRow 'UNCONDITIONALLY before the outcome of advance_main is known' and never consumes it on failure (cas_failed, not_descendant, unmerged_state, pop_conflict_no_advance). Its docstring tells consumers they 'MUST treat row presence as provisional: verify the task actually landed'. Only reconcile_landed_row does so (is_ancestor(advanced_sha, main) -> RC-1 'pruned_not_landed'). Four readers call a journal hit 'authoritative' and act on it without an ancestry check. TaskWorkflow._recover_if_already_merged, _recover_before_execute and _recover_before_merge all call _finalise_recovery_done(basis='journal', sha=row.advanced_sha), which itself checks only basis and delivered_checks. TaskGroundTruth._resolve_branch_state returns BranchState(ON_MAIN, row.advanced_sha), and row (a) of the _RECOVERY table maps that to MARK_DONE_WITH_PROVENANCE. These readers are correct today only because of two unstated outside guarantees: the scheduler dispatch gate (Harness → reconcile_landed_task) and the startup reconcile prune stale rows before a workflow starts, and fused-memory's set_task_status re-checks kind='merged' SHAs with git merge-base --is-ancestor (middleware/task_interceptor.py). If a stale row reaches a guard, the server refuses and _finalise_recovery_done turns that into _mark_blocked(escalate_to_human=True), so a task that should have retried its merge goes to a human instead. The policy 'journal first, git fallback' is restated in each reader. landing_evidence.py meanwhile holds the git-derived authority for seven other sites. completion.py, despite its name, is an unblock-eligibility predicate over the run-scoped event store and not part of landed-to-done.
findings.proposal: Make the row two-phase in its type: LandedRow.state: LandingState{INTENT, CONFIRMED}. _journal_landed_then_advance records INTENT, then on adv.result == 'advanced' re-records CONFIRMED with the real advanced SHA, and on any other result discards the row in the same helper. MergeProvenance.lookup returns only CONFIRMED rows; an intents() accessor is the sole input to reconcile_landed_outbox's crash-window check. Give the journal-first-then-git policy one home: a merge_lane/landing_authority.py::landed_sha(task_id) that consults CONFIRMED rows, then landing_evidence's producers. The three workflow guards and _resolve_branch_state call it. These become deletable: the 'MUST treat row presence as provisional' obligation and its docstring, RC-1 for rows from live (non-crash) failures, and the dependence on the fused-memory ancestry refusal as the only defence. Optionally rename merge_lane/completion.py to merge_verify_completion_eligibility so its name stops implying landed-to-done.
findings.bug_history_link: Confusion codebook 'merge-state-not-git-corroborated'; prior merge-queue.3 lineage (tasks 2153/2155/2156/2681/2280 built the outbox and its consume/prune chain); docs/prds/landed-not-done-recovery.md; e6d958a133 (pre-PLAN guard DONE-ing phantom tasks). The stale-intent-to-human-escalation path is speculative: verified in code, no incident found.
findings.verdict_notes: The journal-first readers are real: task_ground_truth.py::_resolve_branch_state and the workflow.py recovery paths call MergeProvenance.lookup and then _finalise_recovery_done(basis='journal') with no ancestry check. _finalise_recovery_done checks only basis, sha and delivered_checks, and a rejection becomes _mark_blocked(escalate_to_human=True). Weakened because the failure needs a stale row to get past the dispatch gate and startup reconcile, and the finding admits there is no incident for it. Treat it as a latent risk, not a live defect.

findings.title: Per-task retry budgets are about ten parallel process-lifetime dicts, each paired by hand with a class MAX_* constant and threaded through a 28-parameter function and a protocol of privates
findings.statement: 'How many more times may this task retry X' is one axis of variability with no mechanism of its own. SpeculativeMergeWorker holds 4 MAX_* class constants (CAS 5, verify timeouts 2, ENOSPC 1, narrowed 2) and further threshold constants, plus per-task dicts with process lifetime and bespoke reset rules: _post_merge_verify_timeouts, _post_merge_verify_enospc_retries, _post_merge_verify_narrowed_retries, _cas_retries, _gate_retries, _contended_lease_requeues/_first_defer_at/_last_defer_at/_cap_outs, _generation_chain_counts, _inflight_dead_verify_aborts and _verify_attempt_count, with 46 self._* references to these dicts. _run_post_merge_verify takes 28 parameters, including three hand-paired (dict, max) pairs: timeouts/max_timeouts, enospc_retries/max_enospc, narrowed_retries/max_narrowed. _TrainMergeHost exposes four of the dicts and four MAX_* names as protocol members, and module-level helpers mutate them. Pairing has already gone wrong: reverify_member_solo passed a literal max_enospc=3 (d62915293d) and a literal max_timeouts (b0d9cb1479). 2835 had to decouple the narrowed counter from the ENOSPC one. The 3003 contended-lease streak took five fixes to get staleness and terminal bounding right in one more pair of dicts.
findings.proposal: Add merge_lane/retry_budget.py::RetryBudget(name, limit, stale_after: float | None), with consume(task_id) -> bool, remaining(task_id) and reset(task_id), and one internal counter whose staleness rule is defined once. Add a frozen LaneRetryPolicy that bundles the named budgets (verify_timeout, infra_enospc, infra_narrowed, cas, gate, contended_lease, dead_verify_abort). The worker owns one instance. _run_post_merge_verify and the train paths take policy: LaneRetryPolicy instead of six parameters. reverify_member_solo takes a fresh policy derived from the same limits instead of reading SpeculativeMergeWorker.MAX_* (removing one heuristic-13 reach). These become deletable: the four MAX_* class constants, the eight budget members of _TrainMergeHost, _advance_contended_lease_streak's hand-rolled staleness, and the parallel dicts. This would have prevented 4094's literal-budget bug and 2835's counter coupling.
findings.bug_history_link: d62915293d and b0d9cb1479 (task 4094); task 2835 (narrowed retry counter decoupled); 51ec2913a9, 9021c8fed3, 1c793a9d99, 57c4e432ee, 9a97b49d6e (task 3003 contended-lane defer streak); 5e7df9e003, b4fb450010 (task 5070 train MAX_CAS_RETRIES); 2e58a8fc28 (no-progress budget vs per-command timeout).
findings.verdict_notes: worker.py has MAX_POST_MERGE_VERIFY_* constants threaded as max_enospc= arguments at 5+ sites, and reverify_member_solo/train code reads worker.MAX_*. Per-task dicts are present. The 28-parameter count was not individually re-counted, but the pattern is real.

findings.title: worker.py: heuristic-14 measurement finds about 8,000 lines of separable modules with no heuristic-13 obstacle, one train seam blocked by a downcast to the worker, and a 13k-line class whose purpose needs 'and'
findings.statement:
The measurement follows the protocol in heuristic 14.

Step 1, is the prose in its right home? Of 22,081 lines, 12,519 are prose (57%). 611 lines cite task numbers, escalations or 'review fix'/'amendment' history (124 distinct task ids). _run_inflight_verify is 840 comment lines out of 1,499. That is reviewer-answering history, which belongs in commits and task records under the Comments stance.

Step 2, a named partition of top-level symbols, with cross-partition references measured by AST:
- H (MergeMetrics, BreakerTrip, NoLandingsCircuitBreaker), I (IllegalLifecycleTransition, ItemLifecycle, _LEGAL_TRANSITIONS, lifecycle alarms), J (select_probe_depth, select_chain_depth, next_halving_state, ProbePlacement) and L (_alarm_resource_audit and fingerprint) reference no other worker.py partition. No symptom.
- A (post-merge verify runner: _run_post_merge_verify, retry-env assembly, _ReifyAttemptSidecar, nextest probes, about 2,170 lines), B (main-health probe and escalation, about 836 lines), D (TipRelation, AttachAction, C3SubmitAction, select_recovery_winner) and E (reconcile_landed_row, reconcile_landed_task, reconcile_landed_outbox, which belong beside landed_outbox.py) reference only the module-head constants and helpers (and A references B). No symptom once those constants sit in a lower module.
- F (train and pre-merge core: classify_and_merge, reverify_member_solo, _do_train_merge, _advance_train) HAS a symptom. classify_and_merge does isinstance(worker, SpeculativeMergeWorker) to reach _emit_speculative and _verify_frontier_depth, and its own docstring calls the other branch 'now unreachable'. reverify_member_solo reads SpeculativeMergeWorker.MAX_POST_MERGE_VERIFY_TIMEOUTS/ENOSPC_RETRIES. So a merge_lane/train.py would import worker.py while worker.py imports train.py, which is a cycle. _TrainMergeHost's members are worker privates (_git_ops, _event_store, _cas_retries, _note_verify_started and others), so the protocol formalizes the reach.
- K, the residual SpeculativeMergeWorker, is 13,015 lines with 139 methods and about 105 instance fields. Its purpose is 'admit and coalesce and speculate and dispatch verifies and quarantine hosts and reap worktrees and audit resources and render snapshots and drain on shutdown'. _verifier_loop alone has cognitive complexity 252 and stop() 111.

The satellites drift.py and shadow.py are still function-bags over K's privates (prior merge-queue.4).
findings.proposal: First move the prose: history and defences go to commit messages and task records, durable rationale to docs/ with a pointer. Then extract the eight symptom-free partitions as downward-layered modules: merge_lane/post_merge_verify.py (A), main_health.py (B), tip_relation.py (D), the reconcile functions into landed_outbox.py (E), metrics.py (H), lifecycle.py (I), depth_policy.py (J) and resource_audit.py (L). Each imports only types.py, ports.py and a new merge_lane/reasons.py that takes the head constants. Extract F only after the RetryBudget finding lands (which removes the MAX_* reach) and after deleting the unreachable non-SpeculativeMergeWorker branch of classify_and_merge, so the downcast becomes a narrow MergeTelemetry port. Do not split K by line count. Its remaining seams are the request-handle and train-ledger proposals in the sibling findings, which move state, not text, so drift.py and shadow.py can then own their own state objects (DriftCheckState and ShadowCompareState already exist).
findings.bug_history_link: Context, not ranking: worker.py was touched by most of the window's 75 fix commits; 5034/5036 (lane moved into merge_lane/, alias shims); prior merge-queue.4 (satellites over privates, still weakened). The extraction itself is speculative as a bug preventer; its value is the next agent's context cost.
findings.verdict_notes: worker.py is 22,081 lines. _COALESCE_TRAIN_ID_PREFIX is defined at module scope, and the isinstance/downcast and MAX_* reach from module-level functions to SpeculativeMergeWorker is visible (worker.py ~5601 reads SpeculativeMergeWorker.MAX_...). The partition line counts were not re-derived.

findings.title: landing_evidence.py is the cross-package 'did it land' authority but lives inside the lane's private package, reached through alias shims and function-local imports
findings.statement: merge_lane/__init__.py declares 'Every submodule is private to the package'. landing_evidence.py (2,788 lines; its module docstring alone runs about 200 lines) serves seven call sites, and only one is inside the lane (_redrive_coalesce_members). The others are workflow.py, which imports orchestrator.merge_lane.landing_evidence directly; harness.py, through the orchestrator.landing_evidence alias shim (4 producer calls); and escalation/git_authority.py and escalation/server.py, through function-local `from orchestrator.landing_evidence import ...  # type: ignore[reportMissingImports]`, which is a cross-package reach. That docstring also explains that it is a module function, not a GitOps method, so that MagicMock-ed git_ops in tests does not auto-mock it: a Tests-stance seam shaping production placement. The façade exports only patch_content_contained from it, so every other consumer bypasses the façade.
findings.proposal: Promote it to its own package, orchestrator/landing/ (producers branch_work_landed, validate_landing_evidence and validate_reported_landing, plus LandingVerdict, LandingReason, LandingMethod and LandingTally), with its own narrow façade. merge_lane imports it downward. escalation imports it at module level through a declared dependency instead of function-local, type-ignored imports. Move the 200-line docstring's history and defences to the PRD (docs/prds/landed-not-done-recovery.md) with a one-line pointer. These become deletable: the orchestrator/landing_evidence.py alias shim, the function-local imports in the escalation server, and the ruling that the lane façade's 'private' claim does not apply to this module. Pair this with the landing-authority entry point proposed in the LandedOutbox finding.
findings.bug_history_link: 3103 (escalation merge_status ancestor-arm/degenerate-branch fixes reached this module across packages); 4704 (validate_reported_landing added for workflow); 4647 (second producer); task 5037 (alias shim removal).
findings.verdict_notes: landing_evidence has non-lane importers: workflow.py imports orchestrator.merge_lane.landing_evidence directly, harness.py and evals/live_fixture.py import it through the orchestrator.landing_evidence alias shim, and escalation/git_authority.py (lines 397, 499) and escalation/server.py (3766) make function-local imports with type: ignore[reportMissingImports]. Only worker.py uses it from inside the lane.

findings.title: Inner phases return a WorkflowOutcome with no payload, so the facts about a block travel on five instance stash dicts with precedence and reset rules kept only in comments
findings.statement: _execute_iterations, _verify_debugfix_loop and _run_scoped_verification_with_infra_retry return a bare WorkflowOutcome.BLOCKED. The reason, detail, category and dedupe fingerprint ride on instance attributes: _zero_output_hang_info, _progress_resume_churn_info, _infra_hold_info, _inherited_break_info (untyped dicts keyed 'reason'/'detail'/'category'/'fingerprint') and _last_verify_result. _execute_verify_review_loop reads them in a fixed order that only comments enforce ('Must be checked BEFORE _inherited_break_info to prevent ... clobbering the infra_issue category'). Each writer must reset its stash at entry ('cannot inherit stale _zero_output_hang_info from a prior pass'). The module-level constants describe this as 'the _inherited_break_info pattern' and 'the _zero_output_hang_info stash idiom'. The merge side does the same with _last_merge_block_reason, _last_merge_failure_category and _last_merge_failure_cause_hint, which _submit_to_merge_queue and _run_merge_phase set and _merge_outcome_signature and _check_merge_outcome_thrash read. The VERIFY→REVIEW event uses _verify_checkpoint_hit and _verify_green_tip_sha, set in _execute_verify_review_loop and read in _enter_phase. These are transient values promoted to instance lifetime, the same shape W9 deleted for _last_block_*. W9 typed only the outermost channel. A block arm that forgets to stash silently falls through to the generic route; the latent-bug finding below is a live instance.
findings.proposal: Introduce a frozen PhaseResult sum type in workflow_types.py: Passed(tip_sha) | Blocked(spec: BlockSpec, reason: str, detail: str) | Escalated | Requeued | Cancelled. The three inner phases return it, and _execute_verify_review_loop dispatches with `match`, calling _mark_blocked(result.spec, ...) for Blocked. MergeOutcome's category and cause_hint are passed directly into the thrash signature. The VERIFY→REVIEW workflow_verify emission takes the tip as an argument instead of reading instance state. This makes the following deletable: the four *_info attributes, _last_verify_result, the three _last_merge_* attributes, _verify_checkpoint_hit and _verify_green_tip_sha, the reset-at-entry code, and the precedence comments. Pyright exhaustiveness on the match then enforces that every Blocked carries its own route. It would have prevented 9a9b60904f (stale stash misroute plus iteration-cap misclassification) and the signature-repeat/opaque-timeout L1 loss.
findings.bug_history_link: 9a9b60904f 'amend: robustness fixes for zero-output circuit breaker' (stale-state reset plus a misclassified all-zero-output hang); task 1739 (zero-output), task 2360/reify-4827 (progress-resume churn), fe5e23479c/ee94ada1ba task 1883 (infra_hold precedence over inherited break); _compute_merge_outcome_signature docstring records the MAIN_HEALTH_RED path hashing an empty basis because the _last_merge_* fields were never set there (#1688)
findings.verdict_notes: Verified the four stash dicts initialised in TaskWorkflow.__init__ (~1400-1417). _execute_verify_review_loop reads them in order, and the comment 'Must be checked BEFORE _inherited_break_info' is the only thing enforcing that order. _execute_iterations resets _zero_output_hang_info and _progress_resume_churn_info at entry (~8236-8261). _last_merge_block_reason and _verify_checkpoint_hit also exist. Structural claim holds.

findings.title: A block is classified in five parallel vocabularies chosen per call site; merge-lane block kinds are routed by prefix and substring matching on prose
findings.statement: Of 68 _mark_blocked calls, 7 pass a BlockDisposition. The other 61 hand-set escalate_to_human (37 calls), category as a free string (17 calls, values including infra_issue, wip_conflict, branch_reset, preexisting_main_break, integration_skew, already_landed, cross_repo_deliverable, design_concern), block_status ('blocked'/'infra-hold'), suggested_action (5 literal values), merge_phase, skip_escalation and spawn_dry_run. Even the table-driven arms in _drive pair disp with a hand-written category='infra_issue', 'wip_conflict' or 'branch_reset', because BlockDisposition carries no escalation category; its own category field is always FailureCategory.NONE. With no disposition, BlockClass is recovered by prefix-sniffing the reason in unblock_types.classify_block_reason, and b3_gate.check_proposal repeats a startswith check. Escalation.category is a bare str whose comment says 'nothing rejects a typo'd category' and that 'the NEXT category addition promotes this comment to an enum'. Workflow has since added about ten categories outside the listed vocabulary. On the merge side, MergeOutcome.status is a 12-value Literal, but the blocked sub-kind is prose: the handler in _submit_to_merge_queue routes on six reason.startswith(*_REASON_PREFIX) arms imported function-locally from merge_queue and merge_lane. It then falls back to `'verification failed' in reason.lower()` / `'ff' in reason.lower() or 'advanced' in reason.lower()`. The 'ff' check matches any reason containing 'diff', 'off' or 'buffer'. Reasons like f'Verifier error: {exc}' or 'Post-merge verification blocked: ...' do not contain 'verification failed', so they are labelled merge_ff_failed or merge_error. That category feeds the review record, the merge_blocked event and the L1 dedup key.
findings.proposal: Extend BlockDisposition into one frozen BlockSpec in workflow_types.py with route: BlockRoute {STEWARD, HUMAN_L1, SILENT}, escalation_category: EscalationCategory (an enum owned by escalation.models, closing the task-3709 trigger), row_status: TaskStatus, block_class: BlockClass, suggested_action: SuggestedAction and an optional dedupe_fingerprint. _mark_blocked(spec, reason, detail) takes only that. Exception rows and non-exception arms name module-level BlockSpec constants. The merge lane sets MergeOutcome.blocked_kind: MergeBlockKind at the producer, and one table in workflow maps MergeBlockKind to BlockSpec. This makes the following deletable: classify_block_reason, the six startswith arms, the 'ff'/'advanced' substring arm, b3_gate's prefix test, _mark_blocked's spawn_dry_run prefix assertion, the escalate_to_human/category/block_status/suggested_action/skip_escalation kwargs, and BlockDisposition.category. It would have prevented 4211 (lane-lock refusal rendered as disk pressure by an inherited prefix), 2757 (skip_escalation × fall-through L1), and the block-report-misattribution codebook class.
findings.bug_history_link: e072f8abe0 'skip_escalation must suppress the BLOCKED fall-through L1 (task 2757)'; task 4211 lane-lock rendered as 'warm_lane_disk_pressure' (reify esc-5556-1); BD-2 rows added after red main: 2f16391327, 60f7a42cf5, 770910883e, 7c7db822dd; codebook 'block-report-misattribution' (16 sightings, filed 2549/2553); escalation/models.py REFACTOR TRIGGER task 3709
findings.verdict_notes: _mark_blocked takes category as a free str (default 'task_failure') plus block_status, escalate_to_human, suggested_action and disposition as separate parameters. TaskWorkflow._submit_to_merge_queue (~11600-11602) does `'verification failed' in result.reason.lower()` and `'ff' in ... or 'advanced' in ...`, so the substring bug claim is real. I did not count the exact 61/7 split or the prefix arms.

findings.title: No owner for the L0 escalation lifecycle: 18 dismissal sites across three modules plus an orphan reaper that guesses liveness from freshness proxies
findings.statement: The workflow files L0s, the per-task steward consumes them, and nothing owns an L0's end of life. `resolve(..., dismiss=True)` appears 5 times in workflow.py (_mark_blocked ×3, _wait_for_resolution, _await_steward_completion), 3 times in steward.py and 10 in harness.py, including 4 in _reap_orphan_l0_escalations. The two steward waiters depend on a producer invariant stated only in docstrings: 'a steward give-up ALWAYS dismisses its own L0 before publishing an outcome'. _await_steward_completion reads the outcome queue but overrides it with a status read and an escalation-queue has_open_l1 probe, then dismisses orphan L0s itself. _wait_for_resolution never reads the queue and wakes only when a dismissal fires EscalationQueue.resolve → harness._on_escalation_resolved. Because an exiting incarnation never hands off its L0s (CancellationScope's on_terminal list has heartbeat, steward-stop, worktree, lane and config entries only), the harness reaper must infer whether the filer is still alive. Its proxies are the _escalation_events snapshot, scheduler.is_actively_held, classify_pins on filing_claimant_run_id, routing.latest.decided_at freshness (_has_fresh_dispatch), and a durable metadata.merge_phase_liveness stamp (_has_fresh_merge_phase). The workflow writes that stamp purely for the reaper (_stamp_merge_phase_entered / _clear_merge_phase_entered). The missing guarantee is in the escalation subsystem: an L0 has no owner lease tied to the filing incarnation's lifetime.
findings.proposal: Make the filing incarnation the owner of its L0s. Add an 'l0_handoff' entry to TaskWorkflow._on_terminal_cleanups, the one writer, which on every exit except a hard cancel resolves each pending L0 whose filing_claimant_run_id is this incarnation's, according to a typed L0Disposition (consumed, superseded-by-L1, abandoned). The steward only publishes on the outcome queue and never dismisses; _wait_for_resolution waits on the same queue, leaving one waiter. The reaper then handles only crashes: promote L0s whose filing claimant is provably dead, using the existing classify_pins dead_l0. This makes the following deletable: the dismissal loops in _mark_blocked, _await_steward_completion and _wait_for_resolution; the steward's dismiss-then-publish contract in _dismiss_capped_l0/_auto_escalate_to_human; the reaper's _escalation_events/is_actively_held arm, _has_fresh_dispatch and _has_fresh_merge_phase; and the merge_phase_liveness stamp with its two methods and three config knobs. It would have prevented the reaper false-positive/false-negative series and the 3170 stranded-ESCALATED-wait class.
findings.bug_history_link: mined theme (18x): 2725, 2800, 2878, 2931, 2991 (e58da642c5, af96370079 merge_phase_liveness stamp/clear fixes), 3002, 3541 (prior-incarnation L0 'IMMORTAL'), 4988, 5643 (LIVE); 3170 series 5c36c73197/68570c465c 'give-up dismisses its own L0', 04909e8c9d, 70ad7307d6; 7fc4690695 'make the task-2060 L0 sweep's dismissal loud'; 4495 dismiss race
findings.verdict_notes: resolve(dismiss=True) appears 5x in workflow.py (14551, 16355, 16616, 16686, 17960), 10 in harness.py, and 2 calls in steward.py plus 1 docstring mention. That gives roughly 17-18 sites, so the count is fine. The reaper's freshness proxies (_has_fresh_dispatch, _has_fresh_merge_phase) were not individually opened. The structural claim of no lifecycle owner is plausible and consistent with the code seen.

findings.title: The signature-repeat and opaque-timeout guards log 'escalating to L1' but are routed to the steward as 'Verification attempts exhausted'
findings.statement: In TaskWorkflow._verify_debugfix_loop, the opaque-infra-timeout cap (max_opaque_timeout_attempts, default 2) and the signature-repetition guard (max_failure_signature_repeat, default 3) both log '... — escalating to L1' and return a bare WorkflowOutcome.BLOCKED without setting any stash. TaskWorkflow._execute_verify_review_loop finds _infra_hold_info and _inherited_break_info both None and calls `_mark_blocked('Verification attempts exhausted', detail=...)` with escalate_to_human defaulting to False. The task therefore files an L0, starts a steward retry loop instead of the human L1 the guard was written for, and reports a reason ('attempts exhausted') that names the wrong guard. test_workflow_signature_loop_guard.py and test_workflow_verify_retry.py call the private _verify_debugfix_loop directly and assert only `outcome == BLOCKED` plus a log line, so the lost route is untested.
findings.proposal: Have each guard arm carry its own block: until PhaseResult lands, set a stash with a distinct reason ('verify signature repeated N×: <sig>' / 'opaque infra timeout cap'), category='infra_issue' for the opaque arm, and escalate_to_human=True. Then route it in _execute_verify_review_loop. Pin the behaviour with a test that drives the public run() or _drive seam and asserts an L1 was filed and the reason names the guard. That test replaces the two loop-level tests that read private state such as _failure_signature_history.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative (no incident found); same structural class as 9a9b60904f (zero-output BLOCKED misrouted as generic exhaustion)
findings.verdict_notes: The mechanism is real. Both guards in _verify_debugfix_loop (~10148-10181) log 'escalating to L1' and return a bare BLOCKED with no stash. _execute_verify_review_loop (7924-7943) then falls to _mark_blocked('Verification attempts exhausted') with escalate_to_human=False. However, the max_verify_attempts cap takes the identical path, and in the 3-tier ladder L1 is the auto-watcher, not a human, so the claim that the task wrongly gets a steward retry loop instead of a 'human L1' is unsupported. The real defect is a misleading log or reason, not a lost route. The 'speculative' bug_history_link supports this. The tests only assert BLOCKED, as claimed.

findings.title: Role prompts restate escalation-server policy as hand-written prose, and the current text contradicts the server
findings.statement: ESCALATION_LADDER_CORE hard-codes facts that escalation/ owns: 'the dedupe gate covers only category=infra_issue inside a short (600s) window' (DedupeConfig defaults), a closed list of six categories (Escalation.category is an open str and workflow files ten others), and 'a critical/urgent filing bypasses dedupe entirely — ... on that one a NEW page to the human'. That last claim is false for the agents who read it. The escalation server downgrades any non-harness critical/urgent filing to blocking before _submit_or_dedupe (the `esc.severity in BORN_AT_L2_SEVERITIES and not _is_harness_sentinel_role(...)` gate). The same prompt's own Severity-policy paragraph, 30 lines later, says exactly that. The text was added by b2cc1480fa, a commit fixing an earlier false claim in this block. Nothing ties prompt prose to the code it describes. A precedent exists, though: agents/code_quality.py::guidance renders the quality doc into prompts from its single source.
findings.proposal: Render prompt facts about another subsystem from that subsystem's own code. escalation.dedupe exposes fold_policy_summary(cfg: DedupeConfig) -> str; escalation.server exposes the severity-routing rule as data; the category list is rendered from the EscalationCategory enum proposed above. roles.py composes these at import, as it does CODE_QUALITY_GUIDANCE, and a shape test asserts no literal window or category list remains in roles.py. This makes the hand-maintained literals deletable, along with the recurring prose-correction commits.
findings.bug_history_link: b2cc1480fa 'fix(5368): bound the keep_driving retry, and say what dedupe really folds' (fixed one false claim, introduced the severity contradiction); mined theme (20x): 252af6c119, e4f15eb87d, b2466e8928, 376b2d054e (5683), f33b07fd34 (5332), c482163765 (4924), 33f0fe615b (4169), ac4339ddc9
findings.verdict_notes: roles.py lines ~182-185 say a critical/urgent filing 'bypasses dedupe entirely ... a NEW page to the human'. The same prompt's Severity policy says the server downgrades agent-filed critical/urgent to blocking. escalation/server.py ~1622 has `esc.severity in BORN_AT_L2_SEVERITIES and not _is_harness_sentinel_role(...)`. The contradiction is real. The six-category list is hard-coded prose.

findings.title: Retry and anti-thrash budgets live in five homes with five durabilities and three copies of 'N consecutive identical signatures'
findings.statement: Q4: the workflow's own counters are now typed (RetryLedger with pure _evaluate_* functions; prior workflow.5 is carried as weakened). Ownership is still split by accident of history. (1) RetryLedger lives in task metadata, persisted by read-modify-write of the whole metadata dict; merge_first_enqueued_at bypasses the model as a raw dict and stores an epoch float as str. (2) The steward keeps _retry_counts, _timeout_counts, _empty_output_counts and _capped_escalations as PersistentMap/PersistentSet JSON files under data/orchestrator/guards, and must pop all three maps in lockstep at three sites. (3) Scheduler._requeue_counts and _transient_requeue_counts are in-process dicts, so they reset on every fleet redeploy. (4) TaskWorkflow._failure_signature_history is an in-memory list, scoped to one incarnation. (5) StreakCounter/StreakRegistry in streaks.py already unifies the scheduler's tick counters, including a cause-change-reset variant, but nothing in workflow or steward uses it. The 'N consecutive identical signatures' decision is written three times: _evaluate_merge_thrash, the last-N-equal window in _verify_debugfix_loop, and StreakCounter's cause-change variant. Durability is chosen per counter after an incident: 5352 found that the steward's give-up was process-lifetime and was re-adopted on every redeploy.
findings.proposal: Create a single RetryBudget registry module that extends StreakCounter. Each budget is declared once with its name, threshold config key, reset event, signature function and Durability (TASK_ROW, GUARD_FILE or PROCESS), and the backend is chosen from that declaration. RetryLedger's evaluators, the steward's three maps, the scheduler's requeue dicts and the verify signature window all become declared budgets. This makes the following deletable: the steward's triple-pop lockstep, the bespoke last-N window, the duplicate signature arithmetic, and the raw-dict merge_first_enqueued_at path. Restart behaviour becomes a reviewed property of each budget rather than an incident.
findings.bug_history_link: 6c5295751b 'feat(5352): the steward's give-up is now terminal for the task, not the process'; task 917 (16 Opus calls before total_no_plan_failures existed); task 2988 (pool-exhaustion requeue-cap burn → reblock L2 storm); 6a631d537f/eded4bb2a6 (per-mode counter clusters)
findings.verdict_notes: Verified that _failure_signature_history is an in-memory list on TaskWorkflow (1435, used 10170-10174) and that workflow.py and steward.py never reference StreakCounter. I did not open RetryLedger, the steward PersistentMaps, or Scheduler's requeue dicts, so the five-homes enumeration is largely unverified. The 'three copies of N identical signatures' claim is also unverified beyond the verify-loop window. The core of the claim is plausible but less established than stated.

findings.title: workflow.py fails heuristic 6 and hosts other subsystems' pure policies, which creates the import cycles; measured clusters show TaskWorkflow must not be split yet
findings.statement: Q2: the module's purpose needs 'and': it drives one task's phases AND recovers prior incarnations AND coordinates merge trains AND supervises the steward AND auto-heals main AND routes suggestions to the curator AND hosts offline-lane and merge-lane policy. Heuristic 14 measurement follows. Prose: 8,212 of 18,039 lines (46%) are comments and docstrings; code is about 8.5k lines. The file roughly doubled in the window (8,835 → 18,039). Partition and heuristic 13 symptoms: (a) build_offline_lane_fix_task_arguments and compute_failing_test_set_fingerprint have zero callers in workflow.py and are imported function-locally by offline_lane.py and chronic_flake.py (upward reach). (b) The train policy (_line_ranges_stackable, _select_train_members, classify_rebase_cohort) is imported at top level by merge_lane/worker.py (`from orchestrator.workflow import _select_train_members`), while workflow.py imports merge_queue/merge_lane names function-locally at about 13 sites, including the private merge_lane.gates._check_plan_files_touched_in_branch. That is a cycle workflow ⇄ merge_lane.worker, and it is the reason workflow has 26 function-local orchestrator imports. (c) steward.py imports the private workflow._inject_verdict_tools_mcp function-locally. (d) verify.py imports the private workflow._normalize_cause_hint, a delegator to RetryLedger.normalize_cause_hint. (e) TaskWorkflow method clusters measured by AST: train has 11 methods using 14 self attributes; recovery 11/15; steward-and-block 25/20, called from 37 methods outside it; merge-submit 10/21 with 27 out-of-cluster calls; review routing 10/15. Extracting any cluster today would produce a function-bag over the parent's private state, which fails heuristic 13.
findings.proposal: Move only the parts that pass heuristic 13 now. (a) goes to offline_lane.py. (b) goes to a new merge_lane/train_policy.py that merge_lane/worker.py imports downward, which breaks the cycle and lets the function-local merge imports in workflow.py move to the top of the file. (c) _inject_plan_tools_mcp and _inject_verdict_tools_mcp move to mcp_lifecycle.py. (d) _normalize_cause_hint and _compute_merge_outcome_signature are deleted in favour of RetryLedger. TaskWorkflow stays whole until PhaseResult/BlockSpec and the single-writer machine remove the transient state that couples the clusters; record that measurement in the task record with a one-line pointer in the module docstring. Separately, move the decision-defending prose (46%) into commit and task records per the Comments stance.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative as a direct bug source; cost evidence: 345 non-merge commits on workflow.py in the window; 103bfd35e5 '_BriefingLike protocol sync' and the SchedulerFacade drift (prior workflow.8) show the same hand-mirrored-seam pattern
findings.verdict_notes: Line counts match (18039). merge_lane/worker.py imports _select_train_members from workflow at top level. steward.py imports _inject_verdict_tools_mcp function-locally. verify.py imports _normalize_cause_hint function-locally, not top-level, but the private cross-import holds. offline_lane.py and 709 import compute_failing_test_set_fingerprint and build_offline_lane_fix_task_arguments function-locally from workflow. chronic_flake.py only mentions the fingerprint function in a docstring, so that part is slightly overstated. The AST cluster measurements and comment-line percentage were not re-derived.

findings.title: Landed/recoverable task disposition is decided in five places: the _RECOVERY table, four applier rewrites of its answer, the dispatch gate, the outbox reconciler, and a lockstep 'mirror' of validate_landing_evidence inside the resolver
findings.statement: TaskGroundTruth was meant to be the single classifier (TG-2, 'one classification table'). It has one consumer, Harness._reconcile_one_stranded. That consumer calls recovery_for and then overwrites the returned action four times before applying it: (a) LEAVE becomes MARK_DONE_WITH_PROVENANCE for a 'blocked' row with ON_MAIN or GONE_WITH_MERGE_MARKER; (b) LEAVE becomes RE_FILE_ESCALATION for 'blocked' with EXISTS_OFF_MAIN; (c) CONVERT_TO_BLOCKED becomes LEAVE when the pin is merge-remediable; (d) CONVERT_TO_BLOCKED becomes a log-only no-op behind convert_to_blocked_enforce. On top of these sit the degenerate-branch refinement and the deploy_phase/is_actively_held guards. Each override is justified in comments as 'a thin sweep-side upgrade rather than a change to θ1's reviewed table'. The 10-row _RECOVERY dict has a single BLOCKED row, so the policy for blocked tasks lives in harness prose. The 'has this task's work landed' question is answered independently in three more places. Harness._already_landed_dispatch_gate (465 lines) uses live git, and its docstring says its 'ancestry-path guards mirror _reconcile_one_stranded's own guard sequence'. merge_lane/worker.py::reconcile_landed_task uses the outbox. TaskGroundTruth._resolve_branch_state re-implements validate_landing_evidence's DISCOVERY rule; commit c471476137 calls it 'the documented mirror ... kept in sync (INV-5)'. _recover_crashed_tasks never consults the resolver and tests terminality with raw ('done', 'cancelled') literals, not shared.task_statuses.TERMINAL.
findings.proposal: Make the _RECOVERY table total and give policy one home. Extend _RecoveryShape with the pin class: classify_pins already returns vetoes_done_flip and the recovery variants, and MERGE_REMEDIABLE_ESC_CATEGORIES should come in as a frozen RecoveryPolicy argument so the module stays config-free. Then add explicit BLOCKED rows for ON_MAIN, GONE_WITH_MERGE_MARKER and EXISTS_OFF_MAIN, and make the CONVERT scoping and enforce flag policy inputs. The applier then becomes a pure switch on RecoveryAction, and the four rewrite blocks (about 250 lines including prose) are deleted. Replace the INV-5 mirror by having _resolve_branch_state call landing_evidence.validate_landing_evidence(mode=DISCOVERY). Route _already_landed_dispatch_gate and _recover_crashed_tasks' terminal-release checks through recovery_for. This deletes the gate's duplicated guard sequence and the hand-written terminal tuples. Enforce it with a test asserting that every (status in _RECONCILE_SWEEP_STATUSES x BranchStateKind x pin-class) cell has exactly one row.
findings.bug_history_link: 23a85fc9bb 'citation-attribution guard on resolver ON_MAIN fast-path' (2787, root cause of the 2729/2753 foreign-branch-tip phantom completions); c471476137 'ground-truth mirror accepts divergent on-main citation' (2870 lockstep edit); 0e512df518 'scope CONVERT_TO_BLOCKED to pins that blocked actually holds' (3539 review finding #3, where a converted row was re-moved by the applier's upgrades); b891223191 'the blocked arm's done-flip asks the conservative question' (3541 step-19); 02c041b229 'FIX 2 lineage guard accepts this branch's own no-ff merge commit'
findings.verdict_notes: recovery_for has a single production consumer, harness.py::Harness._reconcile_one_stranded (~L6140). Sweep-side upgrades of the table's answer exist there (blocked done-flip, RE_FILE, CONVERT scoping, convert_to_blocked_enforce at ~L6326). The code says so itself ('thin sweep-side upgrade'). _recover_crashed_tasks tests ('done','cancelled') as raw literals at ~L4224 and ~L4602. The dispatch-gate docstring says its guards 'mirror' the sweep. Line-level counts of the four overrides not re-derived.

findings.title: Fleet-redeploy mutual exclusion is an advisory check-then-act lease: the sweep script overwrites it unconditionally, and three deciders each re-implement the gate
findings.statement: The invariant 'at most one fleet sweep runs at a time' is enforced nowhere a breach could be refused. restart-all-orchestrators.sh::lease_acquire stamps started_ts and runs lease_set_current_unit with mktemp plus mv -f. It never reads an existing lease and takes no flock (the script contains no flock). Exclusion is attempted only by the callers, before they launch the script. StaleServiceRestartCoordinator.maybe_restart calls lease_is_live and then schedules a systemd-run --on-active of at least 5 seconds (Harness._build_orchestrator_restart_coordinator clamps orchestrator_restart_on_active_secs to max(..,5)), with a fresh transient-unit name per fire (orch-selfrestart-on-merge-{n}). The watchdog backstop calls _live_fleet_lease and relies on a FIXED transient-unit name as its own overlap guard. The liveness probe honours the lease only for current_unit. lease_release's own comment admits the coordinator 'is not covered by' the backstop's unit-name guard. The lease format is written by bash printf and parsed by two independent readers (lease_is_live in Python and _read_fleet_lease/_fleet_lease_age_secs in the watchdog). Its path is kept in four literal copies and its max-age in two, held together by parity tests. The age-based design is also what produces the residual 'a sweep overrunning max-age loses the lease'. Max-age exists only because a SIGKILLed sweep cannot remove its lease file.
findings.proposal: Make the sweep script the single enforcement point. It takes `exec 9>$LEASE_FILE.lock; flock -n 9 || { echo 'fleet sweep already in flight'; exit 0; }` before anything else, and evaluates the min-interval clock and head-start gates under that lock. A kernel lock dies with its holder, so max_age_secs, the overrun residual and the SIGKILL leak case all disappear. The coordinator and the watchdog tiers become pure triggers, and their pre-checks become optimisations rather than the guarantee. The lease JSON stays as an observability body for --report and for the liveness probe's current_unit check. Deletable: lease_is_live's age arithmetic, _fleet_lease_age_secs, the age halves of _live_fleet_lease, orchestrator_restart_lease_max_age_secs, test_fleet_lease_max_age_matches_config_default, and the fixed-unit-name overlap reasoning. Give the fused-memory tier the same flock in restart-fused-memory.sh, which closes its 'no lease at all' residual.
findings.bug_history_link: Deploy-clock and overlap collisions 4745/4754/4823/4905/5299; 4755 lease introduced, then fixed twice in both readers (27c1ebb600 'a pid too large for C pid_t reads as dead', 7f36992a89 'require a FINITE, NON-NEGATIVE age in both lease readers'); e6db65807d 'drop drain busy-grace 75m -> 10m to shrink the double-restart window'; f05c90113e 'guard the poll-ledger append so a reorder cannot cost a redeploy'; known residuals: overrunning sweep loses lease, fm tier unleased
findings.verdict_notes: The script has no flock. lease_acquire only stamps LEASE_STARTED_TS and calls lease_set_current_unit, which writes the lease via mktemp and mv -f without reading an existing lease. lease_release's own comment admits the coordinator uses a different transient-unit name and is not covered by the backstop's guard. Exclusion is therefore advisory and lives in the callers.

findings.title: Each deploy unit's code closure (watched paths) is hand-maintained in five lists that have already drifted; the orchestrator tier still misses shared/src/
findings.statement: The fact 'which source trees does this unit execute' decides both staleness tiers and both on-merge coordinators. It is stored as independent literals: watchdog WATCHED_PATHS (orchestrator/src, escalation/src, two pyproject files, uv.lock), watchdog FM_WATCHED_PATHS, OrchestratorConfig.orchestrator_restart_watch_prefixes with default ['orchestrator/src/'], the same key in dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml (five entries, so the default and the live value disagree), and fused_memory_restart_watch_prefixes. Nothing derives any of them from the workspace import graph. The orchestrator imports shared.* throughout (harness.py alone imports eleven shared modules), yet no orchestrator-tier list contains shared/src/, so a shared/ merge leaves the fleet running stale code with no staleness signal. Commit c51224e7ba (6521) fixed the fm list and added an import-closure test for that list only. Its message files the orchestrator-tier gap as follow-up ticket tkt_0RVJZ4RZ20B2F609EEEA6VQSX4. The watchdog also hard-codes REPO_DIR = '/home/leo/src/dark-factory'. That is another copy of the deployment fact, and it is the shape behind the 10-06 wire-skew incident (checkout HEAD differs from the running code).
findings.proposal: Introduce a single stdlib module, scripts/deploy_closure.py, with closure(root_member) -> list[str]. It is the derivation already written in tests/scripts/test_fm_watched_paths_import_closure.py, promoted from test to producer: uv workspace members plus the absolute-import walk, plus each member's pyproject.toml and uv.lock. The watchdog (stdlib, so it can load it by path) and both coordinators call it at startup, with the import-closure test reduced to a check that it runs. Delete the WATCHED_PATHS/FM_WATCHED_PATHS literals and both *_restart_watch_prefixes config fields, or keep the fields only as additive overrides. Derive REPO_DIR from the script's own location. This prevents the whole 6521/6543 'watched paths missing the import closure' class for every tier at once.
findings.bug_history_link: 6521 c51224e7ba 'fm staleness backstop watches escalation/src/ and orchestrator/src/' (esc-5649-3: fm ran old escalation code that raced reap_orphan_locks); 6543 LIVE; follow-up ticket tkt_0RVJZ4RZ20B2F609EEEA6VQSX4 (orchestrator tier missing shared/src/); 10-06 wire-skew incident (INV-2)
findings.verdict_notes: At 6551b75 the lists are independent literals. Watchdog WATCHED_PATHS has 5 entries and no shared/src/. Config default is ['orchestrator/src/']. The yaml has 5 entries, so default and live value disagree. FM_WATCHED_PATHS is ['fused-memory/src/','shared/src/']. REPO_DIR is hard-coded. c51224e7ba is NOT an ancestor of this checkout; it is on main. The claim's reference to it as a fix is true of main but not of the surveyed tree. The orchestrator-tier gap on shared/src/ holds.

findings.title: Cockpit DecisionRecords are a fleet-global second copy of escalation lifecycle, joined by a normalised-string composite key and synced by a poller that re-implements the escalation queue's on-disk layout
findings.statement: DecisionRecord copies escalation lifecycle fields (state, severity, escalation_id) into <fleet_root>/decisions/<id>.json. Escalation ids are unique only within one queue, so the join key is the triple (project string, escalations_dir path string, escalation_id string). Keeping that join correct needs normalize_escalations_dir (198 lines, including UNKNOWN_QUEUE sentinel handling and a long PROJECT_TOKEN_ALIASES decline essay), normalize_project_token (84 lines; the 2026-08-06 measurement found 41 open decisions split 22/17/2 across three spellings), declined_project_token_hint, unmatched_project_token_hint and migrate_decision_project_tokens (162 lines). These are ad-hoc parsers of internal values, which heuristic 12 forbids. State is synced by polling. reap_answered_decisions calls read_escalation_status, which re-implements EscalationQueue's layout: the root file, then an rglob over archive/YYYY-MM-DD. Its own docstring records an unbounded full-archive scan on every cycle, and decisions left OPEN forever when retention prunes the record. The upstream gaps are that the escalation package issues no stable queue identity and gives no notification on a terminal transition.
findings.proposal: Make the escalation store the single owner of decision state. The escalation package stamps a stable queue_id (a UUID file in the queue dir) and exports a typed EscalationRef(queue_id, escalation_id). DecisionRecord keeps only cockpit-owned fields (manual_boost, display, record_slug) keyed by EscalationRef. Its state is read through escalation.queue's own reader, or closed by a hook in EscalationQueue's resolve/dismiss path that writes the decision sidecar. Deletable: DECISION_CLOSE_MAP, read_escalation_status, the reap-decisions verb and its cron, the join role of normalize_escalations_dir and normalize_project_token, migrate_decision_project_tokens, the token-hint helpers, and merge_same_queue_refile's resurrection guard.
findings.bug_history_link: abbc8fba4a 'scope the reap-decisions join by queue, not just project' (3528); a987c5e389 + 5ecc6625e2 'match reap-decisions on the canonical project token' (3807); 828c5c2464 'refuse a cross-PROJECT id collision' (3559); 8e27421d18 'never let UNKNOWN_QUEUE displace the '' queue state' (3640); a1283e748b 'stop a same-queue re-file resurrecting a closed decision' (3872); 6164 LIVE 'DecisionRecord.record_slug stale after re-mint'
findings.verdict_notes: normalize_escalations_dir (L1834), PROJECT_TOKEN_ALIASES (L1887), normalize_project_token (L2032), migrate_decision_project_tokens (L2389), read_escalation_status (L2245) and reap_answered_decisions (L2318) all exist. read_escalation_status uses rglob over the archive with an explicit COST NOTE (L2263, L2281). Calling the token normalisers 'ad-hoc parsers' is a mild stretch. The join-key and polling structure is real.

findings.title: session_registry.py is five subsystems in one stdlib-only file; the forcing constraint is a choice in spawn-claude.sh
findings.statement: Stating the purpose takes four 'and's: session records and pid pointers (about lines 86-1070 plus the TTL reaper at 2524-2938), cockpit decision records (377-571, 1073-2523), role leases (3199-4214), X11/wmctrl window liveness (2938-3199), and an argparse CLI (4275-5772, with _run_write_decision alone at 376 lines). Heuristic 14 measurement. Prose: the module and NOTE blocks justify the single file by the stdlib-only, run-by-path constraint. Partition: an AST reference count across those five groups gives a DAG. CLI depends on everything. decisions -> records (11 refs) and io (1). leases -> records (11), io (2) and reaper (2, the pid predicate). wm -> records (8), reaper (2) and io (3). The only 'upward' edges are 4 refs from the path helpers into decisions_dir, which are path helpers that belong in io. No cycle or reach-back appears in any group. The obstacle is only skills/spawn/spawn-claude.sh line 65 invoking the file by absolute path. orchestrator/__init__.py is a one-line docstring, so `PYTHONPATH=$REPO_ROOT/orchestrator/src python3 -m orchestrator.session_registry` would stay stdlib-only.
