One porous edge already exists: service_restart.py imports the private session_registry._pid_alive.
findings.proposal: Turn it into a package orchestrator/session_registry/ with _io.py (atomic write, fleet_root and paths), records.py, decisions.py, leases.py, wm_liveness.py and __main__.py (the CLI). Each file imports only downward and all stay stdlib-only. Keep __init__ re-exporting only the public contract consumers use today: SessionRecord, Status, DecisionRecord, normalize_project_token, fleet_root and so on. Change spawn-claude.sh to invoke `-m orchestrator.session_registry` with PYTHONPATH. Keep TestStdlibOnlySelfContainment, pointed at the package. Expose pid_alive publicly (see the pid finding) so service_restart stops importing a private name.

findings.title: harness.py heuristic-14 protocol: the recovery-sweep and escalation-filing strata can be extracted with no cycle; the obstacles are test patch paths and __new__-built fixtures that production code bends around
findings.statement: Heuristic 14 measurement at 6551b75aba. Prose: 18,264 lines, 48.7% comments and docstrings, 461 'task NNNN' citations and 45 review-finding/amendment/esc- notes. Much of it is reviewer-answering prose ('SCOPE HONESTY', 'review finding #3'), which the Comments stance says belongs in commits. Partition by AST: (a) escalation filing, 29 methods and 2,270 lines, using only _escalation_queue, config, event_store and sentinel constants; core calls it 25 times and recovery 6. (b) Recovery sweeps, 32 methods and 4,319 lines, using 22 self attributes, mostly collaborators. Its upward calls into core are helpers (_filing_claimant_run_id x7, _delivered_checks_block x4, _resolve_task_worktree x3), and it owns state the dispatch core later reads (_recovered_plans, _preserved_worktrees, _recovered_sessions), which is transient promoted to instance lifetime (h5). It also reaches into collaborators' privates: git_ops._lane_lifecycle x7, _merge_worker._landed_outbox x4, git_ops._is_registered_worktree, git_ops._orphan_has_commits. (c) The watcher supervisor, 8 methods and 561 lines, using 9 attributes. With (a) at the bottom and (b) above it, neither stratum imports harness, so the split passes heuristic 13. Existing heuristic-13 symptoms show harness is already being reached back into: run_store.py imports HarnessReport/TaskReport from harness under TYPE_CHECKING; storm_window_bound.py imports _BY_DESIGN_RESTORE_OUTCOMES function-locally (noqa PLC0415); scripts/trial_module_tagger_haiku.py imports the private _extract_tagger_entries. Tests stance: 505 dotted-path references to orchestrator.harness.* in 89 test files (McpLifecycle 74, BriefingAssembler 74, Scheduler 70, detect_verified_green 27, MergeProvenance 18) freeze the import namespace. 41 Harness.__new__ constructions in 17 test files bypass __init__, and in response production code reads 26 attributes via getattr(self, '_x', None), with lazily seeded memos (_recovery_streak_memo, _recovery_process_latch). The constructor's invariants are therefore not guaranteed.
findings.proposal: Extract bottom-up. First, orchestrator/harness_escalations.py::HarnessEscalationFiler(queue, config, event_store, run_id), taking all _file_*/_resolve_*_escalation methods and the sentinel constants. Second, orchestrator/recovery_sweeps.py::RecoverySweeps(git_ops, scheduler, filer, ground_truth, event_store, config), whose startup pass returns a frozen RecoveryResult(plans, preserved, sessions) instead of mutating Harness fields. Promote git_ops._lane_lifecycle and _is_registered_worktree, and MergeWorker._landed_outbox, to public accessors. Move HarnessReport/TaskReport to run_store.py (it is their consumer) and _BY_DESIGN_RESTORE_OUTCOMES to storm_window_bound.py. Inject Scheduler, McpLifecycle and BriefingAssembler factories through the constructor so tests stop patching orchestrator.harness.*. Then delete the getattr-tolerance and replace Harness.__new__ fixtures with narrow constructions of the extracted classes. Record this measurement in the extraction commit rather than in the module docstring.

findings.title: _recover_crashed_tasks implements its adopt/preserve/clean decision twice (record-driven and heuristic paths), and the copies have already diverged
findings.statement: Harness._recover_crashed_tasks is 631 lines with one loop body. Its W11 record-driven branch for an ASSIGNED/IN_USE lane re-implements the heuristic branch below it, and its own comments say 'mirrored' ('Mirror the heuristic path's completed-steps / stamped-preservation decision (~2394-2434 below)', 'Semantic identity guard (Fix C, mirrored)', 'T10 amplifier fix, mirrored onto the record-driven path'). The duplicated pieces are the terminal-task release (`term_status in ('done', 'cancelled')` twice), the identity guard (get_task, then read_worktree_title, then quarantine plus emit), the completed-steps list comprehension, and plan.lock clearing. They have already diverged. For a stamped plan with zero completed steps, the heuristic branch calls _clear_recovery_artifact(entry, 'agent_session.json') and the record branch does not. The record branch's identity-mismatch quarantine transitions the durable lane state, and the heuristic branch's does not. The method also calls git_ops._lane_lifecycle.read/transition and git_ops._is_registered_worktree, both private. Step-16's review fix had to guard against re-issuing a RELEASED edge that cleanup_worktree had already written.
findings.proposal: Split the decision from the effects. Add a pure classify_recovered_worktree(entry_facts) -> WorktreeRecoveryAction (ADOPT_PLAN, PRESERVE_STAMPED, RELEASE_TERMINAL, QUARANTINE(reason), CLEAN, DEFER), computed once from a frozen WorktreeFacts covering lane record, registration, branch match, plan, title match and DB status. One applier executes each action, so lane-record transitions happen in exactly one place. Expose GitOps.lane_record(entry) and GitOps.is_registered_worktree publicly. This deletes the mirrored blocks and the two hand-written terminal tuples (use shared.task_statuses.TERMINAL), and it belongs in RecoverySweeps from the harness extraction finding.

findings.verdict_notes: _recover_crashed_tasks (L4075) contains a record-driven terminal-task release (L4223) and a heuristic terminal-task release (L4601), both on ('done','cancelled'). Comments in the method say 'mirrored' and 'Mirror the heuristic path's completed-steps...' (L4359). The agent_session.json clear appears only once, at L4668, in the heuristic path, and the record path has none. The record-path quarantine calls _lane_lifecycle.transition (L4329) via a private attribute. Divergence is real.

findings.title: TaskGroundTruth's private _pid_alive raises OverflowError on a corrupt plan.lock owner_pid, which escapes the stranded sweep and startup step 2d
findings.statement: TaskGroundTruth._resolve_live_claimant parses plan.lock with `parsed_pid = int(owner_pid)` followed by `_pid_alive(parsed_pid)` inside `except (TypeError, ValueError)`. task_ground_truth._pid_alive checks only `pid <= 0` and then calls os.kill. For a value beyond C long, os.kill raises OverflowError (verified locally: 'Python int too large to convert to C long'). OverflowError is caught neither there nor in derive_truth, nor in Harness._reconcile_stranded_in_progress, which catches only SetTaskStatusRejected. Startup step 2d (`await self._reconcile_stranded_in_progress()` in run()) is not wrapped, so one corrupt lock aborts orchestrator startup on every restart. That is a crash loop, and that resolver leg's comments say it exists precisely to degrade on 'one bad lock file'. A JSON `true` owner_pid becomes int 1, os.kill(1, 0) raises PermissionError, and the predicate answers 'alive', a phantom live claimant. Commit 27c1ebb600 hardened only session_registry._pid_alive against OverflowError, and its docstring says the harness and fm copies were left for follow-up. In production there are seven copies of the predicate with three contracts: harness (now dead in production, imported only by test_reconcile_stranded.py), task_ground_truth, shared/config_dir, fused-memory orchestrator_detector, session_registry, fleet_drain.sweep_alive (no pid<=0 guard; it relies on the drain parser) and the watchdog (type-guarded).
findings.proposal: Add shared/src/shared/proc_liveness.py::pid_alive(value: object) -> bool with the watchdog's contract: reject non-int, bool and pid <= 0 before os.kill, and treat OverflowError/OSError as dead. Import it in task_ground_truth, config_dir, fleet_drain and fused-memory's orchestrator_detector. Delete harness._pid_alive and repoint its test import. session_registry and the watchdog keep stdlib copies pinned to it by a parity test. Add a regression test with owner_pid=10**20 and owner_pid=true in plan.lock.
findings.bug_history_link: 27c1ebb600 'a pid too large for C pid_t reads as dead, not as a crash' (4755, fixed only the lease path); session_registry._pid_alive docstring 'widening them is filed as follow-up work'
findings.verdict_notes: _pid_alive guards only pid<=0 and catches ProcessLookupError, PermissionError and OSError. os.kill(10**30,0) raises OverflowError locally, and OverflowError is not an OSError. _resolve_live_claimant catches only (TypeError, ValueError) around int(owner_pid)/_pid_alive (L716). Harness._reconcile_stranded_in_progress catches only SetTaskStatusRejected and says other exceptions 'intentionally propagate'. Startup step 2d (L2803) is a bare await. harness._pid_alive is imported only by a test. Exact crash-loop impact depends on whether run() has an outer handler. I saw none around step 2d, but I did not trace the whole of run(). The precondition is a hand-corrupted lock.

findings.title: A task branch ref has a dozen writers and no owner: nothing enforces that main..task/N is task N's own delta, so each graft route got its own partial guard
findings.statement:
No module states or checks the invariant every consumer assumes: a task branch's commits beyond main are that task's own work, on a base that is on main or recorded as stacked. Measured writers of refs/heads/task/*:
- Creates: GitOps.create_interactive_worktree, GitOps._acquire_warm_lane_impl and GitOps.materialize_member_solo (worktree add -b); GitOps.rebind_branch_to_head and GitOps._reset_warm_lane (checkout -B).
- Rebases: 12 sites. Only 3 go through the post-condition wrapper GitOps.rebase_preserving_task_commits (TaskWorkflow._inter_iteration_rebase, the requeue rebase in GitOps.create_worktree, GitOps._reuse_warm_lane). The plain 'git rebase <target>' in GitOps.rebase_onto_main is called unguarded from TaskWorkflow._run_merge_phase, TaskWorkflow._handle_blocking_dep_report, TaskWorkflow._resolve_and_resubmit (return value ignored), merge_lane/worker.py::_do_train_merge, SuffixConflictTracker.bounce_conflicting_suffix_items (onto a speculative frozen tip) and GitOps._stack_member (onto an unlanded sibling).
- Deletes: GitOps._delete_branch_if_on_main, GitOps._cleanup_leftover_branch, GitOps.materialize_member_solo and GitOps.delete_solo_branch. They use different safety predicates, all of which count foreign commits as own work.
- Rename: GitOps.rename_worktree.
The stack-base ledger from task 5618 (branch_stack.py::StackBaseLedger) is written only in GitOps._stack_member and read only at stacking time and at merge admission (_unstack_before_merge, SpeculativeMergeWorker._unstack_redriven_member). GitOps.create_worktree branches a train member from its predecessor's tip at creation, and rebases onto that tip on requeue (via _resolve_predecessor_tip), without recording a ledger entry. metadata.train is never cleared, so a member whose predecessor derails carries foreign commits that unstack_from_unlanded_base reports as NOT_STACKED. Plain 'git rebase main' replays main..HEAD, so any earlier graft survives every later rebase. Four pending tasks each patch one point of this: 4752 (guard on the onto ref), 5144 (merge-admission check of foreign commits by citation), 5697 (rerere and abort rc on the rebase primitive) and 4669.
findings.proposal: Introduce orchestrator/task_branch.py::TaskBranch. It is the only code allowed to mutate refs/heads/<prefix>*, takes an injected GitRunner the way branch_stack does, and is held by GitOps. It records the branch's own base at creation, in refs/dark-factory/task-base/<branch> next to the stack-base ledger, and exposes create(from_main | stacked_on=predecessor), rebase_to_main(), stack_onto(), delete_if_empty(), rename() and own_delta(). rebase_to_main always runs 'git -c rerere.enabled=false rebase --onto <main> <own_base>', so a foreign prefix can never be replayed. It then asserts own_delta is preserved (today's rebase_preserving_task_commits post-condition, moved into the primitive), and raises with values when the abort fails. Enforce own_delta at creation, before every rebase and at merge admission, through one function. delete_if_empty judges own_delta, not main..branch. stack_onto is the only way to stack, so create_worktree's train path records the ledger too. What becomes deletable: the rebase_onto_main/rebase_preserving_task_commits split and its per-call-site choice, the per-site onto guard 4752 proposes, most of 5144's citation-based foreign-commit admission (it stays as a backstop only), and the separate unstack calls at stacking and admission. Bug classes prevented: 2403 (requeue reset to an unrelated tip), 3269 (sibling-tip graft, 103 foreign commits), 4405 and 4347 (warm-lane reuse leaking another task's commits), 4669, 4752, 5618 (census 10-03 cluster 1.1), and the 4818 review-cycle cost.

findings.verdict_notes: Verified git_ops.py::GitOps.rebase_preserving_task_commits callers: only workflow.py, git_ops 4864 and 8310 (three guarded sites). Unguarded rebase_onto_main callers: workflow.py 3838, 6782, 11867, merge_lane/worker.py 7110, suffix_graph.py 582, git_ops 9938 and 10170. StackBaseLedger.record is called only at git_ops.py 10180 (_stack_member). No single owner-level invariant found.

findings.title: The lane lock and warm-lane scripts form a cross-repo shell protocol defined only in prose: an overloaded exit code, a flag found by grepping script source, and lock ownership rebuilt from /proc/locks
findings.statement:
Several parties take <lane_dir>.lock with raw flock. Inside DF these are the leases, seeding, thinning and merge-verify. Outside DF they are reify's seed-warm-lane.sh and its warm-lane-gc timer, whose passes overlap; the docstring of _seed_rc_to_unavailable measures GC holds of 25-88s against a 30s wait. The lock path is defined in verify_cancel.py::lane_lock_path, and separately as "${LANE_DIR}.lock" in each shell script. The script's result is an exit code whose meaning depends on the script:
- 75 means DISK_PRESSURE from seed (_seed_rc_to_unavailable), but in thin-warm-lane.sh 75 means the lane flock is held by a live consumer.
- 77 means LOCK_CONTENDED, but only when DF passes --distinct-lock-refusal-rc.
- 76 is dormant, 124 is a lock timeout and 127 is a fault. 127 is still compared inline at 6 sites.
Whether a lane's copy of the script accepts a flag is decided by grepping the script's source text (_seed_script_text, which is lru-cached on mtime and size, and _seed_script_supports). Who holds the lock is never passed between the parties. DF rebuilds it from the kernel's /proc/locks (_settled_lane_lock_holder_pids, 157 lines) plus a process-global fd registry (_HELD_LANE_LOCK_FDS, which takes a threading lock) so that it can tell its own leaks from live holds (GitOps._lane_lock_self_owned_leak, 121 lines, and LaneLockSelfOwnedLeak). The missing upstream guarantee is a versioned script interface and an explicit lock handoff. Every fix in the 16x and 10x mined themes is a disagreement about who holds the lock: _seed_warm_lane refusing against its own lock, take_lane_lock=False meaning two things until SeedLaneLock (4913), the 4211 refusal rc, 4930, gc deleting live trees (2599, 3027), 2685, 3003, 4502, 3783.
findings.proposal: Create orchestrator/lane_lease.py::LaneLease as the one way to hold <lane_dir>.lock. It is a context-managed value carrying the fd, the inode and a holder role. Code that needs the lock receives the LaneLease, and a script it spawns inherits the held fd through an env var such as DF_LANE_LOCK_FD, replacing --assume-lane-lock-held. Leak detection then follows from the lease object's lifetime, so the global registry and the /proc/locks inference are no longer needed to discriminate. Version the script interface. Each warm-lane script answers '--protocol' with JSON giving its version, supported flags and outcome codes. DF parses that once per script identity into a typed SeedScriptProtocol, and the script prints its outcome as one structured line (e.g. 'DF-OUTCOME lane_lock_contended') instead of an overloaded rc. The protocol definition lives in scripts/warm-lane/README.md and is mirrored by one Python enum. What becomes deletable: _seed_script_text, _seed_script_supports and the two named probes; the rc 75/77 overloading and the dormant 76 arm; SeedLaneLock's three modes (holding a LaneLease is the mode); _HELD_LANE_LOCK_FDS with its lock and register/forget helpers; _settled_lane_lock_holder_pids; and most of _lane_lock_self_owned_leak. Bug classes prevented: the self-refusal and contended-misclassification classes, and gc-vs-live-holder reaping.
findings.bug_history_link: 92db4c8339 'stop _seed_warm_lane self-refusing on its own lane lock'; c8677e4b26 'ephemeral_worktree asserts its own held lane lock to seed (task 4913)'; e4e952dae3/990e9b0476/644b4037a4 (task 4211); 923371fb5d (task 3003); 6fc699df42/e5c5f07ba6 (task 2685); da93963b34 'a lane lock that will not open is not proof the tree is unleased'; tasks 2599, 3027, 4502, 3783, 4930
findings.verdict_notes: Verified _seed_script_supports/_seed_script_text (source-text grep of flags), _SEED_DISTINCT_LOCK_REFUSAL_RC_FLAG, _seed_rc_to_unavailable, and verify_cancel.py::lane_lock_path exist. The external shell scripts (thin-warm-lane.sh) are outside this tree, so the exit-75 overload in that script is unverified here; the DF-side protocol claims hold.

findings.title: Whether a worktree or branch holds work to keep is answered by seven predicates with opposite failure directions, so some guards read a git error as 'clean'
findings.statement:
One decision is computed in seven places within GitOps:
- _branch_has_commits_beyond_main: fail-safe True.
- _orphan_has_commits: existence gate, then the above.
- worktree_has_unsaved_work: re-inlines both the rev-list count and status, fail-safe True.
- _worktree_dirty: fail-safe True.
- has_uncommitted_work: 'return rc == 0 and bool(output)', so a git error means CLEAN.
- has_dirty_working_tree: ignores both rcs, so a git error means CLEAN.
- worktree_head_beyond_main: returns None both for no unmerged work and for an unreadable HEAD.
rebase_preserving_task_commits adds an eighth inline count with its own fail-safe rules. The fail-open variants guard real decisions. merge_lane/worker.py::classify_and_merge uses has_uncommitted_work as the 'agent started work since snapshot' guard before emitting a terminal already_merged and before the rebased-landing backstop. GitOps._rebase_off_base uses it to refuse un-stacking a dirty tree. Harness._file_dirty_tree_escalation uses has_dirty_working_tree, and a failed git diff there auto-resolves the main-checkout dirty-tree L2 as 'tree now clean at startup'. Callers already compensate: GitOps.reap_interactive_worktrees re-probes with _worktree_head_readable because worktree_head_beyond_main's None is ambiguous (its own comment says so). None of the predicates excludes foreign stacked commits from 'own work'.
findings.proposal: Introduce one typed verdict in a small module, orchestrator/worktree_state.py::WorkPresence. It has a single async probe(worktree, branch) that returns a frozen value: own_commits (int | Unknown), dirty_tracked (tuple | Unknown) and head_readable. Unknown is a distinct variant, never folded into True or False, so every caller states its fail direction explicitly at the call site, which is reviewable. Implement own_commits through TaskBranch.own_delta from the task-branch finding. What becomes deletable: the seven predicates (each caller maps WorkPresence to its own decision), _worktree_head_readable's compensating second probe, and the inline counting in rebase_preserving_task_commits. Bug classes prevented: a git hiccup letting a reap, delete, already_merged eject or L2 auto-resolve proceed on a false 'clean'.
findings.bug_history_link: task 5026 (dce8bddf81 already_merged false positive), task 3576 shape in _cleanup_leftover_branch, the reap_interactive_worktrees readability compensation; the fail-open sites themselves are speculative (no incident traced)
findings.verdict_notes: has_uncommitted_work returns rc == 0 and bool(output), so a git error reads as clean. has_dirty_working_tree ignores both rcs. The other predicates exist at the cited names (_branch_has_commits_beyond_main, _orphan_has_commits, _worktree_dirty, worktree_has_unsaved_work, worktree_head_beyond_main). The reviewer itself labels the fail-open impact speculative.

findings.title: Offline lane: once a fingerprint is promoted to a blocker it is never cleared when its fix lands, so a recurrence is silently appended to a done task for up to 14 days
findings.statement: OfflineLaneWorker._maybe_promote_blocker begins with 'if fp in self._promoted_blockers: return'. The DONE arm sits below that early return; it pops open_fix_tasks and _red_advance_counts and calls self._promoted_blockers.discard(fp). For a promoted fingerprint, that arm is unreachable, and so is the discard. No other code clears open_fix_tasks. Scenario: a fingerprint passes offline_lane_red_advances_before_blocker, the blocker is filed, and the fix task later lands (done). The next red run with the same failing set takes the 'fp in self.open_fix_tasks' branch of _handle_red_run. _update_existing_fix_task then appends a suspect range to the DONE task and returns via the early exit. No new task and no escalation are filed. Since task 5352 (f96d10bbd4) these three sidecars are durable PersistentMap/PersistentSet files with _RED_STATE_TTL = 14 days, so a redeploy no longer clears the stale entry. The same structure caused 3434ee0584: three files, one subject, no joint atomicity. They also mirror task-store status, which the worker can already query through task_client.get_status.
findings.proposal: Immediate fix: run the task_client status check before the promoted-early-return. When status == 'done', clear all three entries regardless of promotion. Structural fix: drop the private open_fix_tasks mirror and key fix-task dedup on the task store itself. Submit with suggestion_hash = fingerprint and query open status by that key, so one record per fingerprint lives where the contract says dispositions live. The three sidecars collapse to one RedRecord{task_id, advances, promoted} map, which removes the divergence 3434ee0584 had to tolerate. A regression test should drive the public run loop through red, promote, done, then red again.
findings.bug_history_link: f96d10bbd4 'the offline lane's red-path state survives a redeploy (5352)' made it durable; 3434ee0584 'count reads tolerate divergent guard files' is the same three-sidecar structure; no incident observed yet
findings.verdict_notes: _maybe_promote_blocker returns at 'if fp in self._promoted_blockers' (line 854) before the DONE arm that pops open_fix_tasks and discards the promoted entry. Grep shows no other clearing of open_fix_tasks. _handle_red_run takes 'fp in self.open_fix_tasks' into _update_existing_fix_task, which appends a suspect range. All three sidecars have the 14-day TTL. The done-clear arm is therefore unreachable for promoted fingerprints.

findings.title: advance_main returns failure details through _last_* instance attributes that the merge lane reads with getattr, never initialised or reset
findings.statement: GitOps.advance_main returns a frozen AdvanceOutcome(result, advanced_sha, rebased_from, rebased_onto). The details a caller needs on four failure results are written instead to instance attributes: _last_overlap_files, _last_stash_dirty_files, _last_recovery_branch, _last_park_lock_info (a dict carrying lock_path, age_seconds and waited_seconds). None of them is set in GitOps.__init__ or reset at the start of advance_main. merge_lane/gates.py::_map_advance_failure reads them after the call with getattr(git_ops, '_last_...', None), five times, falling back to '(unknown)' or {}. That is temporal coupling to a prior call, private-attribute reach across modules, and attribute names as strings that pyright cannot check, so a rename silently degrades an L2 reason to '<unknown>'. The fields arrived one incident at a time (2758 dirty files, 3060 park-lock info, the recovery-branch outcome of task 1671). Each needed matching edits in both modules plus prose explaining the side-channel ('Mirrors the _last_overlap_files / _last_stash_dirty_files shape').
findings.proposal: Make each payload a typed field of AdvanceOutcome: overlap_files, dirty_files, recovery_branch and park_lock (a frozen ParkLockInfo with lock_path, age_seconds and waited_seconds). Validate in __post_init__ that each field is present exactly for its result, so a violation names the result and the missing field. _map_advance_failure reads outcome.<field>. All five getattr reads, the four _last_* attributes and their explanatory prose become deletable. This also takes ~1,400 lines of the advance/park cluster one step closer to a standalone main_advance.py (see the git_ops.py partition finding).
findings.bug_history_link: tasks 2758 (ee1764947f, 4fdcbad165), 3060 (67d240c4d5, 4918285a76, 66060d2fea), 1671; no stale-read incident observed (speculative as a bug)
findings.verdict_notes: _last_overlap_files, _last_stash_dirty_files, _last_recovery_branch and _last_park_lock_info are assigned only inside advance_main (git_ops 14438-14737), with no declarations or init elsewhere. merge_lane/gates.py reads them via getattr at lines 1108, 1129, 1158, 1203 and 1229.

findings.title: rebase_recovery.py compensates on abort paths for rerere settings that the orchestrator already has the means to own
findings.statement: The shared repository's .git/config sets rerere.enabled=true and rerere.autoupdate=true (measured with git config --show-origin). That is the source of the dangling MERGE_RR segfault (rc 139) and the stale MERGE_RR.lock (rc 128) that the 1,133-line rebase_recovery.py exists to survive. Its own docstring says that prefixing with RECOVERY_GIT ('-c rerere.enabled=false') 'neutralises the crash and the stale-lock rc 128 in one stroke'. That prefix is applied only to the four aborts. All rebase primitives still run with rerere on and autoupdate on: GitOps.rebase_onto_main, GitOps.materialize_member_solo, the advance_main remerge and branch_stack.rebase_own_delta. Task 5697 (pending) measured that autoupdate can silently re-stage a stale recorded resolution of merge_lane_ratchet_baseline.json, a correctness hazard and not just a crash. The orchestrator already owns convergence of this same config file: GitOps.disable_shared_repo_auto_maintenance forces gc.auto=0 and maintenance.auto=false with --replace-all (d023b91a93). So the missing guarantee sits in DF's own control.
findings.proposal: Give the orchestrator one owner for the git config of the git processes it spawns. Either have _run (or the GitRunner injected into TaskBranch, branch_stack and rebase_recovery) prepend '-c rerere.enabled=false -c rerere.autoupdate=false' to every rebase, merge and cherry-pick argv, or extend disable_shared_repo_auto_maintenance into a converge_shared_repo_config that pins both keys repo-wide, if Leo does not want interactive rerere. rebase_recovery then shrinks to the stale-lock sweep that agent-run git still needs. The MERGE_RR scan, quarantine and specimen machinery can stay for operator use via the CLI but leaves the merge-lane hot path. An AST tripwire in the style of TestGitOpsAbortUniformity, asserting that no bare ['git','rebase'] vector survives, keeps the rule uniform. Bug classes prevented: rerere segfault on abort, a stale lock wedging an abort, and silent re-staging of a stale resolution.
findings.bug_history_link: task 4797 (12 review-round commits 09-13..09-21, e.g. 657dea9b05, f2a9747883, 17ee985158), task 5030 incident, task 5697 (live), 5029 sighting (602ecf86); d023b91a93 shows the config-convergence precedent
findings.verdict_notes: git config --show-origin shows rerere.enabled=true and rerere.autoupdate=true in the shared .git/config. RECOVERY_GIT (-c rerere.enabled=false) is applied at rebase_recovery.py line 1036 for aborts. The rebase primitives (git_ops 9828, 10378, 14211, branch_stack 288) run without it. No rerere handling exists outside rebase_recovery.py. GitOps.disable_shared_repo_auto_maintenance exists at 4482 as the precedent.

findings.title: git_ops.py partitions cleanly into six modules with no heuristic-13 symptom once _run moves down a layer; the private git_ops._run is today the factory-wide runner and test seam
findings.statement:
This is the heuristic 14 measurement. Prose: 9,280 of 15,857 lines (58.5%). The module docstring is wholly about the retired .task/ guards and records no size measurement. Partition of GitOps by the self-state each cluster touches (AST scan):
(a) lane locks and leases, 3446-4254 plus module 2230-2593: worktree_base, the pools, _lane_lifecycle.
(b) worktree create, seed and scripts, 4254-6582: config, project_root, worktree_base, warm_lane_pool, _interactive_wt_lock, _warm_lane_audit_cache.
(c) lane acquire and release, 6582-9100.
(d) branch lifecycle, 9100-10486: config, project_root, the merge-marker index.
(e) main-evidence probes, 10486-11700: only project_root, config.main_branch and _effect_probe_memo.
(f) merge-to-main and merge worktrees, 12082-14063: config, project_root, worktree_base.
(g) advance, recover and park, 14063-15460: config, project_root, the _last_* side channels.
No candidate needs a private of another cluster. The only heuristic-13 symptom each candidate would hit is an upward import of the module-global git_ops._run and git_ops.WorktreeMissing. For example, main_evidence.py would need 'from orchestrator.git_ops import _run' while git_ops imports main_evidence: a cycle. That same private name is already imported by seven production modules: merge_lane/gates.py, merge_lane/disposition.py, merge_lane/landing_evidence.py, merge_lane/skew_tripwire.py (function-local), verify.py (3 function-local imports), delivered_checks.py (as a default argument) and scheduler.py. Tests patch 'orchestrator.git_ops._run' 235 times across 25 files. A from-import binds at import time, so these patches already miss calls made from merge_lane/gates.py, and any extraction would silently escape them. This is the same divergence that froze merge_queue's split (merge-queue.4). The ratchet makes every git_ops change costly in a way unrelated to the change: 504b996013, a82d7010dd, 8f4182d742 and ef6717321b exist only to trim or move prose so the file stays under its baseline.
findings.proposal: Step 1, which unlocks the rest: move _run, WorktreeMissing and the stderr classifiers into orchestrator/git_runner.py. Make it a public GitRunner protocol that GitOps receives at construction, as branch_stack and rebase_recovery already do. Tests inject a fake runner instead of patching 'orchestrator.git_ops._run', and the seven production importers take the public name. Step 2: extract the clusters measured above as downward-importing modules that take the runner and the minimal state: lane_lease.py (a), main_evidence.py (e, together with CommitEffectProbe/ConflictProbe and the merge-marker index), main_advance.py (g, with the typed AdvanceOutcome from the side-channel finding), task_branch.py (d, from the task-branch finding) and merge_worktrees.py (f). GitOps keeps worktree creation and lane acquisition. Record the measurement in the extraction commit, with a one-line pointer in the module docstring. The heuristic 13 checks per file are: each imports only git_runner, lane_lifecycle, warm_lane_pool, branch_stack and config, and none is imported back by a lower layer. The 235 test patches, the from-import divergence hazard and the prose-trimming commits all go away.
findings.bug_history_link: ratchet-appeasement commits 504b996013 (3778), a82d7010dd (4913), 8f4182d742 (4155), ef6717321b (4797, which is how rebase_recovery.py was born); merge-queue.4 is the precedent for patch-path-frozen extractions
findings.verdict_notes: The _run import fan-out is real: verify.py (3 function-local), merge_lane/gates.py, disposition.py, landing_evidence.py and skew_tripwire.py import it. The cluster line ranges and the 235-patches / 25-files counts were not recounted. The clean-partition claim ('no candidate needs a private of another cluster') is an AST-scan assertion that was not independently re-derived, and 'no heuristic-13 symptom' is stated more strongly than the evidence supports.

findings.title: Dependency readiness has no single definition: _deps_satisfied's meaning is selected by which optional caches each caller passes
findings.statement: Scheduler._deps_satisfied (196 lines) returns a bool. Four optional parameters (external_status_cache, external_resolver_failed, delivered_check_cache, terminal_dep_records) default to 'that gate is off', so each caller picks the meaning of 'dependencies satisfied' by which arguments it passes. Five call sites use three meanings. _eligible_for_dispatch checks local, external and delivered-check deps. _stamp_milestone_deps_satisfied checks local and external deps. _park_gc_reason, _owner_is_live_dispatchable and _phase_redispatch_stranded_blocked check local deps only. _owner_is_live_dispatchable's docstring calls it the 'logical INVERSE of the _park_gc reclaimability predicate', and its body is a hand re-coding of that predicate, not a call to it. The bool cannot express 'unknown' (resolver failed, check not evaluated this tick), so dispatch has to fold unknown into False, and GC has no way to keep parks on unknown. An unfetchable terminal dep record is skipped (a deliberate fail-OPEN 'continue' in both _deps_satisfied and _compute_delivered_check_cache), so a failed read cannot be told apart from a dep that has no checks. Effect in the field: a blocked, deferred or external-dep-waiting owner keeps its parks indefinitely (esc-6040-7). Task 1580 design decision 4 kept park GC on the 'legacy local-only call' because only the kwarg form was available.
findings.proposal: Introduce orchestrator/dependency_verdict.py::DependencyVerdict, a frozen value with an overall tri-state SATISFIED / UNSATISFIED / UNKNOWN. Each blocking dep carries a reason enum: LOCAL_STATUS, EXTERNAL_STATUS, RESOLVER_FAILED, DELIVERED_FAILED, DELIVERED_UNEVALUATED, RECORD_UNAVAILABLE. Compute it once per tick, in a phase placed after external_dep_policy and delivered_check_gate, into ctx.dep_verdicts: dict[str, DependencyVerdict]. Every consumer reads the verdict and states its own policy for UNKNOWN: dispatch waits, park GC keeps the parks, redispatch leaves the task. Delete the four optional kwargs, _owner_is_live_dispatchable's copy, and the per-caller comments explaining why a cache is omitted. The fail-open 'record unavailable' becomes the named reason RECORD_UNAVAILABLE that each consumer must handle. Task 6518 is building dependency_verdict.py for park GC only. Extending it to all five sites makes it the single definition, rather than a sixth spelling.
findings.bug_history_link: esc-6040-7 / task 6518 (park GC ignores external and delivered deps, status-blind D4 guard: 'a second, status-blind copy of the GC predicate'); task 1580 7f8540b892 design decision 4 (GC kept local-only); task 2692 (delivered-check gate a no-op when TERMINAL dep records were absent); task 5910 (FAILED check on a done dep wedges its dependent); 6040 7a04d28d80 (pin-release completion with no eligibility check).
findings.verdict_notes: Signature has the four optional gate kwargs defaulting to off. Call sites differ as claimed: _eligible_for_dispatch passes all, _stamp_milestone_deps_satisfied passes external only, _owner_is_live_dispatchable, _park_gc_reason and _phase_redispatch_stranded_blocked pass none. _owner_is_live_dispatchable's docstring says 'logical INVERSE of the _park_gc reclaimability predicate' and its body re-codes it (terminal, missing, deps) instead of calling _park_gc_reason.

findings.title: Stranded-blocked recovery has two deciders with contradictory rules: the TG-2 recovery table forbids the blocked->pending revert the scheduler sweep performs every tick
findings.statement: task_ground_truth._RECOVERY is documented as the single recovery-action table (TG-2) that the harness reconcile sweep applies through TaskGroundTruth.recovery_for. Its row (g) states that 'blocked discipline forbids a silent blocked->pending revert'. It maps a stranded blocked task with no landing evidence and no open escalation to RE_FILE_ESCALATION. Every other blocked shape, including EXISTS_OFF_MAIN, falls through to LEAVE. Scheduler._phase_redispatch_stranded_blocked (260 lines, task 2408 'mechanism 2') runs every tick and flips those same blocked rows to pending. It does not consult TaskGroundTruth. It applies its own hand-coded gate chain: not dispatched, the deterministic carve-out, workflow_cancel_recent, the cooldown, is_stranded_blocked, local-only deps, and recovery pins. Its docstring says the gates 'mirror harness Fix #1b gate 4/5'. Only the pin predicate is shared, through recovery_pins (task 3541), and that module exists because the pin rule had drifted into 'E7's catalogued five copies'. The harness live-claimant docstring names the scheduler sweep as the recovery edge for the rows it skips, so the two sweeps coordinate only through prose. Because the scheduler sweep runs per tick, it reaches a stranded blocked row before the periodic harness sweep, and row (g) never fires for any shape the scheduler accepts.
findings.proposal: Make TaskGroundTruth.recovery_for the only decider for blocked rows. Add the blocked->REVERT_TO_PENDING shapes as explicit _RECOVERY rows, with the scheduler's gates becoming TruthReport fields (in_cancel_grace, in_cooldown, deterministic, deps_verdict from finding 1). Row (g)'s contradiction is then settled once, in one table, by a ruling. The scheduler phase, or a single sweep, calls recovery_for and applies the returned action. Delete the inline gate chain in _phase_redispatch_stranded_blocked, the 'mirrors Fix #1b' prose, and the cross-docstring coordination. This would have prevented the class where one sweep re-pends a row another mechanism deliberately parked.
findings.bug_history_link: Feedback memory 'park on an INFO-severity L2 does NOT hold the task — the stranded-blocked sweep re-pends it in seconds' (3 specimens, owner 4082); stranding-remediation PRD (stranded-blocked reaper re-pended into a scheduler paused 26 min); task 3535 (silent skips in this phase); tasks 3539/3717 (39 recovery_vetoed emissions over 10.5h churn); esc-3163 (a false 'no records' read routed a pinned strand into a revert); task 3541 (five copies of the pin rule).
findings.verdict_notes: The phase hand-codes its own gates (dispatched, deterministic, workflow_cancel_recent, cooldown, is_stranded_blocked, local deps, records_pin_blocked_recovery) and then calls set_task_status(tid,'pending'). It never consults TaskGroundTruth. task_ground_truth.py::_RECOVERY row (g) says 'blocked discipline forbids a silent blocked->pending revert'. Small overstatement: row (g) is keyed on GONE_NO_MARKER, not on all no-evidence shapes. The contradiction is real.

findings.title: TickContext defaults look like computed results, so a phase ordered before its producer silently reads 'every external dep unresolved' and 'nothing delivered'
findings.statement: W10 (task 2236) replaced the 720-line acquire_next with 21 _phase_* methods. They are invoked as getattr(self, f'_phase_{label}') over a tuple of strings and share one mutable TickContext with about 20 fields. Each phase's read and write sets are stated only in its docstring. Producer-written fields default to values that cannot be told apart from real results. external_cache defaults to {}, which reads as 'every external dep unresolved'. delivered_check_cache defaults to {}, which reads as 'gate on, nothing delivered'; only _phase_delivered_check_gate's explicit None means 'gate off'. A phase that runs before its producer therefore gets a wrong answer, not an error. park_gc and redispatch_stranded_blocked run before external_dep_policy and delivered_check_gate. _phase_redispatch_stranded_blocked's docstring spends a paragraph on why it must NOT forward ctx.external_cache. Task 6518's D3 has to move park GC for the same reason. The only enforcement is test_tick_phase_order_literal in test_scheduler_tick_phases.py. It pins the whole tuple literal, which records the order but none of the pairwise producer-before-consumer constraints that justify it.
findings.proposal: Register phases as data: a frozen Phase(name, fn, reads: frozenset[CtxField], writes: frozenset[CtxField]) list in place of label strings and getattr. A module-import check, also exercised by a test, asserts that every read field is written by an earlier phase or by the preamble. Phase-produced TickContext fields start as an _UNSET sentinel, and the accessor raises an error naming the field and the reading phase (INV-2), so an early read fails loudly instead of returning an empty dict. Delete the getattr string dispatch, the literal-tuple pin test, the docstring 'Reads:/Writes:' paragraphs, and the 'deliberately do not forward ctx.external_cache' caveats. This prevents the 6518 D3 trap, and it lets a new phase (as in 2692) be inserted by a declared dependency rather than by reasoning in prose about position.
findings.bug_history_link: Task 6518 D3 (park GC placed before the caches it would need); the documented trap in _phase_redispatch_stranded_blocked; task 2692 (backfill_terminal_dep_records inserted because a phase's assumption that dep records were present was false); γ2 (backfill_dep_status exists because the active-only fetch broke _deps_satisfied).
findings.verdict_notes: The TickContext defaults are as described (external_cache {}, delivered_check_cache {}) and the phase order matches the finding. The enforcement claim is wrong. tests/test_scheduler_tick_phases.py::test_tick_phase_order_literal contains pairwise order.index(...) < order.index(...) assertions, for example cooldown_gc before redispatch_stranded_blocked, delivered_check_gate right after external_dep_policy, and delivered_check_gate before build_candidates. These are producer-before-consumer constraints. The missing invariant is real only for the default values themselves. It is overstated as having no pairwise enforcement.

findings.title: 'Is the producer's capability on main' is evaluated by three independent runners with separate collapse, timeout and cache logic, and the done-side gate is not on every done path
findings.statement: Scheduler._compute_delivered_check_cache (406 lines) calls run_delivered_check itself. It wraps each call in its own asyncio.wait_for that maps a timeout to ERRORED, and re-implements the verdict collapse 'all DELIVERED, else first FAILED, else ERRORED'. delivered_checks.verify_delivered_checks_on_main implements the same collapse and timeout mapping a second time; its comment reads 'mirror scheduler.py 3116-3129', a line pin that is already stale. merge_lane/landing_evidence._delivered_checks_differential is a third direct caller of run_delivered_check. Only the scheduler copy carries a persistent cache. Its keying and eviction ((dep, main_sha, descriptor_digest), DELIVERED-only stickiness, pruning of stale digest variants) and the never-evicted _terminal_dep_record_cache were each added by a separate fix. The record cache's docstring admits that a checks descriptor added to an already-warmed checkless record is unobserved until restart. On the producer side, gate_mark_done_on_delivered_checks covers a listed set of mark-done seams. Its docstring says the workflow's own post-merge success stamp is 'Deliberately NOT routed'. So a task can reach done while its check evaluates FAILED, and the consumer gate then wedges its dependent. That is the shape 5910 describes, and the codebook's 'unverified-task-premises' (dep done != capability delivered).
findings.proposal: Create one DeliveredCapabilityOracle in orchestrator/delivered_checks.py. It owns evaluation (one runner, one collapse returning DeliveredChecksVerdict), the (dep, sha, digest) cache with its eviction rules, the per-call budget, and record freshness. Both the scheduler gate (through a DeliveredCheckGate that adds the streak and escalation policy) and gate_mark_done_on_delivered_checks call it; landing_evidence does too. A consumer-side FAILED on a done dep then has the same verdict and cache entry the producer gate would have seen. Delete the scheduler's inline wait_for, collapse and cache-key code (most of _compute_delivered_check_cache) and the cross-module 'mirror' comments. Decide the post-merge stamp routing once, in the oracle's caller contract, rather than by an exemption in a docstring.
findings.bug_history_link: 1d73b2290d 'cache only DELIVERED sticky, re-run FAILED every sweep' (2783); 9eb1f2a7e1 / 91c9aae17c / 4f43da9639 descriptor digest in the cache key and stale-variant pruning (2975); task 2977 (record cache served stale descriptors, esc-2911); 74108cf940 (2580 hold detail on cache-hit False); 33a52467db (3057 kill-switch and withhold race); tasks 4545/5998 (stale descriptor resyncs); task 5910 (live); task 2782 (reblock recurrence).
findings.verdict_notes: run_delivered_check is called directly at three sites: scheduler.py (inside asyncio.wait_for at about line 4122), delivered_checks.py::verify_delivered_checks_on_main (about line 366) and merge_lane/landing_evidence.py (about line 961). The collapse and timeout-to-ERRORED logic is duplicated; the delivered_checks.py comment says 'mirror scheduler.py 3116-3129', a stale line pin. The gate_mark_done_on_delivered_checks docstring says the workflow's post-merge stamp is 'Deliberately NOT routed'.

findings.title: DeployState and its legal-transition table were added beside the legacy deploy stamps, and the 1,212-line DeterministicRunner.run still resumes from stamp presence
findings.statement: DeterministicRunner.run is 1,212 lines with 36 return statements and 63 branching nodes. It picks a resume branch by reading the raw metadata stamps gate_escalated_at, before_done_ran_at, before_done_verified_at and before_done_scheduled_at. Tasks 2239/2240 added a typed DeployState with a legal-transition table (deploy_state._LEGAL, enforce_transition). _advance_deploy_phase writes the phase together with the same stamps passed as 'evidence', so the same fact is persisted twice. The resume logic consults DeployState.phase in only two places (ESCALATED as resolution proof, RAN for the crash-window re-verify). Where deploy_state is absent it falls back to a documented 'pre-ζ bare-existence' migration shim. The pure-gate, curator and predicate modes have no phase at all, only gate_escalated_at. The stamps have become a cross-process contract. They are blessed but untyped keys in shared.task_metadata (before_done_scheduled_at is not even in that set). fused-memory stage1_stall_detector parses gate_escalated_at as a raw ISO string, and live_workflow_detector and escalation/server also read the stamps. The modes are orthogonal dimensions (curator, pure gate, predicate, cross-unit, self-restart, unit-less deploy) × resume position × always_escalates, but they are encoded as nested inline ifs. The file is 57% docstring or comment by line.
findings.proposal: Extend shared.deploy_state into one DeterministicProgress record covering every mode: add GATE_FILED for the pure-gate and predicate modes, and carry scheduled-unit evidence in the record. Parse metadata once at entry into DeterministicMode (CURATOR_GATE, PURE_GATE, PREDICATE, DEPLOY_CROSS_UNIT, DEPLOY_SELF, DEPLOY_UNITLESS). Derive the resume position only from the record's phase. Make run() a dispatch table of {(mode, phase) -> handler}. A one-shot backfill stamps a phase on in-flight legacy tasks. After that, the stamps become derived projections written only by the record, or are retired once the fused-memory and escalation readers switch to the shared model. Delete the pre-ζ shim, the stamp reads in run(), the duplicated 'evidence' payloads, and the crash-window inference branches that rebuild the phase from combinations of stamps.
findings.bug_history_link: eaf1e89978 / 9412f85120 (2954 pure-gate resume needs archive-inclusive proof); aafa8cfd2c / 52eb221b31 (2983 crash-window backstop for a completed scheduled self-deploy); 90daea481d / 8f44b67514 / 692d03eeda (4048 milestone_gate redundant ESCALATED advance and a best-effort deploy-path write); e3f11d89bc (guard best-effort advances against illegal-transition fallout); 055df86035 (2331); a1e8c9aed2 / 06fc40ef78 (4157); 7c5ef373b5 (_current_deploy_state narrowing).
findings.verdict_notes: run spans lines 3314 to 4525, about 1212 lines. Both deploy_state.py files exist (shared and orchestrator, with _LEGAL in the orchestrator one). The runner persists deploy_state and the legacy stamps together via _advance_deploy_phase evidence. before_done_scheduled_at is absent from shared task_metadata, and fused-memory stage1_stall_detector reads gate_escalated_at as raw metadata. The parallel-representation point is slightly judgmental because the stamps are documented as the pre-zeta migration path, but the oversized function holds.

findings.title: One per-task dispatch lifecycle is spread over 18 task-keyed dicts whose lockstep invariants live in prose, and the stale sweep GCs four of them
findings.statement: Scheduler.__init__ is 550 lines. Besides 10 StreakCounters, it creates separate task-keyed containers for one task's dispatch life: _dispatched, _dispatched_priority, _last_dispatch_at, _requeue_until, _requeue_cooldown_meta, _requeue_counts, _transient_requeue_counts, _requeue_history, _pending_transient_cooldown, _skip_count, _pending_anchor, _module_cache, _workflow_cancel_at, _merge_phase_at, _backfill_grants, _delivered_check_error_streak, _terminal_dep_record_cache and _fallback_warned. The invariants between them are written in prose. clear_requeue_count explains why _requeue_until is 'deliberately NOT popped' while _requeue_cooldown_meta is ('meta never OUTLIVES its deadline'). _phase_stale_sweep GCs exactly four of them (_last_dispatch_at, _skip_count, _module_cache, _pending_anchor). _terminal_dep_record_cache is never evicted. _delivered_check_error_streak is popped only when its dep is evaluated again. Tests treat these as the interface: _dispatched has 152 test references, _skip_count 42, _requeue_until 30, _requeue_counts 24.
findings.proposal: Introduce a TaskDispatchRecord dataclass. It holds a state enum (IDLE, DISPATCHED, COOLING), dispatched_priority, last_dispatch_at, a Cooldown(deadline, meta) value, a RequeueLedger(counts, transient, history, pending_arm), skip_count, pending_anchor, cancel_at and merge_phase_at. Keep the records in a DispatchLedger keyed by task id with three operations: on_dispatch, on_release and retire(task_id, reason). The stale sweep calls retire. The cooldown invariant (meta implies deadline) and the release invariant (release clears exactly what dispatch set and emits lock_released) are enforced inside those methods. Public queries replace the test reach-ins. Delete the per-dict pops in _phase_stale_sweep, clear_requeue_count's prose, and the bare lock_table.release bypass class, since the record becomes the only release path.
findings.bug_history_link: a41e39da9a (task 3818: blast-radius release bypassed Scheduler.release. It left _dispatched and _dispatched_priority set, skipped clear_parks_for, and produced a lock_acquired with no lock_released); task 3317 (cooldown meta residue presented to operators as a pending retry); ca73435e5a / e5cc73fe4f (2743/2746 streak-GC narrowing with an accepted leak); 827437a44d (GC backstop added for a missed dict).
findings.verdict_notes: All 18 task-keyed containers are initialised in __init__. __init__ is about 488 lines (331 to 819), not 550, a minor overstatement. _phase_stale_sweep pops exactly _last_dispatch_at, _skip_count, _module_cache and _pending_anchor. Other pops are scattered: _dispatched_priority at about line 8846 and the requeue dicts in clear_requeue_count at about line 9645. No single lifecycle owner exists.

findings.title: The scheduler override and park-eviction stores are implemented twice, in orchestrator and in fused-memory tools.py, both writing the same SQLite files
findings.statement: data/orchestrator/scheduler_overrides.db and park_eviction_requests.db are written by two processes through independent code. fused-memory/server/tools.py carries _OVERRIDE_SCHEMA, _PRIORITY_TIERS, _VALID_CLEAR_FIELDS and the park-eviction schema as copies labelled 'intentional duplicate', with line-pinned 'Source of truth: overrides.py' comments. It re-implements pin_order auto-assignment, the collision check, the BEGIN IMMEDIATE upsert with the 'pinned=0 -> pin_order IS NULL' CASE, the clear_override field updates, and reorder_pin_queue. OverrideStore.reorder_pin_queue and ParkEvictionRequestStore.enqueue in the orchestrator have no production caller; only the fused-memory copies run. The two sides canonicalise project_root differently (Path.resolve against _normalize_project_root). stale_priority_override_edge_sweep reads the table a third way. The stated reason for the copies is that fused-memory may not import orchestrator. That is the exact case shared/ exists for: shared.deploy_state and shared.delivered_check_polarity are already placed there for that reason.
findings.proposal: Move OverrideStore, OverrideRow, PinOrderCollision, ParkEvictionRequestStore, the schemas and the db-path helpers to shared/src/shared/scheduler_overrides.py, with a sync core that fused-memory calls through asyncio.to_thread or a thin aiosqlite adapter. Delete the schema, constant and SQL copies in tools.py and the line-pinned 'Mirrors' comments. Upcoming override semantics (6518 D6 reserve_now refusal, 6144 pin-reservation display) then land once.
findings.bug_history_link: Speculative for active drift. The 1287/1295 invariant work (69f0a5fd87 pin_order CASE, 28690b367c / aa817d9f4a BEGIN IMMEDIATE) had to be mirrored by hand on the fused-memory side ('Mirrors source-of-truth at overrides.py'), and 6518 D6 changes reserve_now semantics again.
findings.verdict_notes: fused-memory/server/tools.py defines _OVERRIDE_SCHEMA and a park-eviction schema as 'intentional duplicates' with line-pinned 'Source of truth' comments. Grep of orchestrator/src finds no production caller of reorder_pin_queue or ParkEvictionRequestStore.enqueue, only the definitions and docstring mentions, so only the fused-memory copies run. The rationale (no orchestrator dependency) is stated in the file, and shared/ is the obvious home.

findings.title: scheduler.py's purpose needs 'and' four times; its H14 measurement shows two symptom-free extractions and two that are legitimate only as state-owning classes
findings.statement: scheduler.py selects tasks AND owns module locks and park stacks (ModuleLockTable) AND is the client wrapper for fused-memory status writes, with its own rejection exception family AND runs six escalating watchdogs (delivered-check, external-dep, starvation, warm-base hard-down, fm-read storm, backfill overstay) AND writes state snapshots. It is 9,883 lines, of which 3,250 are docstring and 1,609 comment (49% prose). Much of that is reviewer-answering prose under the Comments stance. For example, _phase_backfill_terminal_dep_records' docstring runs to about 100 lines of amendment provenance and a 'considered and rejected' alternative. Tests reach 117 distinct private Scheduler names 1,493 times across 69 test files (_dispatched 152, _callbacks 148, _deps_satisfied 56, _phase_redispatch_stranded_blocked 47, _compute_delivered_check_cache 46). The real public seam is too coarse to test against. H14 partition measured. (a) ModuleLockTable (about 895 lines) references only _resolve_time_source, _resolve_wall_time_source and logger from scheduler.py. Moved with those helpers to lock_table.py and imported downward, it has no upward import, cycle or reach-back: no symptom. (b) The rejection family, from SetTaskStatusRejected through extract_rejection, is_transient_rejection, is_transient_api_requeue and transient_requeue_cooldown (lines 226-626), references no Scheduler names. harness, workflow, merge_lane/worker and provenance_conflict import scheduler.py today just for these exception types. Moving them out has no symptom. (c) The delivered-check gate and (d) EASY-backfill admission (_backfill_admission through _maybe_escalate_backfill_overstay_rate) read Scheduler instance state (lock_table, _hold_history, _streak_*, _backfill_grants). As function bags they would be reach-back satellites that fail H13.
findings.proposal: Extract lock_table.py (ModuleLockTable plus the two time-source helpers) and fm_status_rejections.py (the rejection family and the transient-requeue helpers), both downward-only. Extract (c) and (d) only as classes that own their state, with collaborators injected at construction: DeliveredCheckGate, owning the cache, streaks and escalation policy over the oracle in finding 4; and BackfillAdmission, owning the grants and outcome window, given lock_table, hold_history and an event emitter. Rehome reviewer-answering docstring prose to commit or task records, leaving at most a pointer. Retarget the tests to the extracted classes' public methods, deleting reach-ins such as scheduler._compute_delivered_check_cache and scheduler._skip_count.
findings.bug_history_link: Speculative as a split; the cost is visible in the reach-in counts and in every finding above landing in this one file.
findings.verdict_notes: ModuleLockTable (line 1098) and the rejection family (SetTaskStatusRejected at line 226 through transient_requeue_cooldown at line 566) are separable top-level definitions in scheduler.py. Harness, workflow, merge_lane/worker and provenance_conflict import from scheduler. ModuleLockTable runs about 1000 lines before Scheduler at line 2101, versus the claimed 895. The measured test-reach counts were not re-derived. The finding is an explicitly speculative split, and its structural claims hold.

findings.title: Test-leg outcome is flattened into text blobs and re-derived by regex at every consumer instead of parsed once into a typed per-module, per-leg outcome
findings.statement: run_verification holds per-leg facts in CheckRun (rc, output, timed_out, segments), but returns VerifyResult. VerifyResult keeps only test_output, lint_output and type_output strings, a summary string, category: str, and parallel lists added incident by incident: failing_test_ids (junit), failing_test_ids_by_module (task 5627) and failing_leg_categories (task 3173). verify.py::_aggregate_results then concatenates child outputs with '\n'. It rebuilds the summary by substring-scanning child summaries for 'tests failed', 'lint issues' and 'type errors'. It recovers no-verdict notes via .split(', '), which is why SIGNAL_KILL_SUMMARY_MARKER carries a 'producer must not contain ", "' constraint pinned by a test. Downstream, the same session facts are re-parsed from merged text at more than 10 sites: _summarize_checks (_is_worker_death_truncated_session, _first_surviving_failure_line), VerifyResult.failure_report (the same predicate, plus 'timed out' in output.lower() to guess which leg timed out, plus 'error' in type_output), run_verification (_is_bare_xdist_worker_crash), _unmeasured_session_reason (_shows_xdist_worker_death), three _extract_failing_test_ids(failing_result.test_output) calls in the confirm and sweep paths, and offline_lane ×3. confirm_isolated_rerun_verdict re-extracts node ids from text although failing_test_ids from junit exists on the same object. It also infers 'another leg failed' from lint_output/type_output being non-empty, and admits in its own comment that a leg that failed silently is missed. Commit ccd4edd4af (task 5492) records the mechanism directly: the -q truncation witness reads only the final progress line, 'which _aggregate_results' per-module join can hand to a later completed module'. Worker-death truncation is not a FailureCategory, so no policy row can express it, and it is re-detected textually wherever it matters. In-flight task 4843 (branch task/4843, not on main) adds another arm (INFRA_ABORT) with an adjacency regex over 'Plugin: ... pytest_sessionfinish' / 'OSError: cannot send' lines.
findings.proposal: Introduce verify_outcome.py with frozen LegOutcome(module_prefix, slot: CheckSlot{TEST,LINT,TYPE}, tool: ToolKind, termination: Exited(rc) | Signaled(sig, source) | TimedOut, category: FailureCategory, session: PytestSession | None, log_path). PytestSession is built once at the leg boundary inside run_verification from the junit report plus the leg's own output: failing ids by phase, crash_attributed_ids, worker_deaths, truncated: bool and tally. VerifyResult becomes legs: tuple[LegOutcome, ...] plus derived read-only properties (passed, worst_category, failing_test_ids, failing_test_ids_by_module, legs_without_verdict). summary and failure_report become pure renderers of legs, never parsed back. The invariant 'per-module attribution covers the failing ids exactly' then holds by construction, instead of the warning-only VerifyResult.__post_init__. Code that dies: _aggregate_results' substring scan and fragment split, _NO_VERDICT_SUMMARY_MARKERS and the comma constraint, _aggregate_failing_ids_by_module, the failing_leg_categories poison loop, _module_attribution_mismatch, failure_report's 'timed out' sniff, the second worker-death parse in _unmeasured_session_reason, the lint_output-emptiness proxy, and text-based id extraction where junit exists. offline_lane consumes PytestSession instead of verify privates. Would have prevented 3173's aggregation drop, 5337 / 5492's cross-module witness hand-off, 5627 step-2/4's lost module attribution, 6247's leg-category gaps, and the 4843 arm. Land the wire-version work (finding 2) first, since this changes the VerifyResult schema.
findings.bug_history_link: 3173 (kill note dropped by aggregation, da5738db41), 5082 + 5337 (32b550b7ce, 2f609f6393 truncation witness), 5492 (ccd4edd4af, f9344a69cf), 6247 (7829ca16ce, f440b6d60e, eafd4727f3), 5627 (06b594c4ad, 8a114f16b0), in-flight 4843 (7df8d90776 on task/4843); codebook block-report-misattribution
findings.verdict_notes: VerifyResult holds string outputs plus parallel failing_test_ids lists. _is_worker_death_truncated_session, _is_bare_xdist_worker_crash and _shows_xdist_worker_death are re-run over merged text at many sites. confirm_isolated_rerun_verdict and the sweep paths re-extract ids from test_output through _extract_failing_test_ids. Slight overstatement: I found only one offline_lane call to _extract_failing_test_ids, not three. The core claim holds.

findings.title: The dispatcher-to-remote verify wire has no schema version, and the INV-2 currency gate syncs to checkout HEAD rather than the running code
findings.statement: result_to_dict is dataclasses.asdict(vr). result_from_dict is VerifyResult(**d), whose docstring says an unknown top-level key is 'still a TypeError'; RemoteRunner.run_merge_verify turns that into RunnerUnavailable. Neither MergeVerifySpec nor the result carries a schema version or code identity. RemoteRunner.sync_if_stale defines currency as `git rev-parse HEAD` of the dispatcher's checkout against the remote checkout. Its branch comment reads 'Current — remote already runs the dispatcher's gate code', which is false for a long-lived dispatcher whose loaded code predates its checkout HEAD (heuristic 1, a name that lies). The remote DF checkout is shared by the DF and reify dispatchers. Measured incident (operator study 2026-10-08): 5627 added VerifyResult.failing_test_ids_by_module, and reify's sync moved the shared laptop checkout to it at 10-06T10:41Z while both dispatchers still ran 10-04 code. Every laptop verdict then failed as 'unparseable VerifyResult … unexpected keyword argument', giving RunnerUnavailable, a 120 s reprobe and a repeat. That is 51 DF + 26 reify verdicts lost and 63 local re-verifies, 16% of the laptop window, until restarts. No owner was found. Every VerifyResult field addition, including finding 1's, recreates the hazard.
findings.proposal: Add verify_wire.py as the single home of WIRE_SCHEMA. It is a hash derived at import from the field names and types of MergeVerifySpec and VerifyResult, so it cannot drift from the dataclasses. The dispatcher sends it in the spec, and the remote echoes its own in the result envelope. Add RUNNING_CODE_SHA, captured once at process start. RemoteRunner.sync_if_stale syncs the remote to the dispatcher's running SHA rather than `git rev-parse HEAD`, and its 'current' branch compares running SHA and WIRE_SCHEMA. A mismatch raises a typed WireSkew, which benches that runner until the dispatcher restarts and emits one event, instead of RunnerUnavailable plus a reprobe loop. Code that dies: the HEAD vs @{upstream} heuristics in sync_if_stale, and the per-field ad-hoc tolerance in result_from_dict. For the shared-checkout case, give each dispatcher project its own remote checkout, or have the shared one reject a sync whose WIRE_SCHEMA differs from another live dispatcher's. Would have prevented the 10-06 to 10-07 incident.
findings.bug_history_link: 10-06T10:41Z→10-07 wire-skew incident (5627 landed b81b019b22; operator laptop utilisation study 2026-10-08, unowned); e3f8f8be0f / 4539 (adjacent sync defects); incident bb834dd42a (the HEAD-vs-origin amendment)
findings.verdict_notes: result_to_dict is asdict and result_from_dict is VerifyResult(**d). There is no schema version. sync_if_stale compares git rev-parse HEAD of the dispatcher checkout against the remote checkout. Its 'current — remote already runs the dispatcher's gate code' comment holds only if the running code equals the checkout HEAD.

findings.title: Local and remote merge verify run from two sources of truth: live config locally, a lossy spec overlaid field by field onto the host's config remotely
findings.statement: LocalRunner.run_merge_verify documents that it 'drives execution from its injected callables + live config, not from the spec (by design)'. Only the remote leg consumes MergeVerifySpec, so the main path never tests whether the spec is complete. On the remote, run_merge_verify_on_worktree rebuilds ModuleConfigs from the spec (_module_config_from_command admits the rebuild is lossy: per-module cold timeouts collapse and lock_depth is lost). It then patches the laptop's own OrchestratorConfig with one overlay per field that was found missing, each a separate false-green fix: merge_verify_workspace/breadth (task 2822), global test/lint/type commands (INV-1, task 2883), the module registry via a direct private-attribute write config._module_configs (task 4536), and verify_env merged with spec-wins (task 5496). Those overlays carry about 110 comment lines for about 20 lines of code, including an admitted residual (reverse-dependency widening becomes a no-op on this leg). The execution environment is likewise 'host ambient os.environ minus a denylist' (_target_subprocess_env) on both hosts, so host differences pass straight into verdicts; the 5/5 laptop preflight false-reds (tzdata, XDG git ignore, CPython point release) were exactly that. The fingerprint and parity machinery that would detect drift (capture_env_fingerprint, compare_env_fingerprints, run_verdict_parity) has no production caller. It probes only rustc/cargo/sccache. plans/verdict-env-dispatcher-authority-prd.md, which proposes splitting verdict env from host env and wiring the fingerprint, has been draft since 2026-07-07.
findings.proposal: Make the spec the only input on both legs. Add resolve_merge_verify(spec, host: HostProfile) -> ResolvedMergeVerify (module configs, profile, verdict env and commands from the spec; timeouts and host-only env keys from an explicit HostProfile). Both LocalRunner and the remote entry call it, and LocalRunner stops reading live config. Enforce completeness with one property test: for any config C, resolve_merge_verify(build_merge_verify_spec(C), HostProfile.of(C)) equals C's merge-verify inputs. A newly added config knob then fails that test instead of silently not reaching the laptop. Code that dies: the four overlay blocks and their comments in run_merge_verify_on_worktree, the config._module_configs private write, _module_config_from_command's lossy rebuild, and the unused capture_env_fingerprint / compare_env_fingerprints / run_verdict_parity, unless wired as the PRD's D3 drift alarm over the verdict-env subset (extend it with python version, TZ and git config). Would have prevented 2822, 2883, 4536 and 5496.
findings.bug_history_link: tasks 2822, 2883 (966f23a6 fidelity hole), 4536, 5496 (9f49c618a1); laptop prefer_remote preflight 5/5 false-red (5097/6021); stalled plans/verdict-env-dispatcher-authority-prd.md
findings.verdict_notes: Config overlay is real, including the direct write config._module_configs at verify_runner.py line 766. capture_env_fingerprint and run_verdict_parity have no production caller outside verify_runner.py; the only other mention is a message string in merge_lane/worker.py. I did not count the overlay comment lines.

findings.title: Isolated-rerun confirmation is implemented three times; the 'ONE discriminator' covers only two of its callers
findings.statement: _RerunPolicy's docstring claims INV-5 'one IMPLEMENTATION of "passes in isolation"', and _CALL_SITE_POLICY routes merge_gate and main_probe through confirm_isolated_rerun_verdict. The main-tip sweep has two more implementations: _sweep_failure_reproduces_in_isolation (prefilter) and confirm_main_tip_failure_is_real (alarm gate). Each re-implements node-id extraction from text, grouping by subproject, and the scoped-serial command (`_with_pytest_timeout_str(_serial_pytest_str(_scope_to_keyword(mc.test_command, 'pytest', ids)))` + replace(mc, lint_command=None, type_check_command=None)), copied verbatim in all three. confirm_main_tip_failure_is_real goes through _run_isolated_confirm_group, which its own docstring calls 'a lossy shim', and still hand-rolls a 3-retry `git worktree add --detach` with a finally remove+rmtree under a literal `_mainsweepconfirm-` prefix that is not a WorktreeKind. Discriminator fixes therefore land in one copy. 5580's commit states the sweep path is 'byte-identical' (unaffected), and the 5492 worker-death and 6247 leg-verdict preconditions exist only in confirm_isolated_rerun_verdict, with no recorded decision that the sweep should differ.
findings.proposal: Register FlakeCallSite.sweep_prefilter and FlakeCallSite.sweep_confirm as rows of _CALL_SITE_POLICY. Each row's engine runs inside git_ops.ephemeral_worktree with a new WorktreeKind.MAIN_SWEEP_CONFIRM. Each row's refuses_partially_measured_sessions is an explicit per-row decision rather than inherited by omission. Extract isolated_rerun_module_config(mc, node_ids, worktree, timeout) as the one builder of the scoped-serial command. Code that dies: the bodies of _sweep_failure_reproduces_in_isolation and confirm_main_tip_failure_is_real (reduced to thin call-site wrappers), _run_isolated_confirm_group, the hand-rolled worktree retry, and _suppressed_flake_records' dict schema (the FlakeSuppression ledger records it). Would have made 5492 / 5580 / 6247 apply, or visibly not apply, to the sweep.
findings.bug_history_link: c6a92c762e (5580: 'confirm_main_tip_failure_is_real is byte-identical'), ccd4edd4af (5492), eafd4727f3 (6247), 3095 (prefilter), 2370 (a1c9642309)
findings.verdict_notes: The same scoped-serial command build, replace(mc, lint=None, type=None), grouping by subproject and node-id extraction appear in _sweep_failure_reproduces_in_isolation, confirm_main_tip_failure_is_real and confirm_isolated_rerun_verdict. confirm_main_tip_failure_is_real hand-rolls a worktree under the '_mainsweepconfirm-' prefix. The INV-5 'ONE implementation' docstring claim is therefore not accurate for the sweep paths.

findings.title: verify.py is a god module whose purpose needs five 'and's; a measured partition gives clean layers, and tests patch its private executor 199 times
findings.statement: Purpose: verify.py runs verify commands AND parses pytest output AND archives logs and junit AND probes main for pre-existing failures AND sweeps the main tip AND discriminates flakes. Heuristic 14 protocol, step 1 (prose): 5,939 of 11,086 lines (54%) are comments or docstrings, much of it reviewer-answering history ('accepted tradeoff', 'deliberately NOT', task-number chronologies). Step 2 (partition): an AST cross-reference over the top-level symbols, grouped by contiguous region, gives these candidates. (a) pytest_output (lines 628-1396): its only outward edge is WORKER_DEATH_SUMMARY_MARKER, which moves with it, so it is a leaf with no heuristic-13 symptom. (b) verify_exec (_run_cmd, _run_segmented, cgroup scope, clock-stop, env, admission, ruff probe, lines 4280-6365): it references only VerifyInfraError, _is_infra_oserror and logger, so it is a leaf. (c) verify_archive (2329-3073): it references _should_archive_category and _build_summary_payload, which move with it or into verify_categories. (d) verify_confirm (main baseline 1397-1745 plus probe/sweep/flake 8738-11086): it is downstream of run_verification and run_scoped_verification. Only three of its symbols are referenced upward (_load_sample and _xdist_workers from run_verification, _emit_trivial_pass_escalated from run_scoped_verification), and all three belong in verify_exec or the trivial-pass block. Once they move, verify.py never imports verify_confirm and no cycle or reach-back remains. The tests stance: 199 dotted-path patches of orchestrator.verify._run_cmd across 19 test files, 64 distinct verify privates imported by 25 test files, and production reach-ins from offline_lane (_extract_failing_test_ids, _serial_pytest_str), workflow / workflow_types (_is_infra_oserror), evals/snapshots (_target_subprocess_env) and merge_lane/worker (_derive_task_files_from_git).
findings.proposal: Split along the measured partition. pytest_output.py: the regexes and session predicates, superseded by PytestSession in finding 1. verify_exec.py: exposes a CommandRunner protocol (run(cmd, *, cwd, env, timeout, scope) -> LegTermination) that run_verification takes as a parameter. verify_archive.py. verify_confirm.py: main baseline, preexisting probe, sweep and flake discriminator, importing verify downward only. Move _worst_category and _should_archive_category into verify_categories. Rehome reviewer prose to the commit and task records, and invariants to tests, per the Comments stance. Code that dies: the 199 _run_cmd patches (tests inject a fake CommandRunner), and the private imports in offline_lane, workflow and evals, which become public names of the new modules. Each new file passes heuristic 13 by the edge measurement above.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative for the split itself; the concentration is evidenced by 44/277 fix commits and 22/56 in three weeks on this one file (context only, not severity)
findings.verdict_notes: verify.py is 11,086 lines and mixes execution, pytest parsing, archiving and sweep/confirm. 199 patches of orchestrator.verify._run_cmd in tests confirmed by grep. I did not independently verify the AST partition or the comment-ratio figures; the finding is flagged speculative for the split.

findings.title: verify_runner reaches back into verify privates and up into merge_lane, and bundles the codec, runners, pool, allocator, drift and dead parity code
findings.statement: verify_runner imports the private verify._archive_merge_verify_logs at module level, and imports verify_categories._assert_sentinels_disjoint. It calls verify.apply_merge_flake_suppression through the module object 'so it stays monkeypatchable'. Inside run_merge_verify_on_worktree it does two function-local imports to dodge cycles. One is orchestrator.verify.run_scoped_verification, carrying a stale `# type: ignore[attr-defined]`. The other is the private orchestrator.merge_lane.worker._run_unscoped_typechecks, an upward reach: merge_lane.worker imports verify_runner at module level, and the symbol is actually defined in merge_lane/gates.py and re-exported. LocalRunner.run_merge_verify duck-types the gate result with hasattr(gate, 'detail') and getattr(scoped, 'flake_suppression', None). The file is 3,759 lines. Its purpose spans the wire codec, LocalRunner/RemoteRunner, VerifyRunnerPool, HostAllocator, DriftDetector, sccache stats, cold/warm delta and EnvFingerprint/parity; the last has no production caller. Unscoped-typecheck sentinel categories (UNSCOPED_TYPECHECK_*, FLOCK_CONTENTION_CATEGORY) are minted here as bare strings outside FailureCategory.
findings.proposal: Pass the unscoped typecheck gate into run_merge_verify_on_worktree as a typed UnscopedGate protocol, owned by merge_lane/gates.py and supplied by the CLI entry, so verify_runner never imports merge_lane. Make _archive_merge_verify_logs public in verify_archive (finding 5), and give the gate result a typed UnscopedGateResult so the hasattr/getattr checks go. Split verify_runner into verify_wire.py (spec and result codec plus WIRE_SCHEMA from finding 2), verify_hosts.py (Local/RemoteRunner, pool, HostAllocator) and merge_lane/drift's own detector module. Delete or wire EnvFingerprint per finding 3. Fold the sentinel categories into FailureCategory rows.
findings.bug_history_link: 4536 (registry install via private write), 2883 / 3789ε (flake_suppression threaded with getattr), 5349 (remote-verify integrity events had never emitted)
findings.verdict_notes: Function-local imports at lines 611 and 614 confirmed: run_scoped_verification with a type: ignore[attr-defined], and _run_unscoped_typechecks from merge_lane.worker. That symbol is defined in merge_lane/gates.py and re-exported, while worker.py imports verify_runner at module level. The file is 3,759 lines and holds dead parity code.

findings.title: The verify plan's tool slot is recovered by routing on reason-string prefixes
findings.statement: verify_plan.PlannedRun has no typed field naming which ModuleConfig slot (test, lint or type) it renders into. verify.py recovers the slot with _MC_ATTR_BY_REASON_PREFIX, a match on run.reason.startswith('lint:' / 'pyright:' / 'pytest:'). Two helpers (_mc_attr_for_run, _mc_attr_for_run_or_none) handle reasons that carry no prefix, such as the fallback's SKIPPED run, and _FALLBACK_TOOLKIND_BY_ATTR maps back to ToolKind. A reworded reason in verify_plan silently changes which command executes or is recorded. PlannedRun's own docstring states that its scoped_targets invariant is deliberately NOT asserted in __post_init__, because _safe_derive_verify_plan_dict catches every exception and would lose the whole plan record. Invariant enforcement is subordinated to a catch-all.
findings.proposal: Add slot: CheckSlot (TEST, LINT, TYPE) to PlannedRun, set by derive_verify_plan where the run is created. CheckSlot is shared with LegOutcome from finding 1.
