Assert the scoped_targets invariant in PlannedRun.__post_init__, and narrow _safe_derive_verify_plan_dict's except so a violated invariant surfaces as a named error event rather than a silent None. Code that dies: _MC_ATTR_BY_REASON_PREFIX, _mc_attr_for_run, _mc_attr_for_run_or_none and _FALLBACK_TOOLKIND_BY_ATTR.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative (task κ verify-scope-inversion introduced the reason-prefix bridge)
findings.verdict_notes: _MC_ATTR_BY_REASON_PREFIX is a tuple of (prefix, attr) pairs matched with run.reason.startswith. _mc_attr_for_run_or_none returns None when no prefix matches, and _mc_attr_for_run raises on None.

findings.title: Metadata write semantics are a per-call mode chosen by the caller, not a per-key policy, so every caller works around the patch language
findings.statement: update_task merges metadata by one whole-call mode ('merge' shallow last-write-wins, 'additive' recursive union where old wins on scalars, 'replace' whole blob), resolved from two interacting flags in sqlite_task_backend.py::_resolve_metadata_mode. That function carries two rejection carve-outs: bare append=False (task 2180 wipe) and merge+append=True (task 3581, the DF-3260 memory_hints clobber). The same append flag also drives details/prompt text concatenation in SqliteTaskBackend.update_task. The 'append IS NOT SCOPED TO METADATA (task 4216)' comment block documents that a details rewrite plus a metadata attach under append=True silently duplicates details. Three tests pin that behaviour rather than removing it. No key has a declared merge semantics: _merge_values unions every list, including ordered argv such as before_done.args (5810). The patch language has no unset-key operation, so retiring a key means a client read-modify-write sent as 'replace'. The orchestrator does exactly that in workflow.py::TaskWorkflow._clear_merge_retry_pending / _clear_merge_phase_entered and harness.py::Harness._clear_merge_retry_pending_for_restart. To avoid the #4271 sibling clobber it needs a fresh-read/require_fresh protocol (tasks 2991, 3024). Other per-key properties are declared in at least six places across four modules: write authority for done_provenance (backend floor plus _assert_done_provenance_passthrough), machine-authored keys (_MACHINE_AUTHORED_METADATA_KEYS, stripped), reserved control keys (_RESERVED_METADATA_CONTROL_KEYS, task 2735), terminal-clearable keys (recon_write_policy.CLEARABLE_ANNOTATION_KEYS), the x_ namespace (recon_write_policy.X_ANNOTATION_PREFIX, commented 'keep the two in sync by hand' with shared/task_metadata.py), and vocabulary and cardinality (_BLESSED_METADATA_KEYS, _SUBMODEL_CARDINALITY). Ownership of metadata.files is the open structural item of live task 3260 ('making files an OWNED field with a single sanctioned writer').
findings.proposal: Create shared/task_metadata_keys.py with a MetadataKeySpec registry, one entry per Tier-A key: {merge: REPLACE | SET_UNION | APPEND_LOG | ORDERED_REPLACE, writer: ActorClass set or 'machine', terminal_writable: bool, cardinality}. Derive TaskMetadata field annotations from it. Replace the metadata_mode/append inputs with a typed MetadataPatch (per-key set / unset / append ops). Add one shared function, apply_metadata_patch(stored: TaskMetadata, patch: MetadataPatch, writer: ActorClass) -> TaskMetadata, called only from SqliteTaskBackend.update_task inside the transaction, so the merge, the authority check and the schema check are a single pass. append is then scoped to details only. Code that becomes deletable: _resolve_metadata_mode and both carve-outs, _merge_values, _strip_reserved_control_keys and _RESERVED_METADATA_CONTROL_KEYS (control flags are no longer in the payload), strip_machine_authored_metadata (becomes a writer check), the in-transaction done_provenance passthrough comparison (becomes a writer check), CLEARABLE_ANNOTATION_KEYS and the X_ANNOTATION_PREFIX mirror (become terminal_writable in the spec), the orchestrator's delete-by-omission RMW and require_fresh dance (replaced by unset ops), and the 4216 concatenation hazard. It would have prevented 2180, 3581/DF-3260, 4039, 4216, 2735/2682, 5810, 4271, 3446 (curator replace wiping files) and the 3579/3260 stale-snapshot files clobbers.
findings.bug_history_link: 2180 (append=False wipe), fa0ab95084/f5d88109d4 (3581 merge+append clobber), 48d834ec3d (4039 append on description), 4216 (details duplication documented, not fixed), 2735/2682 (literal append key persisted), 687a9adb27/5356636292 (3777 replace may not drop done_provenance), 3446 (curator combine replace), live 3260/3579/3113/5810; orchestrator 2991/3024/#4271 sibling-clobber guards
findings.verdict_notes: _resolve_metadata_mode has both carve-outs (merge+append=True 3581; bare append=False 2180) as stated. _merge_values docstring references before_done.args/5810 and the orchestrator clear helpers are named. recon_write_policy.py has the 'keep the two in sync by hand' note. Per-call mode rather than per-key policy is real; the six-site count was not exhaustively re-enumerated.

findings.title: Caller identity and authority are self-reported agent_id strings classified by prefix at ~35 sites through at least 7 independent rule sets that already disagree
findings.statement: server/tools.py::_resolve_identity gives an explicit caller agent_id precedence over clientInfo. done_provenance_authz.py's own docstring says that under stateless HTTP the id is 'SELF-REPORTED ... a determined caller can claim any prefix'. That string is then classified independently at each consumer. shared/task_transitions.py::derive_actor_class maps both 'recon-stage-*' and 'reconciliation-stage*' to RECONCILIATION. Every gate that actually restricts recon writers tests only agent_id.startswith('recon-stage-'): TaskInterceptor._apply_status_transition and update_task (is_recon_stage_write, which turns on ReconWritePolicy and the lifecycle-reset guard), execution_class_error, premise_lint_error, recurring_gate_guard_error, _validate_done_provenance's is_recon_stage factor 1, and 11 sites in tools.py. A caller named 'reconciliation-stage-1', the literal example in CLAUDE.md's write-tagging convention, is therefore RECONCILIATION to the transition table but escapes every recon write gate. Further rule sets: stats_verifier._KNOWN_STAGE_AGENT_IDS (exact ids), internal_writers.INTERNAL_WRITER_AGENT_ID_PREFIXES, standing_decision_writer's HUMAN_AUTHORED_AGENT_ID_PREFIXES, and three configured prefix allowlists in done_provenance_authz / mem0_update_authz / entity_mint_authz. The internal_writers docstring explains why each neighbour 'would give a wrong answer here'. done_provenance_authz describes itself as mirroring mem0_update_authz 'clause for clause'. grep counts 35 agent_id startswith checks across fused-memory and shared.
findings.proposal: Resolve identity once at the MCP boundary into a frozen CallerIdentity(actor: ActorClass, stage: StageId | None, raw: str). It is built by one parser in shared/task_transitions.py, which absorbs derive_actor_class and the StageId lookup, in server/tools.py::_resolve_identity. Pass it down instead of agent_id: str. Gates test identity.actor is ActorClass.RECONCILIATION or identity.stage. The three authz modules become one AuthorizationPolicy table keyed by (capability, ActorClass), read live from config. Deletable: the about 18 startswith('recon-stage-') sites, is_recon_stage_write and its pyright re-assert, the is_recon_stage side parameter threaded into _validate_done_provenance, and two of the three mirrored authz modules. A wrong prefix becomes a parse error at the boundary rather than a silently ungated writer.
findings.bug_history_link: f45184479a (pyright fallout of the is_recon_stage_write hoist, task 2624), 2684/2695/2697 (recon terminal-annotation exemptions keyed on the same prefix), b45d9a84f6 (3250, classify every mutating tool for recon stages), incident 5156 / task 5241 (recon stage self-authorized a deterministic close; fixed by yet another prefix check plus allowlist), esc-5564-1 (internal_writers registry added because existing classifiers disagreed)
findings.verdict_notes: derive_actor_class maps ('recon-stage-','reconciliation-stage') to RECONCILIATION. Gates use startswith('recon-stage-') only. 30 agent_id/recon-stage startswith hits in fused_memory by my grep (the claimed 35 includes shared). The disagreement is real. The 'self-reported' premise is taken from the done_provenance_authz docstring.

findings.title: SqliteTaskBackend read-modify-writes read outside any SQLite transaction; atomicity rests only on an in-process asyncio.Lock
findings.statement: SqliteTaskBackend._get_connection opens the cached write connection through connect_daemon with no isolation_level, which is Python sqlite3's legacy implicit-transaction mode. SqliteTaskBackend._txn issues no BEGIN. In that mode a SELECT does not open a transaction; only the first DML does. So update_task's 'SELECT * FROM tasks' and the UPDATE that writes the merged metadata are not atomic against another connection. The same holds for stamp_audit_metadata's 'SELECT metadata' and its UPDATE. A scratch probe confirmed it: after the SELECT, in_transaction is False, and a second connection's committed write between the SELECT and the UPDATE was overwritten ('old+merged'). The asyncio _write_lock serializes only same-process writers. Second processes do open the live store through their own SqliteTaskBackend and write: fused-memory/scripts/correct_found_on_main_backlog.py (update_task and set_status_and_stamp_audit), audit_duplicate_tasks.py (set_task_status cancelled), audit_found_on_main_provenance.py (update_task). The _assert_done_provenance_passthrough docstring states that the stored value 'cannot change before the UPDATE' because the check runs 'inside its transaction'. Under these semantics that is false across processes. The legacy-mode connection is also what made a leaked read pin a stale WAL snapshot (task 2388). The fixes for that added two more connection kinds instead of changing this one.
findings.proposal: Open the write connection with isolation_level=None and have _txn issue 'BEGIN IMMEDIATE' before yielding, with commit/rollback as today. The read-modify-write is then serialized by SQLite across processes. The asyncio lock becomes an optimization, not the correctness mechanism, and the docstring's atomicity claim becomes true. The write connection can no longer pin a snapshot, so get_statuses_fresh's 'never shared' rationale (task 2388) is moot.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative for a cross-process lost update (no recorded incident); same mechanism as task 2388's pinned-snapshot class (2455/2651/2694)
findings.verdict_notes: Structure confirmed: the write connection comes from connect_daemon without isolation_level=None, and _txn issues commit with no BEGIN (the comments at ~860 and ~2211 say so). The only BEGIN is in a migration. The docstring claim 'cannot change before the UPDATE' is therefore only same-process. Several scripts open SqliteTaskBackend, including audit_duplicate_tasks and correct_found_on_main_backlog. The failure is speculative: no incident is recorded, and the cross-process window is narrow. 'Medium' is overstated.

findings.title: Table A is consulted at one middleware site, after an earlier gate that encodes its terminal rule, and stores opened outside the interceptor bypass it
findings.statement: In fused-memory, is_legal_transition is called from exactly one place: gate 2e of TaskInterceptor._apply_status_transition, a 595-line method with about 12 sequential early-return gates. In order: ReconWritePolicy, same-status no-op, bulk-reset breaker, 2a terminal-exit, 2b done-provenance, 2c phantom-done, reopen freshness, 2d pre-done hook, 2d-bis consolidation closure, 2e the table. Gate 2a rejects any exit from TERMINAL without reopen_reason. That is the same rule as the table's 'frm in TERMINAL -> legal only when reopen' clause. Since 2a always runs first, the table's terminal clause cannot fire from its only consumer, so one rule has two encodings and two error shapes (terminal_exit_rejected vs illegal_transition). 2e also treats a ValueError from out-of-vocabulary status coercion as legal. SqliteTaskBackend.set_task_status and set_status_and_stamp_audit enforce vocabulary only. A process using the backend directly (scripts/audit_duplicate_tasks.py set_task_status 'cancelled'; correct_found_on_main_backlog.py set_status_and_stamp_audit) bypasses legality, the terminal-exit and provenance gates, and event emission. The orchestrator side, by contrast, does consume the same table (workflow_types.py WorkflowStateMachine).
findings.proposal: Give the store write a required actor: ActorClass parameter (SqliteTaskBackend._write_status_and_verify and set_status_and_stamp_audit). Make is_legal_transition the store-level floor, with the transition and its audit in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, so every writer, scripts included, is covered. In the interceptor, turn the remaining gates into an ordered list of gate objects over a frozen StatusWriteRequest(task_snapshot, frm, to, actor, provenance, reopen_reason), each returning a typed Refusal or None. Delete gate 2a and _terminal_exit_error (the table's reopen rule plus a 'reopen requires reason' request validator replace them), and the swallow-ValueError branch (vocabulary is validated at request construction). Under the store floor, the orchestrator's TerminalExitRejection / illegal-transition split collapses to one refusal code.
findings.bug_history_link: 2175 (thread reopen into the transition-legality gate), 2182/2188 (protocol sync for claimant kwargs), d553bc9571 (third persist site broke when the floor moved), mined theme 'task-status writes lack a single authority' (task-status-authority PRD, infra_hold bolted on by 1883), operator memory 'Table A refuses merge-deferred->deferred'
findings.verdict_notes: is_legal_transition is called once, at the 2e gate (line ~1642 of task_interceptor.py). Gate 2a (line ~1468) rejects terminal exits without a reopen_reason. After 2a, reopen is always True, so the table's 'frm in TERMINAL' clause (task_transitions.py line 275) is unreachable from the interceptor. 2e catches ValueError and treats it as legal. The terminal rule has two encodings and two error shapes. The backend-bypass part was not independently exercised.

findings.title: server/tools.py create_mcp_server is one 9,386-line function whose task tools form a closed, cleanly extractable group
findings.statement: Heuristic 14 measurement. tools.py is 10,561 lines: 1,980 comment lines, 3,513 docstring lines (52% prose) and 739 blank. Most docstring lines are MCP tool descriptions served to clients, so they are in their right home. Comments are 19%. All 62 tools plus 28 helpers are closures inside create_mcp_server (lines 1176 to 10561). It holds 37 closure locals and 7 function-local imports, and its largest closures are consolidate_memories at 951 lines, add_memory 727, _citation_repoint_gate 402 and submit_task 390. Its purpose needs 'and': memory write tools and memory read tools and graph-entity admin and queue/WAL ops and task tools and scheduler pin/park overrides. Partition by captured state, measured with AST name analysis. The 24 task, ticket, dependency and pin tools (get_tasks through request_park_eviction, about 2,400 lines) capture only {mcp, task_interceptor, _kp, _VALID_TASK_STATUSES} plus three closures. Two of those closures are pure: _normalize_project_root (validate_project_root plus resolve_main_checkout) and _reject_if_ticket_id. The third is _log_read (write_journal). The 7 pin/park/scheduler tools capture only mcp plus module-level overrides helpers (lines 265-560). Heuristic 13 symptoms for a server/task_tools.py: none, provided the two pure helpers move down to a server/tool_args.py and _log_read becomes an injected callable. No candidate needs to import back into tools.py. One existing symptom: _reject_if_ticket_id imports the private _is_ticket_id from task_interceptor. Change cost: 262 commits from 72 distinct tasks touched tools.py in the window, with merge-conflict resolutions for tasks 3731, 3134 and 3088.
findings.proposal: Split along the measured seam. server/task_tools.py::register_task_tools(mcp, interceptor, known_projects, read_log) takes the 17 task, ticket and dependency tools. server/scheduler_override_tools.py::register_override_tools(mcp) takes the pin, park and scheduler-state tools and the module-level overrides/park DDL (which is fm-task-layer.3's subject and the natural place to then share orchestrator/overrides.py). server/tool_args.py holds _normalize_project_root, _reject_if_ticket_id (with a public is_ticket_id from the interceptor), _resolve_identity and paging helpers. create_mcp_server keeps the memory tools and calls the register functions. Deletable: the closure capture of task_interceptor by memory tools, and the private import. Verification: each new file imports only downward and none imports tools.py.
findings.bug_history_link: 2f795dfe1a/5a496a423e (decorators lost to rebase in the shared file), 9dbe91eac2/141de9d381/4b6e0b5917 (merge-conflict resolutions in tools.py), operator memory 10-06 'hub-file lock contention' as dispatch serializer
findings.verdict_notes: tools.py is 10,561 lines and create_mcp_server starts at line 1176 and runs to the end. The size and closure structure match. The captured-state partition numbers were not re-derived.

findings.title: TaskInterceptor is three objects sharing a lock: status FSM gating, ticket/curator pipeline, and a module-level done-provenance validator with no public seam
findings.statement: Heuristic 14 measurement. The file is 7,417 lines: 1,293 comment and 1,908 docstring lines (43% prose). TaskInterceptor (lines 432-6043) has 89 methods and 30 instance attributes. Section partition by instance-attribute use, from the AST. Status transition (1113-1883) uses {_bulk_reset_guard, _config, _lifecycle_reset_filer, reconciler, _background_tasks}. The ticket/curator pipeline (3338-5445) uses {_ticket_queues, _ticket_events, _ticket_store, _worker_tasks, _worker_intent, _curator_locks, _write_locks, _usage_gate, _escalator, taskmaster, ...}. Scope routing (1883-3338) uses {_prefix_registry, _path_scope_adjudicator, _scope_violation_escalator, _curator, ...}. These are largely disjoint, sharing only the backend handle, config, the write lock and the background-task set. The 29 module-level functions after the class (lines 6046-7417, about 1,370 lines: _validate_done_provenance at 409 lines, _check_reopen_freshness, _verify_commit_on_main, ...) never reference TaskInterceptor. They use only 7 earlier module names (_DONE_PROVENANCE_KINDS[_TEXT], _CommitResolutionFailure, _AncestorCheckFailure, _parse_metadata_value, _warn_metadata_discard, logger), all movable with them. Heuristic 13 symptom of that split: none. The unit already exists in practice: fused-memory tests import the private _validate_done_provenance 18 times, a Tests-stance smell, and done_provenance_authz.py's docstring says it moved out because a body 'buried in a 6.8k-line module' was unreachable except through a full set_task_status round trip. The interceptor's update_task docstring lists its gates in an order and set that no longer match the code. It names the backend floor as gate 1 and omits the idempotency and recon gates.
findings.proposal: Move the done-provenance block to middleware/done_provenance_gate.py with a public validate_done_provenance(raw, task_id, project_root, *, caller: CallerIdentity, require) -> ProvenanceVerdict. Tests import that, not a private name. Extract a TicketPipeline class that owns the ticket queues, events, workers, ticket store and curator locks, and receives a narrow TaskWritePort (write_lock, backend, journal) from TaskInterceptor by constructor injection, so nothing imports back. TaskInterceptor keeps status/update/dependency writes and the ordered gate list from the transition finding. Deletable: the 18 private-name test imports, and the stale gate list in update_task's docstring.
findings.bug_history_link: 4448 curator degraded-streak chain (ab5999eb2d, 598601d147, 7fcb9d1b19, 55a467aab2) all landing in the same 7.4k-line file as the status FSM; 5241 (authz split out for testability); 141 commits from 51 tasks on this file in the window
findings.verdict_notes: The file is 7,417 lines. class TaskInterceptor starts at line 432 and interceptor_write_succeeded at line 7187, so module-level functions follow the class. 63 test references to _validate_done_provenance, so the test-reach smell is real (the claim says 18, which is not inconsistent with a subset). The attribute-partition detail was not re-derived.

findings.title: Task-write outcomes have no typed contract: two in-process failure channels, and a wire 'error' field that is sometimes a token and sometimes prose, which the orchestrator re-classifies by substring
findings.statement: TaskInterceptor.update_task returns rejection dicts from its own gates (lock_charter_error, BacklogVerdict.to_error_dict, recon Verdict.to_error_dict). It converts exactly two backend exceptions (StatusWriteAuthorityError, DoneProvenanceWriteAuthorityError) and states the contract 'return a dict, never raise'. Yet AppendUnsupportedFieldError, TaskmasterError (mode contradictions, corrupt blob), LeakedEnvelopeMarkupError, DuplicateCandidateKeyError and pydantic ValidationError (enforce mode) all propagate out of SqliteTaskBackend.update_task. Every in-process caller therefore needs both a try/except and interceptor_write_succeeded: targeted.py, citation_verifier.py, manifest_stamping.py. Their comments have drifted. targeted.py says the gates 'do NOT raise' and names _reject_status_in_update_task and _reject_done_provenance_in_update_metadata, both deleted (f0a46af6bd). interceptor_write_succeeded infers success from key presence ('success' defaults True, 'error' falsy), and a no-op write still reports success (live 4867). At the MCP boundary, mcp_tool_errors renders exceptions as {'error': str(e), 'error_type': type(e).__name__}. So 'error' carries a machine token (done_provenance_invalid, terminal_exit_rejected) for dict rejections and human prose for exceptions and BacklogVerdict. orchestrator/scheduler.py::extract_structured_rejection re-parses the text content block as JSON. Its set_task_status ladder routes on error_code string equality into its own mirrored exception family (TerminalExitRejection, DoneGateRejection, ProvenanceValidationRejection). is_transient_rejection substring-matches class names inside the rendered rejection text. No shared module defines the rejection vocabulary; grep finds terminal_exit_rejected only in fused-memory and the orchestrator.
findings.proposal: Add shared/task_write_result.py with a frozen WriteOutcome = Applied(task, changed: bool) | Refused(code: RefusalCode, task_id, details: Mapping). RefusalCode is a StrEnum that is the single vocabulary, covering status_via_update_task, done_provenance_invalid, terminal_exit_rejected, illegal_transition, lock_charter, backlog_exceeded, append_unsupported, duplicate_candidate_key, schema_invalid and so on. Backend exceptions carry a RefusalCode. TaskInterceptor's write methods return WriteOutcome and catch the backend's typed refusal base class once. mcp_tool_errors serializes Refused as {'refusal': code, ...} distinct from {'error': ...} for unexpected faults. The orchestrator deserializes into the same WriteOutcome. Deletable: interceptor_write_succeeded and its shape enumeration, _write_error_code, the per-caller try-plus-classify blocks, scheduler.extract_structured_rejection's content-block JSON sniffing, the string-substring is_transient_rejection fallback for these writes, and the orchestrator's mirrored rejection classes (subclass RefusalCode instead). Applied.changed=False makes 4867's write-nothing case expressible.
findings.bug_history_link: live 4867 (update_task reported success writing nothing; two L2s, one closed on a wrong root cause), 1136/1184 (hints audit trail lied on rejection; interceptor_write_succeeded introduced), mined theme 'catch store errors at the store seam' (3757), prior fm-task-layer.4's two-shape divergence
findings.verdict_notes: interceptor_write_succeeded exists. extract_structured_rejection and is_transient_rejection exist in orchestrator scheduler.py. I did not verify the specific unhandled-exception list, the stale targeted.py comments, or the 'error' token-versus-prose split. The substring-routing claim is plausible but only partly checked.

findings.title: The lock-charter extension allowlist is kept in four Python copies plus a bash copy, synced by equality tests, under a stale rationale
findings.statement: FILE_EXTENSIONS, is_file_path and directory_locks are defined in shared/src/shared/locking.py, which is called canonical. They are defined again 'duplicated here verbatim' in fused-memory/src/fused_memory/middleware/lock_charter_guard.py. The stated reason is that the shared package 'may be pinned to a release that predates the relocation'. That reason no longer holds: lock_charter_guard.py itself imports shared.task_metadata, and 26 middleware modules import from shared. Widening the allowlist is a lockstep edit. Commit 9b824da7db ('add tombstones') updated 'the four gamma copies' (two sources plus two test literals) and two _ACCEPT_PATHS corpora. 10e2da884a records that per-copy equality tests 'are structurally incapable of seeing the other two copies' and adds a bash copy as the transitive pin. A miss means the submit-time guard and the scheduler's lock derivation disagree on whether a path is a directory charter. 43410b3418 shows that class: 'allowlist csv — heal main and break the merge-lane deadlock'.
findings.proposal: Make lock_charter_guard.py import FILE_EXTENSIONS, is_file_path and directory_locks from shared.locking and delete its copies, its _CANONICAL_EXTENSIONS test literal and the drift-guard test. Keep one drift test that compares shared.locking against the bash copy, or generate the bash list from Python at install time. Deletable: one source copy, two test literals, the 'Predicate canonical location' docstring section.
findings.bug_history_link: 9b824da7db (four-copy lockstep widen), 10e2da884a/1f1058a289/ec3ece143d (3248 amends about cross-copy enforcement), 43410b3418 (missing extension deadlocked the merge lane)
findings.verdict_notes: lock_charter_guard.py has its own FILE_EXTENSIONS and is_file_path, and its docstring says 'duplicated here verbatim' because shared may be pinned to an older release. The same module imports shared.task_metadata (line 103), so the rationale is stale. The equality-test sync is documented. The four-Python-copies-plus-bash count was not enumerated.

findings.title: Live task/scheduler state is mirrored into Graphiti as LLM prose and retired by an ever-growing English regex grammar
findings.statement: Answer to ask 1: the 32% fix ratio comes from parsing natural language to recover a fact that the task store already owns. Task status and scheduler overrides reach Graphiti as free-text edges extracted by the graphiti-core LLM from arbitrary agent writes. Nothing structured ties an edge to (task_id, status, as_of). stale_status_snapshot_edge_sweep.py therefore keeps a hand-built English grammar to decide which ids a fact asserts as active, pending, blocked or stalled. The grammar is 11 compiled regexes. _build_snapshot_patterns instantiates five extraction paths (individual, genitive, status-phrase, plural-enum, list-introducer) twice, as a union family and a blocked family. Clause-break heuristics (_last_clause_break, _is_intra_token_dot), a preposition list (_ENUM_PREP_WORDS) and a subset property hold only through threaded rejected_spans. Each new phrasing or false positive is another fix. The window shows 61 commits on this file, including 'restore closed-class connective', 'stop the phrase-form gap absorbing negation', 'scope the preposition guard by clause instead of a determiner list', 'narrow . clause-break detection', 'recognize stalled', 'extract the genitive shape' and 'thread the union family's rejected spans into the blocked family'. The module docstring still lists 6 known residuals, two of them pointed in the unrecoverable over-selection direction. The same pattern has been copied rather than fixed. stale_priority_override_edge_sweep.py (task 2781) says it mirrors 2613 'exactly', extracts its subject 'lexically from LLM-generated edge fact text', and replicates the overrides-DB read in-module. degenerate_task_node_sweep exists because extraction mints 'tasks N' nodes. On the write side, task_filter.py holds a second family of status-prose detectors (is_count_snapshot, is_mixed_temporal_framing, find_conflicting_task_status_ids, frames_live_task_status_as_current_fact, find_present_tense_completion_claim_task_ids). server/tools.py add_episode and add_memory apply them only to agent_ids starting with 'recon-stage-', so writes from every other agent still mint status-snapshot edges.
findings.proposal: Make live operational state a typed claim, never parsed prose. Register a graphiti-core custom edge type, TaskStateClaim(task_id: int, attribute: Literal['status','priority_override'], value: TaskStatus | OverrideKind, as_of: datetime), and emit it from one writer, LiveStateClaimWriter in memory_service. That writer replaces the prose template build_supersede_fact. At ingest, either reject untyped status claims for every caller, not only recon-stage, or normalize them into this edge type. Each sweep then becomes a typed query: claims whose value disagrees with get_statuses or the overrides table. Search results can also annotate task entities with live status at read time instead of storing it. What becomes deletable: INDIVIDUAL/GENITIVE/SNAPSHOT_STATUS_PHRASE/PLURAL_ENUM/LIST_INTRODUCER and both families, _ENUM_PREP_WORDS, the clause-break machinery, COUNT_QUANTITY_RE, the subject extractor in stale_priority_override_edge_sweep, and the status-prose detectors in task_filter that guard against this edge class. A one-time legacy migration still needs the old extractor, run as a script rather than every cycle. This prevents the whole 3042/3079/3037/4149/4644 over- and under-matching series.
findings.bug_history_link: Tasks 2613, 3042 (c19a4c283d, e95f6104d5, 7548b9f8dd, b0d4f2e185, f4b03f36a6), 3079 (1e1212f634, 172e39a6de, ee59db2880, fbe88c7d4a, 3171f0c8f5, ac3f3fa7ba, 5cdf8704b2), 3037 (92cd9d9156, 8a47456ff7), 4149 (3a4b1bb740), 3403 (4e21795ea1), 2885 (4 stale edges survived blocked->done), 2781 priority-override backfills (run 2d59c7de); mined theme 16x + 25x.
findings.verdict_notes: stale_status_snapshot_edge_sweep.py is 2293 lines with 11 re.compile sites, _ENUM_PREP_WORDS and clause-break helpers present. Sibling sweeps (priority override, degenerate node) exist. tools.py gates on recon-stage- agent_id. I did not re-verify every commit hash.

findings.title: Two hand-mirrored S1→S2→S3 run drivers: every lifecycle, cancellation and finally fix lands in pairs
findings.statement: run_full_cycle (463 lines) and _run_remediation_pass (865 lines) each carry their own copy of the run lifecycle. Each one does journal.start_run, a stage loop with a pre-Stage-3 _flush_cycle_summaries, and the run.stage_reports[key] = report assignment. Each then has _spawn_judge, an except ladder (CancelledError, AllAccountsCapped, Exception) that writes run.stage_reports['_error'] and a shielded journal.complete_run(run_id,'failed'), and a finally that flushes summaries and persists and GCs the config dir. Nothing owns the run state machine, so fixes arrive as pairs. Examples: 2adaf7ad2e / 64291f98ce 'shield <driver> finally's update_run_stage_reports'; 3901ecca0d / 05f07dfa04 'reach <driver>'s config-dir GC on a second cancellation'; d42ddcdd09 / ac294b5a1a (task 5545 failure records); 33556bf048 / 15d99d1aea (flush before Stage 3). Some fixes are single-sided: d4aee1ceb0 'widen the remediation try to cover every exit after start_run' and c7d743c5de 'cancelled remediation pass terminalises its row'. _flush_cycle_summaries's docstring says it exists only so the call order 'must not be able to drift' between four sites. Heuristic-14 measurement of harness.py (6,529 lines, 49% prose), measured by self-state touched and harness methods called per group. (a) Cycle-summary backstops (_ensure_stage1/2_cycle_summary, _reattempt_cycle_summary_write, _write_degraded_cycle_summary, _flush_cycle_summaries, about 600 lines) touch only self.memory and call no other harness method, so they could become a clean leaf. (b) Escalation filing (_escalate, _file_finding_task_escalation, _finding_has_open_escalation, _finding_recently_resolved, _finding_persistence_count, _maybe_escalate_stale_task_count_snapshot, _storm_summary, about 620 lines) touches self._escalation_queue and self.journal plus _resolve_known_root and _memoised_resolved_fingerprints, so it can be extracted if those two are passed in. (c) Run recovery (about 574 lines) calls run_full_cycle, _spawn_judge and _escalate. (d) Remediation (_maybe_remediate plus _run_remediation_pass, about 1,205 lines) calls 17 other harness methods. Split today, (c) and (d) would import back from the harness, which is the stitching heuristic 13 forbids. The driver duplication is what keeps them entangled.
findings.proposal: Introduce one ReconRunDriver (reconciliation/run_driver.py) that owns the run lifecycle as an explicit state machine with a transition table: STARTED → STAGE(n) → JUDGED → COMPLETED | FAILED(record). Its single async drive(run, stages, *, anchor) method does start_run, the stage loop, the pre-S3 flush, judge spawning, the shielded terminal transition, and the finally flush/persist/GC. run_full_cycle and _run_remediation_pass shrink to building the stage list and their pre-checks (scope freshness, deferral). Then extract the groups the measurement showed are clean: cycle_summary_backstop.py taking memory_service, and finding_escalation.py taking the queue and journal. What becomes deletable: the second except/finally ladder, _flush_cycle_summaries as a drift guard, and every paired fix. This would have prevented the 5545 single-sided failure-path gaps and the doubled shield/GC fixes.
findings.bug_history_link: 2adaf7ad2e + 64291f98ce; 3901ecca0d + 05f07dfa04; task 5545 (ac294b5a1a, d42ddcdd09, c7d743c5de, d4aee1ceb0, d4d11f6505); 33556bf048 + 15d99d1aea; 0d0603a8c4 'single-source the cycle-summary flush call pair across both drivers'; mined theme 22x (harness cancellation/finally).
