Both finally blocks call _persist_stage_reports_then_gc_config_dir. The duplication is real. Line counts roughly match.

findings.title: Flag/finding identity has no home: four modules recompute it under a 'local-copy' layering rule the same files break, and Stage 2 merges three channels that are filtered differently
findings.statement: Several places derive what makes two flags or findings 'the same', each with its own normalizer. flag_dedup has compute_flag_signature, compute_content_fingerprint_signature, _normalize_content_description and canonical_flag_type_family. recon_report has _canonical_sig_field, _normalize_description, _description_hash and _canonicalize_task_id_string. TaskKnowledgeSync has _flag_content_fingerprint. The copies carry 'keep in sync' notes justified by a no-import-inversion convention, and that justification is false. recon_report.py says _canonical_sig_field is 're-implemented locally ... because server/ must not import from the reconciliation package', yet the same file imports fused_memory.reconciliation.citation_repair at module top. flag_dedup's _COUNT_GROUP_RE calls itself a 'LOCAL copy' of task_filter.COUNT_SNAPSHOT_RE because 'reconciliation must not import from middleware'. task_filter is in reconciliation, and flag_dedup imports is_count_snapshot from it inside _is_task_count_snapshot_finding. Answer to ask 4: recon_report alone holds 9 dedup/fold rules spread across add_finding, cite_task, get_assembled_report and _purge_finding. They are: (task_id, flag_type) signature; null-null description hash; flag_type inheritance (2318); comma-joined task_id canonicalization (2432); project-scoped null+null cite_task fold (2425); entity-scoped derived-signature fold that reuses _run_sig_index (2432), with a cross-project near-collision skip; read-time Stage-1 echo suppression (1654); supersession neutering (4653); and a cross-project routing downgrade. The Stage-1 carve-out is duplicated at write time and read time (6a55d09015). Downstream, TaskKnowledgeSync.assemble_payload merges three channels for one concept. Stage 1 items_flagged passes through the ledger's filter_suppressed. The Mem0 flag_for_stage2 channel is a semantic search capped at limit=100, and no suppression applies to it ('the prompt directive is the only lever', flag_dedup docstring). recon_report systemic findings skip suppression and are supersession-filtered only. The merge is first-wins on two join keys (signature, content fingerprint), and an item's channel is tagged by a '_source' string.
findings.proposal: Create reconciliation/flag_identity.py as a leaf with no imports from server or stages. It defines a frozen FlagIdentity(task_ids: tuple[int,...], flag_type_family: str | None, content_fp: str | None) with one constructor, FlagIdentity.of(raw), that owns every normalization: str/int task_id, comma-joined ids, casefold/whitespace, flag_type family. Equality and hashing follow one documented precedence. recon_report, flag_dedup and TaskKnowledgeSync import it. Their copies and 'keep in sync' notes are deleted, and so are the false layering claims. Turn Stage-2 intake into one typed StageTwoFlag(identity, source: FlagSource enum, ...) produced by a single intake function. That function applies suppression, supersession and standing decisions once, by identity, whatever the channel. Retire the Mem0 flag_for_stage2 channel into the ledger, which fm-recon.1 already calls for. This would have prevented 2078 (double render), 1979 (int vs str key), the 6a55d09015 fold-vs-read-suppression regression, and the near-collision fixes.
findings.bug_history_link: Task 2078 (incident flag 2d2ad790, same finding rendered twice), task 1979 / run 9542fa10 (int vs str signature), 670d43ff5b (2318), 6a55d09015 (2425 fold regressed 1654 suppression), 8d0baa7406 + a8d414365a (cross-project near-collision fold), 4653 (3aa885cae2, 7d60774a4c, 09e6989023, 657af26b03), 4381/4864 cross-project suppression; mined theme 34x.
findings.verdict_notes: The docstring says it is re-implemented locally because server/ must not import from reconciliation. The same file imports fused_memory.reconciliation.citation_repair at line 26. flag_dedup.py claims reconciliation must not import from middleware, yet flag_dedup.py imports is_count_snapshot from reconciliation.task_filter. The false-rationale claim holds. I did not count the 9 recon_report rules.

findings.title: Recon stage identity is a prompt-instructed agent_id string, and stage capability is enforced in four separately maintained homes
findings.statement: BaseStage appends prose to every stage payload: '**IMPORTANT**: For every fused-memory write call, include `agent_id`: "recon-stage-<id>"'. The LLM then chooses whether to echo that string. Everything downstream keys on it. server/tools.py has 12 sites that route the content guards on `agent_id.startswith('recon-stage-')`. Middleware recon_write_policy, execution_class_guard, premise_lint_guard, recurring_gate_guard and task_interceptor test the same prefix. config/schema.py ships three ['recon-stage-','curator-'] allowlists (mem0 content amend, entity mint, and a third) that admit every stage. stage_stats attributes writes by the exact string, and its docstring admits that 'a stage that omits or mistypes its agent_id silently yields 0 for every counter'. An omitted prefix therefore bypasses ReconWritePolicy and the prose lints, while any non-recon caller that claims the prefix gains recon permissions. Capability is a separate set of homes: per-stage deny-lists in cli_stage_runner, so a new tool is allowed by default; the config prefix allowlists; and prompt prose that narrates the deny asymmetries (prompts/__init__.py). Because these must agree by hand, a write primitive has repeatedly shipped callable by read-only Stage 3: update_memory (aa02432724, esc-3623-3), reassign_edge (3009), ensure_entity_node (4932) and get_task_escalations (3023). 47af1638f8 scoped an absence guard to stages that actually deny each tool, and 52547fbb70 removed a prompt that licensed a Stage-3 escalation write. Task 3250 (b45d9a84f6, 10-07) closed 14 unclassified-tool gaps found by a new completeness test. That test now catches unclassified tools, but it does not unify the homes or bind the identity.
findings.proposal: Bind identity at the transport. cli_stage_runner mints a per-run, per-stage MCP credential (session header or token in the generated MCP config). fused-memory resolves it server-side to a frozen CallerIdentity, for example ReconStageCaller(stage: StageId, run_id), and makes it available to tools and middleware. LLM-supplied agent_id no longer carries authority and is ignored for recon callers. Add one capability table, STAGE_CAPABILITIES: Mapping[StageId, frozenset[ToolName]], as an allowlist. Derive from it the CLI --allowedTools, server-side authorization (one check in the MCP dispatch path), and the prompt's Available Tools section. What becomes deletable: the about 25 prefix checks, the recon entries in the three config prefix allowlists, the STAGE*_DISALLOWED fold algebra and its prose mirrors, and stage_stats' string attribution, which would key on the bound identity instead. This prevents the shipped-callable-write class and identity-spoofing or omission bypasses.
findings.bug_history_link: aa02432724 'deny update_memory in Stage 3' (task 3088, esc-3623-3); c8fd434f38 reassign_edge (3009); 7ace787d74 ensure_entity_node (4932); 92ccdc801a (3023); 47af1638f8 (3878); 617e381a58 (4377, esc-4377-10); b45d9a84f6 (3250, 14 gaps); 52547fbb70 (prompt licensed a Stage-3 write); stage_stats docstring on silent zero counters.
findings.verdict_notes: base.py instructs the LLM to echo agent_id 'recon-stage-<id>'. tools.py has 12 startswith('recon-stage-') sites. Eight middleware modules reference the prefix. config/schema.py has three ['recon-stage-','curator-'] allowlists (2838, 2859, 2942). Stage deny-lists are as described.

findings.title: TaskInterceptor returns refusals as untyped dicts, so each recon internal write must remember to classify or it logs a refusal as a landed write
findings.statement: The upstream defect is in middleware/task_interceptor.py: a gate refusal from update_task or set_task_status comes back as a dict. It has several shapes: {'success': False, 'error': ...} for write-authority errors, and {'error': ..., 'error_type': ...} with no success key for BacklogVerdict and lock-charter refusals. interceptor_write_succeeded is the documented classifier, and its own docstring warns that '{}' must count as failure. Classification is opt-in at each call site. targeted.py calls it 13 times and still needed six window fixes where a sweep discarded the response and journaled or acted as if the write had landed. Examples: 81b52fe088 'classify _sweep_block_orphan's status flip and stop stamping refusals', 5ed5d68609 (_sweep_cancel_orphan), 217eb3347d and 6478bd6529 (parent_cancelled stamp), aca7d4ef18 and 3b32b792f0 (missing journal rows). The fix commits themselves say 'a refusal and a raise are the same outcome for the caller: nothing landed'. Any new internal write site defaults to the wrong answer.
findings.proposal: Give internal callers a typed interceptor API. TaskInterceptor.apply_write(...) returns a WriteOutcome sum type (Landed(task) | Refused(error_type: RefusalKind enum, detail)), or raises WriteRefused, so a refusal can never pass as success. The MCP passthrough in server/tools.py renders WriteOutcome to the client dict at that one boundary. What becomes deletable: interceptor_write_succeeded and the per-site capture-classify-journal boilerplate in targeted.py, citation_verifier.py and manifest_stamping.py. Journal skip/write rows could be emitted centrally from the outcome. This prevents the 'classify X's response' fix series.
findings.bug_history_link: 81b52fe088, 5ed5d68609, 217eb3347d, 6478bd6529, aca7d4ef18, 3b32b792f0 (all 2026-09-09); 9ebe465083 (3581 hints-attach write); mined theme 22x 'classify _sweep_block_orphan's status flip / cancel write / parent_cancelled stamp response'.
findings.verdict_notes: targeted.py has 13 interceptor_write_succeeded references. Classification is opt-in per call site, as claimed. I did not re-verify the specific fix commits.

findings.title: Prose dominates the recon core files and goes wrong as code changes; a tenth of the sweep's commits only maintain it
findings.statement: Measured with AST and tokenize (comments plus docstrings over raw lines): stale_status_snapshot_edge_sweep.py is 76% prose (342 code lines of 2,293), flag_dedup.py 60%, task_filter.py 61%, recon_report.py 54%, task_knowledge_sync.py 51% and harness.py 49%. Much of it is reviewer-answering archaeology that the Comments stance assigns to commit messages or task records. The sweep's module docstring is about 250 lines of '(amendment, reviewer_comprehensive ... task 3037)', 'Two hypotheses were investigated and RULED OUT ... AMENDED, task 4340', measured figures, and a list of residuals. Prose maintenance is now its own stream of churn. About 10 of 61 window commits on the sweep only correct it: d28a4231b8 'correct the three prose claims task 3403 made false', 459acfb83b 'correct two records the measurement invalidated', dc0097121f 'soften unverified corpus-safety claim', e6023c29b8 'De-duplicate module docstring', 1f0057f348, eef5fdfc75, 5f25db773e, fca657951c, 9178d652ef and 7264c546f4. Prose that is currently false exists too. The local-copy rationales in recon_report._canonical_sig_field and flag_dedup._COUNT_GROUP_RE describe import restrictions the same modules violate. That violates heuristic 1 for prose, and the stance's warning that comments drift.
findings.proposal: Move the measured figures, ruled-out hypotheses and residual lists to plans/ or docs/reconciliation/ with one path pointer from the module. Move review defences into the commit or task record. Keep at most the invariants the code relies on, stated once at the owning symbol. Delete the false layering rationales in the same change that consolidates the identity code (see the flag-identity finding). Track prose share per file as a report metric, not a gate.
findings.bug_history_link: d28a4231b8, 459acfb83b, dc0097121f, e6023c29b8, 1f0057f348, eef5fdfc75, 5f25db773e, fca657951c, 9178d652ef, 7264c546f4, 8dceb3c3c4 'cut defence prose to the invariants the code relies on', fca4ac0e52.
findings.verdict_notes: My AST/tokenize measurement gives prose fractions of 0.76 (sweep), 0.60 (flag_dedup), 0.49 (harness) and 0.61 (task_filter), matching the claim. The false local-copy rationales are verified under fm-recon.3. The commit count of prose-only fixes was not re-checked.

findings.title: Cycle-summary write state is a four-way flag set built from string keys in the free-form stats dict, read back by a cross-module backstop
findings.statement: After the nonce chain was deleted (fm-recon.2, 3225a1094f), a successor backstop grew in its place. The stage writes its cycle_summary ledger row in-stage, best-effort: write_cycle_summary swallows the upsert failure and returns False. It reports the outcome through StageReport.stats, the dict the LLM also writes and stats_verifier rewrites. The stats carry f'{stage}_cycle_summary_ledger_written' (0, 1 or absent, with three distinct meanings), '_degraded_backstop' (True) and '_write_recovered_backstop' (True or False, where only `is True` counts). The harness parses these back through _cycle_summary_ledger_write_missing. The predicates must use `== 0`, never `!= 1`, because an absent key means 'Stage 2 died before its write'. They must exclude the harness's own synthetic reports and confirmed recoveries, and survive run.stage_reports being typed dict[str, StageReport | dict] because of journal round-trips. The backstop has two arms per stage, a pre-Stage-3 flush and a finally flush. Each subtle predicate rule arrived as a fix.
findings.proposal: Make the harness the single writer. A stage returns its report, and the run driver (see the run-driver finding) writes the cycle summary once from the typed report, retrying inside the driver. No 'in-stage write failed' state exists and no stat carries it. If an in-stage write must stay, return a typed CycleSummaryOutcome enum (WRITTEN | FAILED | NOT_REACHED) on a dedicated StageReport field rather than in stats, and type stage_reports as dict[StageId, StageReport] with a separate RunFailure field for '_error'. What becomes deletable: _cycle_summary_ledger_write_missing and its two wrappers, the marker-stamped-copy discipline in _reattempt_cycle_summary_write, the three stat keys per stage, and the pre-S3 flush. This prevents the 2734, 3732, 4186 and 5127aaacfb predicate fixes and the shield races.
findings.bug_history_link: Tasks 2440 (755ef1852f), 2626 (104b4ab2ff), 2734 (bb7d1b41b5, 248824acd2), 3732 (41f240f424, 17a9d85247), 4186 (33556bf048, 15d99d1aea), 5127aaacfb 'exclude a CONFIRMED write-recovery from the write-missing predicate', fef7e6612f 'shield the degraded arm's clobber-guard read with its write'; mined cycle_summary races 2440/2626/3741/3749/5546.
findings.verdict_notes: The predicate at harness.py reads the string-keyed stats f'{prefix}_cycle_summary_degraded_backstop', '_write_recovered_backstop' (checked with `is True`) and '_ledger_written' (checked with `== 0`). The three-way meaning of an absent key is as described.

findings.title: flag_dedup.py is ledger dedup plus about 12 incident-driven LLM false-positive filters, hand-chained in a 1,140-line MemoryConsolidator.run
findings.statement: Answer to ask 3. flag_dedup.py is 6,021 lines (60% prose), and its purpose needs several 'and's. It runs the ledger marker and suppression lifecycle (filter_suppressed, dedup_flags at 545 lines, write_suppression_record, acknowledge_*). It also performs cross-project fix-task discovery and holds about 12 standalone false-positive filters, each added after an incident: stale count-snapshot (1786), terminal metadata (1725), stale bulk get_statuses (3007), false absence, phantom task creation (2525), already-tracked systemic pattern (2416), blocked snapshot (1840), contamination ceiling (2818), style-only authorship (3138), accounted cluster growth (3476), already-recorded caveat (5271) and entity standing decisions (2896). Measured by intra-module reference: none of the filters references dedup_flags or ledger code. They share only a task-lookup leaf (safe_get_task, _safe_get_task_or_none, confirm_task_*), canonical_flag_type_family, and the tracked-task term matcher (_TrackedTask, _significant_terms), which dedup_flags' discovery also uses. So the split has a named partition with no reach-back, provided those three leaves move downward. Two sibling filters already live in their own modules (sweep_deletion_guard, preservation_specimen_guard), so where a filter lives is arbitrary. MemoryConsolidator.run invokes the filters by hand, each with a before/after length idiom, a hand-named stat key and a comment explaining its load-bearing position relative to _pre_filter_flags, dedup_flags and Hook A's suppressed-signature exclusion. filter_terminal_metadata_flags is the one filter with no drop stat. The same key-by-key projection carries sweep stats (orphan sweep 8 keys, snapshot sweep 7, priority sweep 4), which is the known 'new sweep keys silently die at the boundary' class.
findings.proposal: Define a FlagFilter protocol in reconciliation/flag_filters/__init__.py. It has name, stat_key, phase (PRE_SNAPSHOT | POST_SNAPSHOT | SUPPRESSION; suppression drops join suppressed_signatures instead of being acknowledged), and async apply(flags, ctx) -> FilterResult(kept, dropped, suppressed_signatures). One ordered FLAG_FILTERS tuple is the single statement of order. Put one module per filter under flag_filters/, importing the new leaves flag_task_lookup.py and tracked_task_terms.py. MemoryConsolidator.run calls run_flag_filters(FLAG_FILTERS, ctx) and merges FilterResult.stats uniformly. Give sweeps the same treatment: each returns a typed SweepStats with a to_stats() method merged wholesale. flag_dedup.py keeps only identity and the ledger lifecycle. What becomes deletable: about 160 lines of hand-chained blocks in run(), the order comments, and the per-key stat copies. This prevents the silent-stat-key class and the missing-stat inconsistency.
findings.bug_history_link: Filters added by tasks 1725, 1786, 1840, 2416, 2525, 2818/2826, 2896, 3007, 3138, 3476, 4381, 4864, 5271; known bug class 'sweep stats reach report.stats key by key in memory_consolidator'; mined theme 34x (flag dedup / gate false positives).
findings.verdict_notes: flag_dedup.py is 6021 lines, 60% prose, with 13 filter_* functions among 68 top-level functions. MemoryConsolidator.run spans about 1141 lines and calls filter_terminal_metadata_flags directly at line 712. I did not verify the no-reach-back partition or the drop-stat details.

findings.title: Cap-retry loop re-decides the invocation verdict through four mechanisms beside classify_invocation, with precedence encoded as statement order
findings.statement: invoke_with_cap_retry classifies each result once via classify_invocation(result, strict_confirm=True), but the loop acts on that outcome for only AuthFailed, ModelNotFound, ZeroOutputWedge and ServerError. For cap detection it ignores the outcome and calls slot.detect_cap_hit(stderr, output). That path builds a synthetic AgentResult(success=False, ...) with no api_error_status or timed_out and classifies it a second time (UsageGate.detect_cap_hit). Beside that sit three more decisions made outside the sum type: (a) _should_retry_cli_input_rejected / is_cli_invocation_rejected, a side predicate with no outcome variant; (b) an inline 'heuristic cap net' (not success and cost==0 and turns<=1 and duration<5000) that builds its own CapHit, with a hand-written escape for CliLocalError and ServerError; (c) is_timed_out_with_progress. The cooldown formula min(base * 2**full_cycles, max) is copied at two sites, and the pair _reset_for_fresh_retry plus _rebuild_fresh_prompt is repeated six times. Precedence between these is the textual order of branches across about 700 lines, and the comments say so ('Placement is load-bearing in three directions', 'AFTER slot.detect_cap_hit', 'ABOVE the heuristic cap safety-net'). Every new classification needed a new escape in the heuristic net or a new reorder: the ServerError escape (2026-07-29 incident), ModelNotFound mislabelled as cap, CliLocalError reify-3604, the CLI-input-rejection ordering. The function is 1,016 lines, 595 of them prose, including two measurement narratives with session UUIDs (tasks 3454/3484) that already have a home in plans/cross-account-resume-measurement.md, which the comment cites. Its signature has about 15 parameters, each added by a task (rebuild_prompt, resume_delivers_prompt, park_on_frozen_pool, is_usable_reply, max_cap_retries). The no-gate fast path is a second copy of the rejected-retry loop.
findings.proposal: Make the sum type the only verdict and the loop a thin interpreter. (1) classify_invocation takes the real result and gains the missing variants: CliInputRejected, TimedOutWithProgress, and HeuristicCap(inferred=True) carrying the zero-cost instant-exit rule, with precedence expressed as tiers in that one function (it already has a precedence docstring). (2) Add shared/cap_retry_policy.py with a pure decide(outcome, attempt_state) -> RetryStep, a frozen union of Failover(reason), ResumeCapped, RetryFresh(reason), Terminal and CapWait(cooldown), plus one cooldown(hits, num_accounts) function. attempt_state is a frozen dataclass replacing the invoke_kwargs mutations (prompt, resume_session_id, session_id) through one with_fresh() method. (3) invoke_with_cap_retry becomes acquire slot, invoke, classify, slot.report(outcome), then match decide(...). Replace the two cooldown copies with the one function. Move the long measurement narratives to the existing plans/ file and leave a path pointer. Deletable: UsageGate.detect_cap_hit and its synthetic AgentResult, InvokeSlot.detect_cap_hit, InvokeSlot.settle, the inline heuristic net with its escapes, the cap-like-prefix breadcrumb scan, the duplicated fast-path loop, and the six reset/rebuild copies. This would have prevented the classes behind 3314/3319-3322 (5xx treated as cap), reify-3604 and 3143 (local errors treated as cap) and 4096 (probe slot leak). Structural: needs deliberation then /prd.
findings.bug_history_link: 3314, 3319, 3321, 3322 (5xx classification and requeue); 3143, 3147 (CLI input rejection); reify-3604 (CliLocalError counted as cap); 4096 (release the probe slot in InvokeSlot.detect_cap_hit); 4274 (resume must verify work); 6042 (is_usable_reply parameter); 5637
findings.verdict_notes: Verified in invoke_with_cap_retry: the loop acts on the classified outcome only for AuthFailed (2642), ModelNotFound (2664), ZeroOutputWedge (2751), and ServerError (3128). Cap detection goes through slot.detect_cap_hit (2767), which builds a synthetic AgentResult and classifies a second time in UsageGate.detect_cap_hit. The heuristic net at ~3002 (turns<=1, duration<5000) has its own CliLocalError/ServerError escape at 3005. The cooldown formula is duplicated at 2773 and 3067. The reset/rebuild pair appears seven times (2644, 2758, 2935, 2946, 2959, 3071, 3192), so the claimed six is a slight undercount. The function spans about 1,018 lines, and the 'AFTER/ABOVE' ordering comments are present.

findings.title: Default cap detection scans successful results, so a successful reply that quotes cap text is discarded and the account marked CAPPED
findings.statement: offered_to_cap_detector = (not result.success) or (is_usable_reply is None) or (not is_usable_reply(result.output)). With the default is_usable_reply=None this is True for every result, including successes. slot.detect_cap_hit then builds a synthetic success=False result from stderr and output, which defeats classify_invocation's OK short-circuit, so any success whose text carries a CAP_HIT or NEAR_CAP prefix plus a confirm keyword ('resets', 'usage limit') is read as cap. The docstring records the measurement (2026-10-02: a verdict quoting REAL_CLI_CAP_HIT_MESSAGES[0] is OK() as it is and CapHit once forced to fail) and fixes it only for the legibility runner via an opt-in predicate; the fleet default is 'unchanged'. A hit on that path increments consecutive_cap_hits, calls _handle_cap_detected (account to CAPPED, cap_hit event), sleeps the cooldown and re-runs a task that had already succeeded. NearCap is also a True return from detect_cap_hit, so a mere near-cap warning in a failed result is counted as a hard cap and triggers the same sleep and retry. Dark Factory agents routinely work on this very code, its tests and cap fixtures, and write summaries that quote it.
findings.proposal: Scan only what can be a banner. In the loop, offer a result to cap detection when `not result.success`, or when it is a success whose whole output is banner-shaped (short and starting with a marker, matching the exit-0 banner case of task 5637). Replace the opt-in is_usable_reply default with this rule everywhere. Return the NearCap outcome as a non-retrying annotation rather than a bool 'hit'. Pin it with a regression test feeding a long successful reply that quotes REAL_CLI_CAP_HIT_MESSAGES. This folds into the verdict consolidation of the first finding, but is fixable alone.
findings.bug_history_link: 6042 (is_usable_reply opt-in), 5637 (exit-0 banner route), 2026-10-02 measurement quoted in the docstring
findings.verdict_notes: offered_to_cap_detector at ~2762 is True for every result when is_usable_reply is None. UsageGate.detect_cap_hit builds AgentResult(success=False,...), which bypasses classify_invocation's OK short-circuit. Its CapHit and NearCap branches both go to the handlers. The docstring (~2296) records the 2026-10-02 measurement and says the default is 'unchanged for the fleet', which matches the claim. The hazard is known and documented, not guarded by default.

findings.title: UsageGate is a 2,300-line class that owns the account machine, the scope overlay, the probe subprocess and config reload; the probe mutates account state and returns a bool
findings.statement: UsageGate spans lines 710-3028 (2,315 lines, 79 methods, 1,156 of them prose). Its purpose needs 'and': (a) account selection, leasing and the phase machine (try_lease, before_invoke, _transition, about 900 lines); (b) a per-(account, model) ScopeCap overlay (_scope_cap_for through _refresh_scope_capped, about 250 lines); (c) probe machinery that spawns a CLI subprocess and runs resume and auth loops with a spawn-fault latch (_run_probe, _account_resume_probe_loop, _reprobe_account, _note_probe_spawn_failure, about 700 lines); (d) SIGHUP reload; (e) cost-event emission. Heuristic 14 measurement: the partition (c) is the one that can split without stitching, because its only inputs are an oauth token, a config dir and a config. It does not do so today. _run_probe takes an AccountState and performs the AUTH_FAILED to CAPPED demotion itself: it cancels acct.auth_reprobe_task, sets acct.auth_reprobe_task = None, writes acct.resets_at and calls self._transition, inside a method documented as 'fire a probe and return bool'. That is why a split would currently fail heuristic 13: a probe module would need the gate's private _transition, _config_dir_for and AccountState, an upward reach-back import. The return type is a bool because, per the docstring, about 60 test call sites stub _run_probe with AsyncMock(return_value=True/False), so the tests' interface dictated the design (Tests stance).
findings.proposal: Introduce shared/usage_probe.py with a stateless `async def run_probe(token, config_dir, timeout) -> ProbeVerdict`, a frozen union Served | StillBlocked(outcome: CapHit|NearCap) | Inconclusive(detail) | SpawnFault(ProbeSpawnError), importing only AgentResult, classify_invocation, resolve_claude_binary and proc_group (all downward). The two loops stay in the gate and call the probe, and a single `_apply_probe_verdict(acct, verdict)` owns every transition, including the AUTH_FAILED to CAPPED demotion, so the probe never touches AccountState. Move the scope overlay behind a ScopeCaps collaborator (see the AccountState finding). Deletable: the probe's direct acct writes, the bool-return rationale and the roughly 60 AsyncMock(True/False) stubs (replaced by verdict stubs). Measured trade-off: the gate stays about 1,300 lines, with the probe file about 500, in line with heuristic 14's 'file stays whole only with a recorded measurement'.
findings.bug_history_link: 4512 (probe-spawn fault latch), 5944 (probe re-admission on a served call), 3086/3288 (probe-dir and background-task leaks), 3273
findings.verdict_notes: UsageGate runs from line 710 to about 3028 and combines the account machine, scope overlay, probe machinery and reload. _run_probe has a bool return, and its docstring cites about 60 AsyncMock call sites as the reason. In the AUTH_FAILED to cap-prefix arm (~2718-2745) it cancels acct.auth_reprobe_task, sets it to None, writes acct.resets_at and calls self._transition. That is state mutation inside a method documented as 'fire a probe and return bool'. Line counts are approximate.

findings.title: The orchestrator re-implements the whole claude spawn recipe instead of using the sandbox_wrap hook, and the copy has already diverged (no VllmBridge)
findings.statement: shared.cli_invoke._invoke_claude builds argv (build_claude_argv), encodes stdin, builds the env (drop ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, env_overrides, apply_spawn_env, oauth token, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR), optionally starts a VllmBridge when ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is overridden, applies sandbox_wrap, runs _run_subprocess, parses, and unlinks temp files. orchestrator/agents/invoke.py::_invoke_claude_with_sandbox repeats every step except the bridge, with 'lockstep obligation' comments in place of sharing (both for the blank-prompt guard and for the env block), and imports four underscore-private shared names to do so (_run_subprocess, _parse_claude_output, _materialize_stdin, _SubprocessResult, re-exported with noqa). invoke_claude_agent already accepts sandbox_wrap, and the fused-memory recon runner uses it (cli_stage_runner.py), so the hook the orchestrator needs exists. Concrete divergence: with env_overrides['ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL'] set (the vLLM path) and sandbox_modules active, the orchestrator copy points the CLI directly at the upstream URL while the shared path starts the translating bridge. The wrapper _invoke_claude is itself a 24-parameter pure forwarder of invoke_claude_agent. orchestrator/usage_gate.py is a 10-line star-import shim kept 'for backwards compatibility' with five production importers.
findings.proposal: In _invoke_claude_with_sandbox, call invoke_claude_agent(..., sandbox_wrap=lambda cmd: wrap_command(cmd, cwd, sandbox_modules, writable_extras=sandbox_extras)) when resolve_active_backend() != 'none'. Delete the copied block (about 70 lines), the four private re-exports, and the lockstep comments. Collapse invoke_claude_agent and _invoke_claude into one function. Replace orchestrator.usage_gate imports with shared.usage_gate and delete the shim. Prevented class: argv/env drift ('forward backend to custom invoke_fn only', 'extract build_claude_argv', 'resolve argv[0]') where each fix had to be made twice.
findings.bug_history_link: 2465/2512 (dedup of argv build and spawn env between the two paths); 3143 (the blank-prompt guard had to be added to both); 3983 (--system-prompt-file on resume); 4448
findings.verdict_notes: The sandbox branch repeats build_claude_argv, stdin encoding, env construction (drop ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, overrides, oauth token, config dir, apply_spawn_env), _run_subprocess and temp-file unlink, with 'lockstep' comments. It has no VllmBridge handling: grep for vllm or bridge in orchestrator agents/invoke.py finds nothing, while shared _invoke_claude starts the bridge when env_overrides carries ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (~3520). This is a real divergence. orchestrator/usage_gate.py is a star-import shim and five production imports still use it.

findings.title: cli_invoke, invocation_outcome and usage_gate form an import cycle resolved by five function-local imports
findings.statement: shared/invocation_outcome.py imports is_server_error_status and is_zero_output_timeout at module level from shared.cli_invoke (line 39). cli_invoke therefore cannot import invocation_outcome at module level, and takes it with function-local imports at four sites (the CLI-input-marker lookups in _stderr_has_cli_input_required and is_cli_invocation_rejected, classify_agent_failure, and the loop body of invoke_with_cap_retry, which carries a comment explaining it breaks the cycle). A fifth local import (`from shared.usage_gate import scope_for`) breaks the usage_gate to cli_invoke cycle, because usage_gate imports AgentResult from cli_invoke; scope_for is a pure function of UsageCapConfig and lives in the wrong module. usage_gate itself has a function-local import of the prefix tables to satisfy a single-ownership test. Heuristic 14 measurement for cli_invoke.py (4,459 lines): top-level symbol partition is (1) result types and failure predicates (AgentResult, is_zero_output_timeout, is_server_error_status, is_timed_out_with_progress, about 400 lines); (2) transcript readers and evidence (read_transcript_records through transcript_evidence_for_session, about 900 lines, pure over paths and records); (3) taxonomies (classify_agent_failure, classify_cap_kill, about 400); (4) the retry loop; (5) argv build and subprocess runner (build_claude_argv through _run_subprocess, about 1,200). Candidates (2) and (5) have no upward import: both depend only on (1), so they split cleanly. The only real cycle is (1)'s predicates being imported by invocation_outcome while the loop imports it back, and that disappears once (1) is its own module.
findings.proposal: Create shared/agent_result.py (AgentResult, is_zero_output_timeout, is_server_error_status, is_timed_out_with_progress, the CLI-input marker table's owner), importing nothing from the three modules. invocation_outcome imports downward from it. cli_invoke imports invocation_outcome at module top, and the four local imports die. Move scope_for into config_models next to UsageCapConfig, which kills the fifth. Then split cli_invoke into transcript_evidence.py (group 2), claude_process.py (group 5) and the loop, each importing downward only. This is legitimate under heuristic 14's no-cheating rule because every resulting file passes 13. The measurement above is the record that heuristic asks for.
findings.bug_history_link: reify-3604 and the circular-import comments added with W4 classification; speculative for future cycles
findings.verdict_notes: invocation_outcome.py line 39 imports is_server_error_status and is_zero_output_timeout from cli_invoke at module level. cli_invoke takes function-local imports from invocation_outcome at 1469, 1493, 1816 and 2610. The fifth local import is `from shared.usage_gate import scope_for` at 2578. usage_gate imports AgentResult from cli_invoke at module level (32). scope_for is a pure function of UsageCapConfig at usage_gate.py. usage_gate also has a local prefix-table import at ~1618. The cycle structure is as claimed.

findings.title: Probe spawns a bare 'claude' argv[0], the PATH-resolution failure that build_claude_argv was changed to avoid
findings.statement: build_claude_argv now resolves argv[0] through resolve_claude_binary / claude_binary_spec (CLAUDE_BINARY override, tasks 4448/6520) because the 2026-08-13 to 08-18 incident showed a bare 'claude' failing to resolve off an unpinned systemd PATH. UsageGate._run_probe still builds its own argv with the literal 'claude' as the first element. It is the only remaining literal outside cli_invoke's definition and docstrings (a grep for the quoted name across the production trees finds nothing else), and also the third independent claude argv builder. On a host where CLAUDE_BINARY is set but PATH lacks claude, real invocations spawn fine while every probe raises ProbeSpawnError, and the gate latches probe_infra_fault. Capped accounts then never get re-admitted by the probe loop and recover only through the clock-driven _refresh_capped_accounts path.
findings.proposal: Replace the literal with claude_binary_spec() / resolve_claude_binary() (or, better, build the probe argv through a small `build_probe_argv()` beside build_claude_argv so one function owns every claude command line). Add a test that sets CLAUDE_BINARY to an absolute path with an empty PATH and asserts the probe spawns it. Natural place to fold into the probe extraction of the god-module finding.
findings.bug_history_link: 6520 (CLAUDE_BINARY single source), 4448 (resolve argv[0]), 4512 (probe-spawn fault latch)
findings.verdict_notes: _run_probe builds cmd = ['claude', '--print', ...] with a literal argv[0]. It spawns cmd[0] and raises ProbeSpawnError on failure. build_claude_argv uses claude_binary_spec / resolve_claude_binary (cli_invoke 309-341, 3301). usage_gate.py has no reference to CLAUDE_BINARY or resolve_claude_binary. The probe therefore ignores the override.

findings.title: Cost and timing are recorded once at loop exit, so discarded cap-retry attempts spend money invisibly and resumed totals are cumulative
findings.statement: account_name, started_at, completed_at, unattributed_cap, resume_fallbacks and resume_fallback_session_ids are loop-lifetime locals stamped onto the returned result at the exit (heuristic 5), and cost_store.save_invocation is called exactly once, after the loop, for the final result. Every attempt the loop discards (an exact cap hit after real work, an auth failover, a failed resume retried fresh, the wedge guard, the rejected-input retry) never reaches save_invocation, and slot.confirm(result.cost_usd), which feeds gate.on_agent_complete and the session budget, runs only for the final attempt. A cap hit with cost_usd above zero is discarded without being recorded anywhere except a cap_hit account event without a cost. When the retry resumes the capped session, the final result reports the session's cumulative total_cost_usd, so recording only the final attempt is right for resumed chains and wrong for fresh restarts (the cause of the mixed semantics tracked in 5727/5818). The invariant 'every attempt that spent money has exactly one cost row, and summing rows equals provider spend' is stated nowhere and enforced nowhere, and started_at/completed_at describe only the last attempt.
findings.proposal: Introduce a frozen AttemptRecord(account_name, started_at, completed_at, cost_delta_usd, tokens, outcome_kind, resumed_from) built per attempt, and record it in the loop's per-attempt finally via one `record_attempt()` helper that calls save_invocation and slot.confirm/on_agent_complete with the delta (cost minus the cost already attributed to that session_id on a resume). The post-loop block then only stamps the final result. Add the invariant check (sum of attempt deltas equals the final result's cumulative cost for a resumed chain) as a runtime assertion with a message naming both values (INV-2). Deletable: the loop-lifetime locals and the end-of-function save block.
findings.bug_history_link: 5727 (cap-retry discarded attempts invisible to cost, LIVE), 5818 (resumed session reports cumulative total_cost_usd, LIVE), 3578 (resume_fallbacks stamped at exit)
findings.verdict_notes: cost_store.save_invocation is called once, after the loop (~3217), for the final result only. Inside the loop the cap path writes only save_account_event('cap_hit') (2779) with no cost. slot.confirm(result.cost_usd) runs only on terminal exits, so discarded attempts never get a cost row. started_at, completed_at and account_name are loop-scope locals stamped at exit. No invariant stating one cost row per spending attempt was found.

findings.title: Write-content policy has no home: guards are inline per tool body, scoped by caller-asserted category and a self-asserted 'recon-stage-' prefix, so each sibling entry point bypasses a different subset
findings.statement: The add_memory tool closure in server/tools.py::create_mcp_server is about 530 lines. Before calling MemoryService.add_memory it runs about 17 gates as inline if-chains: project canonicalize, validate, known-project, backlog, category, entities_gate, markup override strip, three recon-only content guards (count snapshot, mixed framing, conflicting status), _flag_kind_refusal_block, live-status, premature-completion (I/O), write triage (LLM judge), topic-cluster, cosine near-dup (I/O), completion-claim label, and the attach/fallback logic. MemoryService.add_memory then applies about 6 more (enforce_flag_record_write_contract, classifier, _normalize_task_id_metadata, cycle-summary tagging, _apply_memory_metadata_validation, resolve_referents). Each gate is scoped by its own category frozenset (_TRIAGED_CATEGORIES, _TOPIC_GUARD_GATED_CATEGORIES, _LIVE_STATUS_GATED_CATEGORIES, _COMPLETION_CLAIM_GATED_CATEGORIES). Those sets test the caller-supplied category above the layer that resolves category=None, so an auto-classified write skips every category-scoped guard. CLAUDE.md documents this as a caveat rather than fixing it. The recon content guards are hand-copied into the add_episode body with different conditions. add_system_record (recon-only) runs only _flag_kind_refusal_block, so a recon-stage observations_and_summaries write skips the live-status and premature-completion guards that add_memory applies to the same agent. update_memory's content arm runs only authorization, so an amend skips every content guard. Role is decided by `agent_id.startswith('recon-stage-')`: 23 literal sites across tools.py (12), execution_class_guard, premise_lint_guard, recurring_gate_guard, recon_write_policy, task_interceptor, stats_verifier and recon_lifecycle_filer, plus three config prefix lists. That agent_id is self-asserted, because _resolve_identity lets explicit caller values win over the MCP client identity. The guard exemptions interact (triage_enabled, allow_near_duplicate, caller_owns_attach_keys, dup_guard_base_exempt, resolve_near_dup_guard_enabled), and the code carries long comments defending deferred arms and truth-table equivalences.
findings.proposal: Create fused_memory/write_policy/ with a frozen WriteIntent: entry_point (EntryPoint enum: add_memory, add_episode, add_system_record, update_memory_content, consolidate_canonical, replay), caller (CallerRole enum parsed once in _resolve_identity: recon_stage(stage_id), curator, agent, unknown), resolved_category, project_id, content, override flags. Add a declarative WRITE_POLICY table of Guard(name, applies(intent), check(intent) -> Refusal|Label|None) in which each entry-point exemption is a table cell. Run a single evaluate_write_policy(intent) inside MemoryService after category resolution, and call it from every content-producing method (add_memory, add_episode, add_system_record, update_memory content arm). That puts category=None and every sibling path under one policy (enforced uniformly, per heuristic 10). Tool bodies shrink to argument validation plus one call. A table-driven test over (guard x entry point) becomes the spec. Code that dies: the five inline recon blocks in add_memory and four in add_episode, dup_guard_base_exempt and its truth-table comments, the per-gate category-frozenset interplay prose, all 23 startswith('recon-stage-') spellings, and the CLAUDE.md 'category=None is covered by neither guard' caveat. This would have prevented the 24x guard theme's bypass and coverage-gap half (2845/3430/4729-style widenings done per copy; 3430's 'two conjunct chains can silently drift').
findings.bug_history_link: Mined guard theme (24x): 2845, 3054 (ded8a0c84e), 3114, 3430, 3435, 3862, 3899, 3908, 3968, 4179, 4255, 4729, 4738, 4739, 4773, 4815, 4849/4898 hardening, 5483, 5541, 5933, 5881, 4493; 3127 triage fixes b63750de81, 3dc1f3fdec, 7a1ae5d1bc; 3658 f62f8901e9; 3111 a0ff128d42 (candidate-set consumers opt out of topic pin); 4458 (markup gate moved to one boundary, the precedent this proposal generalises)
findings.verdict_notes: Category frozensets (_TRIAGED_CATEGORIES, _TOPIC_GUARD_GATED_CATEGORIES) are defined inside create_mcp_server and gate on the caller-supplied category; add_system_record is a separate entry point; 12 recon-stage- prefix sites in tools.py. Exact gate counts not re-counted.

findings.title: The write-time identity lock is a docstring contract honoured at only two sites; merge/rename/delete/reassign and out-of-process maintenance mutate entity identity unlocked
findings.statement: W6 made identity a write-time guarantee by having MemoryService._execute_graphiti_write hold GraphitiBackend._identity_lock_for(group_id) across add_episode and the nine-pass _reconcile_episode_identity. That chain includes _dedup_episode_nodes, which collapses duplicates through _resolve_or_create_entity and merges. The lock is a private accessor that MemoryService reaches into (`self.graphiti._identity_lock_for`). It is acquired in exactly two places in fused-memory/src: _execute_graphiti_write and MemoryService.ensure_entity_node, whose own docstring calls itself 'the SECOND acquisition site'. GraphitiBackend._resolve_or_create_entity, _resolve_without_collapsing and ensure_entity_node say callers 'MUST hold _identity_lock_for(group_id)', and nothing checks that. MemoryService.merge_entities, rename_entity, delete_entity, reassign_edge and update_edge call GraphitiBackend.merge_entities, rename_entity_node, delete_entity and reassign_edge with no lock. Those are the MCP tools recon Stage 1 and link-heal use to repair identity. A recon merge can therefore delete or redirect a node while the ingest reconcile for the same group is collapsing onto it. The lock is also a per-instance in-process asyncio.Lock: maintenance scripts that build their own service (migrate_cross_graph_leak through cross_graph_move, which reaches GraphitiBackend._graph_for 18 times) have a separate registry and are never serialised. GraphitiBackend's startup identity-scan docstring concedes the cross-process gap.
findings.proposal: Promote the lock to a public, checked capability. GraphitiBackend.identity_section(group_id, timeout) returns an async context manager that yields an IdentitySection token. Every identity-mutating backend method (merge_entities, redirect_node_edges, rename_entity_node, delete_entity, reassign_edge, _resolve_or_create_entity, ensure_entity_node) takes `section: IdentitySection` and asserts at use that section.held and section.group_id == group_id, raising an error that names the invariant and both group ids (enforced informatively and redundantly, per heuristic 10). MemoryService's mutators acquire it through one bounded helper factored out of ensure_entity_node's wait_for(lock.acquire()). Inside the section, take a FalkorDB-side advisory key (SET NX with TTL per group) so a second process is covered too. Code that dies: the three 'MUST hold' backend contracts and their service-side echoes, ensure_entity_node's lock-rationale prose, and every `self.graphiti._identity_lock_for` private reach. This would have prevented the original duplicate-node and manual FalkorDB merge class (2073/2081/2110/2118) from re-entering through the remediation tools instead of through ingest.
findings.bug_history_link: W6 2198/2202 (lock introduced on ingest only), 2207 W6-delta, 50bab12521 'group_id property filter on exact-name queries', 4986 merge series (74ee2c38e4, d9cdb80a68, 321644a533), 4932 ensure_entity_node lock-timeout, operator duplicate-node manual-merge runbook (2073/2081/2110/2118); the unlocked-mutator race itself is speculative (no incident yet attributed to it)
findings.verdict_notes: Lock acquired only at memory_service.py::_execute_graphiti_write (about line 5955) and ensure_entity_node (about line 10166); MUST-hold contracts are docstring only; merge_entities, rename_entity, delete_entity and reassign_edge take no lock; the lock is a per-instance dict (_identity_locks). The structure is real, but the finding itself concedes the race is speculative with no incident, so severity high is overstated.

findings.title: RELATES_TO edge lifecycle (live / invalidated / restored / merged-away) is encoded as two nullable timestamps whose meaning each reader and writer re-decides
findings.statement: No type or transition table holds an edge's state. 'Live' is the inline Cypher text `invalid_at IS NULL`, spelled at five query sites in graphiti_client.py and mirrored in Python in MemoryService._search_graphiti and get_entity. 'Restored' is an implicit signature: expired_at SET with invalid_at NULL. That signature is produced because the restore hooks (MemoryService._restore_superseded_dependency_edges, _restore_falsely_superseded_sibling_edges) clear only invalid_at through update_edge(clear_invalid_at=True). Four more writers set invalid_at independently: _invalidate_stale_superseded_ttl_edges, _check_dependency_direction, _repair_edge_findings and graphiti_core itself. The property set that must survive any edge copy is hand-written as SET lists in eight places: GraphitiBackend.reassign_edge x2, redirect_node_edges x2, and cross_graph_move's move_entity_across_graphs, _recreate_subgraph_relationships_batch x2 and merge_foreign_duplicate. The four cross_graph_move copies omit expired_at, superseded_edge_uuid and reassigned_from_node_uuid. Task 4714 shows the cost. It routed readers through a shared active-edge predicate that also filtered expired_at, which hid every restored edge (3,024 of 15,766 active edges). Its branch then went through fix, revert, a revert of a revert and an L2 ruling (esc-4714-9) before settling. Task 4986 lost expired_at in one redirect SET list but not its twin. The redirect_node_edges docstring now relies on keeping the two lists visually adjacent as the safeguard.
findings.proposal: Add backends/edge_lifecycle.py, owning an EdgeState enum (live, invalidated, restored, merged_away) and classify(props) -> EdgeState. It provides the one ACTIVE_EDGE_PREDICATE Cypher fragment and its Python twin, both generated from classify's rule. Its transition functions invalidate, restore and retire_by_merge are the only writers of invalid_at/expired_at, and each returns its SET fragment. Restoration gets an explicit property (restored_at, or state) instead of overloading expired_at. The module also owns RELATES_TO_PROPERTIES and edge_copy_set_clause(src, dst), from which every copy/recreate SET list in graphiti_client.py and cross_graph_move.py is generated. A property added there reaches all eight sites. Code that dies: five inline predicates, the Python mirror, eight hand-maintained SET lists, and the 'keep them adjacent so omissions are visible' prose. This would have prevented the 4714 predicate saga, the 4986 expired_at loss and the cross_graph_move loss reported separately.
findings.bug_history_link: 4714 branch: eefb4f1a6e, 267881aaa3, 70de2a0fb6, c81ab035fa, 9a10182ab8, 8a8083ff98 (esc-4714-9, Leo ruling A; branch not on HEAD, still live); 4986 d9cdb80a68 'redirect_node_edges preserves expired_at'; 2319/2349/2351 under-invalidation (aac4ba972c, 4f2d9fdb4b); 2451 cross-graph-move null-tolerant CREATE series (6 commits re-editing the same SET lists)
findings.verdict_notes: expired_at is copied in the graphiti_client.py redirect and reassign SET lists (lines about 2224, 2244, 2988, 3030) and absent from cross_graph_move.py entirely. 'invalid_at IS NULL' appears 10 times in graphiti_client.py; the finding claims five query sites, so that count is a loose but not load-bearing point. The 8-copy SET-list duplication holds.

findings.title: GraphitiBackend has no Cypher egress: timeout, cancellation, row-cap, scoping and liveness are re-decided at about 52 raw query sites, and four reads still turn timeouts into empty answers
findings.statement: graphiti_client.py has about 52 direct `graph.query`/`graph.ro_query` call sites and 15 asyncio.wait_for sites with two opposite postures. Most raw Cypher has no bound at all, and the FalkorDB connection sets no socket timeout. GraphitiBackend.search, search_nodes, retrieve_episodes and get_episode_by_uuid catch TimeoutError and return [] or None. With backend_read_timeout_seconds=30 above search_timeout_seconds=15, MemoryService.search gets its own timeout, but MemoryService.get_entity (fuzzy branch), get_episodes and get_episode_content receive a silent empty result that reads as 'not found'. This is the false-absence class task 5265 fixed for Mem0, where Mem0Backend._timed is 'THE single asyncio.wait_for call site' and propagates. Row-cap handling is opt-in per method: _paged_ro_query at 5 sites, a `len(rows) >= _RESULTSET_SIZE` warning at one site (find_entity_nodes_by_name_substring), and nothing elsewhere. Group scoping (`n.group_id = $group_id`) is hand-added at 9 sites. The backend also hands raw graph handles out through private accessors: cross_graph_move calls GraphitiBackend._graph_for 18 times and _require_falkor_client 5 times and writes its own Cypher. Every policy above therefore has a second copy outside the class.
findings.proposal: Add backends/falkor_gateway.py::GraphGateway as the only Cypher egress, with read(group_id, cypher, params, shape=Rows|Single|Paged) and write(group_id, cypher, params). It owns one timeout helper that propagates a TimeoutError naming the operation, as Mem0Backend._timed does. It owns one cancellation convention (fail_after plus shield at this single egress, the lesson recorded for httpcore). It owns row-cap detection: a non-aggregate Rows read returning >= _RESULTSET_SIZE raises IncompleteEnumerationError unless shape=Paged. It owns group scoping, binding and asserting $group_id. GraphitiBackend methods and cross_graph_move call the gateway, and _graph_for/_require_falkor_client stop being reachable outside the backend. Flip the four swallowing reads to propagate (task 5699 becomes a one-line change), and let MemoryService report a failed store as search already does. Code that dies: 15 scattered wait_for blocks, the four swallow arms, ad-hoc cap warnings, and 23 private reach-ins. This would have prevented the 4869 pagination fixes (three separate commits), 5265/5699 timeout false absence, 3898/4857-style false absence, and the 50bab12521 per-query group filter.
findings.bug_history_link: 4869 d3ee7e26aa, f30fec8020, ac25b02135 (paginate past the result-set cap, three readers fixed separately); 5265 53311e9fbf, 6777f90b28, 7eed36eac1 (Mem0 read timeouts made to propagate, Graphiti not); 5699 live (five TimeoutError swallows); 50bab12521 group_id filter; d15f909990 list_indices columns by name; e8cdc4a42f/e6681598bc drop_vector_indices fixed twice; operator note: Graphiti query timeouts cleared only by the 10-04 restart
findings.verdict_notes: graphiti_client.py has 48 query calls (claim says about 52). search (1777), search_nodes (1805), retrieve_episodes (1853) and get_episode_by_uuid (1877) catch TimeoutError and return []/None. memory_service.py docstrings at about 1813 admit that GraphitiBackend still swallows its inner TimeoutError, while the Mem0 path propagates. cross_graph_move calls _graph_for 24 times.

findings.title: Per-store write outcome is not a type: AddMemoryResponse folds leg failures into a message string, two producers disagree on an empty Mem0 result, and three consumers reconstruct 'did it land'
findings.statement: AddMemoryResponse carries memory_ids, stores_written, category and a free-text message. MemoryService.add_memory catches each store's exception into _graphiti_error/_mem0_error and appends ' [graphiti_error: ...]' / ' [mem0_error: ...]' to message. It journals a single success = not(either error) across both legs, and puts graphiti into stores_written when the enqueue succeeds, not when the write lands. The two Mem0 producers disagree on the same evidence. When mem0.add returns zero ids, add_memory still appends SourceStore.mem0 and journals success=True, logging a warning only. add_system_record treats the same case as not written: stores_written=[], success=False, error 'empty_result: ...'. Consumers rebuild the leg outcome on their own. write_triage.attach_write_landed infers failure from an explicitly empty memory_ids and resolves ambiguity toward 'landed'. stage_stats._count_add_memory/_count_graphiti_queued read result_summary shapes with a source carve-out because success is 'the AND across both legs'. dead_letter_escalator keeps a _REPORTED_TO_CALLER table because add_memory claimed graphiti at enqueue time.
findings.proposal: Add a LegOutcome type (landed(ids) | enqueued(write_op_id) | failed(error) | empty) and give AddMemoryResponse and the write-journal row legs: dict[SourceStore, LegOutcome]. Produce the Mem0 leg through one function, _mem0_leg_outcome(result, exc), shared by add_memory, add_system_record, _execute_mem0_write and recover_mem0_intents, so the empty-result decision has one home. Derive message for display only. Point attach_write_landed, stage_stats and dead_letter_escalator at legs. Code that dies: the message-folding, attach_write_landed's ambiguity heuristic, stage_stats' source carve-out and per-leg prose, and _empty_result_error. This would have prevented 4322 (counting the Mem0 leg off the per-op mask), 4045 (add_system_record claiming mem0 without an id), the 4069 digest/re-issue fixes and the 4770/4812/4872 timed-out-write-masks-landed-write class.

findings.title: canonical_labels' four regexes each re-decide the same fragments (padding, digit class, number edge, qualifier); fixes land one pattern at a time and are defended by about 550 lines of comments
findings.statement: canonical_labels.py is now the single home of the task-label vocabulary, and task_naming.py and cross_project_refs.py correctly delegate to it. Inside it, though, only _TASK_WORD is shared. Each of the four compiled patterns hand-assembles its own separator padding, digit capture, right-edge lookahead, anchoring and (for the two qualified patterns) a literally duplicated qualifier class `([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{2,})`. The file is 864 lines: 144 code, 414 comment and 270 docstring lines (79% prose). Most of that prose is measurement and task archaeology on the regex constants: which task narrowed which pad, why '\Z' not '$', which asymmetry is declared, which sibling was 'out of that task's scope'. The fix history shows the same decision fixed pattern by pattern. Colon padding was narrowed on three patterns in 4123 and on the fourth in 4850 (two commits). The digit class was narrowed for LOCAL (1fa8433e14) and then QUALIFIED (28ba2af6cc). The IGNORECASE-to-case-class change was applied twice. The qualifier's three-character minimum also silently diverges from validation.py's project-id charset `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+`.
findings.proposal: Define named fragments once (_LINE_PAD = r'[ \t]*', _WRAP_WS = r'\s+', _NUMBER = r'([0-9]+)', _NUMBER_EDGE = r'(?!\d)', _QUALIFIER, _LOCAL_SEP, _anchored(body)) and compose each of the four patterns as a one-line expression over them, so a deliberate asymmetry shows up as a different fragment name rather than a paragraph. Move the measured cases into a table-driven fixture (tests/fixtures/canonical_label_cases.yaml: input, entry point, expected Referent/None, reason). The fixture becomes the tracked home for the rationale, and the module keeps a one-line pointer (Comments stance). Derive _QUALIFIER from, or check it against, validation.py's project-id rule. Code that dies: about 450 lines of reviewer-answering prose and the per-pattern fix pattern.

findings.verdict_notes: File is 864 lines. Four separate re.compile patterns are at lines 184, 258, 346 and 403, with heavy comment prose about 4123/4850/4174 narrowing history. Duplicated fragments are real. Low-severity quality matter.

findings.title: memory_service.py is a ten-responsibility god module; the identity-reconcile third separates cleanly, and tests reach its passes through 383 private-attribute touches
findings.statement: Purpose needs 'and' about ten times; see architecture_notes. Heuristic 14 measurement. Step 1, prose: the file is 11,323 lines with 2,196 comment and 3,833 docstring lines (53%). Much of it is reviewer-answering prose that belongs in commit messages or PRDs, e.g. _check_canonical_uniqueness's roughly 190-line docstring of measurements, corrections of its own earlier claims ('THAT SPECIFIC HAZARD IS NOW CLEARED') and 'do not flip from this docstring alone'. Step 2, partition. (a) Episode identity reconcile: fact predicates (_is_dependency_fact, _priority_override_*), ReconcileStats/ReferentRepair/ReferentRepairStats, and the methods from _dedup_episode_edges through _reconcile_episode_identity plus the referent_*_counts accessors, about 3,400 lines. A self.* census shows this section uses only self.graphiti, self.taskmaster, self._write_journal, self._known_projects and its own four counters, and calls no MemoryService method outside itself. Its one inbound edge is _execute_graphiti_write calling _reconcile_episode_identity and bumping _referent_source_counts. Heuristic-13 symptom: none. (b) The module-level metadata seam (_apply_memory_metadata_validation, _check_canonical_uniqueness, cycle-summary tagging, _normalize_task_id_metadata, about 900 lines) already takes its collaborators as injected callables. Symptom: none. (c) Entity administration (ensure_entity_node through delete_entity) fails heuristic 13 today. It would have to import MemoryService._journaled_backend_call back from the parent, a reach-back from a new entity_admin.py into memory_service.py, unless journaling moves into WriteJournal first. Tests stance: five test files (test_memory_service.py 149, test_referent_repair.py 113, test_referent_verification.py 113, test_referent_queue_threading.py 7, test_dependency_direction_check.py 1) assign or call the private pass methods 383 times (`service._dedup_episode_nodes = ...`, `service._reconcile_episode_identity(...)`), plus 26 `service._write_journal =` assignments. The reconcile chain has no public seam. Heuristic 7: wiring happens by five set_* calls plus `memory_service.taskmaster = ...` after construction, which is temporal coupling.
findings.proposal: Extract services/episode_identity.py::EpisodeIdentityReconciler(graphiti, taskmaster, write_journal, known_projects). It owns the counters, stats dataclasses and fact predicates, and exposes reconcile(result, group_id, referents, ambiguous, content, referent_source) -> ReconcileStats, record_referent_source(src) and counts(). Its passes become an ordered tuple of ReconcilePass objects passed to the constructor, so tests inject or observe passes through the public constructor instead of patching 383 private attributes. Extract services/memory_metadata_seam.py for the module-level validation and uniqueness helpers. Before any entity_admin.py split, move journaling into WriteJournal.journaled_call. Construct MemoryService with its collaborators rather than setters. Record this measurement in the extraction commit, and move the reviewer prose into the commits and PRDs it answers. Code that dies: the private-attribute patching in five test files and the setter lifecycle.
