chains.name: Caller identity and capability are self-reported strings, so every write gate and every server re-derives authority
chains.description: MERGE: fm-task-layer.9 `fk-7aff55dd1465` and fm-recon.10 `fk-a3598aec7dca` have one root seen from two sides. fm-recon.4 is the producer: BaseStage tells the LLM in prose to echo agent_id "recon-stage-<id>". fm-task-layer.2 is the consumer: about 35 sites classify that string. Spot-checked: shared/task_transitions.py::derive_actor_class matches `startswith(('recon-stage-', 'reconciliation-stage'))`, while 23 `startswith('recon-stage-')` sites in fused-memory/src gate recon writes (ReconWritePolicy, execution_class, premise_lint, recurring_gate, _validate_done_provenance, the tools.py content guards). The transition table therefore calls a caller named 'reconciliation-stage-1' (the CLAUDE.md example) RECONCILIATION, yet that caller escapes every recon write gate. fm-memory.6 `fk-330a60eef271` is the same root on the memory-write side: the guard scoping keys on the same prefix plus a caller-asserted category, so add_episode, add_system_record and category=None each skip a different subset. Capability is kept in four hand-synced homes: CLI deny-lists, three config prefix allowlists, prompt prose and per-tool inline checks. That is why Stage 3 repeatedly shipped with write tools callable (aa02432724, c8fd434f38, 7ace787d74). The escalation server has the same defect in its own vocabulary. escalation.11 `fk-755f786c32be` shows four inline header reads with four meanings and no server-side gate on operator tools. escalation.10 `fk-bbb0a7b3c8a8` shows sentinel role decided by a `('harness-','orchestrator-')` prefix defined twice. escalation.2 `fk-ece88b7661b7` and escalation.3 `fk-2674ce12f83e` leave header-less callers open. The W2 role-derived level ceilings and the W5 ReconWritePolicy both landed on top of the string, so the string is still the authority.
chains.proposal: Define one frozen shared/caller_identity.py::CallerIdentity(actor: ActorClass, stage: StageId | None, run_id, raw). A transport middleware resolves it once per request, the same way in fused-memory and in the escalation server (next to MarkupGuardMiddleware). For recon stages it comes from a per-run credential that cli_stage_runner mints into the generated MCP config. For orchestrator roles it comes from the identity header. agent_id becomes attribution only. One capability table, STAGE_CAPABILITIES / TOOL_POLICY, keyed by (ActorClass|StageId, tool), drives the CLI --allowedTools, server authorization and the prompt tool list. fm-memory.1's WRITE_POLICY table and escalation.5's Principal rules key on CallerIdentity. This deletes the ~25 prefix checks, is_recon_stage_write, the three config prefix allowlists, the duplicated sentinel-prefix tuple and the per-tool 'not gated by design' prose.

chains.name: Did-it-land and how-to-recover have no single authority: TaskGroundTruth (W10) and the landed outbox (W1) landed beside the deciders they were meant to replace
chains.description: MERGE: harness.7 `fk-17b789fe3ce6` and scheduler.9 `fk-cc01eb7b143f` share one root: TaskGroundTruth._RECOVERY is not total. The harness applier rewrites four of its answers and adds blocked-row policy in prose. The scheduler's per-tick _phase_redispatch_stranded_blocked runs a hand-copied gate chain that performs the blocked->pending revert that row (g) forbids, and because it runs every tick it always fires before the harness sweep (the feedback-memory INFO-park re-pend specimens). MERGE: merge-queue.11 `fk-a152341e38ed` is the present form of merge-queue.3 `fk-e501862ffe2c` and workflow.1 `fk-175ebf5a366b`. The three journal-first workflow guards and TaskGroundTruth._resolve_branch_state treat a write-ahead LandedOutbox row as a confirmed landing. They are correct only because of two guarantees encoded elsewhere. (a) The Harness dispatch gate prunes rows first (reconcile_landed_task). (b) fused-memory's set_task_status re-checks kind='merged' SHAs with merge-base --is-ancestor in task_interceptor.py. Git-derived detectors remain as fallbacks at seven sites. The 'has it landed' question is answered by the outbox, by Harness._already_landed_dispatch_gate (465 lines that 'mirror' the sweep), by an INV-5 mirror of validate_landing_evidence inside the resolver, and by landing_evidence.py. That module sits in the lane's 'private' package (merge-queue.14 `fk-d9e6c03dc259`). The escalation server reaches it through function-local, type-ignored imports. Spot-checked: 13 `from orchestrator` imports in escalation/src, while escalation/pyproject.toml declares orchestrator only in its dev group and orchestrator depends on escalation, so the package edge is a cycle (escalation.7 `fk-a8d3003e9d83`). Fixes to landing authority (3103) therefore land in the escalation package.
chains.proposal: Promote landing to orchestrator/landing/ with one entry point, landed_sha(task_id). It reads CONFIRMED outbox rows: make LandedRow two-phase INTENT/CONFIRMED, discard the row on a non-advanced result, and have lookup return only CONFIRMED rows. It then falls back to the evidence producers in DISCOVERY mode. Make TaskGroundTruth.recovery_for total: explicit BLOCKED rows, REVERT_TO_PENDING rows for the shapes the scheduler sweep accepts (cooldown, cancel grace and the dependency verdict become TruthReport fields), and pin class plus enforce flags as RecoveryPolicy inputs. The harness applier, the dispatch gate, startup reconcile and the scheduler phase all become thin appliers of recovery_for. Row (g) needs one ruling from Leo. Move the escalation server's lane/merge tools, git_authority.py and merge_lane_resolution.py into orchestrator/mcp/lane_tools.py, registered on the same FastMCP instance, so every landing import points downward. This deletes the INV-5 mirror, the four applier rewrites, the 465-line gate's duplicated guards, the 'MUST treat row presence as provisional' obligation and the 14 reverse imports.

chains.name: A merge-deferred task has no durable owner: coalesce trains are unjournaled, and the recovery sweep is barred from them by design
chains.description: Spot-checked both ends. merge_lane/queue_store.py skips every GroupMergeRequest ('train merges are not journaled'). harness.py's _reconcile_one_stranded returns early on merge-deferred, and its comment says 'the stranded sweep provably cannot reach a merge-deferred task'. In fused-memory the members' state is only the status string 'merge-deferred', and Table A refuses merge-deferred->deferred, which hand-carries depend on. So after a crash with a coalesce train buffered or in flight, the members have no queue entry, no journal row and no sweep that will find them: the 09-16/17 class of 11 stranded tasks. 46e0933101 (5371 R7) closed this only for the drain case and named 4737 owner of the crash case. merge-queue.8 `fk-a2984bf98f85` is the same seam for single requests. ItemLifecycle (W1) is the one terminal record not driven by the request's future, so each exit arm hand-retires it. That is the 18x registry-divergence theme and the 16x slot-leak theme.
chains.proposal: Add merge_lane/train.py::TrainLedger. Journal a TrainRecord(train_id, kind, members, tip, state) before any absorbed future resolves, using a FORMED->VERIFYING->LANDED|DERAILED|DISSOLVED transition table. At startup, rebuild callbacks from _train_callback_factory(train_id) and either re-enqueue each non-terminal record or derail it once. State the invariant 'a merge-deferred task is named by a non-terminal TrainRecord' and check it at write and at recovery. Give TaskGroundTruth a merge-deferred row that consults the ledger, so the harness early-return becomes a table row instead of a blind spot. Follow with RequestHandle (merge-queue.2), so that one done-callback drives the lifecycle registry, the in-flight registry and journal pruning together.

chains.name: Merge and block outcome kinds travel as prose, so workflow, unblock, b3 gate, prompts and dashboard each re-parse them
chains.description: MERGE: merge-queue.10 `fk-e61eed486dbc` and the merge half of workflow.11 `fk-d2ba7601c130` describe one defect from producer and consumer. The gate knows the OutcomeKind (GateVerdict.emit_subtype) and sends it only to the event, while MergeOutcome carries a reason prefix. Spot-checked: 31 reason.startswith/REASON_PREFIX hits in workflow.py, 10 in unblock_types.py and 4 in b3_gate.py, plus a `'ff' in reason.lower()` fallback. On the workflow side the kind becomes one of five vocabularies. Only 7 of 68 _mark_blocked calls pass a BlockDisposition (W9 residual), and the payload rides on five stash dicts (workflow.9 `fk-44bc973b1cc4`). workflow.13 `fk-f12106b3adaf` is a live misroute of exactly this shape: the signature-repeat and opaque-timeout guards say 'escalating to L1' but end up as a generic steward L0. Escalation.category is a bare str whose REFACTOR TRIGGER (3709) has been overrun by about ten categories (escalation.10 `fk-bbb0a7b3c8a8`). roles.py restates the category list and the severity policy in prose and contradicts the server's downgrade gate (workflow.14 `fk-89388166d3ca`). The dashboard re-spells OutcomeKind and WorkflowOutcome as stale string sets and SQL fragments (dashboard.11 `fk-c927adb040e9`: five live kinds render grey, and cancels were counted as completions in the 6424 series).
chains.proposal: Move OutcomeKind (the W1/M3 merge enum; the W-program ownership table forbids a competing outcome enum), WorkflowOutcome, EventType and a new EscalationCategory into leaf modules in shared/. Add MergeOutcome.kind: OutcomeKind, required when status=='blocked' and checked in __post_init__. Workflow maps kind to a frozen BlockSpec(route, escalation_category, row_status, block_class, suggested_action) through one table. Inner phases return a PhaseResult sum carrying the BlockSpec in place of the stash dicts. unblock_types, b3_gate, roles.py prompt facts and dashboard families derive from the enums, and a test asserts every member is mapped. This deletes the 17 exported *_REASON_PREFIX constants, the startswith ladders, classify_block_reason, server.CATEGORIES, _CODE_FAMILY and _NOT_A_CANCEL.

chains.name: Task-write refusals are untyped dicts or prose, re-classified on both sides of the fused-memory boundary
chains.description: MERGE: fm-task-layer.14 `fk-f6224c565a9b` and fm-recon.11 `fk-be8ed2cd9ce9` share one root. The TaskInterceptor returns gate refusals as dicts of several shapes and lets backend exceptions propagate, so in-process callers need both try/except and interceptor_write_succeeded. Spot-checked: that helper is used by task_interceptor, targeted.py, citation_verifier.py and manifest_stamping.py, and targeted.py alone needed six 'classify X's response' fixes (81b52fe088 and siblings). On the orchestrator side, scheduler.py::extract_structured_rejection and is_transient_rejection re-parse MCP text and substrings into a mirrored exception family (scheduler.15 `fk-09bf639213ca` part b), so every new fm gate needs a matching orchestrator edit. fm-task-layer.11 `fk-d80c1c44bca1` adds the gate-ordering half. Table A (W2) is consulted at one site, after gate 2a has already encoded its terminal rule with a different error code, and scripts that open the store directly bypass it. escalation.12 `fk-609a1832903b` shows the same ad-hoc `{'error','code'}` refusal shape in the escalation server, a third independent dialect.
chains.proposal: Add one shared/task_write_result.py: WriteOutcome = Applied(task, changed: bool) | Refused(code: RefusalCode, details). Return it, never raise it; this takes fm-task-layer.7's shape over fm-recon.5's raise option. Backend exceptions carry a RefusalCode. The interceptor's gates become an ordered list of gate objects over a frozen StatusWriteRequest, with Table A enforced as the store floor for every writer. mcp_tool_errors serializes Refused separately from unexpected faults, and the orchestrator deserializes into the same type. This deletes interceptor_write_succeeded, extract_structured_rejection, the substring is_transient_rejection fallback, the mirrored orchestrator rejection classes and gate 2a. Escalation's Refusal type (escalation.6) should reuse the same Refused shape.

chains.name: No per-key metadata patch semantics, so the orchestrator retires keys with read-modify-write 'replace', and durable stamps stand in for state machines
chains.description: fused-memory's update_task has only whole-call metadata modes and no unset operation (fm-task-layer.8 `fk-116481623cfb`). Spot-checked: workflow.py (lines ~5776-6687) and harness.py delete merge_retry_pending and merge_phase_liveness by fresh-read plus metadata_mode='replace' under `# type: ignore[reportCallIssue]` and a require_fresh protocol (2991, 3024, #4271). RetryLedger persists through the _merge_fresh_metadata last-writer-wins merge (workflow.5 `fk-d57669feee23`). The RMW is not even atomic across processes (fm-task-layer.10 `fk-04c4612589ea`: no BEGIN, implicit-transaction SELECT). The mined theme 'clear that does not delete, stale stamps' (14x) and 5810 (ordered argv unioned) come from the same gap. Stamps also substitute for typed state. merge_phase_liveness exists only so the harness orphan-L0 reaper can guess liveness (workflow.12 `fk-bab6058b23c8`: 11 references in workflow.py, 6 in harness.py). The W10 DeployState landed beside the legacy before_done_* stamps, which DeterministicRunner.run still resumes from and which fm stage1_stall_detector and escalation parse as raw strings (scheduler.12 `fk-5a5d08e775de`). The update path still validates in enforce=False census mode (fm-task-layer.7 `fk-cc04e61d23ec`), so the W3 schema does not bind writes.
chains.proposal: First, the low-effort part: open the write connection with isolation_level=None and BEGIN IMMEDIATE in _txn. Then add shared/task_metadata_keys.py MetadataKeySpec (merge semantics, writer class, terminal_writable) and a typed MetadataPatch with set, unset and append operations, applied by one apply_metadata_patch inside the store transaction with enforce-mode validation. The orchestrator's clears become unset operations. DeployState becomes the only deterministic-progress record and the stamps become derived projections. Removing the L0 reaper's need for merge_phase_liveness belongs to the L0-ownership chain.

chains.name: Escalation records have no stable identity or owner: an L0's end of life and a record's location are re-derived by every reader
chains.description: An L0 is filed by the workflow, consumed by the steward and dismissed at 18 sites in three modules. No incarnation owns it, so the harness reaper infers liveness from freshness proxies and a stamp the workflow writes only for the reaper (workflow.12 `fk-bab6058b23c8`, theme 18x: 2725, 2800, 2878, 2931, 2991, 3002, 3541, 4988, 5643). In the escalation package, resolving a record moves its file, so identity changes with state (escalation.8 `fk-4a0626fc033d`). That forces four scan loops, a negative cache, a get() retry loop and the locked pending-only RMW copied at about 8 sites, plus the get_by_task two-tier scan (escalation.5 `fk-efdaf58c2177`). Spot-checked: server.py calls `queue._rewrite(escalation_id, rec)` on an unlocked stale snapshot, which can resurrect an archived record and fire the resolve callback twice (escalation.9 `fk-e9e943d0cd2c`). The orchestrator's cockpit keeps a polled DecisionRecord copy of the escalation lifecycle and re-implements the archive/YYYY-MM-DD layout and project-token normalisation to join it (harness.10 `fk-e8c835c3f412`), because the package issues no queue_id and gives no terminal hook. escalation.13 `fk-32903f2e64e0`: the sync file-lock queue runs on the orchestrator's event loop, with 11 hand-placed to_thread hops.
chains.proposal: Make escalation/store.py::RecordStore the only owner of layout and locking: read returns a tri-state, scan, mutate_pending(id, fn), archive, a stable queue_id, and an EscalationRef(queue_id, id). Give it a terminal-transition hook that writes the cockpit sidecar, and later consider not moving files at all. EscalationQueue.resolve takes resolution_action under the lock. Wrap it in an AsyncEscalationQueue facade on a bounded executor for in-loop callers. In the orchestrator, the filing incarnation's on_terminal cleanup disposes of its own L0s, and the reaper handles only provably dead claimants. This deletes the dismissal loops, _has_fresh_dispatch/_has_fresh_merge_phase, the merge_phase_liveness stamp, read_escalation_status, DECISION_CLOSE_MAP and the token-join normalisers.

chains.name: Checkout HEAD stands in for running-code identity across deploy and remote verify
chains.description: Spot-checked: verify_runner.py::RemoteRunner.sync_if_stale compares `git rev-parse HEAD` of the dispatcher's checkout with the remote's (lines ~1454/1458) and labels the match 'remote already runs the dispatcher's gate code'. The wire has no schema version (result_from_dict is VerifyResult(**d)). The 10-06T10:41Z wire-skew incident (51 DF and 26 reify verdicts lost, 16% of the laptop window) happened when reify's sync moved the shared laptop checkout to a VerifyResult with a new field (5627). The deploy side has the same gap. The watchdog's WATCHED_PATHS (spot-checked: orchestrator/src, escalation/src and three manifest files) omits shared/src, although the orchestrator imports shared throughout. The list is hand-kept in five copies, and REPO_DIR is hard-coded (harness.9 `fk-68efae8a36fc`). So nothing in the system knows which code a process is actually running. Fleet mutual exclusion is an advisory age lease that the sweep script overwrites unconditionally (harness.8 `fk-4c21aaf01b82`). verify.10 `fk-8dbae7d39adc` completes the picture: the local leg reads live config while the remote leg overlays a lossy spec field by field (2822, 2883, 4536, 5496). verify.8 `fk-caa8f680e1c2` enlarges VerifyResult and so re-arms the wire-skew hazard unless this lands first.
chains.proposal: Add shared/deploy_identity.py with closure(member), derived from the uv workspace plus the import walk (promoted from tests/scripts/test_fm_watched_paths_import_closure.py), and RUNNING_CODE_SHA captured at process start. The watchdog and both coordinators use closure(), and REPO_DIR is derived from the script's location. Add verify_wire.py with a WIRE_SCHEMA hash derived from the MergeVerifySpec/VerifyResult fields. sync_if_stale syncs to the running SHA and raises a typed WireSkew on mismatch. resolve_merge_verify(spec, HostProfile) becomes the only input on both legs, guarded by a round-trip property test. restart-all-orchestrators.sh and restart-fused-memory.sh take an flock, and the lease JSON stays only as an observability body.

chains.name: No shared MCP client: each consumer re-derives the protocol and is hardened separately
chains.description: MERGE: dashboard.10 `fk-9cdaf62ed9af` and legibility.4 `fk-12f0d08a6ccd` share one root. Both are private MCP protocol implementations (headers, SSE, handshake, result unwrap) next to shared.mcp_post and shared.mcp_envelope, which were created after 4023 and are 'a unit that cannot be partially applied'. The dashboard's _extract_tool_result returns {} on malformed envelopes (an INV-11 silent fail-soft), and legibility raises StatusFetchUnavailable for every escalate_info fault. Each copy took its own incident: 4023 (orchestrator), 2953 and 3644 (legibility posters, every escalation dropped), 4958, 5319 and 6063 (the dashboard CLOSE-WAIT wedge, 19.8h). dashboard.9 `fk-99f44f47a6cc` shows the dashboard's MCP client living in memory.py, with mcp_fanout reaching back through a function-local import and session eviction decided at four layers. dashboard.13 `fk-b224cb5b2566`: the dashboard's write proxies use read-style failover, so an ambiguous timeout can re-apply a mutating tool, and its idempotency note ('only reads') is false. legibility.1 `fk-ef642b412580`: five hand-copied escalate_info posters, of which only one journals before posting.
chains.proposal: Build one shared MCP client with sync and async faces on shared.mcp_post and parse_tool_result. It owns the session registry, eviction on any non-clean result, a default whole-call deadline, and a MUTATING_TOOLS set that disables failover on ambiguous outcomes. dashboard/mcp_client.py and legibility's raise_alarm are thin users of it. This deletes MCP_HEADERS, _parse_sse_response, _extract_tool_result, the legibility transport (about 400 lines), the four poster copies and the function-local import in first_success.

chains.name: Cross-package facts are copied instead of placed in shared/, held together by parity tests and 'mirrors X:line' comments
chains.description: MERGE: scheduler.14 `fk-37f2baab3aec` is fm-task-layer.3 `fk-b84e0aa4e545` re-found from the orchestrator side. Spot-checked: fused-memory/server/tools.py _OVERRIDE_SCHEMA, with 'Mirrors overrides.py:<line>' comments, writes the same SQLite files as orchestrator/overrides.py. Its stated reason is 'fused-memory cannot depend on orchestrator', which is exactly the case shared/ exists for (shared.deploy_state is already placed there). The same pattern recurs elsewhere. The lock-charter allowlist has four Python copies plus a bash copy, justified by a stale 'shared may be pinned' rationale (fm-task-layer.15 `fk-fa355c2c0498`). Spot-checked: seven pid-liveness predicates with three contracts (harness, task_ground_truth, session_registry, fleet_drain, config_dir, fm orchestrator_detector, watchdog). The task_ground_truth copy raises OverflowError on a corrupt plan.lock owner_pid and can crash-loop startup (harness.14 `fk-5d02d7903533`). The orchestrator re-implements the claude spawn recipe through four private shared imports and has already lost the VllmBridge (shared-infra.11 `fk-9854bd9a928f`). The dashboard re-spells orchestrator vocabularies (dashboard.11 `fk-c927adb040e9`).
chains.proposal: Treat 'cannot import X, so copy it' as a signal to move the fact into shared/. Moves: shared/scheduler_overrides.py (stores and DDL), shared.locking as the only allowlist, shared/proc_liveness.py::pid_alive (stdlib callers keep a parity-tested copy), the vocabularies from the outcome chain, and invoke_claude_agent(sandbox_wrap=...) in the orchestrator in place of its copy. Delete the copies, the parity tests that only guard copies, and the 'Mirrors' comments.

chains.name: Verify outcomes are flattened to text and re-parsed by merge lane, offline lane, workflow and the sweep (W7 residual)
chains.description: VerifyResult keeps leg outputs as strings, category as str and per-incident parallel lists. More than ten consumers re-parse them: _aggregate_results' substring scan, failure_report's 'timed out' sniff, confirm paths re-extracting ids although junit ids exist, offline_lane (x3) importing verify privates, merge_lane worker's cross-check veto over failing_leg_categories (3173), and workflow and evals. W7 produced FailureCategory and derive_verify_plan, but PlannedRun's slot is still recovered from reason prefixes (verify.14 `fk-c88f7d3ae54a`). The fallback path has two implementations (verify.2 `fk-d99f146ff901`), and _extract_cause_hint is a tool-blind regex ladder (verify.3 `fk-a2fb58789c14`). The isolated-rerun discriminator is implemented three times, so the 5492/6247 preconditions do not reach the sweep (verify.11 `fk-3756ad2f3357`). verify_runner reaches up into merge_lane.worker privates (verify.13 `fk-e906c4e914c2`). git-worktrees.10 `fk-7541c6b4090c`'s offline-lane state keys on fingerprints computed from the same text.
chains.proposal: Add verify_outcome.py with LegOutcome(slot: CheckSlot, tool, termination, category, session: PytestSession), parsed once at the leg boundary. VerifyResult becomes legs plus derived properties, and summaries are render-only. PlannedRun gets slot: CheckSlot. The three rerun paths become _CALL_SITE_POLICY rows. offline_lane and merge_lane consume PytestSession and public names. Sequence it after the WIRE_SCHEMA work in the deploy-identity chain.

chains.name: No owner of a task branch's ref or the git config its rebases run under
chains.description: Refs under refs/heads/task/* have about a dozen writers. Six rebase call sites bypass rebase_preserving_task_commits, among them merge_lane/worker.py::_do_train_merge and suffix_graph.bounce_conflicting_suffix_items (the merge-queue cross-notes, item 4), so foreign-commit grafts (3269: 103 commits; 4752: 59/386 branches; 5144) are patched per site in git_ops, workflow, merge_lane and suffix_graph. The shared .git/config sets rerere.enabled/autoupdate=true. That is the sole reason the 1,133-line rebase_recovery.py exists, and 5697 shows it is also a correctness hazard. Yet GitOps already converges repo config for gc (git-worktrees.12 `fk-54eb9f7cc0be`). 'Is there work to keep' is answered by seven predicates with opposite fail directions (git-worktrees.9 `fk-ad8c0528c5e1`). advance_main hands its failure details to merge_lane/gates.py through _last_* attributes read by getattr (git-worktrees.11 `fk-eb7b9f65f412`). The private git_ops._run is the factory-wide runner, imported by seven modules and patched in 235 tests (git-worktrees.13 `fk-d73aeaebb792`).
chains.proposal: Make orchestrator/git_runner.py a public GitRunner injected everywhere; it prepends -c rerere.enabled=false -c rerere.autoupdate=false to rebase, merge and cherry-pick argvs. Make TaskBranch, built on it, the only mutator of task refs: it records own_base and rebases with --onto <main> <own_base>, asserting own_delta. Add a WorkPresence verdict with an explicit Unknown, and make AdvanceOutcome carry its failure payloads.

chains.name: A raw-line ratchet and prose-as-defence feed each other
chains.description: The merge-lane ratchet gates 'lines' and 'prose_lines', the measures the definition puts first under 'Do not steer by'. The result is reflow and trim commits (64d8021a19, 435869ea61, a82d7010dd, 504b996013, 8f4182d742, ef6717321b in git_ops) and line-only authorized raises. At the same time the core files of several clusters are 46-76% prose made of reviewer-answering archaeology, and 10 of 61 commits on stale_status_snapshot_edge_sweep.py only correct prose. The ratchet penalises rehoming prose into docs/ less than it penalises a net-additive bug fix, and it rewards the trimming the definition warns against.
chains.proposal: Drop lines and prose_lines from the ratcheted set and keep the structural measures. Report prose share per file as a metric. Rehome prose per edit under the Comments stance, never as a sweep.

top_priorities: 1. Close the coalesce-train stranding: journal a TrainLedger (merge-queue.7 `fk-c55b12f4b66d`) and give TaskGroundTruth a merge-deferred row. This removes the only known open crash path that strands merge-deferred tasks with no sweep able to reach them (the 09-16/17 11-task class, owner 4737, 5371 R7). It is medium effort and lane-local, and it is a prerequisite for RequestHandle (merge-queue.8 `fk-a2984bf98f85`).

2. Bind caller identity at the transport into one shared CallerIdentity with one capability table (fm-task-layer.9 `fk-7aff55dd1465` merged with fm-recon.10 `fk-a3598aec7dca`, fm-memory.6 `fk-330a60eef271`, escalation.11 `fk-755f786c32be`, escalation.2 `fk-ece88b7661b7`, escalation.3 `fk-2674ce12f83e`). This removes four high findings plus a live gate bypass (a 'reconciliation-stage-*' caller escapes every recon write gate) and the repeated Stage-3 write-exposure class. Start with the parser and middleware, then the per-run credential.

3. Make MergeOutcome.kind: OutcomeKind mandatory for blocked outcomes and route workflow, unblock and b3 on it through one BlockSpec table, with Category, WorkflowOutcome and OutcomeKind moved to shared/ (merge-queue.10 `fk-e61eed486dbc` merged with workflow.11 `fk-d2ba7601c130`, workflow.9 `fk-44bc973b1cc4`, escalation.10 `fk-bbb0a7b3c8a8`, workflow.14 `fk-89388166d3ca`, dashboard.11 `fk-c927adb040e9`). It deletes 45 prefix-routing sites and fixes the live misroute in workflow.13 `fk-f12106b3adaf`. Reuse the W1/M3 OutcomeKind, not a new MergeBlockKind.

4. Make landing and recovery single-authority: two-phase LandedRow plus landed_sha() in an orchestrator/landing package, a total TaskGroundTruth table that the scheduler's stranded-blocked phase applies, and the escalation server's lane tools moved into orchestrator (harness.7 `fk-17b789fe3ce6`, scheduler.9 `fk-cc01eb7b143f`, merge-queue.11 `fk-a152341e38ed`, merge-queue.14 `fk-d9e6c03dc259`, escalation.7 `fk-a8d3003e9d83`, merge-queue.3 `fk-e501862ffe2c`, workflow.1 `fk-175ebf5a366b`, harness.5 `fk-bf4197a9a7d9`, scheduler.2 `fk-5cad48d24b6f`). These are the W1 and W10 residuals where both the new and the old deciders are still live. A ruling on row (g) is needed first.

5. Make running-code identity a fact: deploy_closure() for every watch list, WIRE_SCHEMA plus running SHA on the remote-verify wire, a spec-only resolve_merge_verify on both legs, and an flock in both restart scripts (verify.9 `fk-5fa21a4b85cb`, harness.9 `fk-68efae8a36fc`, verify.10 `fk-8dbae7d39adc`, harness.8 `fk-4c21aaf01b82`). This removes the unowned 10-06 wire-skew outage class (16% of the laptop window), the shared/src staleness gap, and the lease-overrun residual. It must land before verify.8 `fk-caa8f680e1c2` grows VerifyResult.

6. Give task writes a typed outcome and per-key patch semantics: WriteOutcome/RefusalCode in shared/ (fm-task-layer.14 `fk-f6224c565a9b` merged with fm-recon.11 `fk-be8ed2cd9ce9`, fm-task-layer.11 `fk-d80c1c44bca1`), BEGIN IMMEDIATE now (fm-task-layer.10 `fk-04c4612589ea`, low effort), then MetadataKeySpec with an unset operation (fm-task-layer.8 `fk-116481623cfb`). This retires interceptor_write_succeeded, scheduler.extract_structured_rejection, and the orchestrator's replace/require_fresh clears (workflow.5 `fk-d57669feee23`, fm-task-layer.7 `fk-cc04e61d23ec`).

7. Land the low-effort latent-bug fixes as one batch now, each with a public-seam regression test: shared pid_alive (harness.14 `fk-5d02d7903533`, startup crash loop on a corrupt plan.lock), resolution_action set under the lock (escalation.9 `fk-e9e943d0cd2c`), offline-lane promoted-fingerprint clear (git-worktrees.10 `fk-7541c6b4090c`), probe argv via claude_binary_spec (shared-infra.13 `fk-7bbea5d4e082`), success-scan default (shared-infra.8 `fk-2baeac877911`), expired_at on cross-graph move (fm-memory.13 `fk-2049b8c631e4`), write-proxy no-failover (dashboard.13 `fk-b224cb5b2566`), census.main prelude escalation (legibility.2 `fk-213e02a4eeab`), per-argv rerere off (git-worktrees.12 `fk-54eb9f7cc0be`), and lines/prose_lines out of the ratchet (merge-queue.9 `fk-f4af080fcd25`).

8. Build one shared MCP client (sync and async) on shared.mcp_post and mcp_envelope, owning eviction, deadlines and a mutating-tool set, and route the legibility posters through one raise_alarm (dashboard.10 `fk-9cdaf62ed9af` merged with legibility.4 `fk-12f0d08a6ccd`, dashboard.9 `fk-99f44f47a6cc`, legibility.1 `fk-ef642b412580`). This ends the per-consumer 4023/2953/3644/4958 hardening series and the silent {} fall-through.
cross_system.contradictions:
1. Direction of the escalation-to-orchestrator edge. merge-queue.14 `fk-d9e6c03dc259` would have escalation import a promoted orchestrator/landing package 'at module level through a declared dependency'. escalation.7 `fk-a8d3003e9d83` would move the lane tools out of escalation so that escalation never imports orchestrator. Orchestrator already depends on escalation, and escalation lists orchestrator only in its dev group, so merge-queue.8's version makes a package cycle. Adopt escalation.1; the landing package is then imported only downward, from orchestrator.

2. Merge kind field. merge-queue.10 `fk-e61eed486dbc` reuses OutcomeKind (MergeOutcome.kind); workflow.11 `fk-d2ba7601c130` invents MergeBlockKind (MergeOutcome.blocked_kind). The 07-06 program's ownership table says no competing outcome enum, so use OutcomeKind.

3. Four retry-budget mechanisms. merge-queue.12 `fk-769c3bb58ce1` proposes merge_lane/retry_budget.py::RetryBudget. workflow.15 `fk-9eb149f0706d` proposes a RetryBudget registry built on streaks.py::StreakCounter with declared Durability. scheduler.13 `fk-b2cd27267851` proposes a RequeueLedger inside TaskDispatchRecord. shared.task_metadata.RetryLedger (workflow.5 `fk-d57669feee23`) already exists. These are one axis of variability (heuristic 3), so build one registry (workflow.7's shape, with durability declared). The merge lane's LaneRetryPolicy and the scheduler's requeue counters become declared budgets in it, and the names must not collide with the existing RetryLedger.

4. Identity. fm-task-layer.9 `fk-7aff55dd1465` parses the self-reported agent_id once at the boundary. fm-recon.10 `fk-a3598aec7dca` binds identity to a per-run transport credential and ignores agent_id. fm-memory.6 `fk-330a60eef271` adds CallerRole and escalation.11 `fk-755f786c32be` adds Principal. Parsing a self-reported string does not close spoofing, so authority must come from the transport credential or header, with agent_id kept for attribution only, and all four should be one shared type.

5. Write outcome shape. fm-task-layer.14 `fk-f6224c565a9b` returns Applied|Refused from shared/; fm-recon.11 `fk-be8ed2cd9ce9` offers Landed|Refused or raising WriteRefused. Choose the returned sum type in shared/; raising re-creates the two-channel problem.

6. Sequencing: verify.8 `fk-caa8f680e1c2` adds and reshapes VerifyResult fields, which is exactly the change that caused the verify.9 `fk-5fa21a4b85cb` wire-skew outage. WIRE_SCHEMA must land first. dashboard.8 `fk-8dfa5e5a75aa` adds a census tool to fused-memory/server/tools.py (a hub file with lock contention) and should follow the fm-task-layer.12 `fk-45cf67bff540` split.

7. Conflicts with existing mechanisms or rulings:
- harness.8 `fk-4c21aaf01b82`'s flock demotes the 4754/4755/5371 age lease to observability. --report's FLEET-LEASE line and the liveness probe's current_unit check read that body, so keep the body.
- workflow.12 `fk-bab6058b23c8` says the steward must never dismiss an L0, which reverses the 3170 contract ('give-up ALWAYS dismisses its own L0') and the 5352 terminal give-up; this needs an explicit migration.
- scheduler.8 `fk-4b35b1adea0d` must extend task 6518's in-flight dependency_verdict.py rather than fork it. Its 'UNKNOWN keeps parks' rule matches Leo's esc-6040-7 ruling (expiry only on known-unsatisfied).
- scheduler.9 `fk-cc01eb7b143f`'s single table must decide row (g) ('no silent blocked->pending') against the per-tick re-pend the scheduler does today. That needs a ruling, not a merge.
- git-worktrees.12 `fk-54eb9f7cc0be`'s repo-wide alternative (pin rerere off in .git/config) overrides the operator's interactive setting; prefer per-argv -c in GitRunner unless Leo rules otherwise.
- shared-infra.8 `fk-2baeac877911` reverses a recorded 6042 choice to leave the fleet default unchanged.
- fm-task-layer.11 `fk-d80c1c44bca1`'s store-level Table A floor must keep the merge-deferred->deferred refusal that the hand-carry procedure relies on.
- escalation.8 `fk-4a0626fc033d`'s 'stop moving files' option breaks harness read_escalation_status, the dashboard and the watchers, which read archive/YYYY-MM-DD directly. RecordStore must become the only reader first.
- fm-recon.7 `fk-9b76dd8a1cdb` (typed TaskStateClaim edges, reject untyped status claims for all callers) overlaps fm-memory.6 `fk-330a60eef271`'s live-status write guard. Let the write-policy table own refusal, and let the typed edge own normalization.

8. W-stream residuals, where the new mechanism landed but the parallel old one remains:
- W1: the outbox sits beside git detectors and intent is read as confirmed (merge-queue.11 `fk-a152341e38ed`, merge-queue.3 `fk-e501862ffe2c`). ItemLifecycle is hand-retired (merge-queue.8 `fk-a2984bf98f85`). QueuedBranch sits beside 27 f-strings (merge-queue.5 `fk-718c82fcc1a2`).
- W2: Table A is consulted after gate 2a and bypassed by store writers (fm-task-layer.11 `fk-d80c1c44bca1`). Escalation legality never narrows (escalation.1 `fk-d0e1094c99cb`).
- W3: the schema runs in enforce=False on update, and parser copies remain (fm-task-layer.7 `fk-cc04e61d23ec`, fm-task-layer.1 `fk-1f8a4c69798f`).
- W4: classify_invocation is re-decided by detect_cap_hit (shared-infra.7 `fk-dcc5dce60bb6`), and the AccountPhase setters bypass _transition (shared-infra.1 `fk-db060c262575`).
- W5: the ledger sits beside the Mem0 flag_for_stage2 channel (fm-recon.1 `fk-9165ae3a1e72`, fm-recon.9 `fk-e30ecd1f36b8`), and ReconWritePolicy is keyed on the prefix (fm-recon.10 `fk-a3598aec7dca`).
- W6: the identity lock covers ingest only (fm-memory.7 `fk-9804ecc4567d`), and the nine post-hoc passes remain (fm-memory.1 `fk-abc3487a3528`).
- W7: the fallback has two implementations and the classifier is tool-blind (verify.2 `fk-d99f146ff901`, verify.3 `fk-a2fb58789c14`, verify.14 `fk-c88f7d3ae54a`).
- W9: the machine sits beside literal set_task_status calls and stash reports (workflow.3 `fk-ee708be4436f`, workflow.9 `fk-44bc973b1cc4`), and BlockDisposition is used in 7 of 68 calls (workflow.11 `fk-d2ba7601c130`).
- W10: TaskGroundTruth sits beside four applier rewrites, the dispatch gate and the scheduler sweep (harness.7 `fk-17b789fe3ce6`, scheduler.9 `fk-cc01eb7b143f`). DeployState sits beside the stamps (scheduler.12 `fk-5a5d08e775de`). The phases share sentinel-less TickContext defaults (scheduler.10 `fk-3e1e7c5129b5`).
- W11: LaneLifecycle is written through a private accessor and the recovery copies have diverged (harness.13 `fk-e6a18c90d2fe`, git-worktrees.3 `fk-31e9856ed662`).
